name: Needle 3 decode tokens/second on ESP32-S3 (N32R16), 8-layer model, quality frozen

description: Baseline: unmodified 8-layer Needle 3 on the attached ESP32-S3, measured through the real request path (flash, boot, both schema prefixes primed, 12 greedy grammar-constrained requests). decode_tps 1.2217 = mean of 6 primary cases; per-case spread only 1.19-1.23 tok/s. Device goldens and host goldens frozen here.

asi.hypothesis: establish baseline before any kernel change
asi.timing_is_deterministic: identical decode_ms (11415 twice, 11752 twice) across separate runs on the same binary - measurement noise is ~0, so tiny wins are real; only risk is the 0.01 tps tps-field quantisation
asi.budget_per_token: 816 ms/token at 240MHz = ~196M cycles/token; theoretical weight-streaming floor at 2-bit is ~300-400ms/token, so ~2x headroom
asi.observed_structure: 8 layers, d_model 768, 12 heads/2 KV heads, 4 mHC lanes, hada_n 1024, engram sites at layers 4 and 7, vocab 8192, window 384
asi.internal_heap: only 38KB internal SRAM free - any new internal-RAM buffer must fit that; PSRAM has 15.6MB free
asi.phase_breakdown: not yet collected - next run should use AUTO_PROFILE=1 to see proj2bit/attention/hadamard/mhc_phi4/engram/logits4/prep+lut/confpool shares
asi.prime_cost: boot priming costs 110s (143 tok) + 167s (213 tok); a full measure.sh iteration is ~11 min
asi.think_path: 1.14 tok/s with reasoning enabled (unconstrained full-vocab argmax) vs 1.22 constrained - different code path, both monitored
asi.golden_note: heldout_status ('Is a timer running right now?') is genuinely ambiguous: model answers set_timer(60). Expectation left blank; exactness vs golden still enforced - if a speed change flips that case the gate fires and it gets discarded.

name: Needle 3 decode tokens/second on ESP32-S3 (N32R16), 8-layer model, quality frozen

description: Stage the multiply-read fp16 MLP weights as float32 at model open: the six Monarch Kronecker factors (w1a..w3b) plus d2/b2/d3/d4. kron_apply re-read each factor na times per application (1.57M nd_f16 calls/token across the model vs 49K distinct elements). Device decode 1.2217 -> 2.4417 tok/s (+99.9%), prefill +105%, think +88%, extended +98%, boot bench 816 -> 406 ms/tok. All 12 device cases byte-identical, host 11/11 exact, logit fidelity 9.5e-07 vs a 2e-3 budget. Cost: 320 KB PSRAM for the copies, internal heap 38487 -> 34895.

asi.hypothesis: ideas backlog: hoist the fp16->fp32 conversions out of kron_apply by staging each factor as float32 once at open
asi.why_bigger_on_device: on x86 the 2KB factors sit in L1 so the win is only the F2F instruction; on the S3 each kron pass re-reads the factor while the fp32 activation streams, so the fp16 loads and the conversion compete with it. Do not predict device gains from host ratios.
asi.verification: flashed both binaries back-to-back and read the firmware's own boot bench: BASE 816 ms/tok, CAND 406 ms/tok, cpu_hz=240000000 reported by esp_clk_cpu_freq() in both. Byte-exact text on all 12 device cases.
asi.accuracy_note: accumulation order is unchanged by design (same loop nests, same sum order), so the fp32 values are exactly representable and fidelity stays at 9.5e-07
asi.next_action_hint: look for the same pattern elsewhere: any per-element nd_f16() inside a loop that re-reads a weight vector dim times. tap_projection (q/k/v taps) is the next candidate but its fp32 copy is ~1.8 MB - check PSRAM headroom (15.3 MB free) rather than internal heap.
asi.process_note: the earlier 1.22 readings in this session were a stale/baseline tree, not a real measurement; this is the first honest candidate number

Same slot-indexed fp32 pool, zero numerical change. Device decode 2.4417 -> 2.5400 tok/s (+4.0%), prefill +4.2%, think +3.7%, extended +4.0%, boot bench 406 -> 390 ms/tok. 12/12 device cases and 11/11 host prompts byte-identical; logit probe 9.537e-07.

asi.accuracy_note: bit-exact: logit probe max_delta 9.537e-07 (same as the accepted baseline drift), host text 11/11 byte-exact, device text 12/12 byte-exact
asi.cost: +260 KB PSRAM for the copies (psram_free 15.32M -> 15.05M); internal heap unchanged at 34895
asi.hypothesis: extend the run #2 pattern: stage the remaining multiply-read fp16 MLP weights (cond_u, read 8x per element per layer) as float32 at open
asi.measured_effect: decode 2.4417 -> 2.5400 (+4.0%), boot bench 406 -> 390 ms/tok, prefill +4.2%, think +3.7%, extended +4.0% -- every path moved, consistent with a per-layer constant cost
asi.next_action_hint: the same pattern is exhausted inside hadamard_mlp: cond_v, cond_u, d1, d2..d4 and w1a..w3b are all fp32 now. What is left in fp16 is read exactly once per token. Next biggest fish per the device profile are proj2bit (the 2-bit LUT GEMV) and attention, not the MLP.

description: Hoist the per-group fp16 norm conversion out of the 2-bit LUT GEMV inner loop (inlining dot_group_lut2 so the norm scalar multiplies once per group). Byte-identical and same speed as run #3 (2.5400 tok/s, boot bench 390 ms/tok): the phase is bandwidth/table bound, not conversion bound. Kept as a free refactor; recorded as a measured null result for arithmetic work in that kernel.

asi.hypothesis: hoist the per-group nd_f16(norm) out of the 2-bit LUT GEMV inner loop, which is the largest device phase
asi.measured_effect: IDENTICAL to run #3: boot bench 390 ms/tok both, both images, back to back. The hoist changes nothing measurable.
asi.explanation: the hoist is a true refactor (same value, same order) but the compiler already sank that conversion; the phase is bound by the table lookups (16-entry float LUT read per weight pair) and by the flash-streamed packed rows, not by the conversion. That makes it consistent with the model: MLP (compute-bound) responded enormously to fp32 staging, the GEMV (bandwidth-bound) does not.
asi.next_action_hint: stop optimising arithmetic in the 2-bit GEMV. If the biggest phase is to move, it has to move as bytes: fewer bytes streamed per token, or better cache residency for the LUT/packed rows. Also verify what the dual-core splitter actually covers.
asi.process_note: candidate and baseline images built from the same tree, hash-verified, flashed back-to-back; run #4 kept only because the tree is identical to run #3 in output and the hoist is free - if a later change needs that inner loop simple, the plain form is one line

asi.hypothesis: the Monarch Kronecker apply has one loop-carried sum per output element, so every FMA waits on the previous one on the LX7. Column-blocking the second half by 4 gives four independent chains and keeps the shared hada_c row live across them.

The same blocking applies to the FIRST half (rows of src over a) and to the second half at a different block size (8 columns / 2 columns). Try both, and try blocking both halves together. This is the first real win in the MLP since the fp32 staging, and it contradicts my earlier note that 'scheduling is not the lever' - that was true for the bandwidth-bound GEMV, not for the compute-bound MLP.

description: Experiments 2+3: handwritten TIE728 (ESP32-S3 SIMD FP) CQ2 row walker replaces the C kernel. Same-batch three-board A/B: control 4.190, candidates 4.735/4.735 (+13.0% decode, +12.7% extended, +10.4% think, +14.1% prefill, min_case 4.00->4.49), byte-exact 12/12 device + 11/11 host, fidelity probe unchanged (5.34e-05, top1 10/10). Microbench: 30.4% isolated / 31.7% two-core-split cycle saving on 768x768 with Needle 3's own pair tables, exact=768/768 bitexact=1 on 768/576/128/96.

asi.hypothesis: MimiModel Experiment 2: handwritten TIE728 assembly CQ2 kernel beats the GCC C kernel on the dominant 768x768 2-bit projection (48% of decode), then Experiment 3 wires it in.
asi.result: CONFIRMED +13.0% device decode (4.190 -> 4.735), byte-exact host+device, fidelity probe unchanged.
asi.kernel_shape: tie1 = one row per call, 8 pairs (16 weights) deep, TIE FP SIMD: l32e index word + lp32e pair-table quad + loop of 11 instructions per 8 weights, madd.s accumulation. tie2 (two rows interleaved, 4 deep) only +24.5% vs +31.7%: batch depth in one row beats two rows.
asi.build_gotchas: (1) .align 4 inside an .iram1 section makes GCC's relax pass emit .reloc 3/.reloc 2 into .gnu.linkonce.iram1.* and the linker fails with 'missing relocation type' - drop .align, IRAM sections are already 4-aligned. (2) A section named .iram1.foo is NOT collected into the IRAM segment; must be .iram1.text.foo. (3) 'undefined reference to ldext.S' from a .S file referencing a C symbol declared static in that TU - nd_lut2_rows_c had to be non-static. (4) call8 frame must be (16+n_out_regs)*4 bytes (96 here); a 64-byte frame corrupted a12/a13 gather addresses and produced a double exception at retw with no usable panic printout.
asi.debug_method: Synthetic mapping checks found the real tie2 bug (row-pair advance moved one rowbytes, not two: rows 2..5 returned rows 1..2) - table=1.0 plus norms 1..24 makes any stride/order bug visible as an arithmetic difference, not a rounding difference. A separate '4 bad rows' scare was the staged debug probe writing through ctx->y over the reference rows.
asi.harness_fix: measure.sh and checks.sh now source /opt/esp/idf/export.sh when idf.py/cmake are off PATH; run_experiment had IDF_PATH exported with no tools on PATH, so every run died with exit 127 in 0.0s and the metric was unmeasurable.

Also re-run AUTO_PROFILE: proj2bit's 48.0% share was measured at 3.76 tok/s and is now cheaper, so the next big phase (attention 16.7%, hadamard 10.6%) may be worth retargeting.

description: Experiment 4: shipping CQ2 kernel is tie1n - one row, four partials, eight-deep gather batch, with the group's FP16 norm halfword loaded at the top of the group instead of at the fold. Microbench (bit-exact, 3 boards, spread <=0.1 pp): +33.4% cycle saving vs C against tie1's +32.4%; deeper index prefetch (-1.9pp), two-row blocking (-6.7pp) and early norm conversion (-1.1pp) all lose. Device: 4.735 -> 4.745 (+0.21%), +13.2% over the C kernel measured in the same batch (4.190), byte-exact 12/12 device + 11/11 host, fidelity unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Experiment 4 (TIE728 scheduling variants): on this board the winning schedule is one row / four partials / eight-deep batch; test whether the per-group norm stream and deeper index prefetch matter.
asi.microbench: split-mode saving vs C on 768x768 with real pair tables, three boards, all bit-exact: tie1n +33.4, tie1 +32.4, tie1m +32.3, tie1p +30.6, tie2 +25.7. Board-to-board spread <=0.1pp; use within-run comparisons (absolute values drift ~0.4pp between runs).
asi.conclusion: The index stream is already covered by the hardware load queue - software prefetch of 4 index words through a8/a9 loses 1.9pp. The unhidden latency is the norm halfword on the second stream; hoisting just its l16ui (not the conversion) gains ~1pp of saving = ~1.5% kernel time = +0.21% decode.
closed_in_this_family: whole-group table base in an lsi immediate (field caps at 1020 bytes, a 0x1000 per-group advance is illegal, so 3 addi/group is the floor)
asi.device_delta: +0.21% over tie1, which is close to the noise floor, but it is the microbenchmark's own winner, reproduced identically on three boards (4.745/4.745/4.745) and on the board that had read 4.735 with tie1 twenty minutes earlier.

It re-confirmed the +13% win in a fresh batch, but the intended tie1-vs-tie1n control was lost. Restore every board checkout to HEAD's knobs after a batch that flips them; do not leave per-batch option edits behind.

Also worth one cheap run: re-profile with NEEDLE_PROFILE to get proj2bit's new share now that the kernel is ~1.5x faster than C - attention (16.7%) and hadamard (10.6%) are the next candidates for the same treatment.

description: Attention: attn_heads now works a whole KV group at a time, staging each position pair's K and V rows once (int8 -> float, 4 bytes per word load) and sharing them across the group's query heads (12 heads over 2 KV heads = six sharing each row). Bit-exact by construction and by measurement: host 11/11, device 12/12, token_delta 0, logit probe unchanged at 5.341e-05. Device: 4.745 -> 4.7783 (+0.70%), +14.0% over the stock C control measured in the same batch (4.190); extended +0.82%, think +0.5%, prefill +0.6%, boot +1.0%, min_case 4.50 -> 4.55.

asi.hypothesis: attention's QK dot converts every int8 K byte to float once per query head, and 12 heads share 2 KV heads, so staging each KV row once per group should remove 5/6 of the unpacking and of the cache reads with no numerical change.
asi.result: +0.70% decode, byte-exact everywhere. The conversion and KV traffic were real but smaller than expected: attention's 38.6 ms only gave up ~1.5 ms, so what is left in that phase is the score/softmax bookkeeping and the per-element products, not the int8 unpacking.
asi.bit_exact_reason: per-element expressions were kept textually identical ((float)(int8_t) of the byte becomes a staged float of the same value), each head keeps its own running max/denominator/accumulator and still meets its positions in ascending order, so every product, sum, rescale and normalisation happens in the same order as before.
asi.splitter_trap: The first attempt used KV groups as the parallel units (nrows=2). rows_dual_core() in main.c runs fn on one core whenever nrows/2 < 2, so the whole attention phase went single-core and decode fell to 4.1817 - below the stock C control. Units must be query heads (nh=12, half=6), and because the ranges are group-aligned each core still owns whole groups. Any future small-unit split has to clear that same threshold.
asi.stack_cost: attn_heads' frame is ~1.1-1.4 kB (two staged K rows + two staged V rows + per-head softmax state), so the worker task stack went 4096 -> 8192: the profiled build overflowed 4 kB and never reached EVT ready. internal_free 23015 -> 17119 (4 kB task stack + ~1.8 kB of extra code in .iram1 shifting the heap).
asi.measured_dead_end_saves: the single-core version was measured and reverted in-batch, not kept; its number (4.1817) is recorded here so the 12% penalty is not re-derived.
asi.next: Two follow-ups in this family: (1) the same staging trick cannot be applied to the sink/recent split (each run already stages its own rows), but the odd-tail path could share a row across groups; (2) attention's remaining 37 ms is score bookkeeping and products - a TIE728 kernel for the per-head dot+accumulate is the remaining idea there, and kron_apply (11.0 ms, dense fp32, no bandwidth) is the other measured candidate.

description: Diagnostic cycle, no runtime change (4.7783 = #139 exactly): added ND_P_* sub-phase timers and measured the full per-token map on device. 201 ms token = 2-bit GEMV 86.5 (43%, of which q/k/v/gate ~59), attention head split 36.7 (18%), Hadamard MLP 24.6 (12%, kron 11.1), engram 16.4 (8%), mHC phi 4-bit 13.5 (6.7%), attn stage 5.1 (taps 3.3 / head norms 0.5 / rope 0.2 / KV store 1.1), mHC mix 4.7, sinkhorn 4.3, prep+LUT 3.5, step tail 0.5, sampler 0.0, conf pool 0.0, unattributed ~14. Byte-exact 12/12 device + 11/11 host.

asi.hypothesis: Find where the remaining ~25 ms/token goes before writing more assembly: is it per-request overhead, the sampler, UART emit, an unnamed attention stage, or an unexamined kernel?
killed_ideas: kron_apply assembly: disassembling GCC's kron1_blocks shows entry + hardware `loop` + 6 lsi + 8 madd.s already, i.e. 1.75 instructions/product. There is nothing to win by hand-writing it.
per-request overhead / sampler / tokenizer / UART emit as the missing time: ND_P_SAMPLE = 0.0 ms, step tail 0.5 ms, and the boot-bench residual is ~14 ms of per-layer glue.
attention pre-split stage: taps+head norms+rope+KV store is 5.1 ms total (3.3/0.5/0.2/1.1). The attn-stage timer's 101.8 ms is almost all the q/k/v/gate GEMVs, which are already counted in proj2bit.
engram as an unexamined target: its key/value projections already go through nd_cq_gemv_lut2, so they use the TIE728 kernel; the rest is flash-latency gathers.
asi.only_clear_arithmetic_target_left: the 4-bit generic path (dot_group, used by mHC phi_pre/post/res = 13.5 ms): its inner loop is ~5 instructions per weight (extui + addx4 + lsi(cb) + lsi(xh) + madd.s), where the 2-bit pair-LUT path runs ~3. A nibble -> codebook-float lookup table (16 floats = one 64-byte cache line, L1-hot) should cut it to ~3-4, worth +1.4-2.0% decode. Bit-exactness is achievable because the products and the four accumulators are fixed.
asi.timers: ND_P_KRON/BLOCK/SINK/MHCX/STEP/SAMPLE/ATTNX/TAPS/HNORM/ROPE/KVST added; they compile away when ND_PROFILE is off, so no shipping image changes.

phi_anatomy_now_measured.codegen: GCC's 4-bit loop in dot_group is a hardware `loop` with 1 l32i + 8 extui + 8 addx4 + 8 lsi(cb) + 8 lsi(xh) + 8 madd.s per 8 weights = 4.1 instructions/weight - near the floor; an asm kernel could win maybe 12% (lsc pairing of xh) = ~1.1 ms = +0.5%

campaign_closures.exp7_compiler_fp_candidate: not applicable as a speed lever: the accepted runtime is bound by PSRAM line fills (2-bit GEMV, 43%), online-softmax exp() plus KV line traffic (attention, 18%), FP latency (kron, 12%) and flash gather latency (engram, 8%). No -ffast-math style change survives the byte-exact golden gate by definition, and none of those phases is issue-limited.
campaign_closures.exp8_cq2_integer_path: rejected on measurement. The 2-bit projection phase is 86.5 ms for ~2.2 MB of packed weights per token, i.e. ~25-30 MB/s effective - the PSRAM/stream floor, not an arithmetic limit. An integer path would shorten arithmetic only, and phi's row blocking (which also shortened nothing observable) is the direct evidence that shortening arithmetic here buys nothing.
campaign_closures.exp9_compact_quantised_pair_LUT: rejected. Halving the 16 KB pair table cannot help: it is L1-resident and the streamed operand is the weights. Quantising its entries also changes products, so it fails the byte-exact gate before it is even measured.
campaign_closures.exp10_one_quantised_activation_for_qkv_g: already true in the shipping code, and small: one nd_cq_prepare + one LUT build serve q/k/v/gate, and the whole PREP phase is 3.5 ms = 1.7% of the token, so the maximum prize was below the quality risk of changing quantisation.
campaign_closures.exp11_xtensa_simd_integer_dot: the accepted kernel is already the TIE728 float path at 3 instructions/weight on a stream-bound phase; int16 SIMD was independently rejected by the MimiModel engine for the same reason (unpack dominates).

description: Noise-floor characterization of the accepted runtime: three byte-identical-source images (fresh-configured, 279184 B each) measured on three boards in one batch gave 4.7800 / 4.7783 / 4.7817 decode - peak-to-peak 0.07%, sigma ~0.03% - all byte-exact 12/12. Also corrected my own bandwidth accounting for the dominant phase (see asi): it is at the instruction floor, not the bus floor, and both floors land on the same number.

asi.hypothesis: Measure the run-to-run and board-to-board spread of the primary metric on byte-identical images, so sub-1% candidate deltas have a sigma to be judged against; and re-derive the dominant phase's floor with exact byte counts instead of my earlier estimate.

noise_floor.implication: the 0.2% keep bar is about 6 sigma, so it is conservative but not vacuous; deltas of 0.1% or less are not resolvable, which retroactively explains why ~20 instruction-scheduling experiments all read within +-0.05%
noise_floor.md5_note: identical sources produce different md5 per board because ESP-IDF stamps the build time; differing md5 with identical sources is expected, identical md5 across different flags is the failure signal

corrected_floor_accounting_for_the_2bit_.bytes: per layer q(576)+k(96)+v(128)+gate(768)+out(768) = 2336 rows x 768 weights = 1.79M weights, x8 layers = 14.3M weights = 3.59 MB packed + ~0.22 MB group norms = ~3.8 MB per token
corrected_floor_accounting_for_the_2bit_.bus: 3.8 MB at ~64 MB/s achievable on octal-DTR PSRAM at 80 MHz = ~59 ms, so the measured 86.5 ms runs at 69% of bus peak
corrected_floor_accounting_for_the_2bit_.instructions: 14.3M weights x 3 instructions per weight (4 extui + 4 addx4 + 8 lsi + 8 add.s per 8 weights = the accepted kernel's floor) = 43M instructions ~ 21M cycles = ~88 ms, matching 86.5 ms at IPC ~2
corrected_floor_accounting_for_the_2bit_.conclusion: instruction floor and 69%-of-bus both land on ~86 ms. Beating it needs fewer bytes (quantisation frozen) or a wider table that gives up address arithmetic and loses to cache misses - the quad table measured 38% slower for exactly that reason.

asi.revival_check: Nothing to revive: the sigma measurement strengthens every prior null, and the corrected accounting confirms the row-blocking and scheduling nulls sat at a real floor, not a measurement artefact.

description: Legality memo for the constrained sampler: cache the candidate list on the grammar state (the state carries the grammar pointer, so tools vs route samplers cannot collide; memcmp can only err toward a rebuild). Correct but worthless for speed - device decode_tps 4.7783, bit-for-bit the accepted value, byte-exact 12/12 device + 11/11 host, fidelity 5.341e-05. Either the state changes on essentially every accepted token (so the list is always rebuilt) or the 14.6 ms I attributed to enumeration is not where it goes; the metric says the memo path is not the cost. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: ND_P_SAMPLE = 14.6 ms of a 207 ms real decode token (7%) was the per-token vocabulary legality walk (~25K nd_gbyte steps). Memoizing the list on the grammar state should skip it whenever the state repeats, which I expected inside JSON string values where accepting a token leaves the state unchanged.
asi.result: Zero change (4.7783 vs 4.7783, spread on this metric is 0.07%), while byte-exactness held everywhere. The memo therefore either never fires or the mass is elsewhere.
asi.bit_exact_evidence: host 11/11 byte-identical with token_delta 0, device 12/12, fidelity probe unchanged at 5.341e-05 / top1 10/10 - so the memo logic is right, it is just not the lever.
asi.most_likely_why: ND_P_SAMPLE wraps nd_sample_hidden, which is enumeration *plus* nd_model_logits_subset. `logits4` is timed separately for the full-vocabulary path only, so the subset projection is inside SAMPLE and was never separated from the walk. Estimating the walk at 25K calls x ~580 cycles/call made it look like the whole 14.6 ms, but that cycle count was inferred from the same aggregate - it is not independent evidence.
asi.next: Before writing another line for the sampler: split the SAMPLE timer in two (enumerate-only vs nd_model_logits_subset) in a profiled build and harvest one tools request. If the walk is small, 14.6 ms is the subset logits projection and the lever is that GEMV's row count/layout, not the grammar. description: First-byte legality table for the constrained sampler. Instead of asking the grammar about every byte of all ~8176 vocabulary pieces each decode step, resolve byte 0 once per byte value for the current state (256 grammar steps) and veto candidates by table lookup before any grammar call; survivors still take the full byte walk, so the candidate set is identical. decode_tps 4.7783 -> 4.8817 (+2.16%, ~70 sigma against the measured 0.03% spread), extended 4.704 -> 4.804 (+2.13%), min_case 4.55 -> 4.66, think 3.84 -> 3.87. asi.hypothesis: ND_P_SAMPLE = 14.6 ms of a 207 ms real decode token is the per-step vocabulary legality walk, and almost every piece is rejected by its first byte - so a 256-entry first-byte table per state should replace ~8000 nd_gstate_byte calls with ~256 plus table lookups, with the survivor set unchanged.
asi.result: +2.16% decode, +2.13% extended, +2.4% on the worst case, and the two paths that never sample (boot bench, prefill) did not move at all. That invariance is the strongest evidence in the campaign: it is an internal control proving the delta came from the constrained sampler and not from build drift.
asi.why_the_previous_attempt_failed: #146 memoized the whole candidate list on the grammar state and measured nothing, which told me the state never repeats. This one does not care whether the state repeats: the table is rebuilt per step for 256 byte values, which is cheap, and it removes the expensive call from the ~8000 candidates that die immediately. Skipping work and repeating work cheaply are different levers.
asi.bit_exactness: A piece whose first byte cannot be consumed from the current state can never be legal, so the table only ever vetoes pieces the full walk would also have rejected; survivors take the identical walk, in the identical order, into the identical argmax. Verified on host (11/11 byte-identical, token_delta 0) and device (12/12, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10). One subtlety worth remembering: the old loop treated a zero-length surface at id>=16 as legal (empty byte walk), this one skips it - no such piece exists in this archive, and the goldens would have caught it.

description: First-byte-per-id cache for the sampler: 8 KB of internal RAM holding piece[0] for every vocabulary id, built once, with a fallback to the tokenizer call if the allocation fails. description: Consolidate the per-token console emit into one write: emit_piece() builds the escaped "TOK ...\n" line (identical bytes) and does a single fwrite plus the existing fflush, replacing printf("TOK ") + one putchar per byte + printf("\n"). asi.hypothesis: The per-token emit (printf + putchar per byte + fflush) sits inside the timed decode window and is invisible to the boot bench, which prints once per run; the sampler precedent (#147, +2.16%) said bench-invisible paths can hide >2%, so one write per token instead of ~5 should recover real milliseconds.

asi.why: ESP-IDF routes stdout through a fully buffered VFS for the USB-Serial-JTAG console, so putchar is a memory store until the fflush; the single submit per token is required by the protocol (the harness reads framed lines as they arrive) and cannot be removed without changing delivery semantics, which is the console contract, not a micro-optimisation.

Three failure layers found and fixed in the notes instead of the code: -DNEEDLE_PROFILE=ON does not define ND_PROFILE in a fresh build dir (confirmed: define token absent, and the request path printed no table); my verification grep looked for -DND_PROFILE=1 when a bare define appears as -DND_PROFILE; Device.complete() swallows raw console lines and prof_dump prints after EVT done, so breaking on EVT done hides the table. Stopped when I realised the answer cannot change any decision. Canonical run green: 4.8817 decode, 4.7986 extended, 14/14 byte-exact, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10.

asi.hypothesis: Measure rather than infer the subset-logits cost; if it were much larger than 7 ms the sampler family might reopen.
asi.why_stopped: Its two possible fixes are a smaller candidate set (changes what the model may emit - forbidden) or a faster 2-bit GEMV (at its measured floor). A measurement that cannot change the next action is not worth 14 minutes of board time per flash here, priming included. Recipe for a future session is in .auto/ideas.md.
asi.self_caught: Two of the three failures were my own verification being wrong rather than the build being wrong: grepping compile_commands.json for '-DND_PROFILE=1' instead of '-DND_PROFILE' (the same class of mistake as grepping the option name NEEDLE_LUT2_ASM instead of the define ND_LUT2_ASM, already recorded in this campaign). Verify the exact token, and better, verify by runtime behaviour - the absence of the request-path table was the real evidence.
asi.next: A live premise I found while re-reading the phi disposition: mHC phi's 9.2 ms is ~7x above BOTH its issue floor (302K instructions ~1.3 ms) and its bandwidth floor (36 KB/token ~0.6 ms), which means it is latency-bound - yet the recorded 'asm ceiling is -12%' analysis assumed it was issue-bound, and row blocking (which does not add load-pipelining depth) measured null exactly as a latency-bound kernel would. The 2-bit kernel's +33% came from batching eight independent gathers, the standard cure for latency-bound code, and it was never tried on the 4-bit path. Cheapest first probe: a C-level 2-word batching of the 4-bit inner loop with bit-exact accumulation order; if null, phi closes for real.
asi.state: Best 4.8817 decode (+99.9%), extended 4.7986, think 3.87, prefill 5.22; 14 device + 13 host byte-exact; make capture green; tree clean.

description: Folded codebook for the 4-bit (mHC phi) GEMV. nd_cact_codebook keys only on archive + bit width, so cb[k]*xh[j] is the same number for every output row - the trick the 2-bit pair table already uses. gemv_rows_folded builds 128 positions x 16 levels (8 kB internal) once per group per worker, reused by all rows that worker owns, with a group-outer / row-inner order and the same four partials as dot_group, so every y[r] is bit-identical. Host 13/13 byte-exact with fidelity 5.341e-05 unchanged; device 14/14 byte-exact, token_delta 0. decode_tps 4.8817 -> 4.89 (+0.17%, ~5x the measured 0.07% cross-image spread), extended 4.7986 -> 4.8086 (+0.21%), min_case 4.66 -> 4.67, and think 3.87 -> 3.97 (+2.6%) - think has not moved at all in ~150 runs, and it is the other consumer of the 4-bit path.

asi.hypothesis: phi sits ~7x above both its issue floor (302K instructions ~1.3 ms) and its bandwidth floor (36 KB/token ~0.6 ms), i.e. latency-bound - and the standard cure for latency-bound code is fewer dependent loads, which is exactly how the 2-bit kernel won +33%. Row blocking (which does not add load parallelism) measured null, as a latency-bound kernel would. So give the 4-bit path the folded table the 2-bit path already has: one gather per weight instead of two.
asi.why_this_was_legitimately_open: The ideas backlog listed '4-bit pair-LUT for the mHC phi GEMVs' with the note 'table is ~48 KB, probably too big; test whether a half-width table beats the multiply path anyway' - untried. The per-group slice is 8 kB, not 48 kB, because 16 levels x 128 positions covers a group and the group is reused by all 24 rows. The earlier -12% 'asm ceiling' analysis assumed the kernel was issue-bound, which its own numbers contradict.
asi.actual_size_of_the_win: Small on decode (+0.17% = ~0.35 ms/token, not the ~1.7 ms a pure instruction-count argument predicted) and large on think (+2.6%). So the fold removed work but phi remains dominated by something other than instruction count - consistent with the latency diagnosis, and a reminder that this board punishes predictions built from op counts. think is a single case, but the same session reproduces to 0.00%, so +2.6% is real.
asi.cost: internal_free fell 17039 -> 8335: the 8 kB static table. Boot and all 14 device cases are fine at 8.3 kB free, but if a future change needs internal RAM this is the first suspect. Halving it to 4 kB is available without touching numerics - process each group in two position halves while carrying s0..s3 across the halves, so the (s0+s1)+(s2+s3) fold is unchanged.
asi.next: Confirm on the three-board batch (control = pre-fold tree) since +0.17% is a small primary delta; the extended/think corroboration plus byte-exactness already argues it is real. Then consider re-trying a real TIE728 kernel for the 4-bit path now that the operand is a single 8 kB resident table: the -12% ceiling was measured against the two-gather shape, not this one.

description: Gate the folded 4-bit path on row count (out >= 32) so tensors right at the build/amortise break-even - the 32-row phi tensors 223/224 - keep the direct loop. Bit-exact (host 13/13, fidelity 5.341e-05) and the arithmetic predicted the result: decode 4.89 vs the ungated fold's 4.89/4.8917, extended 4.8071 vs 4.8114/4.8086, think 3.97 unchanged - i.e. exactly within the ~0.04% cross-run spread, neither helping nor hurting. Reverted; the simpler ungated guard stays. Also learned the honest resolution of my determinism claim: repeated cases inside one session agree to 0.00%, but across flashes/sessions the canonical reading varies ~0.04%, so deltas below that need a batch, not a repeat.

asi.hypothesis: The fold's per-group table costs g*16 = 2048 multiplies and saves one gather per weight, so it breaks even at 16 rows per worker (~32 rows overall). The 8192-row logits projection and the ~1300-row candidate subset are far above that (think gained 2.6%); the 32-row phi tensors sit on the line, so excluding them should be neutral-to-positive.
asi.result: Neutral within noise, exactly as the break-even arithmetic predicted. Kept-code simplicity wins: the ungated guard covers 100% of the archive's 4-bit tensors (all 7 are group=128, verified from the directory) and is one condition shorter.
asi.calibration: This is the third time in this campaign that a first-principles op-count model predicted a *null* correctly (after row blocking and the piece[0] cache). The model is trustworthy for ruling out; it has only ever over-promised on wins.
asi.noise_floor_updated: Same-session repeats: 0.00%. Same code measured across separate flash sessions: 4.89 and 4.8917, ~0.035%. So: within-session is deterministic, cross-session is not, and anything under ~0.05% needs the three-board batch. The 0.2% keep bar stays, but 'is this even a real delta' is now answerable at 0.1% with a batch.

description: Correctness revert: the folded 4-bit codebook kept in #159 (+0.17%) is withdrawn, returning to the accepted 4.8817. Reason found while extending it: gemv_rows_folded wrote ONE static 8 kB table from BOTH cores - rows_dual_core starts the two halves concurrently with no barrier between them, so a scheduler tick landing mid-build mixes two groups' values into one operand. It measured byte-exact on three boards and the host purely by timing luck; the host cannot catch it at all (nd_parallel_rows is rows_serial there). I then built the race-free version (table built by the caller outside the split, per-group nd_parallel_rows) and extended the fold to the candidate-gather path, which is the ~7 ms the constrained sampler actually pays: it measured 4.87 decode / 4.7857 extended / 3.95 think, i.e. worse on every monitor, so the safe form does not pay for itself. Fold family closed as unsafe-at-this-memory-budget. Safe state re-verified: 4.8817, extended 4.7986, think 3.87, 14/14 byte-exact, internal_free back to 17039.

asi.what_i_should_have_checked_before_keepin: Whether the kernel touched any shared mutable state, not just whether its numbers matched. gemv_rows_folded accumulated into a file-scope array from a function that nd_parallel_rows runs on two cores simultaneously. Byte-exact goldens are a strong gate for arithmetic, and a weak one for concurrency: the two halves are equal-sized and start together, so they stayed in phase often enough to look clean across four boards and ~10 runs. Every other GEMV variant in this campaign was pure-per-row by construction, so this is the first time the question even arose.
asi.why_it_cannot_be_fixed_here: Three shapes, all blocked: (a) caller-side build with the group loop outside the split - measured worse (4.87 vs 4.89), because it trades one handshake per projection for one per group (6 for the 768-wide logits, 24 for phi) plus a read-modify-write of y per group; (b) per-core tables inside the worker - 2 x 8 kB against 8.3 kB of free internal RAM; (c) one build per token covering all groups, caller-side, read-only - needs 16 x in_pad floats, 48 kB for the 768-wide logits and 192 kB for phi, and moving it to PSRAM defeats the point, because the operand it replaces (xh) is already internal SRAM.
asi.the_real_lesson: The fold only swaps one internal-SRAM operand (xh) for another (the folded table); it never touches the 4-bit weight stream in PSRAM that dominates the phase. That is why the win was only 0.17% on decode no matter how clean the code was, and why my '7x above both floors' framing was misleading: the phase is not limited by the operand I could cheapen. Worth remembering that a micro-optimisation of a non-dominant operand cannot exceed its share.
asi.memory_budget_note: internal_free is now back to 17039. The campaign's hot buffers live in PSRAM (12 MB tier) precisely because internal RAM is the scarce resource here; 8 kB is a real fraction of what is left, so any future static buffer needs the same arithmetic.
asi.harness_note_on_revert: log_experiment auto-reverts code on 'discard', so withdrawing an already-kept change has to be logged as 'keep' on the reverted tree - otherwise the tool would have restored the racy code it was meant to remove. Kept deliberately, and measured after the revert rather than before.

It is a timer-attribution difference (the engram's GEMVs are counted in both phases, per the documented overlap), not a speed effect: totals agree and the metric is identical. Do not chase it as a decode cost - 105.7 ms is already ~66% of the octal-PSRAM byte peak, and 105.7 + 19 more would exceed it.
asi.why_this_closes_things: logits4 at 5.7 ms rules out the last 'maybe the subset projection is actually huge' theory, which was the only reading under which a faster gather path could pay. Combined with #162 measuring the folded gather slower, the subset-logits and sampler family is closed on measurement, not on arithmetic.

asi.why_the_floor_is_final: A lookup can cover more than one weight only if the entry depends on all those weights. The pair table has 4 entries per position (4 codebook levels x one xh[j]) so a nibble costs one gather - that is the 2 instr/weight floor. Covering two nibbles needs entries indexed by both positions, 16x16 = 256 entries per position pair, i.e. the quad table, measured -38% because it stops fitting the 32 KB L2 (a 768-wide projection already spends 12 KB on the pair table). The ESP32-S3 TIE has packed integer SIMD but no packed-float SIMD, and the int16 PIE variant is independently recorded as slower in the MimiModel cross-check. There is no layout left that gets more than 2 weights per instruction, and fewer bytes means changing quantisation, which is frozen. Do not re-derive this a seventh time.

description: Split the constrained sampler's vocabulary-legality filter across both cores. The filter (piece lookup + first-byte veto + survivor byte walk over ~8176 ids) measured ~1.6 ms per decode token in #149, and it runs at a point where the second core is genuinely idle: the next token's projections depend on the token being sampled. Rows are whole 32-id words so each core writes only words in its own range and builds its own 256-entry first-byte table on its own stack - no shared scratch, no barrier (the contract added at #164 is why the shape is this way). The bitmap is then walked in ascending id order, so the candidate list, the argmax and its tie-break are identical; the count is complete rather than cut off at the cap, which is equivalent because both forms take the full-vocabulary path above the cap. decode_tps 4.8817 -> 4.8917 (+0.20%), extended 4.7986 -> 4.81 (+0.24%), min_case 4.66 -> 4.67, byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10. Boot bench 4.983 and think 3.87 unchanged - neither runs the constrained filter, which is the internal control. internal_free 17039 -> 15759 (the 1 kB bitmap).

asi.hypothesis: The sampler is the one phase whose work happens while core 1 is idle, and #149 measured ~1.6 ms of it as a pure per-id map, so splitting it should return most of 0.8 ms (~0.4%) with the second core's capacity for free.
asi.delivered_less_than_predicted: +0.20% against a +0.39% estimate - the same direction of error as #147 (predicted 12.8 ms, delivered ~4.5). The 93-cycle nd_gstate_byte microbench overstates mid-string states; the filter is cheaper than the stand-alone number suggests, so halving it buys less.
asi.self_audit_against_the_rule_i_just_wrote: s_legal is static and written from a function that runs on both cores, which the contract permits only because rows are whole words: word index = c->w0 + w and the two halves get disjoint row ranges, so no word is ever written twice and no byte is shared (that is also why rows are words and not ids - an id-granular split would put both cores inside one word at the range boundary). cand/score are touched only by the calling core; lex_ctx is on the caller's stack and read-only to the worker, which has joined before the caller reuses the frame.
asi.why_this_was_missed_for_150_runs: Every earlier split decision was made from the GEMV/attention phase map, and this work is invisible to the boot bench, so it never appeared as a share of the token. #147 opened the same territory and #166's measured request map (sample 8.9 ms of 202) is what made the split worth asking about.
asi.next: Confirm under the batch protocol - a ~0.2% delta needs one control image (pre-change nd_sample.c) plus two identical candidate images on three boards, control validated against 4.8817.

description: Pull the PSRAM weight tier's low end down to include the logits embedding, then discard as a verified null. ND_TIER_TRACE (a knob already in the tree) showed emb=11136..3255168 with in_span=0: the output-projection rows and candidate gather rows, read on every token, sat entirely below the staged span while 8 MB of the 12 MB allocation was dead padding. Because hi_p = lo_p + ND_TIER_SPAN_BYTES, including it costs zero extra copy bytes - the padding above the blob simply shrinks - and nd_cact_tier()'s translation is relative to lo_p, so coverage follows for free. Three lines of code. Result: decode 4.8917, bit-for-bit the accepted value, extended 4.81, think 3.87 (which matters most, because think reads all 3.14 MB of the embedding every token), byte-exact 14/14. Re-ran with the trace to prove the change was live rather than a silent fallback - the exact failure mode that has burned this campaign before - and it reports in_span=1 with content 7848512 (was 4602944). So the staging is real and worth nothing: the tier's measured value belongs to the streaming per-layer projections, not to scattered logits rows.

asi.hypothesis: The embedding is read every token, was outside the tier, and could be included for free (dead padding -> coverage), so its flash-mmap reads were a lever the code's own comment called 'the biggest remaining tier candidate'.
asi.why_it_is_worth_nothing: The tier is not a cache, it is a copy into PSRAM, and its measured benefit came from converting large sequential flash reads (14.3 M weights, ~4.4 MB/token of per-layer projections) into PSRAM reads. The subset logits path touches ~1500 scattered rows inside 3.14 MB; the access pattern, not the address space, is what was costing the 5.7 ms, and staging changes the address space only. think reading the whole embedding and still coming back at 3.87 is the cleanest evidence for that.
asi.method_win: This is the first candidate in the campaign that a diagnostic knob answered before it was built: the two-line trace that was already in the tree turned 'is the embedding resident?' from an assumption into a measurement, and the same trace then proved the null was a null instead of a build defect. Cheap knobs that print the state you are reasoning about are worth more than clever models of it.

description: Experiment 12 - paired/interleaved attention exponential. nd_expf_pair() evaluates the two independent exp() chains of the attention online softmax (w0 = s0-m, w1 = s1-m for the two KV positions of a pair) with their operations interleaved, so the scheduler has two independent operands per slot instead of one serial degree-5 Horner chain at a time. Each chain performs exactly nd_expf's operations in nd_expf's order with the same constants, and the out-of-range clamps stay in the scalar path, so the pair is bit-identical by construction. Disassembly of attn_heads showed why there was room: GCC expanded the two calls one after the other and spilled live floats to a1+0x4a0..0x4f8 to do it. Device microbenchmark (kbench, board 2, fixture = 1024 argument pairs captured from the six real primary generations with -DND_EXP_CAPTURE, 49,152 pairs collected): 247.42 -> 198.04 cycles/pair, +19.96%, mismatch=0 over all pairs, CCOUNT calibrated at 24000 cycles/us. Batch (20260921T210606.773089Z... board 1 pristine control, boards 2/3 candidates, fresh configure each, images 279488/279744/279744 B with distinct md5, -DND_KBENCH absent, -DND_LUT2_ASM present x7): control 4.8917 (reproducing the accepted value exactly, so the batch is trustworthy), candidates both 4.9150 with extended 4.8371, prefill 5.2433, min_case 4.70, byte-exact 14/14. Swapped-assignment confirmation on the canonical board (candidate on board 1): 4.9150 decode / 4.8357 extended / 3.88 think / 5.2433 prefill / 4.70 min, 14/14 device + 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10, boot bench 5.016 (199 ms/token, from 201), internal_free 15503 (was 15759; +256 B flash, -256 B internal). Accepted: +0.48% decode, +0.56% extended, +0.51% prefill, think also up (+0.26%) - the first new-campaign win and 4.9150 = +101.4% over baseline.

asi.hypothesis: The two adjacent attention exp() calls are independent serial Horner chains; interleaving them gives the scheduler two independent operands and avoids the spills GCC used to schedule them sequentially, and doing so is bit-exact because each chain's operations are unchanged.
asi.isolated_kernel: kbench on device, real captured arguments: scalar 247.42 cycles/pair vs C pair 198.04 (+19.96%), mismatch=0, CCOUNT valid.
asi.end_to_end: +0.48% decode (4.8917 -> 4.9150), +0.56% extended, +0.51% prefill, +0.26% think, byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host on control, two candidates and the canonical board. Boot bench 201 -> 199 ms/token independently confirms it.
asi.prediction_vs_measured: Predicted +0.86% from 49 cycles x ~8500 pairs/token; realised +0.48%, i.e. about half. The estimate assumed none of the exp latency was already hidden by neighbouring work; it was partially hidden, which is the honest explanation.
asi.remaining_headroom: 99 cycles per exp after pairing is still far above the instruction count of the polynomial (~11 FP ops + a few int ops per exp). A handwritten TIE728 pair with no spill/reload plausibly lands at 60-80 cycles/pair, which would be a further ~+1.5%. Experiment 12's own trigger for assembly ('if C does not schedule it') was not met - C scheduled it and paid off - so this is banked as a new candidate rather than a follow-up to a failure.
asi.capture_tooling: host/nd_dump.c -DND_EXP_CAPTURE + esp32/main/exp_pairs.h is now the reusable fixture path: it records real predicate arguments and the bench refuses to trust synthetic ranges.

description: Experiment 13 - ESP-DSP S3 dot-product audit, CLOSED as rejected with no integration. The shipped attention Q.K dot (one accumulator, two-term groups, 4-wide) measured 138 cycles for n=48 on device and beat every alternative schedule tried against it: an interleaved pair of the two dots of a KV position pair (bit-exact, bad=0) cost 403 cycles per pair against 276 for two shipped calls (-46%); a four-accumulator reorder that models the aes3 schedule took 213 (-54%); and an order-preserving handwritten kernel using ee.ldf.128.ip post-increment loads - bit-exact by construction, also bad=0 - took 286 cycles (-107%). The Kronecker shape (n=32, 97 cycles control) showed the same pattern (-50% pair, -61% reorder). Bench added to kbench with the C variants kept in the tree; the asm variant lived only in board 2's checkout and is not in the shipping tree. espidf's esp-dsp component (dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3) is absent from this tree, from managed_components and from ESP-IDF 5.5.2, and adding it is a forbidden new dependency - that is the concrete blocker for the library-vs-library half, recorded rather than silently substituted. Consequence for the campaign: the dot's ~8.3 ms/token (138 cycles x ~14,400 dots) is not reducible by pairing, accumulator count, load width or hand assembly - only by changing what is computed, which the byte-exact gate refuses.

asi.hypothesis: An optimized (aes3-style) dot-product schedule - multiple accumulators, 128-bit aligned float loads - beats the shipped 4-wide single-accumulator Q.K dot at the real alignments.
asi.measured: QK n=48: control 138 cyc; pair-interleaved 403/pair vs 276 (-46%); 4-accumulator reorder 213 (-54%); ee.ldf.128.ip asm 286 (-107%). Kron n=32: control 97; pair -50%, reorder -61%. All candidates bit-exact (bad=0); rejected on speed.
asi.why_the_asm_lost: A 128-bit float load on the S3 ai engine is not a single LSU operation, and asm volatile is a scheduling fence: GCC's own loop interleaves the two dots of a pair and pipelines across iterations, none of which survives inside an asm body. The loop instruction also adds per-iteration overhead.
asi.what_this_rules_out: Instruction scheduling, load width and accumulator count are closed for the dot family with device numbers, not argument. The remaining lever for this phase is what is computed (Experiment 14's integer path), not how it is scheduled.
asi.blocker_recorded: esp-dsp absent from tree + IDF 5.5.2; new dependencies forbidden, so dsps_dotprod_f32_aes3 cannot be benchmarked as such. Its schedule was reproduced locally instead and lost.
asi.fixture_caveat: reord_maxabs printed 0.000e+00 because the fixture values are near-integers in int8 range, so every partial sum is exact - a reduction-order test with those values would report false exactness. It did not matter (reorder lost on speed), but the lesson is recorded in ideas.md.
asi.microbench_rule: Rotate over several distinct operand buffers and consume every result through an FP register barrier: with one fixed operand pair, GCC hoists a pure noinline call out of the timing loop (a 48-element dot measured 8 cycles) and a variant writing only locals measured 0. Cost two wasted builds; applies to every kbench addition.
asi.next: Experiment 14: CQ2 integer feasibility screen on real shapes/codebooks/captured prepared activations, screened in C against nd_lut2_rows_tie1n (not in asm), with quantization cost, bytes read, staging bytes, cycles, max/mean error and fidelity/top1 reported before any integration.

description: Exponential scale tail by exponent-field insertion, REJECTED on speed. nd_expf/nd_expf_pair built 2^k as integer bits, memcpy'd it into a float and multiplied; this replaced that with an integer add of k<<23 into p's own exponent field, guarded to the range where it is provably equal to the multiply. Bit-exactness was verified the right way - against the previous shipping implementation verbatim, not against the new pair - over 80,184,321 comparisons (dense sweep of [-90,90] at ~1e-3, clamp edges, pair paths): 0 mismatches after the guard was corrected. Device result: 4.8117 vs the 4.9150 control, -2.10%, and it moved every monitor the wrong way - prefill 5.2433 -> 5.1317, think 3.88 -> 3.82, extended 4.8357 -> 4.73, min_case 4.70 -> 4.59, boot bench 199 -> 204 ms/token, internal_free 15503 -> 14735. Measured on three boards (batch 20260921T222845.825872Z boards 2/3 both 4.8117, then the canonical board also 4.8117 exactly), byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: The exp tail (assemble 2^k in an integer register, memcpy to a float, FP multiply) costs a register->stack->register round trip per exponential; adding k<<23 into p's own exponent field is one integer add and is exactly equal while the result is normal.
asi.why_it_lost: The swap is not the saving it looked like: reading p's bits needs the float in an integer domain anyway, so no move disappears, and the correctness guard adds two compares and a branch per scalar call (four per pair) into what was straight-line code - and in the pair the branch also breaks the interleaving that produced Experiment 12's +20%. Net effect -2.10% decode, -2.1% prefill, -1.5% think, 204 vs 199 ms/token on the boot bench: the branch and lost overlap outweigh a saved FP multiply. On this core, trading an FPU op for integer bit math is not free because float<->int transfers go through memory.
asi.method_win: Verifying against the PREVIOUS implementation (kept verbatim in /tmp/expref.c) rather than new-pair-vs-new-scalar caught a real off-by-one: p in [0.61,1) has unbiased exponent -1, so exactness needs k >= -125, not -126, and the first version silently disagreed with the shipped kernel by ~1.7x for x near -87.68. The byte-exact goldens would NOT have caught it, because no real argument goes there - so the correct-gate suite can pass while a latent numerical bug ships. Independent-reference differential testing is now the standard for any change to a numeric primitive.
asi.board1_lock: Harness defect found: stopping the API with 'pkill -f needle-api' leaks its child 'tools/serial_api.py --serial ...', which keeps holding /dev/needle-pi/console and leaves board 1 reporting 'Board 1 is busy' for the next run (it cost a control slot in this batch). Kill serial_api.py, or use the wrapper's stop path, before releasing a board.
asi.state: Accepted runtime unchanged at 4.9150 (+101.3%). Experiment 12's paired exp stands; the exp *scale construction* is now measured and closed.
asi.next: Restore run on the reverted tree, then Experiment 14's numeric screen (host) or Experiment 16/17, both of which can still ship bit-exact.

description: Experiment 17, first measured candidate: IRAM placement of the constrained sampler's driver. The symbol-table audit (not a guess) showed the hot compute is already resident - attn_heads, kron1_blocks/kron2_rows and nd_lut2_rows_c/tie1n all sit at 0x4037xxxx (IRAM) - while the flash-mapped (0x42xxxxxx) functions are nd_gstate_byte (1971 B, but run #149 measured its aggregate at only 0.06 ms so it is worthless), pool_cell, kron_apply (62 B wrapper over IRAM loops), nd_model_logits_subset (58 B), nd_cq_prepare (107 B), nd_tok_piece (37 B) and nd_sample_hidden (312 B). Chose nd_sample_hidden as the flash-resident function with real aggregate time (~8 ms of a request token, the phase the boot bench cannot run) and already-IRAM split kernel next to it. ND_HOT moved it 0x420114d8 -> 0x4037c3c0, verified through nm. Result: decode 4.9183 vs the 4.9150 control = +0.067%, extended 4.8414 (+0.12%), everything else identical to the tick (prefill 5.2433, think 3.88, min_case 4.70, boot bench 5.018, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, 14/14 device + 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0), internal_free 15247 (-256 B). Rejected: one quantisation tick is below the 0.2% keep bar and within the 0.071% spread measured across three byte-identical images, so no batch time was spent confirming it, and keeping it would spend 256 bytes of the campaign's scarcest resource on a win that cannot be resolved. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: The constrained sampler's per-token driver executes from flash-mapped .text, so its instruction fetches miss on every generated token; ND_HOT placement of that 312-byte function should recover part of its ~8 ms without touching arithmetic.
asi.measured: +0.067% decode (one metric tick), +0.12% extended, all other monitors identical to the tick, byte-exact everywhere, -256 B internal RAM. Below the keep bar and within the measured identical-image spread (0.071%), so not confirmable and not worth the RAM.
asi.exp17_disposition_so_far: Code placement is not a lever on this firmware: every loop that owns real time is already in IRAM, and the flash-resident remainder is either a small wrapper (kron_apply, logits_subset), cold in aggregate (nd_gstate_byte 0.06 ms, pool_cell ~0), or a 37-107 B helper whose fetch cost is amortised by an L1 instruction cache that already holds it. The remaining single-function candidates are each <= 0.1% by this measurement, i.e. under the bar by construction; do not spend a build on each of them separately.
asi.ram_note: internal_free is now the binding constraint for placement-style ideas: 15503 B accepted, 15247 with this change. A future candidate must pay for its own IRAM.
asi.next: Experiment 14's numeric screen (host, cheap, and its byte-exactness gate is the honest disposition), or Experiment 16 (compact first-byte grammar index) which is the remaining queue item that can ship bit-exact with a prize above the bar.

description: Experiment 18 - exact KV reciprocal (Markstein residual form): KEPT, +0.204% decode (4.9150 -> 4.9250). kv_store_int8 did `src[i] / scale` per element - 48 elements x two tensors x two KV heads x eight layers = 1,536 divides per decode token, the whole 1.1 ms phase. Since the divisor is invariant across the row, this is division-by-invariant: one correctly-rounded reciprocal per call (one real divide) plus, per element, y0 = RN(x*r); e = fmaf(-scale, y0, x) (the exact residual); q = fmaf(e, r, y0) - Markstein's form, which is provably the correctly-rounded quotient for round-to-nearest, so every stored int8 byte is identical to the divide it replaces. That is materially different from the naive x * (1/scale), which double-rounds and was rejected in run #2e for changing the model's memory. Verified as a numeric primitive, not by goldens alone: 8,000,006 comparisons against the previous implementation with 0 mismatches, covering arbitrary bit patterns, values placed exactly on .5 rounding boundaries after scaling, the +/-127 clamp edge, exactly-representable quotients, tiny and huge scales, and +inf/-inf/NaN (kept on the divide path by a two-compare guard, so non-finite semantics are unchanged too). Device: decode 4.9250, extended 4.8429 (+0.15%), think 3.89 (+0.26%), prefill 5.2500 (+0.13%), min_case 4.71, boot bench 5.022/199 ms, byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10, internal_free 15247 (-256 B). 4.9250 = +101.8% over the 2.44 baseline. Kept on a single canonical run at ~3x the measured identical-image noise floor, following the #176 -> #177 precedent; the swapped-assignment three-board batch is scheduled as the immediate next step and this is reverted if the batch contradicts it.

asi.hypothesis: kv_store_int8's 1,536 per-token divides dominate the 1.1 ms KV-store phase; replacing them with one reciprocal per call plus a two-FMA Markstein fixup keeps the quotient correctly rounded (so every int8 KV byte is unchanged) and removes the phase's real cost.
asi.premise_check: The codegen shows quou.s, i.e. the S3's TIE FP does have a divide instruction, so the ledger's '~340 cycles of __divsf3 per element' was an inference from the phase time, not a measurement. The run settles it empirically: removing the divides moved the whole token +0.204%, so the divide was genuinely the bottleneck even as a TIE instruction.
asi.bitexactness: Proved as a primitive over 8,000,006 differential comparisons with 0 mismatches (adversarial boundaries and non-finite included), not inferred from goldens - the rule banked at #231 after a real off-by-one slipped past the byte-exact suite.
asi.why_not_naive: x * (1/scale) double-rounds and can store a different int8 within an ulp of a .5 boundary; that is the model's memory, and #2e refused it for exactly that reason. The residual fixup is what makes the same speedup admissible.
asi.risk_note: Kept on one canonical run (delta ~3x the 0.071% identical-image spread). Confirmation with swapped board assignments is the next action; revert if it contradicts.
asi.next: Three-board batch: board 1 control (pre-change), boards 2/3 candidate, then swap; then make capture (shipping code changed). After that Experiment 16, or re-examine other divide-heavy hot spots with the same invariant-divisor reasoning.

description: Confirmation batch for run #233 (exact KV reciprocal), plus a canonical repeat - the change stands. Three-board batch 20260921T231859.542050Z with the PRE-change tree (0423bc4) as board 1's control and the candidate on boards 2/3, all freshly configured with distinct image sizes (279744 control / 279712 / 279712 candidate) and -DND_LUT2_ASM present in all 7 compile commands: control read decode 4.9150, exactly the previously accepted value, so the batch is trustworthy; candidates read 4.9217 and 4.9250. Extended decode 4.8357 control vs 4.8429 on both candidates, think 3.88 vs 3.89 on both, prefill 5.2433 vs 5.2483/5.25, min_case 4.70 vs 4.70/4.71, byte-exact 14/14 on all three boards, internal_free 15503 vs 15247 (-256 B) as predicted. The swapped half of the confirmation came from #233 itself (candidate on the canonical board 1: 4.9250), and this session's canonical re-measure reproduced 4.9250 with every gate green (14/14 device + 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, boot bench 5.022 / 199 ms/token). Pool of candidate readings {4.9250, 4.9217, 4.9250} against control readings {4.9150, 4.9150}: direction positive in every comparison, mean delta +0.17%, min +0.14%, max +0.20% - the mean sits marginally under the nominal 0.2% keep bar, but the metric's measured identical-image spread is 0.071% peak-to-peak (sigma ~0.03%), three independent boards agree, and the change is bit-identical by proof rather than by sampling, so the effect is resolved rather than marginal: kept. Accepted runtime stays 4.9250 = +101.8% over the 2.44 baseline. make capture is now overdue (shipping code changed at #233) and is the next action, followed by Experiment 16.

asi.hypothesis: Confirm #233's +0.204% with a real control-plus-candidate batch including the swapped board assignment, rather than accepting a single canonical run.
asi.verdict: Confirmed. Control reproduced the accepted value digit-for-digit; candidates beat it on all three measurements; every secondary monitor moved the same direction; quality gates green throughout.
asi.bar_accounting: mean +0.17% vs the 0.2% bar. Kept because the bar exists to separate signal from churn risk: the effect is 5x the measured sigma, reproduced on three boards, and carries no numerical risk (byte-identical int8 KV proven over 8M differential comparisons). Recording the mean honestly instead of quoting only the best reading.

description: Documentation correction on the kept #233 change, plus the behavioural-capture attempt and a gate run on the final tree. (1) Lead closed without a device candidate: #233's own follow-up hint was to look for other per-element divisions by an invariant divisor, and the obvious one - the online-softmax output normalization - already hoists its reciprocal (engine/src/nd_model.c:1359, `float inv = 1.0f / denom[t]`), so there are no divides left to remove there; its double-rounded result is also frozen by the byte-exact goldens, so making it correctly rounded would be a model change and is out of scope. (2) Corrected an inaccurate comment I had shipped in kv_store_int8: it claimed the ESP32-S3 has no FP divider and pays a ~150-cycle __divsf3 per element, which #233's own disassembly contradicts (quou.s is present, including inside that function). The comment now states the measured fact instead of the inference - removing those divides was worth +0.204% of the token over 1,536 divides, about 65 cycles each. Comment-only: the linked image is byte-for-byte the same size (279712 B), so no measurement validity question arises. (3) make capture was attempted and is BLOCKED, not skipped: it fails with URLError Connection refused because needle-api is not serving 127.0.0.1:8081 in this container session (it must be started in a tmux window first, per AGENTS.md), and capture is still owed for the shipping changes at #233. Note also a self-inflicted failure worth remembering: `pkill -f serial_api.py` matches its own command line and killed the shell mid-chain. (4) Gate run on the tree as it now stands: decode 4.9233, extended 4.8429, think 3.89, prefill 5.2517, min_case 4.71, boot bench 5.022 (199 ms/token), 14/14 device + 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, internal_free 15247. 4.9233 vs the accepted 4.9250 is one quantisation tick, inside the 0.071% identical-image spread, so the accepted runtime and its +0.17% mean confirmation at #234 stand.

description: Behavioural-integrity cycle on the shipping path, and the capture owed by #233 is now discharged. The #235 blocker was that make capture talks to needle-api on 127.0.0.1:8081 and the API was not running; resolved with `tmux new-window -t pi -n api 'make serve'` (health reported ready in 5 s: ready=true, esp32-s3, schema agent-watch-v2, layers 8, 16,155,796 model bytes), then `make capture` (demo/capture.py) ran all seven end-to-end scenarios with routing, local two-pass tool execution, telemetry, sampling interval and timer expiry exercised, and returned rc=0 with ALL NINE verification flags true: routes_match, tools_match, requests_succeeded, no_external_calls, local_has_two_passes, external_stops_at_selection, telemetry_progressed, sampling_interval_applied, timer_expired. So the accepted runtime is now proven behaviourally, not just byte-exactly: the board still routes correctly, still executes tools locally in two passes, and still makes no external calls, on the image that contains #233's exact-KV reciprocal. API then stopped (tmux window killed, serial_api child killed by pid - the bracketed pgrep pattern avoids the self-match trap from #235) so the console was free for the measurement. description: Cache-line-width ablation (deliberately worse, run for information, like run #204's asm ablation): CONFIG_ESP32S3_DATA_CACHE_LINE_64B -> 32B, one line of esp32/sdkconfig.defaults, sdkconfig regenerated, resolved to DATA_CACHE_LINE_SIZE=32, image byte-size identical (279712) because cache geometry is not code. Result: decode 4.4033 against the accepted 4.9250 = -10.6%, with every monitor moving the same way - prefill 4.7083 (was 5.25), extended 4.3371 (was 4.8429), think 3.48 (was 3.89), min_case 4.22 (was 4.71), boot bench 221 ms/token (was 199), and internal_free/psram_free unchanged as expected. Byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10 - the expected confirmation that cache-line geometry is numerically transparent, a config knob that changes speed without touching a single output byte, which is the safest kind of lever to test. Reverted (sdkconfig.defaults restored). Two durable conclusions: (1) the campaign had been carrying an UNMEASURED assumption in the shipping config - the 64 B data cache line was inherited and never A/B'd in 230+ runs - and it is now worth a number: +11.9% (1/0.894), making it one of the largest single levers in the tree alongside the fp32 weight staging and the TIE728 kernel; (2) the direction settles why: halving the line hurts the dominant sequential 2-bit weight stream far more than it can help the scattered logits/engram gathers, so the byte-bound phase really is limited by fill efficiency on long runs, as the instruction-floor analysis predicted. Anyone shortening that line for tidiness loses about a ninth of the throughput.

asi.hypothesis: Data cache-line width was unmeasured in this campaign; 64 B lines favour the sequential weight stream but waste fill on the scattered logits/engram gathers, so 32 B might net a win (or at least quantify the trade-off).
asi.result: Strongly negative and highly informative: -10.6%, all monitors same direction, output byte-identical. 64 B lines are worth +11.9%; the shipping default was right but had never been measured.
asi.why_valuable: Cheap, zero numerical risk, and it converts an inherited-config assumption into a measured number. Negative ablations of kept defaults are the cheapest large knowledge in this campaign (#204's asm ablation, #206's tier trace, this).
asi.closure: Cache-line lever CLOSED: 64 B is the IDF maximum for the S3 data cache, so the only direction was down and it loses 11%. Instruction cache is likewise already at its 32 B maximum. No upward headroom remains in cache geometry.

description: FreRTOS tick rate 1 kHz -> 100 Hz: KEPT, +0.34% decode (4.9250 -> 4.9417, new accepted = +102.6% over the 2.44 baseline), found by continuing #238's method of testing inherited build-config assumptions. CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ was the only value in esp32/sdkconfig.defaults that was not already at a documented maximum (OPI octal flash 80 MHz, OCT octal PSRAM 80 MHz, 240 MHz CPU, WDT off, both caches at their S3 maxima), and nothing in the timed path needs millisecond granularity: a 1 kHz tick fires roughly 200 times inside one 200 ms decode token and each tick costs interrupt entry/exit plus scheduler work on the core running inference. Numerically transparent by nature (no floating point, no model change), and the firmware's own timing comes from esp_timer, not the tick, so the metric measures the same thing before and after: same six frozen prompts, same model, same grammar, device-reported decode timing. Resolved config confirmed at 100 Hz after deleting and regenerating sdkconfig; image grew 16 B (FreeRTOS port tick math). Device: decode 4.9417, extended 4.86 (+0.35%), prefill 5.265 (+0.29%), think 3.90 (+0.26%), min_case 4.72 (best seen; the worst case improved with the mean, so this is not a redistribution), boot bench 5.04 / 198 ms/token (was 5.023 / 199) - the bench improving is the mechanism check, since the bench never runs the console or the sampler, so the saving is tick overhead removed from every token rather than request-path bookkeeping. Byte-exact 14/14 device + 13/13 host, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, internal_free 15247 and psram_free 2,052,252 both unchanged. Delta is +0.34% = roughly ten quantisation ticks, five times the measured 0.067% peak-to-peak spread of identical images, so it is unambiguous on one canonical run; the swapped-assignment three-board batch is still owed, together with make capture, which this change makes due again.

description: Config-assumption probe (the lens that produced #238's cache line and #240's tick): CONFIG_SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL 4096 -> 16384, i.e. IDF's default instead of the repo's unusually conservative value. The shipping value pushes every allocation larger than 4 KB out of internal SRAM and into PSRAM, so if any hot mid-size buffer were malloc'd this would be a real lever; with only 15,247 B internal free, the other outcome (internal OOM at boot) was equally informative. Result: an exactly null run - decode 4.9417, extended 4.8614, prefill 5.2667, think 3.91, min_case 4.72, boot bench 5.040 / 198 ms/token, 14/14 device + 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, and crucially internal_free 15247 and psram_free 2,052,252 both IDENTICAL to the accepted build. Byte-identical heap figures are the proof that nothing moved: no dynamic allocation in this firmware lies in the 4 KB-16 KB window the knob controls, so 4096 and 16384 select the same backing store for every allocation the engine actually makes. That also corrects a loose inference in the run #141 note, where 'xh is internal SRAM' was attributed as if placement policy governed it - the hot per-token buffers (padded activation, KV staging, softmax scratch) are static arrays, which is why they are internal regardless of malloc thresholds, and why the phi analysis stays valid while this knob cannot touch it. Reverted; the shipping 4096 stands (harmless, and stricter is safer for a board with 15 KB internal free). Note for build hygiene: an appended duplicate line in sdkconfig.defaults silently lost to the earlier assignment - last-write-wins in Kconfig - so the first build of this experiment was not the candidate it looked like, caught because the image size and resolved value were both checked before flashing.

asi.hypothesis: If any hot buffer is malloc'd in the 4-16 KB range, forcing it into internal SRAM should speed the token; if internal RAM cannot afford it, the boot fails and that bounds the placement idea.
asi.result: Inert knob: byte-identical decode and byte-identical internal/PSRAM free counts, so no allocation lives in the controlled window. Hot buffers are static arrays, not mallocs.
asi.hygiene_rule: sdkconfig.defaults is last-write-wins: always grep the file for duplicates and confirm the RESOLVED esp32/sdkconfig value, not just the edit, before believing a config candidate was built. Same family of failure as #238's stale-sdkconfig risk.

description: Experiment 14 - CQ2 integer path, MEASURED and CLOSED as rejected (numeric stage failed; no device run, so step 3's kbench speed screen never opened; device monitors below are the accepted control's unchanged values, the host ones re-measured green on the reverted tree). Real fixture: layer-0 q_proj (576x768, group 128) captured through the shipping float kernel - prepared activation, its own pair table, its output vector, 32 spread rows' packed bytes + fp16 norms - 4x8 records from prefill+decode of two frozen primary prompts; float replay on the fixture is bit-exact 1024/1024 rows, so the errors are the integer path's. Errors vs that output (mean|y|=1.771): int8 act x int8 codebook max 4.379e-02 rms 1.235e-02; per-group activation scale 4.315e-02 / 9.739e-03 (21% of rms); int8 act with EXACT codebook 4.310e-02 / 1.192e-02 (error is the activation, not the codebook); int16 act x int8 codebook 1.222e-02 / 2.788e-03; int8-expanded rows algebraically identical to int8 (asserted equal). End to end on the campaign's host probe, substituting ONE tensor (0.73% of CQ2 bytes): int8 logit_max_delta 0.3282 = 164x the 2e-3 gate FAILED; int16 activation + exact codebook (best case of the family) 0.01818 = 9.1x gate FAILED; control reproduces 5.341e-05 / top1 10/10. The int8 substitution still passed 13/13 host goldens with token_delta 0 - the byte-exact suite is blind to a change that moves logits by 0.33. Variant (b) is capacity-dead independently: CQ2 = 46 tensors, 11,959,296 packed bytes (74.1% of 16,143,248) = 45,023,232 weights, so int8 rows need 45.0 MB (3.76x) fitting neither 16 MB PSRAM nor the 12 MB tier, and would raise the per-token stream from 11.96 MB (59 MB/s at 4.94 tok/s) to 45.0 MB (223 MB/s). No integer dequant is bit-identical, so 14/14 + 13/13 byte-exact goldens can never be met at any width and the campaign refuses a model change: rejected independently of speed. dsps_dp_s8_aes3 unavailable (esp-dsp absent from tree and IDF, forbidden new dependency, #230). No image built -> no hashes, no board assignment. Engine probe reverted; fixture + screen + capture-hook patch kept in .auto/exp14. Next: Experiment 15 (operator-internal GDMA double buffering).

description: Experiment 15 - operator-internal GDMA double buffering: MEASURED on three boards, CLOSED as rejected, nothing integrated (tree back at the accepted 4.9417 runtime). Recipe followed: AHB GDMA async memcpy prefetching the next sequential PSRAM weight block into two small internal DMA buffers while TIE728 consumes the current one; 2 KiB and 4 KiB buffers; real 768x768 CQ2 bytes staged into PSRAM the way the tier stages them; shipping tie1n kernel; 5 rounds x 20 blocks, min-of-rounds; all three boards in one concurrent batch, agreeing to <0.1%. Verdict: the proposal is SLOWER than the direct cached-PSRAM read it was meant to beat, -67.8% on 2 KiB blocks and -17.9% on 4 KiB blocks, with bit-exact output on every overlapped row (int/dma row mismatches 0). Ruled out in order: it is not the wait (consumer blocks 0.9% of overlapped time); compute alone (18.3k cyc/blk) plus copy alone (12.8-15.7k) equals the overlapped total (30.7k), so the two streams serialise on the shared octal PSRAM bus - GDMA's own ceiling (61.7 MB/s with two transactions in flight and nothing else running) is the same order as the ~64 MB/s the cached path already sustains, so a prefetch sharing the bus with its consumer is not a free second stream. The target ceiling was measured too: identical operands read from internal RAM buy only +0.11% at 2 KiB, and the +11.2% seen at 4 KiB is L1 D-cache residency of an 80 KB sweep, i.e. the tier mechanism that is already closed. Two hard hazards from the explicit coherency verification the recipe demanded: (1) doing the invalidate correctly inside the loop is impossible on this build - esp_cache_msync briefly disables the cache and the async-memcpy done-callback chain is flash-mapped, so a GDMA done ISR landing in that window panics with InstrFetchProhibited at the same PC on two boards, and the fix needs IRAM budget already spent on lut2_tie728.S; (2) even with nothing in flight, one invalidate costs a fixed 1,416,510 cycles (~5.9 ms, identical for a 64-byte call, reproduced to the last digits on 3 boards) - no plausible win pays that 76 times per token. Coherency itself observed no stale reads in either direction on this access pattern. Heap: the DMA pair costs 4,600 B (2 KiB) or 8,728 B (4 KiB) of internal heap against 15,247 B free. No canonical decode measurement was spent, deliberately: the candidate lost in the microbenchmark before reaching the request path, so measure.sh would only have re-measured the control; the logged secondaries are the control's carried-forward values, labelled as such. Memory-system family now closed from both sides. Bench + raw device output kept in .auto/exp15/; kbench.c and the kbench-only CMake requirement reverted.
