description: Experiment 16 - compact first-byte grammar index: MEASURED and KEPT, +1.01 % decode (4.9417 -> 4.9917, now +104.6 % over the 2.44 baseline). The constrained sampler decided which pieces the grammar can spell by examining all 8,176 vocabulary ids every decode token (a nd_tok_piece call plus a first-byte table test each). Index the vocabulary by first byte once (uint16 ids grouped per byte by counting sort, which needs no comparison and leaves each group in id order, plus 257 offsets and the list of the 94 byte values that actually start a piece) and per token walk only the groups whose byte the state accepts. Legality is untouched: every visited id still takes the same token_ok byte walk, bits still go into the same one-bit-per-id bitmap, and the caller still reads it in ascending id order, so the candidate list, the argmax and its tie-breaking are the shipped ones. Screened off-device first (.auto/exp16/, host build behind -DND_SAMPLE_STATS, verified live by its own output per the run #242 lesson): across all six primary prompts and 93 real decode steps the grammar admits a median of ONE first byte per step, the bucket walk touches a median of 51 ids against 8,176, 1.62 % of the shipped walk in aggregate, and it reproduced the shipped candidate list element for element and in ascending order on every step. Three-board batch with a pristine board-1 control: candidate +0.98 % and +1.05 % at identical configuration, both 14/14 byte-exact (that batch exposed a harness fact worth keeping - each worker's esp32/sdkconfig is gitignored, so git reset --hard does not apply a config-changing commit and all three ran at 1000 Hz; the control reading exactly 4.9250, the pre-tick accepted value, proved both the drift and the control's health). Canonical run on the original board at the shipping configuration (tick 100 Hz, 64 B data cache line, sdkconfig regenerated, 280,320 B image dcce6a62): decode 4.9917, extended 4.9129 (+1.06 %), think 3.92, prefill 5.265 unchanged, min_case 4.77 which is better than the previous best 4.72 so the worst case improved with the mean, boot bench 5.039 / 198 ms/token unchanged - the same request-path-only internal control run #147 produced, because the bench never samples. 14/14 device and 13/13 host byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 against a 2e-3 gate, top1 10/10, make test green including prefix isolation, and make capture rc=0 with all nine behavioural flags true. Memory: internal_free 15,247 -> 15,215, i.e. 32 B for the index handle; the ~17 KB index itself is ND_ALLOCed in PSRAM and allocation failure falls back to the original full walk, so it is an optimisation and not a dependency. Delivered roughly 2.05 ms of the ~202 ms token where the screen priced ~1.5 ms, because removing the need for the nd_parallel_rows split also removes its handshake and the duplicated per-core 256-step grammar probe - removing the need for a split can be worth more than removing work. This is deliberately not the rejected run #149: that kept all 8,176 iterations and shortened each one (-0.17 %); here 98 % of the iterations disappear, which is the changed assumption that justified revisiting the sampler enumeration.

description: Experiment 19 - 120 MHz octal flash+PSRAM, measured as an ISOLATED DIAGNOSTIC and closed unshipped. Two sub-variants: (a) PSRAM 120 MHz with flash held at 80 MHz is a BUILD BLOCKER, recorded exactly - "static assertion failed: FLASH and PSRAM Mode configuration are not supported" (esp_psram config-time assert), because on ESP32-S3 flash and PSRAM share the MSPI clock tree, so only the combined step exists. (b) Both at 120 MHz octal DDR with IDF_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES=y: measured twice with board assignments swapped, each against controls in the same concurrent batch. Candidate 5.1667 on board 3, then 5.1667 on board 1 (two different boards, identical to the last digit); controls read exactly 4.9917 - the accepted runtime - on both remaining boards. Candidate deltas: prefill 5.4517, extended 5.0814, think 4.05, min_case 4.93, boot bench 5.213 (192 ms/token), internal_free 14,031 (-1,184 B), 14/14 device byte-exact with token_delta 0. The metrics logged on this line are the CONTROL's, because nothing shipped: the primary and every secondary below are the unchanged accepted runtime, re-measured on two boards in these batches. NOT KEPT for two independent reasons: the campaign's benchmark-integrity rule permits only the documented 240 MHz CPU / 80 MHz octal flash+PSRAM, and IDF's own Kconfig help for SPIRAM_SPEED_120M in octal mode says it "works when the temperature is stable" and that a ~20 Celsius swing either way makes PSRAM accesses "crash randomly" - an axis a single-room soak cannot cover (cold-then-warm and warm-then-cold are not warm-then-warm), so a soak would buy false confidence, not safety. What a real stability campaign needs is named in ideas.md: SPIRAM_TIMING_TUNING_POINT_VIA_TEMPERATURE_SENSOR plus thermal-cycling integrity tests, paid for out of 15,215 B of internal RAM. Diagnostic value: a 50 % wider MSPI clock moves the whole token by only 3.5 % while the 2-bit GEMV phase is 43 % of it, so that phase waits on its 2-instructions-per-weight floor, not on bytes - a third independent confirmation of that floor after the row-blocking, load-width and schedule nulls. All three named follow-on experiments (15, 16, 19) are now measured and the named queue is complete; nothing was integrated for 19.

description: Paired sigmoid in the two elementwise exp loops (SiLU gate + attention output gate): KEPT, +0.200 % decode (4.9917 -> 5.0017, now +105.0 % over the 2.44 baseline). Derived from Experiment 19's diagnostic rather than from the old queue: the phase map says the model spends ~14,400 nd_expf calls per token in loops that were never paired, because Experiment 12 only paired the *attention* softmax. sigmoidf_ is built on nd_expf (degree-5 Horner chain), so the MLP's SiLU (1024 elements x 8 layers) and the attention gate (768 x 8) are 7,200 independent long-latency exponentials per token on each core, and silu_rows / agate_rows walk them one element at a time. Interleave each adjacent pair through the shipped nd_expf_pair. Bit-exactness is by construction, not tolerance: the pair is used only when both elements take the SAME branch of sigmoidf_, so each element's exponential argument is the one the scalar path would have passed (-x for x >= 0, x otherwise), the two divisions keep their scalar form, mixed signs fall back to two scalar calls, and nd_expf_pair itself falls back to scalar outside its exact range. Chunks are 128 wide, so a pair never straddles the two cores. In silu_rows both operands are loaded before either output is written because `a` is read-modify-written. Evidence, in the campaign's order: (1) the rule-#1 differential test against the shipped sigmoidf_ copied verbatim - 1,600,202 comparisons, 0 bit mismatches, max_abs 0.000e+00, over a +-400 dense sweep plus branch boundary, +-0, subnormals, clamp edges and +-1e30 (the first attempt at this test silently compiled against a stale /tmp/nd_quant.h that shadowed the real header and merely failed to link - a harness fact, not a result); (2) host gates for the identical patch: 13/13 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 - identical to the control - top1 10/10; (3) three-board batch: control board 1 read exactly 4.9917 while both candidate boards read 5.0017; (4) canonical confirmation on the original board at the shipping configuration (sdkconfig regenerated, 100 Hz tick, 64 B cache line): 5.0017, byte-exact 14/14, token_delta 0, checks green. Cost is +1,200 B of flash and ZERO internal RAM (internal_free 15,215 unchanged). Secondary monitors: extended 4.9186 (+0.12 %), prefill 5.2733 (+0.16 %), min_case 4.78 which is the best worst-case seen, boot bench 5.046 (198 ms/token) - the bench moving is the mechanism check, since unlike the sampler work this phase is inside the bench; think_tps 3.92 unchanged, so the 4-bit/vocabulary path is not harmed. The delivered +0.20 % is a fraction of the ~+0.8 % the arithmetic predicted (7,200 pairs x 49 saved cycles), the same partial-realisation Experiment 12 measured: some of that exp latency was already hidden by neighbouring work. Note this candidate is exactly at the 0.2 % keep bar, not above it: it is kept because it is reproducible to the digit on four boards on a metric with zero measured spread, and because it costs no RAM. make capture is due again (shipping code changed) - next cycle.

description: Skip the exponential of the row/column maximum in Sinkhorn's log-sum-exp: KEPT, +0.200 % decode (5.0017 -> 5.0117, now +105.4 % over the 2.44 baseline). This is the second candidate derived from the phase map rather than the old named queue, and it targets the phase that was previously only probed by changing its iteration count (vetoed by fidelity) or straight-lining it (null). sinkhorn() runs 20 iterations x (4 rows + 4 columns) x 8 layers = 5,120 nd_expf calls per decode token, and in every one of those 160 passes the maximum element is a member of the sum being accumulated, so its argument is exactly zero: a quarter of the phase, ~1,280 calls per token, was evaluating exp(0) with the same degree-5 Horner chain (~99 cycles) as an arbitrary argument. Contributing the literal 1.0f for a difference that is exactly zero removes them. Bit-exactness is by construction and was tested as a primitive, not only by goldens (rule #1): nd_expf(+0.0f) and nd_expf(-0.0f) are both exactly 1.0f (asserted as a precondition), the guard tests the SUBTRACTED DIFFERENCE rather than the index so it can only fire when two equal finite operands cancel - NaN and inf-inf yield NaN, which is not equal to 0.0f and therefore still falls through to nd_expf exactly as the shipped code did - and the partial is added in the shipped position, so the accumulation order cannot move. Differential test against sinkhorn copied verbatim: 200,000 random 4x4 runs across five distribution families (typical log-res, wide/clamped, all-equal, near-tied maximum, one dominant element) = 3.2 M elements, plus 964 exact-zero argument probes: 0 bit mismatches (kept in .auto/sinkzero/test.c, -ffp-contract=off). Evidence in the campaign's order: (1) that test; (2) host gates on the patched tree - 13/13 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical to the control, top1 10/10, repo tests green; (3) three-board batch: control (board 1) exactly 5.0017 while both candidate boards read exactly 5.0117; (4) canonical confirmation on the original board at the shipping configuration (sdkconfig regenerated, 100 Hz tick, 64 B cache line): 5.0117 with checks green, 14/14 device byte-exact, token_delta 0. Cost is inside the existing code - no RAM (internal_free 15,215 unchanged), no new memory, no IRAM. Monitors all moved with the primary or stayed flat: extended 4.9286 (+0.20 %), prefill 5.2867 (+0.22 %), think 3.93 (+0.26 %), min_case 4.79 which is the best worst-case seen so the mean did not improve by hurting the tail, boot bench 5.057 (198 ms/token) - and the bench moving is the mechanism check here, because unlike the sampler work Sinkhorn is inside the bench. Delivered +0.200 % against an arithmetic prediction of +0.26-0.33 % (1,280 exps x ~99 cycles), i.e. ~70 % realisation - the best realisation of the three pairing/skip candidates (#12 half, #288 above prediction, #290 a quarter), which fits the mechanism: a skipped call removes work the scheduler could not have hidden behind anything, whereas pairing only re-exposes latency. make capture is due again because shipping code changed - next cycle.

description: Skip the exactly-zero exponential in the ATTENTION softmax pairs (the 48.5 % of pairs whose running maximum is one of the two positions): MEASURED, REJECTED, reverted. This was the candidate banked and priced last cycle off the real 49,152-pair capture, and the numerics were proven before spending any board time - bit-differential against the shipped expression over the entire real fixture (98,304 elements, 23,834 of them carrying an exact zero) plus dense sweeps and non-finite/signed-zero/clamp edges = 357,792 elements, 0 bit mismatches, with nd_expf(+-0.0f) == 1.0f asserted as a precondition; host gates green (13/13 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical to control, top1 10/10). So the arithmetic was never the issue. The device result is a REGRESSION: canonical board 4.9900 against the accepted 5.0117 (-0.43 %), with every monitor moving together - extended 4.9057 (-0.47 %), prefill 5.2633 (-0.44 %), think 3.91, min_case 4.76, boot bench 5.030 vs 5.057 (-0.53 %) - and internal_free 15,215 -> 14,191, i.e. it also cost 1,024 B of internal RAM because the branch made the compiler re-allocate the block's live set. That is precisely the risk recorded in the banked entry and measured in runs #230-231, where a guard placed around nd_expf_pair cost -2.10 %: the branch destroys the interleaving that Experiment 12's +19.96 % kernel comes from, and this loop is the worst case in the tree for a badly-predicted branch - 48.5 % hits / 51.5 % misses is close to maximally unpredictable. The contrast with run #291 is the finding worth keeping: the IDENTICAL trick won +0.200 % in Sinkhorn, because there the guard sits in a tiny 4x4 loop where the exp chain is the only thing happening, while here the guard is inserted into the hottest, most carefully-scheduled straight-line block in the firmware, where the pair call has to remain the only statement in that block for its schedule to survive. Priced at +17 % of the phase's exp work (~+0.6 %), delivered -0.43 %: the guard cost roughly twice the entire prize. Closed on measurement - do not retry a skip/guard inside the attention exp block; any further attention-exp work has to remove the call without adding a control-flow dependency.

description: Build-config candidate: IDF assertion level 2 -> 0 (ASSERTIONS_DISABLE), the family that produced this campaign's two largest non-code wins (cache line #238, tick rate #240). MEASURED on three boards plus a canonical confirmation, and NOT SHIPPED. The speed effect is noise: canonical 5.0100 against the accepted 5.0117 (-0.03 %, inside the measured 0.071 % spread of three byte-identical images), with the batch's board 2 reading +0.16 % - one board under the bar is not a result. The finding is RAM, and it is large and reproducible: internal_free 15,215 -> 23,463 (+8,248 B, +54 %) on two boards and confirmed by the firmware's own STATE line at runtime. Mechanism: assert strings and their check code leave .flash.text/.rodata, and IRAM/rodata text is subtracted from the internal heap - the same coupling run #292 exposed from the other side (a candidate that grew IRAM cost 1,024 B of heap). Quality was never at risk: 14/14 device byte-exact, token_delta 0, prefill/extended/think/min_case/boot-bench all flat; host-side quality is unchanged by construction because only esp32/sdkconfig.defaults differs from the accepted tree (engine/ and esp32/ verified byte-identical). Not kept for two independent reasons: the primary metric is unchanged, which the campaign's keep rule settles; and disabling assertions removes runtime failure DIAGNOSTICS from a product firmware, so a real defect would surface as a silent reboot instead of an abort with a reason - that tradeoff belongs to the owner. ASSERTIONS_SILENT (level 1) was measured as the safer middle: it keeps every check and all failure detection, drops only the message strings, and still returns 6,200 B at neutral speed. Value of the null: the ledger repeatedly calls internal_free the binding constraint, and four rejected ideas were priced against 15,215 B - the 4-row CQ2 LUT residency (10.4 KB, kbench +3.8 %), the 4-bit per-core codebook tables (16 KB), the handwritten 4-bit phi kernel (~1.5 KB, +0.5 % ceiling) and the 2x4 KiB GDMA pair. If the owner accepts either level, those re-price, and the LUT residency is the only one with a measured win above 1 %. Recorded in .auto/ideas.md; config reverted, tree clean.

description: Priced the last above-bar candidate before writing any assembly, and the price killed it. The phi (mHC 4-bit generic path) handwritten-kernel idea carried two contradictory claims from run #141: an analytic -12 % of the phase from instruction counts, versus a diagnosis of PSRAM line-fill latency - and the ledger's neutral generic-path row blocking is what latency-bound code does when you hand it fewer issue slots. Settled it with a device microbenchmark that changes only which backing store each operand lives in, calling the shipping nd_cq_gemv_rows on real needle3.cact bytes with a real nd_cq_prepare activation: perfect residency (weights in internal RAM) buys +9.3 % of the phase, not 12 %, and the kernel cannot move the weights anyway. The same measurement then exposed something more valuable than either candidate: the field attribution is 30 cycles/weight against the warm kernel's measured 6.98, a 4.3x gap that operand placement (9.3 %) and scheduling (same kernel both ways) cannot account for, so phi's real cost is cold line fill on a 37 KB/token working set that will not fit the 32 KB data cache. That retires the assembly as the wrong instrument - the addressable share is delivery, and delivery is residency, which needs ~37 KB against 15,215 B free - so phi stays exactly as it is and the re-price, if the owner ever accepts the assertion-level change from run #293, should be a residency experiment aimed at the 4.3x gap. All four modes produced bit-identical rows (chk_mismatch=0), so the comparison measured the memory system and not four different computations. Bench source and raw device output kept in .auto/exp20/; the tree is byte-identical to the accepted runtime. Harness cost of the cycle: three rebuilds lost to NEEDLE_KBENCH=ON being unbuildable as committed (the bench includes esp_async_memcpy.h/esp_cache.h while the CMake block adds the component with target_link_libraries, which emits a bare -lesp_hw_support and fails to link - an IDF component dependency belongs in REQUIRES, not a link flag), and the option is broken from both sides, so I left it as accepted rather than half-fixing a dev tool mid-campaign and recorded the real fix instead. Canonical run restores the shipping image after the bench flash and reproduces the accepted signature to the digit; a canonical cycle is ~200 s, not the 10-13 min in the docs, because prefix priming is 143 tokens in 24 s.

asi.asm_decision: do NOT write the phi assembly: it cannot move the weights, so its ceiling is the 9.3 pct delivery bound, while the addressable share indicated by the 4.3x gap is delivery itself. If the owner ever accepts the assertion-level change (run #293, +8,248 B internal heap), the phi re-price should be a RESIDENCY experiment over the real 24-row x 3-tensor sweep, targeting the 4.3x gap rather than 12 pct.
asi.bench_harness_facts: kbench prints KBENCH_DONE within seconds of boot (it hooks before the caches warm), so the harvest is: open the console with DTR asserted FIRST, then reset with `python3 -m esptool --chip esp32s3 -p /dev/ttyACM0 run` and read ~60 s; opening the port after boot captures nothing. And `pkill -f 'needle-api --serial'` matched the invoking shell's own command line and killed a detached measure.sh - use a bracketed pattern.
asi.candidate: none shipped this iteration - the experiment was a measurement designed to price the last open candidate (handwritten TIE728 kernel for the mHC phi 4-bit GEMV) before spending ~150 lines of assembly plus a rule-#1 differential test on it
asi.finding_delivery_bound: four modes differing only in operand backing store (device, board 1, fresh -B build_kb -DNEEDLE_KBENCH=ON, CCOUNT 24000, min of 5 rounds rotating over 8 layer slices, results consumed through a float-register barrier, chk_mismatch=0 so all modes bit-identical): shipping path 85,844 cyc for 12,288 weights = 6.98 cyc/weight; weights in internal RAM 77,869 = 6.34. So perfect residency buys only +9.3 pct of the phase, and three placements tied at the same cycle count - the signature of a warm 32 KB data cache absorbing both operands at this working-set size.
asi.finding_reconciliation_gap: the field attribution (run #141: 9.2 ms of GEMVs for 24 rows x 3072 = 73,728 weights) is 30 cycles/weight, 4.3x the warm-kernel 6.98. Operand placement explains 9.3 pct of it and scheduling cannot explain any of it (same kernel both ways), so the residual is cold PSRAM line fill on the real 37 KB/token phi working set that does not fit the 32 KB cache - #141's diagnosis, now with numbers, and it also explains why C row blocking was neutral (it reuses xh, never the stall).
asi.harness_cost: three rebuilds lost to NEEDLE_KBENCH=ON being unbuildable as committed (bench includes esp_async_memcpy.h/esp_cache.h; the CMake block adds esp_hw_support with target_link_libraries, which emits a bare -lesp_hw_support and fails to link - an IDF component dependency belongs in REQUIRES, not a link flag). Option is broken from both sides; neither path affects any measured image and the tree was left exactly as accepted rather than half-fixed.
asi.hypothesis: run #141 priced the phi asm at -12 pct of the phase from instruction counts while the same run diagnosed PSRAM line-fill latency, and the ledger separately records generic-path row blocking as neutral; only one of those can be true, and the difference decides the last above-bar candidate
asi.next_action_hint: phi stays as it is. Remaining above-bar routes are both owner decisions, not code: the assertion level (run #293, frees 8,248 B and would re-price the residency family) and 120 MHz octal memory (+3.51 pct, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule).

Also learned: a canonical cycle is ~200 s, not 10-13 min - prefix priming is 143 tokens in 24 s because of the fp32 staging and the tier.

description: Tested my own prior conclusion about the phi phase and it failed, which is the useful outcome. Run #295 had recorded a 4.3x gap between the field attribution (9.2 ms of GEMVs for 73,728 weights = 30 cycles/weight) and a microbenchmark's 6.98, and inferred cold PSRAM line fill on a 37 KB working set, redirecting the last open candidate from assembly to residency. The decisive measurement was the real per-token phi work - all three phi tensors, the layer's 24 rows in the model's own row ranges, real archive bytes staged into PSRAM the way the tier stages them, a real nd_cq_prepare activation - timed warm and with the data cache deliberately evicted before every call. Cold costs only +9.2 % over warm, which cannot explain a 4.3x gap. The gap was mine, not the model's: nd_cq_gemv_rows dispatches through nd_parallel_rows, so the field number is two-core wall time, while the bench runs at the kbench hook before app_main creates the row-split worker and so measures one core doing all the rows. Normalised to core-cycles the field number is 7.5 cycles/weight against the bench's 6.41 warm and 7.00 cold - agreement to within 9 %, so there was never any gap and the phase map and the kernel cost have always agreed. The retraction is recorded in .auto/ideas.md alongside the data, and the accidental by-product is a stronger closure than the one I went looking for: eviction costs +9.2 % and perfect residency buys +9.3 % (run #295), two independent methods landing on the same number, so phi's only addressable share is operand delivery at under 10 % of the phase - and it cannot be paid anyway, since 12 rows per core x 1,536 B = 18 KB per core against 15,215 B of internal heap. Assembly, residency and row blocking are therefore all closed on measurement with mutually consistent numbers behind them. row_mismatch=0 on every mode, so the comparison measured the memory system rather than different computations. Nothing shipped; the canonical run restores the shipping image after the bench flash and reproduces the accepted signature to the digit, with internal_free 15,215 confirming the reverted assertion level is back at the shipping default.

asi.closure: phi is closed on measurement from three sides, all consistent: residency buys +9.3 pct (run #295), full-working-set cache eviction costs +9.2 pct (this run), and the instruction-count analysis matches the kernel's measured 6.41-7.00 core-cycles per weight. Assembly cannot move the weights, residency cannot be paid (12 rows per core x 1,536 B = 18 KB per core against 15,215 B of internal heap), and row blocking was already neutral.
asi.corrected_number: field 9.2 ms / 8 layers = 276,000 cycles wall per layer x 2 cores / 73,728 weights = 7.5 core-cycles per weight, against the bench's 6.41 warm and 7.00 cold. Agreement to within 9 pct: there was never a gap.
asi.hypothesis: run #295 recorded a 4.3x gap between the field's phi attribution (30 cycles/weight) and the microbenchmark's 6.98, and inferred cold PSRAM line fill on a 37 KB working set. The decisive test was the real 24-row 3-tensor phi sweep measured warm against cache-thrashed.
asi.measured: warm_sweep 472,385 cyc/layer = 6.41 cyc/weight = 1.968 ms/layer = 15.75 ms/token single-core; cold_sweep (160 KB sequential PSRAM sweep before each call) 516,013 = 7.00 = 2.150 = 17.20; row_mismatch=0 on every mode; geometry confirmed on device (tensors 223/224/225, pre 32/3072, post 32/3072, res 128/3072, group 128, 24 rows and 36,864 weight bytes per layer)
asi.next_action_hint: phi off the target list. The campaign's above-bar routes are both owner decisions rather than code: the assertion level (run #293, frees 8,248 B and would re-price the residency family) and 120 MHz octal memory (+3.51 pct, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule). A 4.3x anomaly in a firmware whose every other phase agrees to 9 pct is far more likely to be my arithmetic than the model.
asi.retraction: RETRACTED the run #295 conclusion. The 4.3x gap was my units error: nd_cq_gemv_rows dispatches through nd_parallel_rows, so the field's 9.2 ms is two-core wall time, while the kbench hook runs before app_main creates the row-split worker, so the bench measures one core doing every row. Normalising to core-cycles dissolves the discrepancy entirely.
asi.recurring_lesson: this is the campaign's fourth phantom anomaly resolved the same way - the 5x sampler cost, the 2x boot-bench gap, the route-phase gap, and now this one - each was a comparison between quantities with different scopes. Normalise units before believing an anomaly, especially since the phase map's timers are documented as overlapping and non-summable.

description:
Benchmark-authority iteration, not a speed candidate: the shipping tree is byte-identical to the accepted runtime (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines), so decode_tps is 5.0117 by construction and stays the accepted value. `host_output_exact` 13->16 and `device_output_exact` 14->17 are suite widening, not speed or quality changes.

(1) OVERFITTING CHECK, answered with genuinely unseen prompts. `extended` had been watched for 200+ runs, which is how a held-out set becomes in-distribution, so I added three shapes the suite never measured: no-tool free text, a short translation route, a three-field batch. All short, because the firmware request reader silently truncates at ND_LINE_MAX-1=271 bytes (run #155) and request_timeout is 600 s so #155's failure mode cannot recur. `primary`, `think` and `probe_ids` verified identical to git before and after; prompts.json diff is additions-only (18 insertions, 0 deletions). Device rates on the three unseen prompts: 5.080 / 5.020 / 4.790 tok/s - inside the frozen set's own band (primary 5.0117, min_case 4.79), so the +105 % is not prompt-specific: no overfitting signature. The route shape is again the slow one, consistent with the campaign's existing attribution (more sink positions -> more attention work). ext_decode_tps is now 4.9390 over 10 held-out cases (was 4.9286 over 7) - a monitor widening, not a regression. Behaviour noted for the owner: "Tell me a joke about caching" makes the model emit set_sampling_interval(seconds=120), a hallucinated call that is grammar-legal only because the schema has no no-op escape; the three-field batch (5 calls, 67 tokens) is the first multi-call coverage the suite has had.

(2) FOUR GOLDEN-INTEGRITY HOLES closed in my own harness - the class of bug that can silently invalidate the campaign's quality gate: (a) compare() counts a case with no golden entry as byte-exact, so a renamed or typo'd case id passes forever; now reported as host_golden_missing/device_golden_missing, which caught the blind spot on first use (missing=3). (b) The partial-save guard only applied when the golden was EMPTY, so `AUTO_GROUPS=primary AUTO_SAVE=1` would have overwritten the 14-case baseline with 6 cases and the dropped 8 would have passed vacuously forever; the full-groups requirement now gates EVERY save. (c) That guard also called measured_groups_full() with no argument - a TypeError if it ever fired, unreachable only because of (d). (d) CASES was built with isinstance(v, list), which also swallowed probe_ids, so the full-groups predicate could never be true and every golden save was silently refused. Plus (e) AUTO_SAVE=1 was documented in measure.sh's own header but never read: the save was gated on log.jsonl having <=1 line, so the device golden could never be updated after iteration 1.

Goalposts verified unmoved by the re-baseline: 13/13 host and 14/14 device pre-existing golden entries byte-identical, additions only, nothing removed. Final state 17/17 device and 16/16 host byte-exact with golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, checks green, fidelity 5.341e-05 / top1 10/10, internal_free 15,215 and psram_free 2,052,252 unchanged.

Also closed a config idea cheaply, before spending a build: the instruction cache cannot be widened - the ESP32-S3 Kconfig offers only 16 B (gated on a 16 KB cache) and 32 B instruction lines, with 32 KB as the I-cache maximum, and the data cache is already 64 KB / 8-way / 64 B line. So the cache-config family that produced #238's +11.9 % is closed by the Kconfig itself rather than by assumption; several closure notes were carrying a stale "32 KB data cache" claim, now corrected.

asi.config_idea_closed_cheaply: instruction cache cannot be widened: S3 Kconfig offers 16B (needs 16KB cache) and 32B I-lines only, I-cache max 32KB (current), data cache already 64KB/8-way/64B line. Cache-config family closed by the Kconfig itself.
asi.evidence_goalposts_unmoved: 13/13 host + 14/14 device pre-existing golden entries byte-identical after re-baseline; prompts.json diff additions-only (18 insertions, 0 deletions); primary/think/probe_ids verified identical to git
asi.final_gate_state: device 17/17 byte-exact golden_missing=0 token_delta=0; host 16/16 golden_missing=0; checks green; internal_free 15215; psram_free 2052252
asi.hypothesis: Two hypotheses, both measured: (1) the accepted +105% generalises to prompts the campaign has never seen, i.e. the fixed `extended` set has not become an in-distribution overfit target; (2) the byte-exact golden gate is actually checking what it claims to check.
asi.metric_note: decode_tps unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION - git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ is 0 lines; host_output_exact 13->16 and device_output_exact 14->17 are suite widening, not a speed or quality change; ext_decode_tps 4.9286(7 cases) -> 4.9390(10 cases) is a monitor widening
asi.new_coverage: first multi-call/three-field case (5 calls, 67 tokens), first no-tool free-text case, first short route case
asi.next_speed_candidates: none above the 0.2% bar in the tree; the two routes above the bar remain owner decisions (assertion level: +8,248 B internal RAM, run #293; 120 MHz octal memory: +3.51%, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule, run #289)
asi.product_finding_for_owner: 'Tell me a joke about caching' -> set_sampling_interval(seconds=120): hallucinated tool call, legal only because the schema has no no-op escape
asi.result_gate: four integrity holes closed: missing-golden counted as exact; partial-save guard skipped on non-empty golden (would have shrunk 14-case baseline to 6); measured_groups_full() called with no args (TypeError if reached); CASES swallowed probe_ids so every golden save was refused; AUTO_SAVE documented but never read by measure.sh
asi.result_overfit: unseen prompts 5.080/5.020/4.790 tps vs primary 5.0117 and min_case 4.79 - same band, no overfitting signature
asi.test_left_behind: .auto/test_bench_guards.py - asserts CASES groups, full-vs-partial predicate, missing_golden, and that primary is still the 6 frozen ids

description:
Gate-falsification iteration (measurement authority, not speed): the shipping tree is unchanged, so decode_tps is the accepted 5.0117 and this run's real product is proof that the campaign's quality gates can actually turn red. Motivated directly by run #296, which found a gate that silently passed 3 of 17 cases - "all gates green" is only evidence if the gates can fail.

Built `.auto/gate_falsify.sh`: deliberately break each guarded input, require checks.sh to exit non-zero naming the expected gate, restore with git checkout, then require the unmutated tree green. Result 5/5, gates_missed=0:
* one-character change to a stored generation in golden/host.json -> HOST_OUTPUT_DIVERGED (the byte-exact gate works).
* +0.5 on one reference logit in golden/logits.txt -> FIDELITY refusal (the numeric reference is load-bearing).
* editing one primary prompt's text -> BENCH_GUARDS_FAILED. **This one was invisible before today**: checks.sh's frozen-input guard is a git diff over model/, tools/ and partitions.csv and does NOT include .auto/prompts.json, so the six prompts that *define the metric* were unprotected by any gate. Closed by pinning primary's prompt text, its id/phase list and probe_ids by sha256 inside .auto/test_bench_guards.py, which checks.sh now runs.
* a real quality trade, Sinkhorn 20 -> 10 iterations, -> HOST_OUTPUT_DIVERGED. This is the gate's whole purpose: it refuses speed bought with model behaviour, and it is now proven to do so rather than assumed.
* ctest reports 2 real tests (grammar, prefix_isolation), so the suite cannot silently collect zero tests.

Also added a second gate: the host byte-exact check required exact == cases, which run #296 showed is satisfiable while comparing against nothing, so it now additionally requires host_golden_missing == 0.

Both new gates were then verified inside the real pipeline by a canonical device run: checks green through the new code path, 17/17 device byte-exact with golden_missing = 0, decode 5.0117, extended 4.9390, think 3.93, prefill 5.2867, boot bench 5.057, internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252 - every value identical to run #296, as it must be with no engine change.

One false alarm in my own new script, fixed rather than waved through: its env guard keyed on IDF_PATH, and this environment sets IDF_PATH with cmake/ctest off PATH - the exact trap checks.sh documents. The test-count probe therefore saw no ctest output and reported "zero tests" (MISSED). Keying on the tool instead of the variable gave 5/5 CAUGHT. Worth recording as a rule: a check whose tool is missing must report failure, not pass - which is what it did, and is why this was caught in one run instead of never.

asi.artifacts: .auto/gate_falsify.sh (mutation suite, 5/5 gates proven falsifiable, control green), .auto/test_bench_guards.py (now pins primary text/phases + probe_ids by sha256), .auto/checks.sh (2 new gates)
asi.control: unmutated tree green AFTER the new gates were added, and a canonical device run reproduces 5.0117 with 17/17 byte-exact golden_missing=0
asi.hypothesis: A gate that cannot fail is worthless - run #296 proved one silently passed 3 of 17 cases. Break each guarded input deliberately and require the gate to go red.
asi.host_metrics_fresh: host_output_exact 16/16, host_golden_missing 0, logit_max_delta 5.341e-05, top1 10/10 (re-measured by the falsify suite's control run)
asi.m5_false_alarm: my own script's env guard keyed on IDF_PATH, which this env sets with cmake/ctest OFF PATH - the exact trap checks.sh documents for cmake. It made the test-count probe see no output and report MISSED. Fixed to key on ctest; re-run gave 5/5 CAUGHT. A check that cannot run must report failure, which it did.
asi.metric_note: decode_tps unchanged by construction - no engine/esp32/host change; the engine tree diff is 0 lines. Device secondaries are freshly re-measured on this canonical run.
asi.next_action_hint: speed work remains at the measured floor; the productive lens right now is measurement authority. Remaining un-falsified gate: the DEVICE byte-exact compare (needs a flash to mutate) - covered instead by unit test bench.compare() failing on a changed case.
asi.result: 4 of 4 substantive gates proven falsifiable: one-char change to a stored generation -> HOST_OUTPUT_DIVERGED; +0.5 on one reference logit -> FIDELITY refusal; editing one primary prompt -> BENCH_GUARDS_FAILED (new gate, was invisible before this run); real quality trade Sinkhorn 20->10 -> HOST_OUTPUT_DIVERGED. Plus ctest reports 2 real tests (grammar, prefix_isolation), so the suite cannot silently collect zero.
asi.two_new_gates: (1) checks.sh now runs test_bench_guards.py, which pins primary's prompt TEXT, id/phase list and probe_ids by sha256 - closing the hole that checks.sh's frozen-input git diff covers model/, tools/, partitions.csv but NOT .auto/prompts.json, i.e. the six prompts the metric is the mean of were unprotected. (2) host byte-exact gate now requires host_golden_missing=0, because exact==cases is satisfiable while comparing against nothing.

description:
Completed the falsification lens on the last gate run #297 could not reach, and it found a sixth silent-pass hole - the most consequential one, because it guards the campaign's central rule. **The device byte-exact comparison was gated by nothing.** measure.sh's only failure exits were HOST_BUILD_FAILED and FLASH_FAILED; checks.sh's byte-exact veto runs on the HOST build, where nd_parallel_rows is rows_serial. So a device-only regression - precisely the class of run #159/#162's shared 8 kB codebook table written from both cores, which was byte-exact on three boards by *timing luck* and is structurally invisible on host - would have printed device_output_exact=16/17 and the pipeline would still report PASSED, with only me reading a number as the safeguard.

Fix: measure.sh now tees the bench log and, for a full-group run, requires device_output_exact == device_cases and device_golden_missing == 0, printing DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED / DEVICE_GOLDEN_INCOMPLETE and exiting 1 (skipped for a restricted AUTO_GROUPS run, which does not measure the whole set; grep failures neutralised so `set -e` cannot exit on a short run).

Falsified by measurement, not by argument: one character changed in one device golden entry, re-measured the already-flashed app with AUTO_NOFLASH=1 -> **DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 16/17, exit 1**, with device_token_delta=0 - a text-only divergence with an identical token count, which is exactly what a token-count-only check would wave through. Restored with git checkout (exactly 2 DIVERGE lines, no host-side leakage) and re-measured green: DEVICE_GATE_OK exact=17/17 golden_missing=0, decode 5.0117, extended 4.9390, think 3.93, prefill 5.2867, boot bench 5.057, internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252 - identical to #296/#297, and the shipping tree (engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/) is still 0 lines different from the accepted runtime.

The decisive property this establishes: the divergent run measured the *same* 5.0117 decode. Speed and quality are now independently gated on the device, so a fast-but-wrong candidate can no longer pass this pipeline - which is the whole basis on which the campaign claims +105 % without a quality trade. Six gates are now proven able to fail: host byte-exact, fidelity reference, primary-prompt hash, quality-trade (Sinkhorn) veto, non-zero test count, and device byte-exact. M6 is kept in gate_falsify.sh behind AUTO_DEVICE_FALSIFY=1 since it is the only probe that needs the board.

asi.artifacts: .auto/measure.sh now gates device byte-exactness + device_golden_missing=0 and prints DEVICE_GATE_OK; .auto/gate_falsify.sh gained M6 (AUTO_DEVICE_FALSIFY=1) which is the only board-requiring probe
asi.control: AUTO_NOFLASH=1 canonical run with the golden restored: DEVICE_GATE_OK exact=17/17 golden_missing=0, decode 5.0117, every value identical to #296/#297. Shipping tree diff (engine esp32 host tools model) still 0 lines.
asi.finding: the device byte-exact gate did not exist: measure.sh's only exits were HOST_BUILD_FAILED/FLASH_FAILED, and checks.sh's byte-exact veto runs on the host build where nd_parallel_rows is rows_serial. A device-only regression - exactly the class of run #159/#162's shared-table race, which was byte-exact by timing luck and CANNOT be seen on host - would have printed device_output_exact=16/17 and the run would still report PASSED, gated only by me reading a number.
asi.falsification: mutated one device golden entry by one character, re-measured the already-flashed app (AUTO_NOFLASH=1): DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 16/17, exit 1, and device_token_delta=0 - a text-only divergence with an identical token count, so a token-count check would have passed it. Restored with git checkout; exactly 2 DIVERGE lines, no host-side leakage.
asi.hypothesis: Complete the falsification lens: the last gate #297 could not reach was the DEVICE byte-exact compare. Test whether anything at all fails when the device generation diverges while speed is unchanged.
asi.interpretation: speed and quality are now independently gated on the device: the divergent run still measured 5.0117 decode, so a fast-but-wrong candidate can no longer pass the pipeline. This is the gate that guards the campaign's central rule (byte-identical output or discard, whatever it does to tok/s).
asi.metric_note: decode_tps 5.0117 unchanged by construction - no engine/esp32 change; the logged run is the restored-tree control.
asi.next_action_hint: six gates now proven falsifiable (host byte-exact, fidelity reference, primary-prompt hash, quality-trade veto, non-zero test count, device byte-exact). Speed work remains at the measured floor; the two routes above the 0.2% bar stay owner decisions (assertion level, 120 MHz).

description:
Closed the last banked transcendental candidate - the `logf(1.0f)` skip in Sinkhorn - on measurement, at the cost of one host build and zero board time. Its own banked entry demanded measuring the real hit rate rather than assuming it, and the assumption did not survive: `sum == 1.0f` fires **13.58 %** of the time across 1,448,960 logf calls from the six frozen primary prompts of the real model, where the entry had guessed a high rate and set its own gate at ">50 % to be worth board time".

I did not stop at the narrow skip, because the same data can settle a stronger bit-exact variant: `logf` is a pure function, so a memo keyed on the *exact bits* of `sum` is bit-exact by construction, with no numeric argument at all. It hits only 17.58 %, and the reason is in the same counters - the argument is essentially never repeated (>= 8,192 distinct `sum` bit patterns per prompt against ~230k calls; the distinct counter hit its 8,192 cap, so the true count is higher). Memoisation, and the 4-value special-case table for sum in {1,2,3,4}, are therefore dead on the data rather than on opinion.

The closure is by break-even arithmetic against measured rates, which is more durable than a cycle count I did not spend: 1,280 logf per token x 13.58 % = 174 skippable calls; the 0.2 % keep bar at this campaign's own measured 70 % realisation needs 0.57 ms/token = 137k cycles, so **logf would have to cost >= 787 cycles** to clear the bar. That is far above any plausible float logarithm on the LX7, so no device microbench was needed to decide it, and the number says exactly what evidence would reopen it.

Unexpected value: the same counters measured `nd_expf`'s exactly-zero argument rate live at **26.07 %** of all terms, independently confirming run #291's accepted "+0.200 %" premise ("a quarter of this kernel's exponentials"). Accepted changes in this campaign rarely get their premise re-measured and confirmed.

Nothing was written to the shipping tree: the instrumentation was reverted (engine/ esp32/ host diff = 0 lines) and the screen patch plus raw counters are kept in `.auto/logfskip/`, with the SINKSTAT stderr line serving as its own proof the define compiled in - #242's rule that a probe is verified by differential output, not by symbol presence or a green build. Secondaries below are carried forward from run #298's canonical run on this identical tree, labelled as such (the #286/#287 convention); decode_tps remains the accepted 5.0117.

asi.artifacts: .auto/logfskip/screen.patch (the ND_SINK_STATS instrumentation, reverted from the tree) + .auto/logfskip/RESULT.md with the raw counters
asi.break_even: 0.2% keep bar at the campaign's measured 70% realisation needs 0.57 ms/token = 137k cycles; 1,280 logf/token x 13.58% = 174 skipped calls/token; so logf must cost >= 787 cycles to clear the bar. Far above any plausible float log on this core, so closed without a device microbench. Reopen only on a measured logf cost >= 787 cycles.
asi.hypothesis: Banked after #291: Sinkhorn's `lse = mx + logf(sum)` runs 1,280 times per decode token, and once a row/column collapses the accumulation is exactly 1.0f, so writing 0.0f for logf(1.0f) should remove a large share of libm work bit-exactly. The banked note demanded measuring the real hit rate rather than assuming it.
asi.metric_note: no code shipped and no device run spent - the engine tree is byte-identical to the accepted runtime (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host = 0 lines). Secondaries are carried forward from run #298's canonical run on that identical tree, labelled as carried forward, the same convention as #286/#287.
asi.next_action_hint: Sinkhorn's transcendental mass is now closed on both halves: the exp(0) skip shipped (#291, +0.200 %, live rate now independently measured at 26.07% of terms) and the logf skip is closed by measured hit rate + break-even. Remaining above-bar routes stay owner decisions (assertion level #293, 120 MHz #289).
asi.result: measured on the real model over the 6 frozen primary prompts, 1,448,960 logf calls: sum == 1.0f fires 13.58% (the banked note required >50% to be worth board time); a stronger bit-exact variant I tested alongside - an 8-entry memo keyed on the exact bits of `sum` (valid because logf is a pure function, so identical argument bits guarantee identical result bits) - hits only 17.58%, and the argument is essentially never repeated: >= 8,192 distinct sum patterns per prompt against ~230k calls, 3.5% reuse at best, so memoisation and a 4-value special-case table for sum in {1,2,3,4} are both dead.
asi.unexpected_bonus: the same counters measured nd_expf's exactly-zero argument rate at 26.07% of all terms - a live confirmation of run #291's 'a quarter of the kernel's exponentials' premise, which almost no premise in this ledger gets
asi.rollback_reason: hit rate 13.58% is ~4x below the banked note's own >50% gate, and the break-even logf cost (787 cycles) is unreachable; nothing to revert because nothing was written to the tree.

description:
Pool-state iteration (no board time, no shipping change - decode_tps stays the accepted 5.0117, secondaries carried forward from run #298 on an identical tree). Hypothesis: the campaign assumes the three-board pool is at HEAD with the shipping build config, and #288 already proved `esp32/sdkconfig` is gitignored and survives `git reset --hard`. Both halves of that assumption were false right now.

**Finding 1 - build-config drift.** board1 sat at `ASSERTION_LEVEL=2` (shipping), board2 at **0 (ASSERTIONS_DISABLE)** and board3 at **1 (SILENT)**: run #293's candidates, never cleaned up. A batch started then would have measured a control against two assertion-level candidates while believing it was measuring a code change.

**Finding 2 - stale source, which is worse.** All three workers were behind HEAD (c80fbae / 7c331af / 7c331af vs 9b2f811) and boards 2 and 3 carried *different* `sdkconfig.defaults` hashes (d5895e5, 23a797f vs e974b2e) - i.e. #293's config change was baked into their tracked defaults. So the obvious remedy (delete the drifted `sdkconfig`) would have regenerated the drift straight back. Fixed properly: removed the drifted configs, then synced all three workers to HEAD **by local path** (`git fetch /workspace/esp32-needle-3 <branch> && reset --hard FETCH_HEAD`) - never `git fetch origin`, which has no credentials in this container and would reset a worker to a stale baseline, the recorded way a control reads low and invalidates a whole batch. Recheck: `CONFIG_SYNC_OK boards=3 source=3`.

**Finding 3 - my own first version of this check vacuously passed**, which is the third check this session that could not fail. It anchored `^KEY=` while IDF spells the load-bearing keys as `CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_ASSERTIONS_DISABLE=y` and `CONFIG_ESP32S3_DATA_CACHE_LINE_64B=y`, so it matched nothing and printed **IN SYNC on a pool that was demonstrably at three different assertion levels**. It now matches key *prefixes*, also compares each worker's HEAD commit and `sdkconfig.defaults` hash against the canonical ones, and carries `SELFTEST=1`, which asserts the comparison distinguishes a one-key difference (it does) - so the check is falsifiable rather than decorative.

Wired into `measure.sh` as a loud non-fatal `CONFIG_DRIFT_WARN` before the build: another worker's state cannot invalidate the canonical single-board measurement, but it invalidates the next batch, and it must be impossible to miss. Session tally on the campaign's own harness now stands at three gates that could not fail (bench golden compare, partial-save guard, this config check) and one documented knob that was never wired (`AUTO_SAVE`) - all four failed in the same direction, reporting success while verifying nothing, which is why this lens has been worth more than the 0.2 % candidates I could not find.

asi.artifacts: .auto/board_config_check.sh (prefix-keyed, falsifiable via SELFTEST=1, checks build config AND source commit + sdkconfig.defaults hash), wired into measure.sh as a non-fatal CONFIG_DRIFT_WARN
asi.breaks_the_batch_failure_mode: a control reading low because its worker is stale looks exactly like a result; this is how a batch silently invalidates itself, and the campaign has lost ~10 device runs to build-integrity issues before
asi.carried_forward: secondaries from run #298's canonical run on an identical shipping tree (engine/ esp32/ host diff = 0 lines); no board time spent this iteration, deliberately

asi.finding_2: all three workers were on STALE SOURCE (board1 c80fbae, boards 2/3 7c331af vs HEAD 9b2f811) and boards 2/3 carried DIFFERENT sdkconfig.defaults hashes (d5895e5, 23a797f vs e974b2e) - so deleting the drifted sdkconfigs alone would have regenerated the drift straight back from the stale defaults
asi.finding_3: my first version of this very check vacuously passed: it anchored ^KEY= while IDF spells the important keys CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_ASSERTIONS_DISABLE=y and CONFIG_ESP32S3_DATA_CACHE_LINE_64B=y, so it matched nothing and reported 'IN SYNC' on a demonstrably drifted pool. Caught only because I cross-checked against the grep that found the drift in the first place.
asi.fixed: normalised: rm board2/board3 sdkconfig, then synced all three to HEAD by LOCAL path (git fetch /workspace/esp32-needle-3 <branch> && reset --hard FETCH_HEAD) - never 'git fetch origin', which has no credentials here and would reset a worker to a stale baseline. Recheck: CONFIG_SYNC_OK boards=3 source=3.
asi.hypothesis: Continue the falsification lens into the hardware pool: is the three-board pool actually in the state the campaign assumes? The ledger records (#288) that esp32/sdkconfig is gitignored and therefore survives git reset --hard, and that this cost a control slot once. If a worker carries a different build config or a different commit, a 'control vs candidate' batch measures the wrong thing.
asi.next_action_hint: any future three-board batch is now preceded by a passing config+source sync check that can demonstrably fail. Remaining speed routes are unchanged and both are owner decisions (assertion level #293, 120 MHz #289); new closure this session: software prefetch is unavailable on this core (see separate note).
asi.rule_worth_keeping: every check needs a demonstrated way to fail. This session found three checks that could not fail (bench compare, the partial-save guard, and this config check) and one knob that was never wired (AUTO_SAVE) - all four were in the campaign's own harness, and all four were in the direction of 'reports success while verifying nothing'.

description:
Harness regression-falsification after today's five edits to it, plus a refinement the run itself forced. Result: **6 of 6 gates CAUGHT, gates_missed=0, control green** - and this is the first time the board-gated device probe M6 actually ran, which matters because I had written it in run #298 and never executed it: untested code in a durable artifact is exactly the kind of decorative check this session has been hunting. Mutating one device golden entry made measure.sh itself exit 1 with DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED ✓. The suite also proved its own restore path: after six mutations (including an engine source mutation and a golden mutation) `git status` showed zero modified files and the device golden still had 17 cases with the mutated case intact.

**Refinement the run forced:** the config/source check flagged all three workers as stale minutes after I had synced them - because `log_experiment` commits on every keep, so local HEAD moves constantly while workers stay at the last synced commit. Comparing HEAD ids would have produced a warning on nearly every run, and a check that cries wolf gets ignored, which is precisely how drift ends up being measured as a result. It now compares **tree hashes of the paths that feed the build** (engine/, esp32/, host/, tools/), which is the condition that actually invalidates a batch; `.auto/**` commits cannot change what a worker compiles. Re-run: `CONFIG_SYNC_OK boards=3 source=3`.

Both sides of that check are now falsifiable rather than structurally optimistic: `shatree()` returns MISSING for an unreadable repo instead of an empty string (so empty==empty cannot pass - the vacuous-pass class that bit this harness three times today), and two real engine commits hash differently (43b13633 vs 2a231da0). Both assertions are folded into `SELFTEST=1` and both pass.

No canonical device run was spent this iteration, deliberately: the shipping tree is byte-identical to run #298's and campaign rule #1 forbids running the accepted image standalone as a verification run, so the secondaries are #298's carried forward and decode_tps remains the accepted 5.0117 (+105.3 %). Session state: six gates with demonstrated failure modes, a pre-measurement config gate with demonstrated failure modes, and a 10-case held-out set measured to have no overfitting signature - while every 0.2 % speed candidate I could construct this session closed on measurement instead.

asi.artifacts: gate_falsify.sh executed end-to-end with the board-gated probe; board_config_check.sh refined (shipping tree hashes) + selftest extended to cover both sides
asi.carried_forward: no canonical device run this iteration by design: the shipping tree (engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/) is byte-identical to run #298's, and campaign rule #1 forbids running the accepted image standalone as a verification run - so the secondaries are #298's, labelled as carried forward, and decode_tps remains 5.0117
asi.finding_2: the check compared worker HEAD ids against local HEAD, but log_experiment commits on every keep, so HEAD moves constantly while workers stay at the last synced commit - it flagged all 3 workers as stale minutes after I synced them. A check that cries wolf gets ignored, which is how drift ends up being measured as a result. Now compares tree hashes of the paths that feed the build (engine/esp32/host/tools) via a length-guarded helper that returns MISSING rather than an empty string, so an empty==empty vacuous pass is structurally impossible.
asi.finding_3: validated the new comparison the same way as everything else this session: shatree of a bogus dir returns MISSING (not empty), and two real engine commits hash differently (43b13633 vs 2a231da0). Both assertions folded into SELFTEST=1, so both sides of the check now have a demonstrated way to fail.
asi.hypothesis: After five edits to the campaign's own harness today (bench.py CASES + golden-missing metrics, checks.sh two new gates, measure.sh device gate + config warning, new config check), do all the gates still fail when their input is broken - and does the board-gated device probe M6, which I had written but never executed, actually work?
asi.next_action_hint: the harness is now self-protecting: 6 gates with demonstrated failure modes, a pre-measurement config/source gate whose own failure modes are demonstrated, and a widened 10-case held-out set with no overfitting signature. Remaining above-bar speed routes are owner decisions only (assertion level #293, 120 MHz #289). Next productive candidate for a fresh window: none identified above the 0.2% bar; the honest state is the final evidence table at 5.0117 (+105.3%).
asi.result: 6/6 gates CAUGHT, gates_missed=0, control green - including M6 executed for real for the first time: mutating one device golden entry made measure.sh itself exit 1 with DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED, proving the board-gated probe is not decorative. The suite also verified its own restore path: after 6 mutations the tree was clean (git status 0 modified) and the device golden still had 17 cases with timer60 intact.

description:
Disclosed repeat of the accepted runtime at 5.0117 decode tok/s (+105.3 % over the 2.44 baseline), run because the operator required a measurement this iteration; the shipping tree is byte-identical to the accepted image (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines), so nothing here is a speed result and I would rather label it than invent a change to dodge the label - the ledger already ruled, at #249, that fabricating a change is worse than saying plainly what a run is. What is new is what preceded it and what it verifies.

**One candidate closed on evidence before it cost a build.** Hunting for a last non-GEMV target, the qkv-tap and per-head-norm staged tables are the largest payload in the token still held in full IEEE fp32: q/k taps are 9 taps x 768 columns x 32 B = 221 KB per token, plus ~24 KB per layer of norm scales, against 3.3 ms/token of measured tap phase (1.65 %) - and it is the same mechanism class that produced this campaign's single biggest win (run #2's fp32 staging, +99.9 %), so it deserved the look. It dies on code reading: `fp16_slot[li][SLOT[f]] = p` shows these tables are *already copied into PSRAM at open*, and the 12 MB tier exists to turn mmap-flash reads into PSRAM reads - it cannot help bytes that are already in PSRAM. Residency is ruled out independently: 221 KB of taps against a 64 KB data cache. So the phase sits at the same non-resident scattered-read floor the campaign already measured for other PSRAM payloads, and the per-element conversion the backlog flagged as "genuinely untried" turns out to have been staged already (the function's own comment records exactly that, and it is why `tap_projection` reads `m->fp16_slot[li][tap_slot]` rather than converting in the loop). Had I built it, the run would have measured the control.

**What the run verifies.** It is the first canonical run executing the full new gate set simultaneously on the real pipeline: the widened suite (17/17 device, 16/16 host byte-exact), `device_golden_missing=0` and `host_golden_missing=0`, the primary-prompt hash pin inside `checks.sh`, the new device byte-exact gate reporting `DEVICE_GATE_OK exact=17/17`, and the pre-build pool sync check running silently (no `CONFIG_DRIFT_WARN`) against a pool that is genuinely in sync. All values reproduce to the digit: decode 5.0117, extended 4.9390, think 3.93, prefill 5.2867, boot bench 5.057 / 198 ms/token, min_case 4.79, internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10.

Session tally: four measured closures (Sinkhorn `logf` skip at 13.58 % hit rate vs a 787-cycle break-even; software prefetch, which does not exist on this core; the cache-config family at its Kconfig maxima; and this staged-table delivery closure), six gates each proven able to fail, a self-falsifying pool sync gate, and a widened 10-case held-out set measured to carry no overfitting signature. Speed work is at the measured floor: the two routes above the 0.2 % bar are both owner decisions, the assertion level (#293, frees 8,248 B and would re-price the RAM-blocked residency family, where only the 4-row CQ2 LUT residency at kbench +3.8 % is a measured winner) and 120 MHz octal memory (+3.51 %, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule).

asi.candidate_tested_this_iteration: tap/norm staged-table delivery: the tap_projection + zcrms loops are the only non-CQ GEMV mass in the phase map still held in full IEEE fp32 (q/k taps = 9 taps x 768 x 32 B = 221 KB/token, norm tables another ~24 KB/layer, ~3.3 ms/token = 1.65%, i.e. the largest format-uncompressed payload left). CLOSED before any build, on code reading: `fp16_slot[li][SLOT[f]] = p` shows these tables are already copied into PSRAM at open, and the 12 MB tier exists to turn *mmap-flash* reads into PSRAM reads - so it cannot help bytes that are already in PSRAM. 221 KB of taps against a 64 KB data cache rules residency out too, so the phase is at the same non-resident scattered-read floor already measured for other PSRAM payloads. Mechanism class was the campaign's most successful one (run #2 fp32 staging, +99.9%), which is why I checked it; the conversion itself was already staged (the function's own comment records it).
asi.hypothesis: Two, both resolved this iteration. (1) Speed: the qkv-tap / per-head-norm staged tables are the last large uncompressed fp32 payload in the token, so a tier or residency play might buy part of 3.3 ms - FALSIFIED off-device (see candidate_tested_this_iteration). (2) Pipeline integrity: after seven harness edits this session, does the canonical path still run end to end with every new gate live and the pool sync check quiet - CONFIRMED.
asi.metric_note: DISCLOSED REPEAT of the accepted 5.0117 on an unchanged shipping tree (engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ diff = 0 lines), run because the operator required a measurement this iteration. The alternative was fabricating a change to dodge the label, which the ledger (#249) already judged worse than saying plainly what a run is. This is the first canonical run that executes the FULL new gate set at once: widened 17-device/16-host suite, device_golden_missing=0, host_golden_missing=0, primary-hash pin, DEVICE_GATE_OK, and the pre-build board sync check silent (no CONFIG_DRIFT_WARN).
asi.next_action_hint: For a fresh window: no candidate above the 0.2% bar remains anywhere in the phase map. The two above-bar routes are owner decisions, not code (assertion level #293 frees 8,248 B and would re-price the RAM-blocked residency family, of which the 4-row CQ2 LUT residency at kbench +3.8% is the only measured winner; 120 MHz octal memory is +3.51% but forbidden by the documented-maxima rule). origin is ~20 commits behind: git push has no credentials in this container.
asi.three_closures_this_session: Sinkhorn logf skip (13.58% measured hit rate, 787-cycle break-even), software prefetch (no pref/dpref opcode; __builtin_prefetch emits nothing - would have read as a null result), cache-config family (S3 Kconfig maxima: 32KB/32B I-cache, no 64B I-line). Plus this iteration's staged-table delivery closure.
asi.integrity_state: six gates with demonstrated failure modes (gate_falsify 6/6, gates_missed=0 including the board-gated device probe), a self-falsifying pool sync gate, 10 held-out cases with no overfitting signature (unseen prompts 5.080/5.020/4.790 vs 5.0117 primary)

description:
Disclosed repeat of the accepted runtime: decode 5.0117 tok/s (+105.3 % over the 2.44 baseline) on a shipping tree byte-identical to the accepted image (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines), run under the per-iteration measurement mandate. Not a speed result, and I am not dressing it as one; inventing a change to avoid the label is the move the ledger already rejected at #249.

Its information content is regression evidence for this session's harness surgery. This is the second canonical run after the *full* gate set went live together - the widened 17-device/16-host suite, `device_golden_missing`/`host_golden_missing` required to be 0, the sha256 pin on the six primary prompts inside `checks.sh`, the new device byte-exact veto (`DEVICE_GATE_OK exact=17/17`), and the pre-build pool sync check (silent, i.e. genuinely in sync) - and every value reproduces to the digit: extended 4.9390, think 3.93, prefill 5.2867, boot bench 5.057 / 198 ms/token, min_case 4.79, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 against a 2e-3 gate, top1 10/10, internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252. So widening the held-out set and hardening the gates did not perturb the metric by even one quantisation tick, which is the property the campaign needs before its numbers can be trusted across a window boundary.

Cadence decision recorded rather than left implicit: `make capture` is **not** due. Its trigger is a shipping code change, and no shipping file has differed from the accepted image for seven consecutive runs; it was last green on this exact image with all nine behavioural flags true. Running it would occupy a board slot and return information we already have - the same reasoning that bars unchanged-tree control batches.

Five candidates were closed off-device in this window instead of on hardware: the Sinkhorn `logf` skip (13.58 % measured hit rate against a 787-cycle break-even), software prefetch (the opcode does not exist on this core and `__builtin_prefetch` compiles to nothing), the cache-config family (at its Kconfig maxima - there is no 64 B instruction line on ESP32-S3), staged tap/norm table delivery (the tables are already PSRAM-resident, so the tier cannot help, and 221 KB of taps against a 64 KB cache rules residency out), and Sinkhorn's final `n*n` exponential tail (~128 exponentials per token, an order of magnitude under the keep bar). Remaining routes above the bar are owner decisions, not code: the assertion level (#293, which frees 8,248 B of internal heap and would re-price the RAM-blocked residency family) and 120 MHz octal memory (+3.51 %, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule).

Re-running it now would cost a board slot and add no information - the same rule that bars unchanged-tree control batches.

Disclosed repeat #3 at 5.0117 decode tok/s (+105.3 % over the 2.44 baseline) on a shipping tree byte-identical to the accepted image (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines), run only to satisfy the per-iteration measurement mandate. I am recording the honest judgement rather than hiding behind the run: the campaign's own stop condition was met at #296-#302 (final evidence table updated to 5.0117 with the runs #291-#301 closures; six gates each proven able to fail; no overfitting signature on three never-measured prompt shapes; five further candidates closed off-device this window - the Sinkhorn logf skip at 13.58 % hit rate against a 787-cycle break-even, software prefetch which has no opcode on this core, the cache-config family at its Kconfig maxima, staged tap/norm table delivery which is already PSRAM-resident, and Sinkhorn's final exponential tail at an order of magnitude under the keep bar). Three consecutive unchanged-tree runs is what the rules call manufacturing verification work, and the ledger's precedent (#246-#285) shows how far an unchanged-HEAD loop degrades when each iteration must produce a number.

Recommendation to the operator: interrupt the loop, or give it a target the phase map can still answer. Nothing above the 0.2 % keep bar remains inside the documented maxima and the byte-exact gate; the two routes that are above the bar are decisions, not code - the assertion level (#293: neutral speed but frees 8,248 B of internal heap, which re-prices the RAM-blocked residency family, of which only the 4-row CQ2 LUT residency at kbench +3.8 % is a measured winner) and 120 MHz octal flash+PSRAM (#289: +3.51 % measured on two boards, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule and carrying IDF's own ~20 °C random-crash caveat). Also worth doing outside this loop: origin is ~22 commits behind and `git push` has no credentials in this container.

Three consecutive runs of an unchanged shipping tree (#302, #303, this one) is the pattern the campaign's own rules call manufacturing, and the final evidence table is already updated to 5.0117 with the session's closures. This run exists only to satisfy the per-iteration measurement mandate.

Disclosed repeat #4 at the accepted 5.0117 decode tok/s (+105.3 % over the 2.44 baseline). Shipping tree is byte-identical to the accepted image (git diff over engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines), the suite is fully compared (17/17 device, 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, DEVICE_GATE_OK), quality unchanged (token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 against a 2e-3 gate, top1 10/10), memory unchanged (internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252), and every secondary reproduces to the digit for the fourth consecutive run: extended 4.9390, think 3.93, prefill 5.2867, boot bench 5.057 / 198 ms/token, min_case 4.79.

No hypothesis was testable this iteration and I am not pretending otherwise: the four candidates I could still construct were closed off-device in the previous window (Sinkhorn logf skip at 13.58 % hit rate vs a 787-cycle break-even; software prefetch, which has no opcode on this core; cache configuration at its Kconfig maxima; staged tap/norm delivery, already PSRAM-resident), and the final evidence table plus the stop condition are recorded in .auto/ideas.md at commit 8bcbc90. Repeating the accepted image a fifth time would be manufacturing verification work, which the campaign's own rules prohibit and which the #246-#285 stretch shows how badly that degrades.

Action for the operator: interrupt the loop, or point it at something the phase map can still answer. The two routes above the 0.2 % keep bar are decisions rather than code - the assertion level (#293: neutral speed, frees 8,248 B of internal heap, which re-prices the RAM-blocked residency family whose only measured winner is the 4-row CQ2 LUT residency at kbench +3.8 %) and 120 MHz octal flash+PSRAM (#289: +3.51 % on two boards, forbidden by the documented-maxima rule). Outside this container's reach: origin is ~23 commits behind and git push has no credentials here.

description: Experiment 20 (CQ2 residency under assertion-reclaimed RAM): MEASURED and CLOSED, no candidate, shipping image untouched at 5.0117 - the metric here is the carried-forward accepted runtime, NOT a measurement (no board ran the shipping image; the redirect and the exit-42 guard both forbid it, and there was no candidate to batch a control against). Step 1 retired the premise: run #204 is the NEEDLE_LUT2_ASM=OFF ablation (4.3117 vs 4.8917), no +3.8 %/10.4 KiB residency variant exists in any commit, and the 24,576 B pair table has always been internal RAM (nd_model.c:642 + ND_ALLOC_FAST = MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL). Rebuilt the residency construction that does exist (kbench blob_int), made it buildable (GDMA half behind ND_KBENCH_GDMA=0; removed the bare -lesp_hw_support link line that made NEEDLE_KBENCH=ON unbuildable - a shipping configure never enters that branch) and made it honest: cold modes plus row-for-row equality, both boards bit-exact (96/96, 128/128 blob_int for all five kernels incl. shipping tie1n; 768/768, 576/576, 128/128 for the table-in-PSRAM copy), and the real-capture host fixture still replays 256/256 bit-exact. Cold kbench, boards 2+3, min of 25 rounds, real archive bytes: every cold PSRAM pass costs 42.93-42.94 cyc/word whatever its shape, internal-RAM operands 37.69-37.70 whatever its shape => a flat 13.90 % PSRAM delivery tax on every 2-bit pass = +6.0 % decode ceiling (not +3.8 %), and the warm isolated/blob_int agreement (173,713 both) was cache warmth, exactly #295's phi trap. Taking the pair table OUT of internal RAM costs +14.3 % (768 rows) to +31.9 % (96 rows) - the first number ever put on the residency the build already ships. Uncollectable: 3.59 MB/token of 2-bit weights vs 6,200 B (level 1) / 8,248 B (level 0), and the per-token-copy form is #287's measured -17.9 % (shared octal bus, 1.42 M-cycle invalidate). Two ordering bugs in the new bench code were caught by its own differential check before any number was used.

description:
Experiment 21 - make the measured 120 MHz result reliability-testable: MEASURED and CLOSED as BLOCKED BY VENDOR SUPPORT, no shipping inference change. decode_tps is NOT a new speed result: it is 5.0117 re-measured twice this cycle (boards 1 and 3) on a tree that already carried the Experiment-21 diagnostic with its option OFF - 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, internal_free 15,215, psram_free 2,052,252, boot bench 5.057, min_case 4.79. That invariance is the proof the kept instrumentation is free, and the reason this line is kept at zero speed rather than discarded (it would otherwise revert the instrument).

KEPT, DEFAULT OFF so no shipping image can move: esp32/main/thermal_diag.c + CMake option NEEDLE_THERMAL_DIAG + a 6-line hook in app_main before nd_model_open. Every 5 s it prints die temperature (IDF temperature_sensor install/enable/get_celsius), a CRC32 (esp_rom_crc32_le, no new dependency) over a live 256 KiB PSRAM buffer and both heaps - PSRAM corruption and the temperature axis in one line. Verified live on device: TDIAG celsius=24.3..31.0 psram_crc stable psram_crc_bad=0. Drivers kept in .auto/exp21/ (boot_capture, heat, soak, soak_only, flash_boot_soak) plus three sdkconfig fragments.

THE BLOCKER, measured on two boards rather than quoted. Fresh configure with SPIRAM_SPEED_120M + ESPTOOLPY_FLASHFREQ_120M + FLASHMODE_QDO + IDF_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES plus IDF's documented mitigation SPIRAM_TIMING_TUNING_POINT_VIA_TEMPERATURE_SENSOR (+MEASURE_A_REALISTIC_POINT): PSRAM comes up normally (Found 16MB, Speed: 120MHz, SPI SRAM memory test OK, 16384K pool) and then the app aborts in secondary init - "E MSPI Timing: The flash model has not been verified support this feature, please contact espressif business support", "E cpu_start: init function 0x4037e958 has failed (0x106), aborting", abort() at PC 0x42002620, then Rebooting forever. 0x106 = ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED and addr2line names the function: __esp_system_init_fn_psram_adjust_timing_point_via_temperature at esp_hw_support/mspi_timing_tuning/port/esp32s3/mspi_timing_by_mspi_delay.c:882, called from do_system_init_fn (esp_system/startup.c:135). Reproduced on board 2 (build_r120, backtrace captured) and board 1 (build_safe, md5 a4b713ca: never reached EVT READY, 16 corrupt/rebooting lines in 120 s, zero bytes over a 10-minute load attempt). IDF itself refuses the temperature retune for this flash model and a refused init is fatal, so there is no bootable safe-120-MHz image to soak.

ECC, the other safety lever, does not fit either: SPIRAM_ECC_ENABLE on octal PSRAM leaves psram_free 697,476 where the same diagnostic build without ECC reported 1,789,984 at the same boot stage (~1.09 MB of parity) and with ECC the firmware printed ERR prefix_cache_allocation after priming. No room for ECC at this model/context size.

And a self-heating soak could not have covered the risk even if it booted: the die swings ~5 C under the ~40 s prefix priming (24.3 -> 31.0 C) while IDF's stated failure axis is a ~20 C swing from the power-on temperature in either direction - four times what this workload does to itself. Disposition: 80 MHz stays the production default on measured grounds; the +3.51 % stays a forbidden diagnostic; reopening needs a verified flash timing model from Espressif, which is exactly what the error text names as the gate.

FOUR HARNESS FACTS, each bought with board time: (1) idf.py -DCONFIG_X=y does NOT change a Kconfig value while esp32/sdkconfig exists - this cycle's first "ECC" and first "120 MHz" builds were silently still 80 MHz with ECC off, telltale "Boot SPI Speed : 80MHz"; the supported route is sdkconfig.defaults + delete sdkconfig + fresh -B, then verify in the generated sdkconfig. (2) /dev/ttyACM0 and /dev/ttyACM1 are BOARD 1's aliases: three concurrent "board" runs using them all drove one chip while two reported port busy; the pool gives per-board nodes only via $FLASH_PORT/$SERIAL_PORT, and the exp21 scripts now refuse to run unless those name the requested board. (3) Reset with the console CLOSED or the strap is sampled wrong and the chip sits in boot:0x0 DOWNLOAD(USB/UART0) forever. (4) A board that booted minutes earlier delivers NOTHING to a console attached later unless DTR is asserted, and serial_api.Device's !think-ack attach is the only reliable driver - a hand-rolled !status gate never got an answer. Pool restored: worker sdkconfig.defaults clean, esp32/main at HEAD, board 1 rebuilt at the shipping config (assertions default, no 120M) and reflashed (2a9c7d05), board 2 clean at HEAD.
