description: Experiment 22 - handwritten 4-bit phi kernel, SCREENED on device: the campaign's first above-bar speed candidate since #291. No shipping inference change yet, so decode_tps is the accepted 5.0117 carried forward (no board ran the shipping image this cycle; the exit-42 guard forbids a control-only run and there was no shipping candidate to batch). RESULT: a handwritten CQ 4-bit row walker that changes only STRUCTURE (one function per row instead of a call per group) and uses ordinary lsi loads is BIT-EXACT against the shipping nd_cq_gemv_rows on real needle3.cact bytes (0 mismatched rows of 128; known-answer probe exact 64.000000) and 11.6 % faster: 5.647 vs 6.338 cycles/weight, min of 25 rounds, CCOUNT calibrated 24000, board 2, on all three real phi tensors 223/224/225 (+11.58/+10.93/+10.9 %). phi's GEMVs are 9.2 ms of a ~200 ms token, so ~1.07 ms/token = +0.53 % decode - above the 0.2 % keep bar and above run #141's analytic +0.5 % ceiling. WHY IT WINS: in the shipping build dot_group is a real function call per group (symbol 0x4037bba8, not inlined), so the C path pays call overhead plus a per-group fp16 norm conversion across the boundary 24 times per row, while the asm keeps all 24 groups in registers inside one loop instruction. That retires run #295's "do not write the phi assembly" closure: its 9.3-10 % operand-DELIVERY ceiling and #141's instruction counts are both real, and neither is where this win comes from - call/inline structure is a third category, bigger than the two the closure considered. A ceiling measured inside one category is not a ceiling on the phase. THE TIE WIDE-FLOAT LOADS ARE NOT THE WIN AND THEIR NUMBERS ARE INVALID: ee.ldf.128.ip measured 4.774 cyc/weight (+25 %) and ee.ldf.64.ip 5.023 (+21 %), but both FAIL the known-answer probe (63.0 where the answer is exactly 64.0) - one of the eight floats per index word is not the value asked for, so those kernels are fast because they drop a term. Do not use either until the fill order of the instruction's register list is determined; the 63/64 signature says exactly one contribution per word, i.e. register order or a stale register, not the load itself. TWO ABI FACTS, paid with four boot-looping harvests: (1) a C float return value arrives in the INTEGER return register - GCC's own float epilogue is ssi f0,a1,0 / l32i.n a2,a1,0 - so an asm kernel ending in mov.s f0,f13; retw hands the caller a stale float, symptom: ONE IDENTICAL WRONG VALUE FROM THREE DIFFERENT KERNELS independent of inputs (fix: ssi f0,a1,16 + l32i a2,a1,16); (2) addx4 ar,as,at means ar=(as<<2)+at with the DESTINATION FIRST, as lut2_tie728.S already writes it - addx4 idx,base,idx silently computes (base<<2)+idx, which on device was LoadProhibited at EXCVADDR 0xf40c03d4 = (0x3d0300f4<<2)+4, and that arithmetic confirmed the semantics. Method finding worth more than either fact: the real-fixture diff only said "all rows differ", while a known-answer probe on hand-computable inputs (cb[i]=i, row 0x10 bytes, xh=1.0, norm 0x3C00, one group -> exactly 64.0) localised which stage was wrong in ONE build. Rule for this repo's asm screens: ship a known-answer probe in the same kbench run as the differential, not instead of it. SHIPPING IMPACT SO FAR NONE, AND PROVEN NONE: the screen lives in esp32/main/dot4_tie728.S plus the if(NEEDLE_KBENCH) branch of esp32/main/CMakeLists.txt; same-checkout A/B (fresh build_s1 with the change, fresh build_s2 without) both 281,072 bytes with 68 differing bytes in 4 regions = header stamps 0x74-0x77, the 32-byte build id 0xb0-0xcf, MD5 footer 0x449cf-0x449ef - nothing but build identity, the run #330 pattern. Pool/tree: board 2 restored to HEAD (kbench.c/CMakeLists restored, dot4 file removed from the worker), board 1 at the shipping config from #331. Kept rather than discarded so the kbench-gated screen and its CMake gate survive; the accepted image is unchanged.

asi.abi_fact_float_return: a C float return arrives in the INTEGER return register (GCC epilogue: ssi f0,a1,0 / l32i.n a2,a1,0). Leaving the result in f0 gave three different asm kernels ONE identical input-independent wrong value.

description: Experiment 22A - integrated plain-load CQ 4-bit (mHC phi) row walker: MEASURED and KEPT, +0.365 % decode (5.0117 -> 5.0300, now +106.1 % over the 2.44 baseline). engine/src/gemv4_tie728.S replaces the per-group dot_group CALL walk in nd_cq_gemv_rows for 4-bit / group-128 tensors with ordinary fp16 norms (gate nd_gemv4_asm_ok, cached per blob+rows, C path kept as fallback, row split via nd_parallel_rows unchanged). Canonical board-1 run at the shipping config: decode 5.0300, extended 4.956 (+0.34 %), prefill 5.3067 (+0.38 %), think 3.94 (+0.26 %), boot bench 5.076 / 197 ms per token (from 5.057 / 198 - the bench moved, which is the mechanism check because phi is inside it), min_case 4.80 (best worst case seen), 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact with golden_missing=0 and DEVICE_GATE_OK, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 IDENTICAL to the control, top1 10/10, checks green. Cost internal_free 15,215 -> 14,903 (-312 B of IRAM text, the #292 heap coupling), psram unchanged. app_md5 f1fde82570d0, engine_md5 4ef369a806b3. Realisation 69 % of the isolated +11.6 % / +0.53 % prediction, in this campaign's measured band. TWO FAILED ATTEMPTS ARE RECORDED SEPARATELY, because both are findings. (1) ATTEMPT 1 was a NULL, not a result: I saved the forced-inline variant with `git diff` + `git checkout engine/src/nd_quant.c` and forgot to re-apply, so the shipping C wiring was missing while the .S still compiled and the CMake define was present. The linker GC'd the unreferenced kernel (nm showed NO nd_gemv4_rows_tie1), so that run re-measured the accepted runtime - 5.0117 and internal_free 15,215 to the digit - and the exit-42 anti-repeat guard did NOT catch it, because the extra object file changes the shipping signature. Loophole recorded: the signature catches config drift, not an unreferenced new file; the cheap guard is to assert the candidate's new symbol is in the ELF before believing the number. (2) ATTEMPT 2 was the first real build and it DIVERGED: device_output_exact=5/17, device_token_delta=175, DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED, exit 1, while being faster (5.0283) - the row-range kernel advanced its packed and norm cursors TWICE per row (the word loop already consumes a whole row: 4 B per index word = 64 B per group, 2 B per group, so both cursors land exactly on the next row when the groups run out) and the row epilogue then added rowbytes and normstep again, skipping every row after the first. The isolation screen could not see this: it called the kernel once per row, where the CALLER did that stepping. Fix = delete the two epilogue advances (documented in the .S at the site), and the correct primitive test is a multi-row differential (row-range kernel vs per-row calls), banked in .auto/ideas.md. THIS IS THE DEVICE BYTE-EXACT GATE (#298) CATCHING ITS FIRST REAL CANDIDATE: the fast-but-wrong build could not be logged as a win, and no host gate could have seen it (x86 uses the C path). LANES B AND C (owner directive: three independent lanes, pinned 5.0117 baseline, no live control; measured in the same window). 22B forced-inline C dot_group (board 2): +0.10 % decode (5.0167), extended 4.946, prefill 5.2917, think 3.94, 17/17 byte-exact, and -1,024 B of internal heap - below the bar and inside the 0.071 % three-board spread, so not confirmable and not kept; it is also the free control on mechanism: removing the same call in C buys +0.10 % end to end, so the asm's win is the whole schedule (loop + all partials in registers + the norm converted once inside), not call overhead alone. 22C wide-load fill-order probe (board 3, kbench): the ee.ldf question is ANSWERED and closed - on the two hand-computable probes (A: nibble k = k, xh[j] = 2^(j%8), cb[i] = i, expected 24608 exactly; B: all nibbles 1, cb = 1, expected 4080, permutation-invariant) the plain-load kernel is EXACT on both (A 24608.0, B 4080.0), while ee.ldf.128.ip and ee.ldf.64.ip return 4080 for A, i.e. exactly the all-one-nibble answer: with distinct nibbles they collapse to one codebook operand, so the +21/+25 % was never a permuted register list that a reorder could fix, it was lost nibble identity. The extra ~10 % above the plain form is not available this way. HARNESS, cost four dead board lanes: measure.sh died with rc=1 and a ZERO-BYTE log on a freshly synced checkout because its anti-repeat guard ended with `[ -f esp32/sdkconfig ] && sha256sum ...` inside a command substitution under `set -euo pipefail` - sdkconfig does not exist yet there (gitignored, generated by the build), so the pipeline failed and killed the run before it printed anything; fixed with if/fi plus `true` inside the hashed group (hash content unchanged) and the reason is now a comment. Also: tmux windows must run `needle-board run N -- bash .auto/measure.sh` INSIDE the window (the wrapper sets NEEDLE_BOARD/FLASH_PORT/SERIAL_PORT and takes the lock) - a direct call silently used board 1's ports and lock and died with 'Board 1 is busy'. Encoding rule added to .auto/lanes.sh, which now fails if the candidate is not visibly in the tree.

description: Experiment 22A cross-board confirmation + capture cadence, not a new candidate: the accepted runtime (run #333's integrated plain-load CQ 4-bit row walker, commit 0cbc742) measured on a SECOND board and the repo behavioural suite re-run on the shipping image. Board 2 ran the same shipping tree/config through the pool wrapper (`bash .auto/measure.sh` inside `needle-board run 2`, batch 20260922T2135L - logged here rather than through run_experiment because the campaign's run_experiment is bound to board 1/main and this measurement had to be on another board by the owner's cross-board-confirmation protocol). CROSS-BOARD RESULT: decode 5.0283 on board 2 against the pinned accepted baseline 5.0117 = +0.33 %, and against board 1's 5.0300 = -0.03 %, i.e. two boards agree to 0.03 % (five times the campaign's measured 0.071 % board spread is the discovery threshold; the agreement itself is inside it). Monitors identical: extended 4.956, think 3.94, boot bench 5.075, internal_free 14,903 (the same -312 B as board 1), psram_free 2,052,252, device_output_exact 17/17, device_golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, DEVICE_GATE_OK. So the +0.365 % is not board identity and not prompt-specific: it is promoted from discovery to confirmed, and the accepted runtime stays 5.0300 (board 1's canonical reading, the campaign's standard board). ALSO CLOSED THIS ITERATION, the cadence the campaign owes when shipping code changes: `make capture` rc=0 on this exact image with all NINE behavioural flags true (routes_match, tools_match, requests_succeeded, no_external_calls, local_has_two_passes, external_stops_at_selection, telemetry_progressed, sampling_interval_applied, timer_expired) across seven real end-to-end scenarios (translation routed externally, status/sampling/timer/batch executed locally). description: Experiment 22D-lane-A, forced-inline sigmoidf_pair: MEASURED, +0.13 % decode on board 1 (5.0367 vs the accepted 5.0300) and +0.17 % on board 2 in the crossover (5.0367 there vs 5.0283) - BELOW the 0.2 % keep bar and the more expensive of the two variants tested against it (-1,792 B of internal heap), so not kept. Hypothesis was sound and came straight out of run #333's finding: `static inline` is a request, not a decision - GCC kept sigmoidf_pair as a real function at 0x4200ceb4, which is FLASH-mapped, while its two hot callers silu_rows (0x4037c3a4) and agate_rows (0x4037c358) are in IRAM, so the Monarch MLP's gated stage and the attention output gate paid an IRAM-to-flash call per element pair, ~3,600 times per token. Forcing always_inline removes it. Bit-exact by construction (inlining changes no operation, no argument, no order): 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, DEVICE_GATE_OK, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical to the control, top1 10/10. Every monitor moved with the primary, including the boot bench (5.085 vs 5.076), which is the mechanism check because SiLU is inside the bench: extended 4.966 (+0.20 %), prefill 5.3167 (+0.19 %), think 3.94, min_case 4.81 (best worst case seen so far). The reason it is discarded rather than kept is the bar: +0.13 % on the canonical board, +0.17 % on the crossover board, mean +0.15 % - genuinely below 0.2 % on a metric whose per-variant spread is zero, not a noisy near-miss. The sibling lane (22D-B, ND_HOT on the same function, keeping the call but moving the callee into IRAM) measured BETTER on both boards (+0.165 % and +0.20 %) for half the RAM (-768 B), which is the informative result: this phase's cost was the flash crossing, not the call itself. Both variants are reverted; see 22D-B's own log line for the 2x2 table.

asi.2x2_cross_board_table: accepted 5.0300 (b1) / 5.0283 (b2); D1 always_inline 5.0367 (b1) AND 5.0367 (b2); D2 ND_HOT 5.0383 (b1) AND 5.0383 (b2). Each variant reads the same value on both boards, so per-variant board spread is ZERO and a +0.13 % delta is a measurement, not noise - but it is still below the bar.

description: Experiment 22D-lane-B, ND_HOT on sigmoidf_pair (keep the call, move the callee out of flash): MEASURED on two boards with a full crossover, +0.165 % decode on the canonical board 1 (5.0383 vs the accepted 5.0300) and +0.20 % on board 2 (5.0383 vs that board's 5.0283 accepted reading) - the better of the two variants tested (half the RAM cost of forced-inline: -768 B vs -1,792 B, and faster on both boards) but still under the 0.2 % keep bar on the canonical board, so NOT kept, and this is the campaign's best sub-bar candidate on record. THE 2x2 TABLE IS THE REAL RESULT, and it is the cleanest measurement-integrity result this campaign has: each variant reads the SAME decode on BOTH boards - accepted 5.0300/5.0283, D1 always_inline 5.0367/5.0367, D2 ND_HOT 5.0383/5.0383. Per-variant board spread is ZERO, so a +0.165 % delta is a measurement rather than a coin flip; what stops it being kept is the bar, not the evidence. Mechanism, measured rather than assumed: GCC kept `static inline` sigmoidf_pair out of line at 0x4200ceb4 (FLASH-mapped) while its two hot callers silu_rows (0x4037c3a4) and agate_rows (0x4037c358) sit in IRAM, so ~3,600 element pairs per token paid an IRAM-to-flash call. D1 deleted the call (+0.15 % mean, -1,792 B); D2 only moved the callee into IRAM and did BETTER (+0.18 % mean, -768 B). That ordering is the finding: for this phase the cost was the flash crossing (instruction-cache/fetch across the memory boundary), not the call-and-return itself - which is the opposite of what the run #333 phi result implied, where removing the call was worth +0.365 % because the callee's whole schedule also changed. Quality never at risk: 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, DEVICE_GATE_OK, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical to the control, top1 10/10, and every monitor moved with the primary: extended 4.966 (+0.20 %), prefill 5.3167 (+0.19 %), boot bench 5.086 (from 5.076 - the mechanism check, SiLU is inside the bench), min_case 4.81, think 3.94. BOTH 22D variants are reverted; the exact one-line change is kept as .auto/exp22/d1-always-inline.patch and the ND_HOT form is a single sed, so re-applying D2 is one command if the owner ever sets the bar at 0.15 % or wants +0.17 % for 768 B of internal heap.

Re-apply: sed -i 's/^static inline void sigmoidf_pair/static ND_HOT inline void sigmoidf_pair/' engine/src/nd_model.c. First retry if the keep bar ever moves to 0.15 %.

Both 22D variants beat that and are CALLEE placements, so the placement family is closed only for hot callers and OPEN for flash-mapped callees that hot IRAM loops call.

description: Diagnostic iteration: phase map re-derived after the phi asm landed (board 3, profiled image) + a callee/divide audit of the accepted ELF that found the campaign's biggest remaining lever, and it is not a kernel. decode_tps here is the ACCEPTED 5.0300 CARRIED FORWARD (no shipping change; the only image built was the ND_PROFILE diagnostic on board 3, which reads 5.0200 because the timers cost ~0.2 % - labelled, not passed off as a speed result). PHASE MAP (ms/token, boot bench 197 ms/token, board 3, batch 20260922T2250L): attn-stage 99.9, proj2bit 86.2, attention heads 35.3, hadamard 24.4, engram 16.4, mhc_phi4 12.6, mhc-mix 4.7, sinkhorn 3.8, prep+lut 3.6, step-tail 0.5, rope 0.2, logits4/confpool/sample 0.0 (bench never samples). Against the pre-#333 map, mhc_phi4 fell 13.5 -> 12.6 ms, i.e. its GEMV share fell 9.2 -> ~8.3 ms, which is exactly what run #333's +1.07 ms/token prediction said, and everything else is unchanged to 0.1 ms - so the ranking of what is left is confirmed rather than assumed: 2-bit GEMV at its instruction floor, attention stage, MLP, engram. THE AUDIT, which is the finding. I asked the question #232 did not: #232 audited which hot CALLERS sit in flash and found the loops already resident (+0.067 %, rejected); run #335/#336 showed CALLEE placement is a different and larger thing (+0.15-0.20 % per site). Resolving every indirect call in the accepted image against IDF's own esp_rom/esp32s3 symbol maps gives the answer: attn_heads' nine callx8 sites are ROM memcpy x7, memset x1 and __divsf3 x1 - and `div.s` occurs ZERO times in the entire image. This core has NO hardware single-precision divide: every '/' in the model is a call to the ROM software divider. Counting the sites against the C source: sigmoidf_pair carries TWO divisions per pair (nd_model.c:72-76, 1/(1+e) and e/(1+e)) at ~3,600 pairs/token = ~7,200 divides, plus rms_unit/zcrms_head_rows at three in-loop sites each (line 132/159/184, 1/sqrtf(ss/n+eps), and sqrtf itself calls __divsf3), plus pool (826), prepare, kv_store. Order 8-10k software divides per token. At even 150 cycles each that is ~1.3 M cycles = 5.4 ms = 2.7 % of the token, and unlike every other remaining idea, replacing it is bit-exact BY DEFINITION: IEEE correctly-rounded division has exactly one correct answer, so a faster divider that is correctly rounded produces identical bits everywhere, and the byte-exact gate is satisfied by the algorithm rather than by luck. Design that keeps the risk near zero: fast path = TIE recip0.s approximation + two Newton refinements (each doubles precision) + one Markstein correction step to recover correct rounding, all in hardware mul.s/fma.s, guarded to ordinary normal operands; anything else (subnormal in/out, exponent extremes, zero/inf/NaN) falls to a plain exact shift-subtract implementation ~30 lines of C. Verifiable exhaustively on the host, where the hardware divider IS correctly rounded: the candidate written in C with __builtin_fmaf can be diffed bit-for-bit against the host's own division over tens of millions of random pairs drawn from the model's REAL operand distributions (captured the way Experiment 12 captured its pairs) plus every edge class. NEXT: implement + host-verify, then kbench ROM divide vs candidate on real captured operands, then a three-lane batch. This is the first candidate since the phi asm that is priced above 1 % rather than above 0.2 %.

asi.divide_audit: div.s appears 0 times in the accepted image; all fp division goes to ROM __divsf3 (0x40002274). Call sites by function: sigmoidf_pair 4 (2 per pair x ~3,600 pairs/token), zcrms_head_rows 3 in-loop, rms_unit 3 in-loop, kv_store_int8 2, attn_heads 1, nd_cq_prepare 1, pool_cell 1, sqrtf 1. Estimated 8-10k divides/token.

Profiled image reads 5.0200 because timers cost ~0.2 %.
asi.next: implement a correctly-rounded fp32 divide (recip0.s + 2 Newton + Markstein correction, exact shift-subtract fallback for edge classes), verify bit-for-bit on the host against the host's own correctly-rounded division over the model's real captured operands plus edge classes, then kbench vs ROM __divsf3, then three lanes.
asi.rom_call_sites: attn_heads indirect calls = ROM memcpy x7, memset x1, __divsf3 x1 - i.e. the staging copies are ROM calls, which is a separate (much smaller) class: ~112 memcpys/token, sub-0.05 %.
asi.hypothesis: Nothing speed-side was testable on the accepted tree; instead re-measure the phase map after the phi asm and audit which flash/ROM callees the hot IRAM loops still call. The audit found NO remaining callee-placement win (22D was the last of its class) but found a much larger one: the core has no hardware fp divide.

description: Experiment 23 - correctly-rounded reciprocal-refinement division replacing the ROM software divider: MEASURED, REJECTED, and the premise is retired with numbers. Triggered by run #337's audit fact that the accepted image contains ZERO div.s instructions, so ~8-10k divisions per decode token (two per sigmoid pair alone) call the ROM __divsf3 at 0x40002274 - which looked like several percent of the token, and looked admissible because IEEE-754 division is *specified* correctly rounded, so a faster correctly-rounded divider returns identical bits. Implementation: engine/include/nd_div.h (kept in .auto/divf3/) - magic-subtract inverse, three Newton refinements via hardware fma, one quotient multiply, exact residual, Markstein correction, behind an integer-only guard (both operands normal, quotient exponent inside the normal range); everything else falls through to `a / b`, i.e. the division the build already does, so subnormals/zeros/infinities/NaN payloads keep their current implementation bit-for-bit. QUALITY WAS NEVER IN DOUBT and was proven twice over before any board time: (1) .auto/divf3/test_div.c now INCLUDES THE SHIPPING HEADER (not a copy of it) and compared bit-for-bit against the host's correctly-rounded hardware divider - 1,572,864 pairs over six classes (model-shaped sigmoid 1/(1+e) and e/(1+e), RMS 1/(ss/n+eps), uniform exponents, small integers, exponent extremes, and a special-value class of +-0/inf/NaN/subnormal/denormal-limit pairs) with 0 mismatches; the guard is what made the two hard classes pass: without it the fast path returned -NaN where the answer is -inf on an overflow pair; (2) the real pipeline on the host with all 15 engine division sites converted: host_output_exact=16/16, host_golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 IDENTICAL to the control, top1 10/10, and on device 17/17 byte-exact with DEVICE_GATE_OK and token_delta 0. So this is a pure speed verdict. DEVICE: decode 5.0017 against the accepted 5.0300 = -0.56 %, with every monitor moving together (extended 4.929, prefill 5.2733, think 3.92, boot bench 5.045 down from 5.076 - the bench moving is the mechanism check, and it moved the wrong way), internal_free 14,391 (-512 B from inlined expansions in IRAM-resident callers). THE KBOOTCH THAT KILLED IT (board 2, kbench, min of 25 rounds over 256 rotated real-shaped operand pairs, results consumed through a float register barrier, both variants reached through a noinline function so call overhead cancels): rom_divsf3 = 7.95 cycles per divide, newton_markstein = 30.92, a bare multiply as the loop floor = 2.92, and bit_mismatch = 0 over all 256 pairs - so the algorithm is exactly as correct on the target as on the host, and 3.9x slower. PREDICTION AND RESULT AGREE: 10k divisions x (30.92 - 7.95) = 230k cycles = 0.96 ms of a 198 ms token = -0.49 % predicted against -0.56 % measured. THE FINDING IS ABOUT ROM, not about my code: Espressif's ROM __divsf3 costs about 5 cycles net of call and loop overhead, which a shift-subtract divider cannot do and a hand-written TIE reciprocal-refinement can - the ROM authors almost certainly did exactly what I wrote, in assembly, without the float-to-integer round trips that `nd_f2u`/`nd_u2f` need on this core (runs #230/#292's measured fact that float/int transfers go through memory, which is also why the C version paid 31 cycles for ~12 FP ops). Ceiling on any future handwritten divider: 7.95 - 2.92(mul floor) = ~5 cycles per divide, across ~10k divides = 0.2 ms = +0.1 % of the token, i.e. below the keep bar before any risk is even considered. Division is therefore NOT a lever on this target and the observation "there is no div.s" is harmless: the software divider is already at the FMA-chain floor. Engine changes reverted; the bench (bench_div in esp32/main/kbench.c, kbench-gated so it cannot affect a shipping image, kept in .auto/divf3/kbench.c.with_div_bench) and the verified header stay in .auto so nobody re-derives this.

asi.ceiling: any handwritten divide can save at most ~5 cycles/divide (7.95 - 2.92 loop floor) x ~10k divides = 0.2 ms = +0.1 % of the token -> below the keep bar. Division family CLOSED on measurement.
asi.correctness: bit-exact proven twice: host test over 1,572,864 pairs in 6 classes with 0 mismatches (compiling the SHIPPING header), device kbench bit_mismatch=0 on 256 real-shaped pairs, and full byte-exact goldens on host (16/16) and device (17/17) with fidelity 5.341e-05 unchanged. This was never a quality question.
asi.kbench_numbers: rom_divsf3 7.95 cyc/div, newton_markstein 30.92 cyc/div, mul_floor 2.92 cyc/div (min of 25 rounds, 256 rotated pairs, float-register barrier).

My C version pays for float<->integer transfers (nd_f2u/nd_u2f = memory round trips, the #230/#292 measured fact) and 12 dependent FP ops.

Board ports come from the wrapper: /dev/needle-pi/boardN-{flash,console}.

description: Experiment 24 screen - put the subset-logits gather on the shipped TIE728 2-bit kernel: MEASURED IN ISOLATION at +97.7 %, and BLOCKED on a named exactness question, so nothing shipped (decode_tps is the ACCEPTED 5.0300 CARRIED FORWARD; the only image built was a kbench diagnostic on board 3, which by design never runs the request path - labelled, not a speed result). HYPOTHESIS, from the phase map rather than the backlog: the constrained sampler's dominant cost is nd_model_logits_subset, 5.7 ms of a real request token (2.8 %, measured in run #166 and invisible to the boot bench). It prepares the activation once and projects ~1.3k grammar-legal embedding rows through nd_cq_gemv_gather -> gather_rows, which walks each row in C with a dot_group CALL PER GROUP - the exact structural cost run #333 just proved is worth +0.365 % on the 4-bit phi path. The dense 2-bit projections never pay it: they use nd_lut2_rows_tie1n, worth +13.45 % end to end over the C walker (run #204). The gather path missed the kernel only because the kernel walks a consecutive row range and a gather needs an id indirection - and the lazy integration needs NO assembly: call the existing kernel once per gathered row with r0=ids[i], r1=ids[i]+1 into a full-size scratch indexed by row id, then compact. DESIGN IS NOW WRITTEN (kept in the kbench bench_gather): the per-row calls go through nd_parallel_rows via a 4-line row function, so the two-core split is unchanged, and the only new per-token cost is one nd_cq_lut_build, measured at 32,345 cycles = 0.135 ms against a 5.7 ms phase. SCREEN (board 3, real archive bytes, real prepared activation, 512 spread ids of the size the real grammar admits, min of 5 rounds): C gather with dot_group-per-group = 5,089.50 cycles/row; lut2 asm one-call-per-row + compaction = 2,574.61 cycles/row = **+97.68 %**. Applied to 5.7 ms that is ~2.8 ms = **+1.4 % of the request token**, which would be the largest single candidate since the phi asm - if it is bit-exact. IT IS NOT, on synthetic data: the same bench compared the two paths row-for-row and got **mismatch = 417 of 512**, first at i=1 with ref=-87.5963516 against got=-87.596344, i.e. one-ULP-class differences in 81 % of rows, not garbage. That is the signature of a different accumulation ORDER, not a wrong operand: the pair-LUT kernel sums precomputed cb*xh table entries, the gather walk sums cb[k]*xh[j] products in dot_group's order, and the two orders are not identical. WHY THE CAMPAIGN COULD STILL THINK THEY WERE EQUAL, stated precisely because it changes what to test next: the dense 2-bit path has used the pair-LUT since before this campaign's first baseline, so its byte-exact goldens prove 'the model's outputs equal the LUT path', never 'the LUT path equals the dot_group walk'. Nothing in the tree ever compared those two on the SAME data, which is exactly what a gather needs. THE DECISIVE CHEAP TEST, banked as the next step: capture a real fixture from the host engine (which runs the same code) - the embedding's prepared activation, the ids list, and the shipped gather's outputs from a real decode step - then replay it on the host, where the C pair-LUT walker (nd_lut2_rows_c) is compilable without any assembly, and diff it row-for-row against nd_cq_gemv_gather. If they agree on real data (and the reason they disagree on mine is that my synthetic activation has a dynamic range the model's FWHT-prepared activations do not), the candidate is worth ~+1.4 % and gets a three-lane batch. If they disagree, this whole idea closes for the price of one host replay, and the campaign keeps a newly-verified fact: pair-LUT and dot_group are NOT interchangeable primitives. BENCH ASSET KEPT: bench_div (run #338's divide screen) and bench_gather both live in esp32/main/kbench.c behind NEEDLE_KBENCH, which cannot appear in a shipping configure; raw device output in /root/board-pool/batches/20260922T2358L/board3.kbgather.txt.

description: Experiment 25B - embedding reads through the PSRAM tier instead of mmap'd flash: MEASURED, EXACTLY NEUTRAL, reverted - and it converts run #206's inference into measured fact. FOUND BY run #340: nd_model_logits_subset, nd_model_logits_all and the per-token nd_cq_dequant_row passed nd_cact_data(&m->c,&m->embedding) = the mmap'd FLASH pointer, while every dense projection passes nd_tier_ptr(m,t) = the 12 MB staged PSRAM copy that run #206 measured to cover the embedding (in_span=1, content 7,848,512 B). So ~512 scattered 4-bit rows per constrained token, and all 8192 (6.29 MB) per think token, came from flash while an identical copy sat in PSRAM. CHANGE: one line per site, bit-exact by construction (identical bytes; host build has no tier so the host path is literally unchanged - 16/16 byte-exact, fidelity 5.341e-05 unchanged). VERDICT: decode 5.0317 = +0.034 %, the same single tick as run #340, all 17 per-case values identical between the two runs, image md5 different so both really built and flashed (the campaign's known determinism, not a stale image). The decisive monitor is think_tps, which reads the whole embedding every token: 3.94 -> 3.94, literally zero movement; prefill 5.3117, extended 4.961, boot bench 5.079, min_case 4.81 all unchanged to the tick; 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, top1 10/10, internal_free 14,903, psram_free 2,052,252. WHY IT MATTERS: run #206 widened the tier to cover the embedding, measured think unchanged, and concluded scattered rows are access-pattern-limited rather than address-space-limited - but that run could not have moved because the code never asked for the tier. This run did ask and got zero, so the conclusion is now measured rather than inferred: on ESP32-S3 a scattered cache-line fill costs the same from mmap'd flash as from PSRAM, and the tier's documented +1.5 % belongs to big sequential streams only. Sampler-gather delivery is therefore unbuyable three ways: residency (this run, +0.03 %), DMA prefetch (#287, -17.9 %), external clock (#289, forbidden by the documented maxima). NEXT is structural, not memory-side: measure the real per-step candidate count n and take the singleton case for free - when the grammar admits exactly one legal candidate, return it without preparing or projecting anything, bit-exact because the argmax of a singleton is its own element.

Same bytes, different backing store, bit-exact by construction: 17/17 device + 16/16 host byte-exact, golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, memory unchanged.
asi.found_by: run #340's null: the gather passed nd_cact_data() while every dense projection passed nd_tier_ptr().

Identical bytes already resident in PSRAM - 6.29 MB/token for think, ~0.2 MB/token for the constrained gather - so one line per site.

asi.not_this: Not evidence the tier is worthless for the dense sequential streams it was built for (+1.5 %, run #206 family, unchanged). It says PSRAM residency cannot buy scattered row reads.
asi.reinterpretation: Run #206 widened the tier span to cover the embedding, measured think_tps unchanged, and inferred 'scattered rows are limited by the access pattern, not the address space'. That run structurally could not have moved, because the code never asked for the tier. This run did ask and got exactly zero, so the inference is now a measured fact: a scattered cache-line fill costs the same from mmap'd flash as from PSRAM on this part.
asi.result: think_tps 3.94 -> 3.94 - EXACTLY ZERO on the path that reads the entire embedding every token. prefill 5.3117 -> 5.3117, extended 4.961 -> 4.961, boot bench 5.079 -> 5.079. Below the 0.2 % bar -> discarded and reverted.
asi.why_340_underdelivered: the same arithmetic also explains run #340: if the real per-step n is well below the 512 cap, the gather is a couple of ms rather than 5.7, and a +7.68 % schedule win on it is ~+0.1 %.

description: Measurement-authority iteration - the free variable behind two nulls, measured on the host for the price of one build (no board time; decode_tps is the accepted 5.0300 carried forward from run #333 because the shipping tree is byte-identical to it). WHAT WAS MEASURED: the real candidate-set size n that nd_model_logits_subset projects per decode step, counted inside nd_sample_hidden under a define, over three real prompts through the host engine (which runs the same code and reproduces the goldens byte-exact, so its distribution is the device's). Result: mean_n = 6.8 rows per token. Distribution over 25 sampled steps of two prompts: n==1 in 3, 2..3 in 11, 4..7 in 8, 8..15 in 2, one step in 64..512 (the first constrained step, max_n=68), and never above the 512 cap that would take the full-vocabulary path. WHY THAT MATTERS: run #166's request-path map attributed 5.7 ms/token to this projection, and runs #340 (handwritten 4-bit kernel per gathered row, +7.68 % measured in isolation) and #341 (PSRAM tier for the embedding reads) were both priced from that figure and both measured +0.03 %. At n~7 the projection is ~20k cycles two-core = 0.08 ms, so +7.68 % of it is +0.003 % - the two nulls are now explained quantitatively rather than suspiciously, and run #166's 5.7 ms must be read as overhead bracketed by ND_P_LOGITS (the once-per-token prepare, timer placement), not as a projection budget. The sampler family is therefore closed at an order of magnitude smaller scale than the ledger believed: everything that scales with n - the candidate projection, the per-candidate token_ok byte walk, the piece lookups - is bounded by n~7, while what scales with the vocabulary was already reduced by run #288's first-byte index to a median of ~51 visited ids. CANDIDATE KILLED WITHOUT BUILDING IT: the singleton shortcut (when the grammar admits exactly one legal id, return it without preparing or projecting anything - bit-exact because the argmax of a singleton is its own element) would have been 3 lines and is worth ~one row, ~0.01 ms, even at its 12 % hit rate. The distribution killed it for one host build instead of one device run. HARNESS FACT for the campaign's own tooling, and it belongs to the vacuous-pass family this session keeps finding: both counters I wrote printed on a 250-step cadence while a real nd_dump generation is 23-35 steps, so 'no output' looked like 'the instrumented code never runs' when it was a threshold no real process ever reaches (this is what made run #340's differential probe look dead before the unconditional print showed the embedding is 4-bit); and .auto/bench.py captures the generator's stdout, so engine-side printf diagnostics never appear in its log - run host/build/nd_dump directly to see them. Tree is back to the accepted runtime: engine/src/nd_sample.c reverted, host build reconfigured with no extra flags, host_output_exact=16 with token_delta 0 re-verified afterwards.

The singleton shortcut I was about to build (return cand[0] when the grammar admits exactly one legal token, bit-exact because the argmax of a singleton is its own element) was killed off-device by the measured n distribution: at a 12 % hit rate and n=1 it saves ONE projected row = ~0.01 ms, i.e. +0.005 %. Building it would have spent a board on noise.
asi.hypothesis: Runs #340 and #341 both measured +0.03 % against a screen that priced +7.68 % of a 5.7 ms phase. The arithmetic only fits one unmeasured variable: the real candidate count n per decode step, which the sampler caps at 512 and which run #166's phase budget implicitly assumed was near the cap.
asi.metric_provenance: No device run this iteration: the accepted runtime's tree is unchanged (engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ diff = 0 lines against run #333's accepted image), so decode_tps is 5.0300 by construction and the secondaries are #333's canonical values carried forward and labelled (#299/#300 convention). The measurement this iteration is host-side: the engine runs the same code and produced byte-identical generations (host_output_exact=16, token_delta=0) with the counter build, so its n distribution is the device's.
asi.method: Measure the free variable before pricing the lever. Two consecutive nulls were priced off a phase estimate inherited from a profile that structurally could not separate the once-per-token prepare from the n-proportional rows.
asi.next_action_hint: The request-path-only time (bench 5.076 vs primary 5.0300, ~2 %) is now unattributed: with the projection at 0.08 ms it is not the sampler's arithmetic either (#288 left a median of ~51 visited ids). Harvest prof_dump on the CURRENT image for a tools request and a route request to find where the bench-invisible milliseconds actually are before writing another sampler or projection optimisation.
asi.not_this: Not a criticism of run #166, which measured 5.7 ms honestly: ND_P_LOGITS brackets nd_cq_prepare plus the gather, and at n~7 whatever it measured is overhead around the call, not a projection budget.
asi.result: mean_n = 6.8 rows per token (buckets: n==1 in 3/25 steps, 2..3 in 11, 4..7 in 8, 8..15 in 2, one step at 68, none above 512). Seven 4-bit rows two-core is ~20k cycles = 0.08 ms, so +7.68 % of the gather is +0.003 % of the token - which is exactly the +0.03 % that #340 and #341 measured, once you add a tick of noise.

description:
Experiment 26 - request-path phase harvest with the candidate count measured on the same image: MEASURED, no shipping change (decode_tps is the accepted 5.0300 carried forward from run #333, secondaries carried forward from that canonical run on an identical shipping tree; the only image built was the ND_PROFILE diagnostic on board 3, whose timers cost ~0.2 %, so its 5.02 is labelled and is not a speed result). This is the harvest run #341's own `next:` asked for: "the request-path-only time (~2 %) is now unattributed ... harvest prof_dump on the CURRENT image for a tools request and a route request before writing another sampler or projection optimisation."

METHOD (two harness facts made this its own scripts, kept as .auto/prof_request.py + .auto/lane_prof.sh + .auto/prof_harvest.sh): measure.sh's log contains ONLY the boot-bench table, because serial_api.Device's complete() reads with _line_quiet() while the per-request EVT prof block is printed after EVT done - the request tables were being swallowed, not absent. The harvester attaches to an already-booted, already-primed board (no reflash, ~40 s), patches the reader to echo, and drives one tools and one route request through the real API call path. A candidate-count counter (kept as .auto/exp26/nstat.patch) went into the same image so n and the phase come from one boot.

TABLE (board 3, batch 20260923T0200L; ms per token, one dump per request):
  boot bench : whole block 158.7 (80.4 %), proj2bit 86.2, attn-stage 99.9, sample 0.0, logits4 0.0
  tools (27 tok, 5.08 tps): whole block 176.0 (89.4 %), proj2bit 99.0, attn-stage 108.4, prep+lut 4.1, sample 4.5, logits4 3.8 | cands steps=26 rows=174 mean_n=6.7 max_n=68
  route (14 tok, 4.79 tps): whole block 208.2 (99.8 %), proj2bit 110.8, attn-stage 132.5, prep+lut 4.6, sample 7.6, logits4 7.1 | cands steps=13 rows=45 mean_n=3.5 max_n=68

WHAT IT SETTLES. (1) The device agrees with the host: mean_n = 6.7 (tools) / 3.5 (route), max 68, so run #341's host counting IS the device distribution and the sampler's n-scaled work stays closed. (2) The projection cannot be worth 3.8 ms: at the cycles/row this campaign measured for that same tensor and kernel in kbench (2,885,800 cycles / 512 rows two-core = 5,636 wall cycles/row), 6.7 rows is 37.8k cycles = 0.16 ms, and one nd_cq_prepare is ~0.22 ms (this table's own prep+lut 3.6 ms over ~16 calls). So ~3.4 ms of a 3.8 ms bracket - 1.7 % of a request token - is inside nd_model_logits_subset and is neither the rows nor the prepare by this table's own numbers. That is now the largest unattributed block in the token and the only lead above the bar; .auto/exp26/split_lg4.py (written this cycle) prints prepare and gather separately per call to localise it, and either answer is actionable: if the gather owns it, the once-per-token nd_parallel_rows wake (tiny work, worker possibly blocked, 100 Hz tick) is the suspect and running <=N rows serially on one core is bit-exact by construction because per-row order does not move; if the prepare owns it, the 4-bit pad/FWHT path is. (3) Sampler work that is NOT the projection = sample - logits4 = 0.7 ms (tools) / 0.5 ms (route), independently reproducing run #149's ~0.4 ms for piece lookups and byte walks.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CLOSURE FOUND WHILE CHECKING THE ABOVE - it kills a banked +1.4 % candidate for the price of two geometry facts: run #339's screen (put the subset gather on the TIE728 pair-LUT kernel: +97.68 % in isolation, "worth ~+1.4 % if bit-exact") compared the gather against a kernel that CANNOT compute the same function on this tensor. The embedding is 4-bit (run #340's differential probe: dims 8192x768 bits=4 group=128) and the pair table stores 16 entries per pair slot, which is exactly the combination count of a 2-bit pair; a 4-bit pair has 16x16 = 256 combinations, so no pair-LUT of this shape represents a 4-bit row. #339's 417/512 one-ULP "mismatches" were therefore a wrong-function comparison, and the 4-bit gather's only kernel lever is the plain-load row walker that already shipped for phi (#333) - at n=6.7 rows/token that prices at ~0.02 ms = +0.01 %, under the bar twice over (by n and by the 11 % kernel delta). Gather delivery is now closed four independent ways: residency (#340), tier pointer (#341), n (#341), kernel bit-width (this run).

Tree after: engine/ esp32/ host/ tools/ model/ = 0 lines different from the accepted runtime (diagnostics reverted; two patches + three harvester scripts kept under .auto). Pool: board 3 free after its lane's cooldown; boards 1/2 untouched.

asi.lead: 3.4 ms/token (1.7 %) inside the ND_P_LOGITS bracket that is neither the rows (0.16 ms) nor the prepare (~0.22 ms) by this table's own numbers; localise with .auto/exp26/split_lg4.py
