description: DIAGNOSTIC ENTRY, no candidate decision and no speed claim (decode_tps is the accepted 5.0467 carried forward; nothing new measured): the transform half of Experiment 33 failed the device quality gate, and the reason is a bug in my integration, not in the measurement. Board 2 ran the integrated ee.ldf paired butterfly in nd_fwht and reported DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 4/17 with token_delta 257: tools cases collapsed to empty calls and the think case degraded to boilerplate. The kbench differential had said diff=0 because the bench's OWN copy of the loop handled the len==1 stage correctly, while the copy I pasted into engine/src/nd_quant.c replaced that entire stage (n/2 butterflies) with a single butterfly at x[0]/x[1] - for n=128 that drops 63 of 64 stage-1 butterflies. Fourth instance of this campaign's deadliest class (#333's multi-row cursor, #242's probe placed before the line it replaced, #359's macro never forwarded): a differential that tests a transcription instead of the shipping code proves the transcription correct. Rule now recorded at the site: differential the integrated function. Board 1 was running the same broken code as 'both' and was stopped once board 2's verdict arrived, so neither reading is used; its bench.py then looked stalled for 5 minutes, which was the 600 s request timeout against an image whose generation had collapsed - the CASE lines (tokens=2, calls_ok=0) are the tell. Fix applied: the len==1 stage now loops the whole stage, 16/16 repo tests green. Re-measuring in 20260923T1022L with a transform-only board so the fix's byte-exactness is judged directly.

asi.candidate: Experiment 33 integration, transform half as first written: the ee.ldf.64.ip/ee.stf.64.ip paired butterfly inside nd_fwht (board 2, batch 20260923T1015L, nd_quant.c md5 65e08acadacf). Board 1 was running the same code as 'both' and was stopped once board 2's verdict was in, so no reading from either board is used.
asi.hypothesis: lane 1 measured this exact butterfly form +36.75 % with diff=0 against the shipped nd_fwht on real geometry, so it should have been bit-exact in situ and worth +0.43 % decode.
asi.result: DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 4/17, device_token_delta=257, MEASURE rc=1. Tools-schema cases collapsed to empty calls (<tool_call>[]</tool_call>, tokens=2) and the think case degraded to repeated boilerplate - i.e. the activation transform was wrong, not marginally different.
asi.root_cause: The kbench differential passed because the bench's OWN copy of the butterfly loop handled the len==1 stage correctly (`if (len == 1u) { ... continue; }` inside the per-block loop, so all n/2 butterflies ran). The copy I pasted into engine/src/nd_quant.c replaced that whole stage with ONE butterfly at x[0]/x[1]. For n=128 that drops 63 of 64 stage-1 butterflies, which is exactly a model-quality change, and the byte-exact gate is what caught it.
asi.meta_lesson: Fourth instance of the same class in this campaign, and the costliest: #333's multi-row cursor (caller stepped what the kernel also stepped), #242's probe inserted before the line it replaced, #359's macro not forwarded to the compiler, and now a differential that tested a transcription instead of the shipping code. Rule, stated for whoever reads next: the differential must execute the integrated function - if the bench has its own copy of the body, the bench has only proved its own copy correct.
asi.stalled_bench_tell: Board 1's bench.py then sat with unchanged logs for 5 minutes and looked like a serial stall. It was the 600 s per-request timeout against a broken image whose generation had collapsed; the CASE lines (tokens=2, calls_ok=0) are the tell, not the process state. A broken candidate that shortens generation looks like a hung harness on this bench.
asi.fix: engine/src/nd_quant.c now loops the whole len==1 stage (for i = 0; i < n; i += 2), with the measured failure recorded at the site. 16/16 repo tests green on the fixed tree.
asi.next: 20260923T1022L re-measures it on three boards: board 1 both halves, board 2 transform alone (its byte-exactness is the direct verdict on the fix), board 3 the same image as board 1 for the cross-board confirmation. If board 2 is byte-exact the transform is real; if not the half is reverted and 5.0467 stands alone.

description: Experiment 33 transform half, FIXED and MEASURED: bit-exact but worth exactly zero, so REJECTED and reverted (accepted runtime stays 5.0467). Board 2 ran the repaired paired-butterfly transform alone and read 5.0300 - the pre-rescale accepted value to the digit - while boards 1 and 3 ran it on top of the rescale and both read 5.0467, exactly #362's rescale-only figure. Two independent decompositions agree the transform contributes +0.000 %. Quality was never the issue after the fix: DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, on all three boards - which confirms #363's len==1 stage was the entire defect. WHY ISOLATION AND FIELD DISAGREE: the kbench screen re-swept the same 768-float block 25 times, so the transform ran on data the 64 KB data cache had absorbed (the #295/#330 warmth trap), while the field calls nd_fwht on a freshly prepared activation each time. Third independent measurement - after #330's flat 13.90 % cold delivery tax and #295's phi warmth correction - that instruction-level wins in a cold PSRAM-touching loop do not transfer, and the strongest one yet because the isolated delta was +36.75 % and the transferred delta was exactly zero. Dead TIE helper deleted from engine/src/nd_quant.c: 16/16 tests, host 19/19 byte-exact, no warnings. Rule reinforced: a warm kbench number prices nothing; isolate cold or do not price from isolation.

asi.why_isolated_and_field_disagree: The kbench loop re-swept the same 768-float block 25 times, so the transform ran on data the 64 KB data cache had already absorbed - the #295/#330 warmth trap again, this time on the loop that looked like the cleanest win of the window. description: Experiment 35 - the aliasing lever on the prepare phase's per-cell loops: MEASURED ON THREE BOARDS, ALL NULL, nothing kept. 35A board 1 'hoist' (lutb_rows reads c->cb[0..3] once, not once per pair): 5.0450 = -0.034 %. 35B board 2 'hoist2' (plus two pairs per iteration): 5.0317 = -0.297 % and -512 B internal heap. 35C board 3 'fwathoist' (fwht_rows hoists c->g/c->scale/c->xh; c->scale is read per element today): 5.0500 = +0.065 %, free (internal_free 14,647 unchanged, boot bench 5.098, extended 4.977, prefill 5.3317, think 3.95), 17/17 device + 19/19 host byte-exact, DEVICE_GATE_OK, golden_missing 0. All three were host-proven byte-exact before flashing, which is how the #363 transcription class gets caught without a board. Conclusion: the unroll lever and the alias-hoist lever are not interchangeable - GCC already had the alias information the const-qualification implies (matching run #358's restrict-null on the same loop), so what the rescale loop lacked was independent work in flight, not loads. Aliasing/const-hoisting is closed in this phase. Off-device free closure: prepare's copy stage is memcpy+memset, so 'unroll the copy' is null by inspection. 35C banked as a sub-bar free option alongside sigmoidf_pair IRAM. Next: E36 on the loops matching the shape that paid - kv_store_int8 and zcrms_head_rows, both in nd_model.c.

asi.candidates: Three distinct images, one per board, all bit-exact by construction and all host-proven byte-exact (19/19, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0) BEFORE any flash - which is how run #363's transcription-bug class gets caught without spending a board. 35A board 1 'hoist': lutb_rows reads c->cb[0..3] once instead of once per pair (md5 2ad908c37fc1). 35B board 2 'hoist2': as 35A plus two pairs per iteration, two independent chains to interleave (md5 74925317e879). 35C board 3 'fwathoist': fwht_rows hoists c->g / c->scale / c->xh out of both loops, where c->scale is today read once PER element (md5 e87d8e8dc77c). Batch 20260923T0905L.
asi.hypothesis: The lever that just shipped (#362's rescale unroll, +0.332 %) is an instruction-level win in a per-element loop, so try the OTHER mechanism that class responds to - aliasing. `const fwht_ctx *` and `const lutb_ctx *` are not `restrict`, and both loops write through a pointer the compiler cannot separate from their operand reads, so loop-invariant operands (four codebook floats; the group size and scale) may be re-loaded every iteration.
asi.result: All three are nulls against the accepted 5.0467. 35A 5.0450 = -0.034 %. 35B 5.0317 = -0.297 % and it cost 512 B of internal heap (14,135 vs 14,647). 35C 5.0500 = +0.065 %, the only one that moved up, and it is free (internal_free 14,647 unchanged, boot bench 5.098 from 5.091, extended 4.977 from 4.975, prefill 5.3317 from 5.3217, think 3.95 unchanged, 17/17 device + 19/19 host byte-exact, DEVICE_GATE_OK).
asi.verdict: Nothing kept. 35A/35B are worse. 35C at +0.065 % is a quarter of the 0.2 % keep bar - banked with sigmoidf_pair IRAM (#336/#342, +0.18 % mean) as a sub-bar free option, not shipped.
asi.conclusion: The unroll lever and the alias-hoist lever are not interchangeable. GCC already had the alias information the const-qualification implies here (exactly the run #358 finding that `restrict` on the same rescale loop measured exactly zero); what the rescale loop was missing was independent work in flight, not loads. That closes aliasing/const-hoisting as a lever in this phase, and it narrows the remaining elementwise-hypothesis to the specific shape that paid: an un-unrolled loop of independent per-element arithmetic, in nd_model.c rather than nd_quant.c.
asi.off_device_closure: prepare's copy stage is memcpy + memset, so 'unroll the copy loop' is null by reading the function - retired for the price of a grep, no board time.
asi.next: E36 targets the loops that actually match the winning shape: kv_store_int8 (runs per layer per position per head, independent per-element quantise + int8 store) and zcrms_head_rows (per-head-row elementwise). Both are in engine/src/nd_model.c, so the lane harness now carries a second engine file. Board 1 simultaneously re-flashes the accepted image and runs the behavioural capture the campaign owes since #362.

description: Experiment 36 lane 2 - zcsplit_rows emit loop unrolled by 4: MEASURED, -0.133 %, REJECTED (decode 5.0400 vs accepted 5.0467, batch 20260923T1000L, nd_model.c md5 c5e6e8a6e441). This was the largest mass of the shape that paid in run #362 - one independent expression per element, d_model=768, three calls per layer, ~18,432 elements per token - and it came back slower. Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10), extended 4.968, think 3.95, prefill 5.3217, min_case 4.81, so it is a pure speed verdict. Host-proven byte-exact before flashing. Conclusion: the unroll lever pays only where a loop's latency is genuinely exposed; the FWHT rescale follows the transform with nothing to overlap, while the ZCRMS emit already has its work hidden by the two-core split. With run #365's aliasing nulls this closes the elementwise-unroll family at one win. Repo tree unchanged at the accepted image.

asi.candidate: E36 lane 2 (board 2, batch 20260923T1000L): `zcsplit_rows` emit loop unrolled by 4 - `out[i] = (1.0f + s[i]) * x[i] * inv` over d_model=768, called through nd_parallel_rows three times per layer (nd_model.c:1813/1815/1829), so ~18,432 elements per decode token - the largest mass of exactly the shape that paid in run #362. nd_model.c md5 c5e6e8a6e441. Host-proven byte-exact (19/19, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0) before the flash.
asi.hypothesis: run #362 proved an un-unrolled independent-per-element loop can carry +0.33 %, and run #365 proved the aliasing lever is not the same lever. This is the biggest remaining loop of the winning shape.
asi.result: decode 5.0400 = **-0.133 %** against the accepted 5.0467. Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10) so this is a pure speed verdict: it is slower. Monitors: extended 4.968 (-0.14 %), think 3.95, prefill 5.3217, min_case 4.81, gen_tokens 99.
asi.verdict: REJECTED, not kept. Variant lived only in board 2's worker tree; the repo tree is the accepted 5.0467 image (engine md5 b914e2703852, verified).
asi.conclusion: Unrolling an independent per-element loop pays only where that loop's latency was actually exposed. The FWHT rescale sits immediately after the transform, where the scheduler has nothing else to overlap; the ZCRMS emit already has the parallel-row split plus adjacent work hiding its latency, so adding four-deep grouping only added register pressure and tail-handling. Measured alongside run #365's aliasing nulls, the elementwise-unroll family now has one win and three non-wins, so it is closed at one win and the remaining elementwise candidates are not worth a board.
asi.next: E37 tests the last two loops of the winning shape inside the 24.4 ms Hadamard MLP (the d1*x scale loop and the p1 permutation gather) on boards 2/3; board 1 is finishing the KV store unroll. If both MLP loops are null the family closes and the remaining honest work is the owed behavioural capture plus the two sub-bar banked levers that need an owner bar decision.

description: Experiment 36 lane 1 - kv_store_int8 per-element clamp+convert loop unrolled by 4: MEASURED, EXACTLY NEUTRAL (decode 5.0467 = the accepted value to the digit), costs 256 B, not kept (batch 20260923T1000L, nd_model.c md5 2ca9f38dad06). Premise corrected before building: the ELF calls flash-mapped lrintf per element but this part has NO rounding instruction at all (frint.nf/z.f/xf/mf/pf, itrunc.s, quou.s all rejected by the shipped assembler), so call removal is unavailable and this lane tested the unroll only. Verified the unroll really was in the measured image before believing the null (app_md5 74c7a00fa71c; 5 lrintf refs inside the function = 4 instances + tail). NOT MEASURED ON THIS IMAGE, carried forward from the accepted run: ext/think/boot-bench/psram/device-exact/token-delta/fidelity/top1 - the lane hit the known console-fatigue defect (drained 26 stale lines, then a think-toggle timeout, #345/#346) AFTER the primary group completed with gen_tokens=99 identical to the accepted value, so decode/prefill/min_case/internal_free are measured and the rest are not. Unrolling around a per-element library call cannot help because the call is the loop; with lanes 2/3 (-0.13 %, +0.03 %) and the Hadamard nulls the elementwise-unroll family closes at one win (#362). Repo tree unchanged.

asi.candidate: E36 lane 1 (board 1, batch 20260923T1000L): kv_store_int8's clamp-then-convert loop unrolled by 4, non-finite fallback replicated per lane so no value changes path. Generated from the shipped loop text by .auto/exp36/make_kvvariant.py, which ASSERTS the four unrolled expressions are the shipped text with i, i+1, i+2, i+3 substituted (the generator's first version failed: the store is (int8_t)lrintf(q), not (int8_t)q) - a generated patch whose arithmetic is a hand transcription is the #363 failure class, so the assertion is the check. nd_model.c md5 2ca9f38dad06.

Premise corrected BEFORE the build: the accepted ELF calls flash-mapped lrintf (0x42013f48) per element, and this part implements NO rounding instruction at all (frint.nf / frint.z.f / frint.xf / frint.mf / frint.pf / itrunc.s / quou.s all rejected by the shipped assembler), so removing the call is not available and this lane tested the unroll alone.
asi.result: decode 5.0467 = +0.000 % against the accepted 5.0467; internal_free 14,391 (-256 B). Verified the unroll was really in the measured image before believing the null: app_md5 74c7a00fa71c (distinct from every other lane), kv_store_int8 present, objdump shows 5 lrintf references inside it (4 unrolled + tail). Code changed, speed did not.
asi.carry_forward_disclosure: MEASURE rc=1 and it is NOT the candidate: the lane died in the think group with 'WARN drained 26 stale line(s) before the think toggle' then TimeoutError - the #345/#346 console-fatigue signature. The primary group had completed first (decode 5.0467, prefill 5.325, gen_tokens 99 identical to the accepted run, min_case 4.82), so the decode reading and internal_free are MEASURED here. ext_decode_tps, think_tps, boot_bench_tps, psram_free, device_output_exact, device_token_delta, logit_max_delta and logit_top1_match were NEVER MEASURED for this image and are carried forward from the accepted 5.0467 image so the scoreboard stays populated - read them as 'not measured', not as passing gates. The variant is bit-exact by construction and was host-verified 19/19 with token_delta 0 before any flash.
asi.verdict: REJECTED, not kept: neutral speed for 256 B of a 14,647 B heap. Repo tree verified unchanged at the accepted image (engine/src/nd_quant.c md5 b914e2703852, engine/ clean).
asi.conclusion: Unrolling around a per-element library call cannot help: the four lrintf invocations were already independent, so the scheduler had nothing to regroup - the call IS the loop. With lane 2 (-0.13 %), lane 3 (+0.03 %) and the Hadamard nulls, the elementwise-unroll family is closed at exactly one win (run #362's FWHT rescale, +0.332 %), and the residual lrintf cost is closed by an ISA fact rather than by opinion, since the float/int-transfer alternative was measured expensive twice (#230, #292).

description: Experiment 37 lane 2 - Hadamard MLP permutation gather (hada_b[p1[i]], 8,192 elements/token) unrolled by 4: MEASURED, -0.133 %, REJECTED (decode 5.0400 vs accepted 5.0467, batch 20260923T1030L, board 3). Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10), extended 4.968, think 3.95, prefill 5.3217, boot bench 5.089, min_case 4.81. Type trap caught pre-build: p1 is a float array whose values are truncation-cast to indices, so the unrolled form casts floats exactly as the shipped line does instead of reinterpreting the buffer as uint32_t (which would have been a fast wrong kernel). Random-index loads were already back-to-back, so grouping four added register pressure and a tail loop. With lane 1 the two remaining independent MLP loops are closed; the elementwise-unroll family now stands at one win (#362, +0.332 %) and five non-wins across three phases. Repo tree unchanged.

asi.candidate: E37 lane 2 (board 3, batch 20260923T1030L): the Hadamard MLP's permutation gather `for (i=0;i<n;i++) m->hada_a[i] = m->hada_b[(uint32_t)p1[i]]` unrolled by 4, 1024 elements per layer = 8,192 per token, inside the 24.4 ms MLP phase. Bit-exact by construction (one output per iteration, no accumulation). A type trap was caught before the build: p1 is a float array whose values are truncation-cast to indices, so the unrolled form reads floats and casts exactly as the shipped line does - reinterpreting the buffer as uint32_t* would have read different numbers and produced a fast wrong kernel, the campaign's fourth failure class.
asi.hypothesis: unrolling a per-element dependent-load gather lets the scheduler keep several loads outstanding, which is the only cure this core has for load latency since it has no prefetch instruction (#300 measured __builtin_prefetch emitting nothing and pref/dpref not assembling).
asi.result: decode 5.0400 = -0.133 % against the accepted 5.0467. Gate-clean and bit-exact: DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, extended 4.968, think 3.95, prefill 5.3217, boot bench 5.089, min_case 4.81 - a pure speed verdict, and it is slower.
asi.verdict: REJECTED. Lived only in board 3's worker tree; repo tree verified unchanged at the accepted image.
asi.conclusion: Random-index loads through a 1024-entry permutation do not benefit from four-deep grouping on this core - the loads were already issued back to back, and the unroll added register pressure plus a tail loop. Together with lane 1 (hadascale, exactly 0.00 %) the two remaining independent loops of the MLP are closed, which with runs #365/#366/#368 closes the elementwise-unroll family on six measurements: one win (run #362's FWHT rescale, +0.332 %) and five non-wins spanning three phases.
asi.family_state: Elementwise unroll: FWHT rescale +0.332 % KEPT / zcsplit -0.133 % / zchead +0.032 % / kvstore 0.000 % / hadascale 0.000 % / hadagather -0.133 %. Do not re-run at other unroll factors: the two ZCRMS emits bracket the result and the two MLP loops are both null, so there is no exposed latency left of this shape to buy.

The 8-way conditioning reductions and the softmax sums in the same function were deliberately left untouched because they are accumulations.

asi.result: decode 5.0467 = **+0.000 %**, exactly the accepted value. Gate-clean: DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, extended 4.975, think 3.95, prefill 5.3233, boot bench 5.091, min_case 4.82, internal_free unchanged.

asi.conclusion: Sixth measurement of the elementwise-unroll lever, fifth non-win: FWHT rescale +0.332 % / zcsplit -0.133 % / zchead +0.032 % / kvstore 0.000 % / hadascale 0.000 % / hadagather -0.133 %. The lever is not 'unroll independent loops' - it is 'give the scheduler work at the one place where a loop follows a long dependency chain with nothing else to overlap', which is why the loop right after the FWHT transform paid and six others in three different phases did not. Recorded so the shape of the one win is not generalised again.

description: Experiment 38 - cold-vs-warm x backing-store calibration of the shipped nd_fwht: MEASURED, no shipping change (decode_tps is the accepted 5.0567 carried forward; only a kbench image ran, which by design never executes the request path). It refutes run #364's CAUSE. On the operand the field actually uses (fwht_rows transforms c->xh = ND_ALLOC_FAST internal SRAM, not routed through the data cache on this part) emptying the cache with a 160 KiB PSRAM sweep changes the cost by exactly nothing: 47,470 cycles warm and cold. On a PSRAM operand the cold penalty is only +8.98 % (51,731 vs 47,470), and warm PSRAM equals internal exactly. All four modes byte-identical. So operand warmth can explain at most ~9 of a 36.75-point isolated gain, and zero of the field case - #364's decision not to ship the wide-load form stands on its own two field measurements, but its recorded explanation cannot, and the plain C unroll it therefore killed is being measured now (Experiment 40: unroll-2, unroll-4, and inlining nd_fwht into fwht_rows to remove a call per group). Method rules replaced: for an internal-SRAM operand cold-isolation is inapplicable so warm numbers are not cache-inflated; what a tight bench loop inflates is instruction mix, so per-call kernels must be screened with the field's call structure. Harness assets and three fixed bugs: idf.py needs the project dir, idf.py has no --before/--after, and a static single-call-site function is inlined so the right macro-candidate proof is a body-unique string in the ELF, not an nm symbol.

asi.candidate: Experiment 38 (board 1, kbench, batch 20260923T1300L): a 2x2 calibration of the shipped nd_fwht - {internal SRAM, PSRAM} x {warm, cold}, cold meaning a 160 KiB PSRAM sweep between timed calls, real n=128 six-group field shape, min of 25 rounds, all four modes byte-identical to one another (mismatch_vs_ref=0). No candidate; this prices a measurement method. Guards proved the body was really in the image before flashing: macro on kbench.c's OWN compile line (with_flag=1) and the string only the E38 body prints present in the ELF.
asi.hypothesis: Run #364's closure - 'the paired-butterfly transform screened +36.75 % bit-exact and delivered exactly +0.000 % on device, because the bench re-swept one block so it ran warm in the 64 KiB data cache while the field transforms a freshly prepared activation' - was the campaign's strongest methodological conclusion, and it had never been numbered. If operand warmth is the mechanism, evicting the cache must reproduce most of the delta.
asi.result: internal-SRAM operand (which is what the field actually uses: fwht_rows transforms c->xh, allocated ND_ALLOC_FAST): 47,470 cycles warm and 47,470 cold - a 0.0 % difference, bit-exact. PSRAM operand: 47,470 warm vs 51,731 cold = +8.98 %. And warm PSRAM equals internal exactly, so a cached PSRAM operand costs nothing extra when warm. The printed evict-penalty line was mangled by my own %.2u%% format ('. 8%' and '. 0%'); the per-field cycles are the authority and are quoted above - fourth instance this session of trusting fields over summaries (#351 wrong sign, #355 units, #341 cumulative divide).
asi.conclusion: Warmth can explain at most ~9 points of a 36.75-point isolated gain, and for the field's actual operand it explains ZERO, because internal SRAM is not routed through the data cache on this part and no PSRAM sweep can touch it. So #364's recorded CAUSE is refuted as an explanation, even though its DECISION (do not ship the ee.ldf/ee.stf wide-load form) stands on its own field measurement. The remaining explanation for that +36.75 % is the bench's instruction mix - 25 back-to-back transform calls with nothing else in the pipeline - not the data.
asi.invalidates_prior_discard: YES, and the retries are already running as Experiment 40: #360's plain C unroll-2 of the butterfly loop (+17.95 %, bit-exact, never integrated because its wide-load sibling died on device) was rejected by a mechanism E38 shows cannot be the cause, so its assumption genuinely changed and it deserves a board - along with the unroll-4 curve point and, separately, inlining nd_fwht into fwht_rows to remove a call per group (~96 calls/token), which is the third category run #333 established. The wide-load variant itself is NOT retried: it was bit-exact and still measured +0.000 % twice, which is a field verdict independent of the diagnosis.
asi.method_rule_updated: The old rule 'a warm kbench number prices nothing' is now too coarse and has been replaced by two sharper ones: (1) for a kernel whose operand is internal SRAM, cold-isolation is not even applicable, so a warm screen of it is not inflated by cache state and may be taken at face value; (2) what a tight back-to-back bench loop actually inflates is the instruction mix, so a screen of a per-call kernel must reproduce the field's call structure (one call per group, immediately followed by the consumer) rather than the cache state.
asi.asset: esp32/main/kbench.c bench_e38 (kbench-gated, so no shipping configure evaluates it) and .auto/exp38/lane.sh, which syncs its own files, proves the macro reaches kbench.c's own compile line, proves the body string is in the ELF, and refuses to flash otherwise. Three separate real bugs were fixed to get here: idf.py must run from the project directory, idf.py has no --before/--after, and a static single-call-site function is inlined so an nm-based symbol probe cannot find it (the correct artifact for a macro-gated candidate is a string only that body prints).

description: Experiment 40 lane 3 - nd_fwht's body inlined into fwht_rows via one shared static-inline definition, removing a call per group (~96/token): MEASURED, -0.166 %, REJECTED (decode 5.0483 vs 5.0567, batch 20260923T1330L, board 3). Bit-exact and gate-clean on both sides (host 19/19 byte-exact, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical; device DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0), prefill 5.3217, extended 4.977, think 3.95, boot bench 5.088, gen_tokens 99. Counterexample to run #333's call-structure category: removing the phi call paid because the callee's schedule changed with it, while here the callee is a compact IRAM function and inlining only bloats the caller. The generator's assert also caught that a naive single replace would have hit the wrong one of two identical call lines. Repo tree unchanged.

asi.candidate: Experiment 40 lane 3 (board 3, batch 20260923T1330L): nd_fwht's body inlined into fwht_rows through ONE shared static-inline definition (fwht_inplace) used by both the exported nd_fwht and the hot per-group call site, removing a call per group - about 96 calls per decode token. Deliberately a single definition with no second copy of the butterfly loop anywhere, because a hand-typed transcription of this transform is exactly what made run #363 diverge 4/17 on device while its benchmark reported diff=0. The other call site (the dequant/prepare walk) was left calling the exported symbol - one lever. An assert in .auto/exp40/make_variants.py is what caught that the naive single replace would have hit the first of two identical call lines rather than the intended one.
asi.hypothesis: Run #333 established call/inline structure as a third category bigger than delivery and scheduling - the phi kernel was worth +0.365 % precisely because dot_group was a call per group. fwht_rows calls nd_fwht once per group, so the same lever should apply here.
asi.result: decode 5.0483 = -0.166 % against the accepted 5.0567. Bit-exact and gate-clean (host 19/19 byte-exact with fidelity 5.341e-05 identical before the flash; device DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, gen_tokens 99, prefill 5.3217, extended 4.977, think 3.95, boot bench 5.088), so it is a pure speed verdict and it is slower.
asi.verdict: REJECTED. The repo tree never contained it (engine/src/nd_quant.c verified back at the accepted md5 e87d8e8dc77c).
asi.conclusion: Call removal is NOT a universally positive category, and the contrast with run #333 is the finding: removing the phi call paid because the callee's whole schedule changed with it (a per-group C call became a per-row assembly kernel), whereas here the callee is a compact ND_HOT IRAM function and inlining it merely bloats fwht_rows - the caller loses registers to the transform's temporaries and pays for it. So the category must be evaluated as 'does the body get better, not just closer', and this is the measured counterexample to keep alongside #333. Two of the three E40 levers are now closed (this and fw4 below); the third, the plain 2-way butterfly unroll, is the campaign's largest candidate since the phi asm.
asi.next: fw2 is being confirmed on boards 2 and 3 (batch 20260923T1400L) after reading 5.0800 on board 1 with zero measured heap cost.

description: Experiment 40 lane 2 - FWHT butterfly inner loop unrolled by 4: MEASURED +0.461 % (decode 5.0800 vs 5.0567) but REJECTED ON COST - it costs 6,144 B of internal heap for zero speed over unroll-2 (batch 20260923T1330L, board 2). Every monitor up: extended 5.009 (+0.48 %), prefill 5.3617, think 3.97, boot bench 5.123 (+0.39 %, the mechanism check), min_case 4.85, DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, bit-exact and host-proven 19/19 before flash. Cost priced mechanically with nm -S rather than inferred: nd_fwht is 100 B accepted / 174 B in fw2 with heap unchanged at 13,879 / 284 B in fw4 with heap 7,735, because this code is IRAM text and IRAM text is subtracted from the internal heap (#292's coupling). Unroll factor is therefore chosen by cost, not speed - 2 and 4 tie at 5.0800, so the campaign takes the 74-byte version; combined with #362's -28 % at unroll-8 the curve is now measured at three points.

asi.candidate: Experiment 40 lane 2 (board 2, batch 20260923T1330L): the FWHT butterfly inner loop unrolled by 4, generated by .auto/exp40/make_variants.py from the shipped loop text (the first generator attempt failed to compile - declarations wrapped in a nested block - which is the generator earning its keep rather than a hand-typed diff being wrong on device). Bit-exact by construction: butterflies inside one stage are disjoint index pairs, each element read and written once per stage, so grouping four moves no value, operand or order. Host-proven 19/19 byte-exact with fidelity 5.341e-05 identical before any flash.
asi.hypothesis: The curve point. Run #362's rescale shipped at unroll-4 (+0.332 %) and unroll-8 there measured -28 %, the LX7 register-file ceiling already recorded for kron_apply, so the question was whether the transform's optimum is at 2 or 4 - #360's isolated screen had measured unroll-2 at +17.95 % and a 4-butterfly block form at -0.30 %.
asi.result: decode 5.0800 = +0.461 % over the accepted 5.0567, with every monitor up together: extended 5.009 (+0.48 %), prefill 5.3617 (+0.47 %), think 3.97 (+0.25 %), boot bench 5.123 (+0.39 %, the mechanism check - the transform is inside the bench), min_case 4.85, gen_tokens 99, DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0. But internal_free 7,735 against 13,879 = -6,144 B.
asi.verdict: REJECTED on cost, not on speed: it is exactly as fast as fw2 (both 5.0800, from independent builds on different boards) and costs 6,144 B of a 13,879 B heap.
asi.mechanical_pricing: nm -S on the three images makes the asymmetry concrete rather than inferred: nd_fwht is 0x64 = 100 bytes in the accepted image, 0xae = 174 bytes in fw2 with internal_free UNCHANGED at 13,879, and 0x11c = 284 bytes in fw4 with internal_free 7,735. So the transform's code is IRAM text and IRAM text is subtracted from the internal heap (#292's documented coupling); the 184-byte growth in fw4 crosses a placement granularity and costs 6 KiB of usable heap. A 3x code growth for zero speed over fw2, on a kernel that already runs once per group, is not a trade worth making.
asi.conclusion: The transform unroll is worth +0.46 % and the unroll factor is chosen by cost, not by speed: 2 and 4 are indistinguishable at 5.0800, so the campaign takes the 74-byte version. This also retires the last 'we should try a bigger factor' instinct for this kernel - the curve is flat between 2 and 4 and #362 measured it falling off a cliff at 8.
asi.next: fw2 confirmed on boards 2 and 3 in batch 20260923T1400L; board 1's own fw2 run was still completing its extended/think groups at the time of writing, and its gates are recorded in the fw2 keep/discard line rather than here.

description: CORRECTION to run #376's causal claim, no engine change (accepted runtime stays 5.0567, metric carried forward): the 6,144 B heap cost I attributed to the transform's unroll-4 belongs to Experiment 39's -O3, which was still appended to boards 2 and 3's copies of esp32/components/needle/CMakeLists.txt. Those lanes therefore ran fw4+(-O3) and fw2+(-O3), so the two 'cross-board confirmations' of fw2 (5.0800, 5.0833) are withdrawn as confirmations, and fw4's heap cost is simply unmeasured. Clean facts: board 1's fw2 read 5.0800 with internal_free 13,879, identical to accepted, so the 74-byte unroll is free at the heap; nm -S shows nd_fwht at 0xae in both fw2 and fw4 images. Decision unchanged (fw2 is the candidate; a clean fw4 curve point is not worth a board) but the reason is fixed. Root cause: a lane appended to a build file and no lane removed it, and while sdkconfig drift has had a guard since #300, an edited CMakeLists had none, so the contamination was invisible to every check including the config check. Fixed: both workers restored and md5-verified, and .auto/board_config_check.sh now hashes the two CMakeLists plus bench.py against main for all three boards with BUILD_FILE_DRIFT output and an extended selftest. Standing rule: when two runs of different code agree on a number that is supposed to be incidental, suspect shared state before believing the agreement. Re-confirmation of clean fw2 plus a distinct silu4 screen are running now (batch 20260923T1430L).

asi.what_was_wrong: Run #376 recorded: 'fw4 costs 6,144 B of internal heap' and priced it mechanically as nd_fwht growing 100 B -> 284 B of IRAM text under #292's heap coupling. The measurement was real but the attribution was not. Boards 2 and 3 still carried the `-O3` line Experiment 39 had appended to their copies of esp32/components/needle/CMakeLists.txt (worker md5 5b207489a1e2 vs main 7085cb108638, EXPERIMENT-39 marker present), so what those lanes ran was fw4+(-O3) and fw2+(-O3), not the clean variants. nm -S on the fw2 and fw4 images shows nd_fwht at 0xae in both, and the 6,144 B reading appears on every lane that ran on boards 2 or 3 regardless of the candidate - it belongs to -O3, which is itself rejected.
asi.corrected_facts: fw4's heap cost is NOT measured (it has never been measured without -O3). fw2's clean reading is board 1's: decode 5.0800 with internal_free 13,879 - identical to the accepted image - so the 74-byte unroll is free at the heap. The two 'cross-board confirmations' in batch 20260923T1400L (5.0800, 5.0833) are withdrawn as confirmations of fw2: they are measurements of fw2+(-O3), and are interesting only as a second instance of the -O3 result (about the same speed, ~6 KiB of heap).
asi.corrected_decision: The unroll-factor choice does not change: fw2 is kept-if-confirmed and fw4 is not needed, but for the stated reason 'fw4 was measured only in combination with a rejected flag', not 'fw4 costs 6 KiB for zero gain'. A clean fw4 curve point is not worth a board, because #362 measured unroll-8 falling off a cliff and fw2 already delivers the whole gain that the two 4-way readings showed.
asi.root_cause: A lane applied a compile-time flag by appending to a build file and no lane removed it. sdkconfig drift has had a guard since run #300 precisely because sdkconfig is gitignored and survives `git reset --hard`; an edited CMakeLists is the same class - worker state that git cannot see - and had no guard, so the drift was invisible to every check in the pipeline including the config check, and the two lanes looked perfectly healthy (fresh builds, gates green, plausible numbers).
asi.fix: Both workers restored from the main checkout and verified by md5. .auto/board_config_check.sh now hashes esp32/components/needle/CMakeLists.txt, esp32/main/CMakeLists.txt and .auto/bench.py against main for all three boards and prints BUILD_FILE_DRIFT board=N file=F, with its equal/different selftest extended to prove the new comparison can distinguish a one-byte change. Rule for this repo: a lane that mutates a build file is responsible for restoring it, and if it cannot prove restoration then the pool's file hashes must be compared before the next lane trusts a number.
asi.meta: Fifth instance this campaign of a check that could not fail, and the second where the failure direction was 'plausible result from a contaminated input' rather than 'obvious error'. The tell that found it in one step was not a gate but an arithmetic oddity: two supposedly different candidates reporting the identical internal_free, which is exactly the kind of incidental value nobody thought to falsify. Recorded as a standing habit: when two runs of different code agree on a number that is supposed to be incidental, suspect the shared state before believing the agreement.

description: Experiment 40 integration - FWHT butterfly loop unrolled by 2: MEASURED AND KEPT, +0.461 % decode (5.0567 -> 5.0800, now +108.2 % over the 2.44 baseline), the largest single win since the phi asm (#333). Read 5.0800 on THREE independent fresh builds on THREE boards (board 1 in batch 20260923T1330L, boards 2 and 3 in 20260923T1430L after the -O3 contamination was found and removed) with per-variant board spread exactly zero and internal_free 13,879 - byte-identical to the accepted image, so nd_fwht's 100 -> 174 bytes is free. Bit-exact by construction (butterflies in one stage are disjoint pairs), host-proven 19/19 byte-exact before the flash and re-proven on the applied tree, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17 with golden_missing=0 and token_delta 0 on two full rc=0 suites, top1 10/10, make test green. Monitors all up: extended 5.004/5.005, prefill 5.3617, think 3.97, boot bench 5.126/5.127 (+0.45 %, the mechanism check), min_case 4.85 (best worst case in 377 runs). Delivered 1.6x its isolated pricing (+0.28 %), second over-delivery in this phase after #362, because prepare runs ~16 times per token. description: Experiment 41 integration - two FWHT groups transformed together (cross-group ILP): MEASURED AND KEPT, +0.492 % decode (5.0800 -> 5.1050, now +109.0 % over the 2.44 baseline), the second-largest win of the last 20 runs. Three readings on two boards (discovery 5.1050 board 3, confirm 5.1000 board 2, confirm 5.1050 board 3; mean +0.459 %), all far above the 0.2 % bar and the 0.071 % board spread. Bit-exact by construction (each group's stages complete in its own order), remainder path guarded by .auto/exp41/test_odd_split.c under the 3+3 split the host cannot produce. Monitors all up: extended 5.031, prefill 5.39, think 3.99, boot bench 5.151 (+0.47 %, the mechanism check), min_case 4.87 (best worst case in 382 runs). Cost internal_free 13,623 (-256 B). Quality: DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17 x3, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, host 19/19 on the applied tree, checks rc=0. Disclosed: the three readings came from two byte-different files (hand-written helper vs clean regeneration) that are identical after comment/whitespace stripping, and both were measured. Geometry finding worth more than the win: with ngroup=6 split 3+3 each core owns exactly 3 groups, so a 4-group walk would never have run on device and would have silently re-measured the accepted path - hence fw3pair is the curve point and fw4pair was never built.

asi.candidate: fw2pair - two FWHT groups transformed in one stage walk (nd_fwht2), on top of the shipped within-stage 2-way butterfly unroll. Bit-exact by construction: each group's stages still complete in its own order (stage k of a group before stage k+1 of the same group), so every cell ends with the value nd_fwht would have written. Rescale shared verbatim through fw_scale so neither path's rescale text differs from what ships. A single-group remainder path is kept because the device hands each core an ODD group count; .auto/exp41/test_odd_split.c proves it under the 3+3, 1+5, 5+1, 2+4 and one-group splits that the host's rows_serial never produces.
asi.hypothesis: fw2 (#378) put more independent work inside one iteration of a single group's butterfly chain. The remaining independent work of the same kind is the NEXT GROUP's chain: fwht_rows calls nd_fwht once per group with nothing else in flight, and the transform is ~80 % of prep+lut, so two chains in flight should pay again.
asi.result: decode 5.1050 = +0.492 % over the accepted 5.0800, now +109.0 % over the 2.44 baseline. Three readings on two boards: discovery 5.1050 (board 3), confirmation 5.1000 (board 2), second confirmation 5.1050 (board 3); mean 5.1033 = +0.459 %, every reading far above both the 0.2 % bar and the 0.071 % board spread. Monitors all up together: extended 5.031/5.030 (+0.54 %), prefill 5.39/5.3883 (+0.53 %), think 3.99/3.98, boot bench 5.151/5.15 (+0.47 %, the mechanism check - prepare is inside the bench), min_case 4.87 (best worst case in 382 runs), gen_tokens 99.
asi.cost: internal_free 13,623 against 13,879 = -256 B, and nd_fwht2's text is IRAM code (the #292 heap coupling). Accepted on measurement, not on assumption.
asi.quality: DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17 with golden_missing=0 and token_delta=0 on all three device runs, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical to control, top1 10/10, host 19/19 byte-exact with golden_missing=0 re-verified on the applied tree (checks.sh rc=0).
asi.byte_form_disclosure: The three readings come from two byte-different source files: the hand-written helper (image engine_md5 2a41969e43f1, discovery and board-2 confirmation) and the clean regenerated form now in the tree (bdcf0c7c8b0c, board-3 confirmation). asi.geometry_finding: The guard must be `gi + (ng-1) < g1`, not `gi + ng < g1`, and ng must fit the per-core group count: ngroup=6 split 3+3 means each nd_parallel_rows call owns exactly THREE groups, so a 4-group walk would never execute on device and would silently re-measure the accepted path (run #333's garbage-collected-kernel null in a new guise). That is why the curve point queued next is fw3pair (exactly one triple per core, no tail) and why fw4pair was never built.
