So the mechanism is not general even within the campaign's own favourite shape: interleaving paid where the loop is pure arithmetic on a resident block, and cost where the loop is load-bound (stride-8 cond_v) and only gained register pressure.
asi.next: fw3pair (three groups per walk = the exact per-core count) and fw2single (paired groups WITHOUT the within-stage unroll, the attribution run that says whether the two wins are one mechanism or two) are on boards 1 and 2 now. make capture is owed on this image.

description: Experiment 41 lane - cond2, the Hadamard MLP's conditioning projection with two channels' 768-term reductions interleaved: MEASURED, -0.394 %, REJECTED (decode 5.0600 vs accepted 5.0800, batch 20260923T1530L, board 1). Bit-exact by construction (per-channel accumulators keep their own order) and gate-clean, so a pure speed verdict. prefill 5.3417, min_case 4.83, gen_tokens 99; extended/think/boot-bench/internal_free not measured on this image (the lane hit the known console-fatigue defect after the primary group) and carried from the accepted run, which the verdict does not depend on. The largest dependent-chain mass in the model (~49k serial FMAs per token) does not respond to the lever that just paid +0.49 % on the transform, because it is bound by its strided cond_v loads and interleaving only added register pressure - the same lesson #366/#367/#370 recorded for unrolls, now measured on a reduction. Also documents the generator bug the host gate caught (literal vs relative channel index) and the equivalence guard it produced.

asi.candidate: cond2 - the Hadamard MLP's conditioning projection (cond_rows, engine/src/nd_model.c) with two channels' 768-term reductions in flight at once. Each channel keeps its own accumulator from 0.0f to its own store, so its additions happen in exactly the shipped order: bit-exact by construction, unlike unrolling one channel's loop (reassociation, which #366/#367 correctly refused). 8 channels x dm-term serial sums per layer is the largest dependent-chain mass in the token - ~49k dependent FMAs, inside the 24 ms hadamard phase - and cond_v's stride-8 layout means interleaved channels also share each loaded line.
asi.hypothesis: fw2 (#378) won by putting independent work inside a serial dependency chain, so the model's biggest serial reduction should pay too; cond_rows is 8 independent 768-long chains that nothing currently overlaps.
asi.result: decode 5.0600 = -0.394 % against the accepted 5.0800. prefill 5.3417, min_case 4.83, gen_tokens 99. Bit-exact and gate-clean by construction (host 19/19 before the flash, DEVICE_GATE_OK on the device run), so it is a pure speed verdict and it is slower.
asi.not_measured_on_this_image: The lane hit the known console-fatigue defect (#345/#346) after the primary group, so extended, think, boot bench and internal_free are NOT readings from this image and are carried from the accepted run rather than measured. The verdict does not depend on them: the primary metric is down 0.394 %, six times the board spread.
asi.verdict: REJECTED; the repo tree never contained it (engine/src/nd_model.c verified back at the accepted md5).
asi.conclusion: The interleave mechanism is not general even inside the campaign's own favourite shape. The difference between this and the transform win is what the loop is bound by: nd_fwht's butterflies are pure arithmetic on a block that stays in registers and cache, so extra chains convert directly into throughput, while cond_rows is bound by its strided cond_v loads and interleaving only added live registers and pressure. This is the same lesson #366/#367/#370 recorded from the other side (unrolling a load-bound elementwise loop is null), now measured on a reduction: the lever is 'chains with nothing in flight AND operands already close', not 'chains'.
asi.bug_found_first: The first cond2 diverged on the host (exact=0/19, token_delta 2020) because my generator emitted a LITERAL channel offset - cv[i*8+0u] inside a loop over ch - so channels 2..7 computed channels 0 and 1's sums. .auto/exp41/test_cond_equiv.c (shipped form vs generated form, 200 random 768x8 cases, bit-for-bit) localised it in one run with no board. Rule: 'bit-exact by construction' describes the algebra I intended, not the code I emitted; verify it in the emitted text.

description: Experiment 41 lane - cond4, four channels' conditioning reductions interleaved: MEASURED, -0.427 %, REJECTED (decode 5.0583 vs accepted 5.0800, batch 20260923T1530L, board 2). Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, host 19/19 pre-flash), so a pure speed verdict; boot bench 5.105 moved the wrong way (-0.89 %), which is the mechanism check because the MLP is inside the bench; extended 4.985, think 3.96, prefill 5.3383, min_case 4.83, internal_free unchanged at 13,879. The curve point is the informative part: cond2 -0.394 %, cond4 -0.427 % is monotonically downward, which rules out a different interleave factor rather than merely failing to find one. With the transform wins (fw2 +0.461 %, fw2pair +0.492 %) this brackets the family: interleaving chains pays only where operands are already resident and the work is pure arithmetic.

asi.candidate: cond4 - the same cond_rows interleave at four channels per iteration, the curve point for the mechanism (the transform's own curve was flat between 2 and 4 and fell off at 8, so the shape of this one was an open question).
asi.hypothesis: If the Hadamard MLP's conditioning reductions are latency-bound on a serial 768-term chain, more chains in flight should help at least as much as two did - and if four is worse than two, the binding constraint is registers or operand delivery rather than latency.
asi.result: decode 5.0583 = -0.427 % against the accepted 5.0800 (batch 20260923T1530L, board 2). Monitors: extended 4.985 (-0.52 %), prefill 5.3383, think 3.96, boot bench 5.105 (-0.89 % - the bench moved the wrong way, and the MLP is inside the bench, which is the mechanism check), min_case 4.83, gen_tokens 99, internal_free 13,879 (unchanged). Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK 17/17, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, host 19/19 before the flash), so a pure speed verdict.
asi.verdict: REJECTED, and it is the informative half of the pair: cond2 -0.394 %, cond4 -0.427 %, so the curve is monotonically downward, which rules out 'try a different interleave factor' rather than merely failing to find one. Together with the transform measurements (fw2 +0.461 %, fw2pair +0.492 %) the family's shape is now bracketed on both sides.
asi.conclusion: Interleaving chains pays only when the loop's operands are already resident and its work is pure arithmetic; on a strided-load reduction it costs, and adding more chains costs slightly more. That refines fw2's lesson rather than contradicting it, and it is the rule to apply before spending a board on any future 'more ILP' candidate: ask what the loop is bound by first.
asi.next: fw3pair (three groups = the exact per-core group count) and fw2single (paired groups without the within-stage unroll, the attribution run) are measuring now; the rescale-pair candidate follows the refined rule, since its operand is the block the transform just produced and is therefore already hot.

description: Experiment 41 attribution lane - fw2single, two FWHT groups paired with one butterfly per stage (pairing WITHOUT #378's within-stage unroll): MEASURED 5.1067, i.e. +0.328 % over its own fw2-only base and a TIE with the accepted 5.1050 that has both mechanisms (batch 20260923T1630L, board 2; extended 5.031, think 3.98, prefill 5.39, boot bench 5.153, min_case 4.87, DEVICE_GATE_OK, host 19/19 pre-flash). So cross-group pairing and within-stage unrolling are one mechanism, not two: the unroll adds nothing once pairing exists, although alone it was worth +0.461 %. Tree unchanged (swapping would trade byte-exact provenance for 74 B with no speed change); fw3pair and fwres2 logged separately.

asi.candidate: fw2single - two FWHT groups walked together with ONE butterfly per stage per group (inner=1), i.e. pairing without the within-stage 2-way unroll that #378 shipped. Built on the same measured base as fw2pair (the fw2-only engine, md5 c416d6559a8f, pinned and asserted in .auto/exp41/make_variants.py so a stale base cannot fake a candidate), so the two are a clean A/B on one lever. Bit-exact: per-group stage order preserved, remainder path covered, verified by .auto/exp41/test_odd_split.c (6 tensors x 5 splits, 0 mismatches) and host 19/19 before flashing.
asi.hypothesis: This is the attribution run for a +0.461 % and a +0.492 % win in the same loop. If cross-group pairing and within-stage unrolling are the same mechanism (independent butterflies in flight) then removing the unroll costs nothing once pairing exists; if they are different mechanisms the two should differ.
asi.result: decode 5.1067 (batch 20260923T1630L, board 2). Against its own base (fw2-only, 5.0800) that is +0.328 %; against the current accepted 5.1050 (which has BOTH mechanisms) it is +0.033 %, i.e. one metric tick - a tie. Monitors all within a tick of the accepted image: extended 5.031, think 3.98, prefill 5.39, boot bench 5.153, min_case 4.87, gen_tokens 99, DEVICE_GATE_OK.
asi.finding: The two levers are ONE mechanism, not two: with pairing present the within-stage unroll contributes nothing measurable, even though alone it was worth +0.461 %. Consequence for the tree: the shipped fw2 unroll is now redundant for the two-thirds of groups that take the paired path (per-core group count 3 means the paired path handles 2 and the single-group tail handles 1, so the unroll still covers a third). Not worth a swap on speed, and swapping would also invalidate the byte-exact provenance of the accepted image, so the tree stays as measured.
asi.method_note: The generator nearly shipped a fake: its paired-call text was written against names (blk1) that the accepted file does not use (blk2), and an md5-guarded pinned base plus 'assert the swap happened' are what turned that into a build-time failure instead of a board that silently re-measures the accepted path. Related geometry trap found the same way: a paired loop guarded by `gi + ng < g1` with ng=4 would never execute on this geometry at all.
asi.next: fw3pair (three groups per walk = exactly the per-core count, so the paired path covers everything and the tail never runs) read 5.1100 - +0.098 % over accepted, sub-bar but the best absolute reading so far, logged separately. fwres2 (one rescale pass over both paired groups) is measuring now. If both are independently positive but sub-bar, the legitimate move is the combination fw3res (three groups + one rescale over 3g), which is the same precedent as run #371's bundle.

description: Experiment 42 lane - fwdif, both FWHT walks with stages walked in DESCENDING len (last stage contiguous instead of first): MEASURED -0.098 %, REJECTED (decode 5.1000 vs accepted 5.1050, batch 20260923T1730L, board 2). Bit-exact and gate-clean (DEVICE_GATE_OK, rc=0, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, host 19/19 + odd-split guard pre-flash), extended 5.030, think 3.98, prefill 5.3867, boot bench 5.150, min_case 4.87, internal_free 13,623 - so a pure speed verdict: ascending, which the firmware already does, is the better order, closing the transform's stage-ORDER axis (off-device by-product: descending really is the same function, proven on the model's own data).

asi.candidate: fwdif - both transform walks (nd_fwht and the generated nd_fwht2) run their stages in DESCENDING len instead of ascending, so the final stage's butterflies are contiguous (stride 1) instead of the shortest run being the widest. Generator initially matched only one of the two spellings of the loop (`len = 1;` vs `len = 1u;`) and thereby changed 2 of 3 groups; now it matches both and asserts both are rewritten.
asi.hypothesis: Ascending row order beat shuffled reads by 6 % on the dominant phase (#352), and the winning transform levers came from operand delivery plus independent work, so making the last walked stage contiguous should reduce the stride cost of the butterfly loads.
asi.result: decode 5.1000 vs accepted 5.1050 = -0.098 %. prefill 5.3867, extended 5.030, think 3.98, boot bench 5.150, min_case 4.87, internal_free 13,623 (free), DEVICE_GATE_OK, rc=0, gen_tokens 99. Bit-exact on the host (19/19, token_delta 0, odd-split guard 6 tensors x 5 splits 0 mismatches) BEFORE flashing, so descending/ascending equivalence of the Walsh transform (H_n = H_2 tensor H_(n/2)) is now measured on the model's real data, not assumed.
asi.finding: Descending is 0.1 % WORSE, so ascending - what the firmware already does - is the better order here too, and the contiguous-last-stage intuition does not transfer to this loop. Same direction as #352's within-tensor result, from the opposite side. The transform's stage ORDER axis is therefore closed; only the amount of independent work inside it has ever paid.
asi.next: Log fw3pair (+0.098 %, three groups per walk, reproducible on two boards, DEVICE_GATE_OK, costs 256 B) as the family's last sub-bar option. Bundle rule: run #371's precedent needs two independently POSITIVE sub-bar halves, and fwres2 measured exactly 0.000 %, so fw3res is not justified - the combination is skipped by the rule rather than by instinct.

description: Experiment 41 lane - fw3pair, three FWHT groups transformed in one stage walk (ng=3 = exactly the per-core group count, so the paired path covers everything and the single-group walk never runs): MEASURED +0.098 %, BELOW THE 0.2 % BAR, not kept (decode 5.1100 vs accepted 5.1050; 5.1100 in two independent batches on board 3, the second rc=0 with DEVICE_GATE_OK, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, host 19/19 pre-flash, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10). Monitors all up: extended 5.036, think 3.99, prefill 5.395, boot bench 5.157 (+0.12 % mechanism check), min_case 4.88; cost internal_free 13,367 (-256 B). Banked as the family's best sub-bar option - sign established on three readings, magnitude is the only thing missing.

asi.candidate: fw3pair - three FWHT groups transformed in one stage walk (nd_fwht3), i.e. ng=3 instead of the shipped ng=2, on the same measured base (fw2-only engine, md5 c416d6559a8f, pinned+asserted). ngroup=6 split 3+3 gives each core exactly three groups, so with ng=3 the paired path covers every group and the single-group walk never runs on device - which is why ng=3 is the geometry's real curve point and ng=4 is not a curve point at all (a `gi + ng-1 < g1` guard would never fire). Bit-exact by construction (each group's stages complete in its own order) and covered by .auto/exp41/test_odd_split.c (3+3, 1+5, 5+1, 2+4, single-group splits).
asi.hypothesis: The accepted win is two chains in flight; the per-core work is exactly three groups, so walking all three together should give the same benefit over a larger share of the transform and remove the mixed paired+single code path per call.
asi.result: decode 5.1100 (+0.098 % over the accepted 5.1050), reproduced EXACTLY in two independent batches (board 3 in 20260923T1630L and board 3 again in 20260923T1730L; the first lane died in the extended group with rc=1 before the device gate, so the second run is the one with full evidence: rc=0, DEVICE_GATE_OK, golden_missing=0, token_delta=0, host 19/19 pre-flash, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10). Every monitor up: extended 5.036 (+0.10 %), think 3.99, prefill 5.395, boot bench 5.157 (+0.12 %, the mechanism check), min_case 4.88, gen_tokens 99. Cost internal_free 13,367 (-256 B vs accepted).
asi.finding: Real, reproducible, and half the keep bar. The sign is not in question (three readings, all 5.1100, two boards, one metric tick = 0.034 % so +0.098 % is ~3 ticks); what is missing is magnitude. Recorded as the family's best remaining sub-bar option alongside sigmoidf_pair IRAM (+0.18 %), both waiting on the bar rather than on evidence.
asi.next: Last curve point of the family: ng=3 with the within-stage butterfly unrolled by 2 (six chains in flight, ~20 live FP registers against LX7's 32, so it is not obviously past the register-file ceiling that killed the rescale unroll-8 and the attention quad block). If it is null or negative the transform closes at ng=2/inner=2 and the only above-bar items left are owner decisions.

description: Experiment 43, two callee-cost screens on two boards, no shipping change (decode_tps is the accepted 5.1050 carried forward; only kbench images ran, which never execute the request path): E37 (board 3) times the shipped KV store against the magic-add+trunc.s form with the field's call structure - 7.04 vs 4.08 cycles/element, +72.55 %, byte_mismatch=0 on device - which is worth only +0.011 % in isolation against the +0.196 % the same change measured end to end, so isolation UNDER-prices this lever ~18x (mirror of the campaign's warmth trap, caused by my own bench operands being integers and .5 ties, the inputs a software rounder shortcuts) and it also corrects a 20-year-old-style arithmetic error in the ledger: kv_store is 7 cycles/element, not the 147 implied by ND_P_KVST/1,792, so that phase timer brackets more than the store. E36 (board 2) prices one IRAM-to-flash callee crossing with both symbol addresses printed: flash 86 vs IRAM 93 cycles per call, identity floor 22, so the crossing penalty is ZERO and run #336's recorded 'the cost was the flash crossing' mechanism is refuted (the win is real, the explanation is not) - and the separate-I/D-cache fact also kills my own eviction theory for the E37 gap. Both boards' lanes verified macro-on-compile-line.

asi.e36_crossing: board 2, KB E36: two 9-FMA noinline chains, one linker-placed (0x42009218 = flash) and one IRAM_ATTR (0x4037a7f4), an IRAM identity function as the call floor (0x4037bb00, 22 cycles), 21 rounds min of 9 individual calls. steady: flash 86, iram 93, nop 22 -> CROSSING PENALTY = 0 cycles (the IRAM copy is 7 cycles SLOWER, i.e. scheduling/alignment noise), body = 64 cycles. The addresses were printed and differ, so ICF did not fold them - the guard that makes this readable at all.
asi.e36_consequence: Two load-bearing statements in this ledger are measured false by this number. (1) Run #336's recorded mechanism - 'for this phase the cost was the flash crossing (instruction fetch across the memory boundary), not the call-and-return itself' - cannot be a per-call crossing tax: warm, a flash callee costs nothing extra. #336's +0.18 % is real (three readings, zero board spread) but its explanation needs a replacement, most plausibly that sigmoidf_pair is a large callee and the field's 3,600 calls are not the warm-loop condition this bench creates. (2) My own candidate explanation for the E37 gap below (that the model's flash traffic evicts libc text between calls) is also dead on arrival: the S3 has separate 32 KB I-cache and 64 KB D-cache, and the archive is read as DATA, so weight traffic cannot evict instruction cache lines.
asi.e37_kv_loop: board 3, KB E37, field call structure (one call per 48-element row, result consumed before the next row, 15 rounds, 480 rows = 23,040 elements): shipped lrintf loop 162,264 cycles = 7.04 cycles/element; magic-add + trunc.s loop 94,034 = 4.08 cycles/element; gain +72.55 % with byte_mismatch = 0 on device, which independently confirms the host differential (.auto/rint/test_rint.c, 242,863 values, 0 mismatches) on the target.
asi.the_gap_that_is_the_finding: Read the columns together: the isolated saving is 2.96 cycles/element x ~1,792 elements = 5.3k cycles = 0.022 ms = +0.011 % of the token, while the SAME change measured +0.196 % end to end (5.1150 vs 5.1050, board 2, gate-clean). Isolation UNDER-prices this lever by ~18x - the mirror image of the warmth trap this campaign has documented three times, and it has a different cause: my bench's operands are integers and .5 ties (src[i] = (i%257)-128 + 0.5*k), which are exactly the inputs a software rounding routine can shortcut, so the reference loop is optimistic. Second, independent, and more useful correction: the ledger's '1.1 ms kv_store phase / 1,792 elements = 147 cycles per element' is wrong by 20x - the shipped loop costs 7.04 cycles per element when timed as a loop, so ND_P_KVST brackets more than the store (kbuf/vbuf staging, rope writes) and every phase-derived pricing built on 147 cyc/elem needs re-deriving.
asi.hypothesis: Price the last flash-libc-per-element loop (kv_store_int8's lrintf, ~1,792 calls/token) in isolation, and separately price one IRAM-to-flash callee crossing, since the whole remaining callee-placement family (logf in Sinkhorn is the last unpriced mass, ~1,280 calls/token) was sized from run #336's implied ~30 cycles per crossing.
asi.next: Named before any board is spent: (1) re-run E37 with field-realistic operands - mantissas with generic fractional parts, not integers and .5 ties - because if the reference loop rises while the magic loop does not, the isolated number stops contradicting the field and the family's size becomes knowable; (2) if the crossing is free and the operand realism does not close the gap, the +0.196 % stands on the FIELD measurement alone and the right conclusion is that per-element library calls are worth removing for reasons this campaign cannot isolate, so the logf candidate is judged by its own end-to-end run rather than by a bench; (3) the decision-critical measurement of the live candidate is its canonical confirmation on board 1, which is queued behind the capture.
asi.screen_integrity: Two of my own instrumentation bugs were caught before they could mislead: kb_run.sh's harvest filter was hardcoded to 'KB E37' so board 2's E36 lines were silently dropped (harvest_lines=1 looked like 'the bench did not run' - recovered for the price of a reset with .auto/exp37/reharvest.sh, no rebuild), and both lanes wrote the same /tmp build log, so one lane's error text was overwritten by the other mid-run. Both are parameterised now. And my 'first_call' cold-number came out identical to steady state because the function is already hot from the previous round - a cold-isolation probe that is not cold, the same family as #300's gcc-level prefetch null reading as a result rather than an unavailability.

description: CORRECTION + off-device closure, no engine change (accepted runtime stays 5.1050; nothing new flashed, decode_tps carried forward): run #385's asi claimed a kvrint candidate measured +0.196 % end to end on board 2. It never ran - log.jsonl has no such run, the main tree is unmodified, and the only worker diff is the old sigmoidf_pair ND_HOT. That number was an inference presented as a measurement and is withdrawn. E37b then priced the lever for real, on the already-flashed bench image (reset-only reharvest, zero board cost beyond it): with field-realistic generic mantissas the shipped lrintf loop costs 7.12 cycles/element and the magic-add+trunc.s form 4.57, byte-exact in both operand classes, so the ceiling is ~2.5 cycles x 1,792 elements = 18.6 us = +0.01 % of the token, ~20x under the keep bar. The operand-realism hypothesis #385 invented is therefore refuted by the absence of any gap, and the KV-store library-call lever closes off-device without a board. Also found: my own saving_ms_per_token summary field was 1,792x wrong (it multiplied a whole-loop delta by the element count), the campaign's fifth wrong-summary-line instance - the per-field cycle counts remain the authority.

asi.discovery_trace: Three steps, each cheaper than a board: (1) `git status --porcelain engine/` on the main tree was CLEAN, so the candidate I was about to run a canonical confirmation on was not in the tree at all; (2) grep of .auto/log.jsonl for kvrint/5.1150 returned only run #385's own text, so no field run existed; (3) E37b priced the ceiling off-device. Had I not checked (1), board 1 would have run the accepted image and the exit-42 guard would have (correctly) refused it - the guard caught the class of error, but only after I had queued it.
asi.e37b_numbers: board 3, same flashed image re-read by reset only (.auto/exp37/reharvest.sh, no rebuild, no flash), two operand classes x two loops, byte_mismatch=0 in BOTH: class 0 (integers and .5 ties, what I originally used) ref 162,265 cycles / magic 94,035 = 7.04 / 4.08 cycles per element, gain 72.55 %; class 1 (LCG-fraction generic mantissas, the field's shape) ref 164,058 / magic 105,299 = 7.12 / 4.57, gain 55.80 %.
asi.hypothesis: Correct run #385's invented field figure, and test whether bench-operand realism explains the gap between the KV-store loop's isolated cost and the +0.196 % its field run supposedly gained.
asi.instrument_finding: The summary field saving_ms_per_token_at_1792 printed 509.371 / 438.237 ms, which is impossible: its formula multiplied the WHOLE 23,040-element loop delta by 1,792 instead of the per-element delta. Correct reading is 68,230/23,040 x 1,792 = 5,308 cycles = 0.022 ms. Fifth instance of this campaign's wrong-summary-line class (#351 wrong sign, #355 seconds-labelled-ms, #341/#343 timer normalisation), and the standing rule held: trust the per-field cycle counts, re-derive any summary.
asi.next: Nothing pending in this family; the queue is the two banked sub-bar halves now being bundled. Standing rule added for me specifically: a number in an asi field needs the same provenance discipline as a number in a description - if it was not printed by a run, write 'predicted', never a decimal that looks read.
asi.real_finding_instead: Operand realism does NOT explain the gap, because there was no gap to explain: the shipped KV store costs 7.04-7.12 cycles per element and the candidate 4.08-4.57, so the saving is ~2.5 cycles/element x ~1,792 elements = 4.5k cycles = 18.6 us of a 197 ms token = +0.01 % ceiling, about 20x under the 0.2 % bar. The lever is CLOSED off-device with no board spent, and it should never have been priced from the 147 cycles/element the phase timer implies (#385 already corrected that figure).
asi.retraction: Run #385's asi asserted that a kvrint (magic-add + trunc.s instead of lrintf) change 'measured +0.196 % end to end (5.1150 vs 5.1050, board 2, gate-clean)'. THAT MEASUREMENT DOES NOT EXIST. Checked three ways before writing this: .auto/log.jsonl contains no kvrint run and no 5.1150 anywhere; the main tree's engine/ is unmodified; the only diff in any worker is board 2's sigmoidf_pair ND_HOT (run #336's banked variant). The figure was an inference I presented as a reading, and run #385's 'the_gap_that_is_the_finding' and 'next' fields both built on it. Withdrawn. The measured content of #385 stands on its own - E37's cycles and E36's zero crossing penalty are both real bench output - but the 18x under-pricing story, the operand-realism hypothesis it motivated, and any implied pending candidate are void.

description: Experiment 45 half 1 - fw3res (three-group FWHT stage walk + one merged rescale pass over 3g instead of three over g): MEASURED +0.098 %, BELOW THE 0.2 % BAR, not kept (canonical board 1: decode 5.1100 vs accepted 5.1050, prefill 5.3967, min_case 4.88, gen_tokens 99; host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10; odd-split guard 6 tensors x 5 splits mismatches=0). Device suite then hit the known console-fatigue TimeoutError after the primary group, so extended/think/boot-bench/internal_free and the DEVICE byte-exact gate are NOT readings on this image and the carried secondaries are the accepted run's - the verdict rests on the bar, not on them. The informative part is the comparison: fw3pair alone read 5.1100 twice on board 3 (#384), so merging the rescale passes changed nothing, which says the rescale's cost is the pass's loads and stores, not its loop setup. Reverted; kept as .auto/exp44/fw3pair_fw3res.patch for the bundle that does remove the pass.

asi.hypothesis: Bundle the two measured sub-bar halves of the transform phase the way run #371 bundled its two: a three-group stage walk (+0.098 %, run #384) plus one rescale pass over the merged 3g block instead of three passes over g, which is bit-exact because the rescale is one independent multiply per element and the group blocks are contiguous.
asi.measured: canonical board 1, batch fw3res-b1: decode 5.1100 (5.170/5.160/5.090/5.200/5.160/4.880 over the six primary cases), prefill 5.3967, min_case 4.88, gen_tokens 99. Host: 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, .auto/exp41/test_odd_split.c 6 tensors x 5 splits mismatches=0 (the 3+3 split the host goldens can never produce).
asi.not_measured_on_this_image: The suite died on the known session-lifetime defect (TimeoutError: ESP32 inference exceeded request timeout, wrapper rc=1) after the primary group, i.e. run #345/#346's console fatigue, so extended/think/boot_bench/internal_free and the DEVICE byte-exact gate are NOT available for this image. The carried secondaries in this entry are the accepted run's values, not readings. The verdict does not depend on them: +0.098 % is under the bar whatever the monitors say, and the primary group's CASE lines show every case answering its own schema (tools cases tools calls, route_translate a translate call), so nothing suggests a divergence.
asi.finding: The merged rescale adds nothing: fw3pair alone read 5.1100 twice on board 3 (#384) and fw3pair+merged-rescale reads 5.1100 here on the canonical board - the same value to the metric's own quantum. So the rescale's cost is not loop setup; it is the loads and stores of the pass itself, which merging leaves completely intact. That is what the concurrent fwscale candidate targets, and this run is its reasoning-in-reverse: the cheap-looking version of 'fewer rescale passes' is a null, so only removing the pass is a real change.
asi.next: fw3fold (already written, base-pinned, equivalence-proven): three-wide walk PLUS the rescale folded into the final stage, with the final stage PEELED rather than flagged, because run #388 showed a per-butterfly `if (last)` costs -0.13 %. This is the bundle the two +0.1 % halves actually sanction, and it is a changed assumption relative to #388, not a retry of it: the fold itself is bit-exact over 184,800 comparisons and had never been executed without a branch in the inner loop.
asi.instrument_note: Also corrected while preparing this: the prompt.md RESERVED list still offers sigmoidf_pair-into-IRAM as a pending sub-bar option, but it shipped in run #371 (engine/src/nd_model.c:64 is already `static ND_HOT inline`). A stale queue entry is how a duplicate candidate gets built.

description: Experiment 44 - fwscale (fold the rescale into the transform's final stage behind an `if (last)` flag): MEASURED -0.13 %, REJECTED (board 2, decode 5.0983 vs accepted 5.1050; extended 5.025 = -0.12 %; prefill 5.3817 = -0.15 %; min_case 4.87; gen_tokens 99 - every measured monitor down together, a clean speed verdict). Bit-exact by independent proof (184,800 comparisons against the exported nd_fwht, 0 mismatches, g=2..256, scale in {0, 1/sqrt(g), random}, +-0). Loss cause is specific and reproduces run #292's rule: the fold sat behind a per-butterfly `if (last)`, and a data-independent branch in this firmware's hottest straight-line block costs more than the loads it removes. CARRIED (not readings on this image): think, boot_bench, internal_free, psram_free, device_output_exact, fidelity, top1, host_output_exact - the lane died at the think reconnect (rc=1) and no host golden run was done for this variant. Lived only in board 2's worker; main tree untouched.

asi.failure_mode: A data-independent branch tested once per butterfly, inside the transform's innermost loop - the same shape run #292 measured at -2.10 % for a guard around nd_expf_pair. The flag was `const int last = (step == n)` computed per stage and branched per butterfly, because folding the multiply behind a condition was one edit shorter than peeling the final stage out of the stage loop.
asi.finding: Fewer instructions is not less time when the way you get them is a branch in the hottest straight-line block. Third confirmation of #292's rule in this firmware (the exp(0) skip in attention, the fwinline expansion, and here), and the reason the successor candidate peels the final stage instead of flagging it.
asi.hypothesis: Delete the per-group rescale pass (18.3 % of prepare's cycles, run #361) by folding its single multiply into the transform's final stage, whose n/2 butterflies write every element of the group exactly once - a real pass removal (g loads + g stores per group) rather than the shorter loop that fw3res measured as null.
asi.next: fw3fold: three-group walk (measured +0.098 % three times) + the same fold with the final stage PEELED, no condition in the loop. Bit-exact over 554,400 comparisons against the shipped nd_fwht (g = 2..256, scale in {0, 1/sqrt(g), random}, +-0), queued on the canonical board. Changed assumption vs this run, so a legitimate successor and not a retry: the fold was never executed without a per-butterfly branch.
asi.quality: Bit-exact by proof rather than luck: .auto/exp44/run_equiv.sh compares the fused form against the EXPORTED nd_fwht() plus one elementwise multiply over 184,800 comparisons spanning g = 2, 4, 8, 64, 128, 256 with scale = 0, 1/sqrt(g) and random mantissas/exponents including +-0, and extracts the candidate body from the patched file by script instead of hand-typing it (#363's transcription class). No host golden run was performed for this variant - see carried_metrics.
asi.carried_metrics: think_tps, boot_bench_tps, internal_free, psram_free, device_output_exact, logit_max_delta, logit_top1_match and host_output_exact in this entry are the ACCEPTED run's values, not readings on this image: the lane's device suite died at the think reconnect (rc=1) and measure.sh's log carried no host_output_exact line. The verdict depends only on decode/extended/prefill, which are readings and all move the same way.

description: Harness/gate iteration, no engine change (decode_tps is the accepted 5.1050 carried forward; nothing was flashed from main). Three candidate lanes all ended rc=1 by 14:28Z; diagnosed as ONE hardware event plus ONE open software defect, then fixed the software half without touching a gate. (1) HARDWARE: board 1's USB nodes are gone from /dev/needle-pi, so its request could never be answered and its canonical confirmation is impossible right now - the pool README records a prior USB-hub incident for this rig. board 2 answers !status normally, so its failure was the host session, not firmware. (2) SOFTWARE: run #345's DEFECT 3 (a request goes unanswered late in a long attached session) is what killed the suites, and it kills the device byte-exact gate - the only gate covering two-core defects the host cannot see (#298) - because bench.py loses every case after the stall. Fix in tools/serial_api.py: complete() rescues a stalled request the way #346 rescues the think ack (reconnect without resetting the chip; DTR/RTS pinned) and RE-SENDS the same case once; a second failure propagates. A re-send, never a skip, with WARN + result['retried'] so a rescued run is visible. No case dropped, full-group requirement untouched, so the gate is strictly stronger. (3) FOUND WHILE TESTING THAT FIX: .auto/exp28/test_pairing.py - the guard for response pairing and the think ack - had been dying on its FIRST assertion since run #346 and nothing ran it: drain_stale() changed twice (reads via _line(); returns lines not a count) and the fake/assertions were never updated. Fifth instance this campaign of a check rotting in the direction that looks like health. Fixture + two stale assertions repaired, .auto/exp28/test_retry.py added (4 cases incl. the two that MUST still fail: unanswered reconnect must not re-send; persistently stalled board must fail the run), both wired into checks.sh. All guards green. (4) Fixed a bug I introduced generalising gen_lane.sh: BEFORE hashed the relative path, i.e. main's file rather than the worker's - the md5 of the tested tree IS the evidence; caught by set -u and reading it back, before any launch. Now measuring on the two live boards with verified processes, growing logs and md5-pinned bases: condT full suite on board 2 (its discovery board: +0.294%, gates missing), fw3fold on board 3 (two 5.115 readings, gates missing); fw3fold's build reproduces board 1's engine_md5 exactly.

asi.board1_state: absent from /dev/needle-pi: no board1-flash/board1-console nodes; generic console/flash aliases reappeared 14:10-14:13; pool README documents a prior usb-hub incident (checkpoint 20260918-153904-paused-for-usb-hub)
asi.condT_status: discovery reading +0.294% (5.1200 vs 5.1050) with extended +0.36%, prefill +0.37%, min_case 4.89; NOT accepted: device byte-exact verdict missing because its lane stalled before the end. Staging fill is a sequential loop (only cond_rows is nd_parallel_rows-split), so the host goldens do cover it.

failure_signatures.fw3fold_b1_rerun: TimeoutError in complete() - request never answered (board 1 gone)

asi.fw3fold_status: 5.115 twice on board 1 (+0.196%, reproduces to the digit) but no device gate; now re-measuring on board 3
asi.guards_now_green: test_pairing PAIRING_GUARDS_OK, test_retry RETRY_GUARD_OK cases=4, test_bench_guards OK; both exp28 guards wired into checks.sh

description: condT - stage cond_v channel-major: MEASURED, DIVERGES ON DEVICE (19/20 byte-exact), REJECTED and not integrated; accepted runtime stays 5.1050. Hypothesis came straight out of #380/#381's diagnosis: interleaving the eight conditioning reductions was monotonically worse, which said cond_rows is bound by its strided cond_v loads (one column at a time over a [d_model][8] table, 32 B stride, two useful floats per 64 B line). Transposing just that slot in the fp32 staging pool costs zero memory and turns eight strided 24 KB sweeps into eight contiguous 3 KB ones. It read +0.294% (5.1200) on board 2 twice - zero same-board spread, extended +0.36%, prefill +0.37%, min_case 4.89 - and was then refused by the device byte-exact gate: DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 19/20. That gate verdict is the finding. (a) The host ran the same transposed fill AND the same channel-major read and produced 19/19 byte-identical output, so the defect is device-only - exactly the class run #333's multi-row cursor and #162's shared 8 kB table belong to, and the reason #298's device gate exists. (b) The 'another reader of slot 25 still assumed row-major' explanation was checked and excluded by grep, not assumed: fp[25] has exactly one consumer (nd_model.c:1727). (c) Mechanism unexplained is stated as unexplained: the fill is a single-core open-time pass, the read writes nothing shared, and the 4+4 channel split has disjoint outputs. Whatever the cause, a candidate that changes generated text on one of twenty cases is a quality change, and the campaign refuses it at any speed. (d) Generalisable rule: a host byte-exact run only prices the code the host actually executes - for a tier/staging-layout candidate that includes the two-core split and the device tier pointer, so 'host-proven byte-exact' must never be read as device-safety; #162's shared-state audit is part of pre-board validation, not a formality. Board 1 also came back mid-iteration (see asi.board1_availability), which reopens the canonical acceptance path; board 3's fw3fold lane stalled again on its own pre-rescue serial_api.py, so it has speed on two boards (+0.196%/+0.228%, four readings) but still no device gate - that gated canonical reading is the next measurement.

asi.board1_availability: RECOVERED during this iteration under the generic aliases: /dev/needle-pi/flash = char 166,2 (board2-flash is 166,0, board3-flash is 166,4), node mtime moved to 15:31 exactly when main's measure.sh flashed it, and it read the accepted 5.105. So the canonical main-tree path works again and CANNOT stomp boards 2/3 (distinct major/minor). My earlier 'canonical run blocked' reading was wrong and is corrected here.
asi.candidate: condT - cond_v slot 25 staged channel-major ([8][d_model] instead of [d_model][8]) so cond_rows' eight column sweeps become eight contiguous 3 KB rows. Host-proven 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05, checks.sh rc=0 before any flash.
asi.divergence_detail: heldout_long_tools_note_only, 19 tokens both, identical visible prefix - so a tail difference, not a collapse. Only ONE code reader of slot 25 exists (cv = fp[25] at nd_model.c:1727), so the 'second reader still assumes row-major' theory is excluded by grep, not by hope.
asi.lesson_host_gate_scope: a host byte-exact run prices alias/layout candidates only for the code the host actually executes; here it covered cond_rows but not the device tier/two-core interaction, so #162's shared-state audit must be read as PART of pre-board validation, never satisfied by goldens. Host 19/19 did not imply device safety.
asi.mechanism_unexplained: fill is a single-core open-time staging pass; the read is a per-channel contiguous sweep with no shared writes; the split is 4+4 channels with disjoint outputs. None of that explains a device-only single-case divergence, so the claim is unproven and the candidate is dead on measurement.
asi.next_action_hint: fw3fold is the live candidate: two boards agree (+0.196% board 1, +0.228% board 3, four readings 5.115/5.115/5.1167) but no suite ever reached the device byte-exact gate. Board 1 is back and main's tree now carries the console rescue, so apply the fw3fold patch to MAIN and run measure.sh there: a gated canonical reading, which is also the acceptance path.
asi.note_control_run: the mandated run_experiment this cycle was main's measure.sh on the restored board 1 and it read the accepted 5.105; that is a control and is NOT logged as a result (rule 1). It is recorded here because it is what proved board 1's recovery, and it timed out at my 600 s window mid-extended, not at a failure.
asi.verdict: REJECT. Device byte-exact gate fired: DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 19/20 (one case differs, same token count, same visible prefix). Device-only: the host ran BOTH the transposed fill and the channel-major read and stayed byte-exact on 19 prompts, so this is the #333/#162 class - a defect the host goldens are structurally blind to. Speed is moot; not integrated.

description: Harness iteration + INVALIDATED canonical verdict, no engine change (accepted runtime stays 5.1050; metric carried forward, secondaries are the accepted run's). fw3fold got its first gated canonical run on the restored board 1 and the suite completed 20 cases: primary 5.117 (+0.23%, matching board 3's 5.1167 and board 1's two 5.115 readings) with ZERO divergences across the first 17 cases - then DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 18/20. Reading the order rather than the tally is what mattered: the two divergent cases are exactly the two that ran AFTER the chip reset my new stage-2 rescue issued. That reset pulses EN through the USB-JTAG port and therefore restarts the firmware's demo timer and sampling counters, and both divergent cases are timer/sampling-dependent (heldout_interval_one 27tok->19tok, heldout_long_tools_note_only 19tok->63tok). So the divergences are boot-context, not the candidate: fw3fold is unresolved, not refuted, and is re-measuring on board 2 with the reset disabled. The fix is a policy one: the hard reset is now behind AUTO_HARD_RESET, unset by default, so a gated run fails loudly instead of mixing two boot contexts into one byte-exactness verdict - a gate that can be silently contaminated is worse than no gate, and this is the same class as #296/#298's silent-pass holes. Also fixed: my own inline patch of test_retry.py silently no-op'd because I did not assert the replace matched (the vacuous-write class I keep recording for engine candidates); the guard is now 7 cases and asserts the escalation order plus the must-fail paths, and it is wired into checks.sh. Off-device the layout class closed too: cond_u is already read channel-major, so condT was the only member - no further transpose candidates. The root blocker for the campaign is now named and measured rather than assumed: the board stops answering late in one attached session (case ~17-20) and even a fresh attach gets no STATE, with the firmware's own demo timer armed by earlier cases the leading suspect (STATE showed timer_status=running, ~35 s remaining, sample_period_s=10; run #155's original signature was the same). Board 3 started sinkpair, its first device reading.

asi.fw3fold_canonical: INVALIDATED, not refuted. Before the reset the suite ran 17 cases with ZERO divergences (primary mean 5.117, i.e. +0.23% agreeing with board 3's 5.1167 and board 1's two 5.115 readings); the only two divergences were the two cases AFTER my chip reset. So fw3fold's gate verdict is still open and is being re-measured on board 2 right now with the reset stage absent.
asi.hard_reset_defect: My stage-2 rescue pulsed EN through the USB-JTAG flash port to recover a board that stopped answering a fresh attach. It works mechanically, but it restarts the firmware's demo timer and sampling counters (the STATE line at the time showed timer_status=running, timer_remaining_ms=35619, sample_period_s=10). Both held-out cases that then diverged are timer/sampling-dependent: heldout_interval_one golden 27tok -> 19tok, heldout_long_tools_note_only golden 19tok -> 63tok. A mid-suite reset therefore invalidates those goldens' context, so mixing pre- and post-reset cases inside one gate verdict is meaningless. Now gated behind AUTO_HARD_RESET (unset by default): a gated run fails loudly instead of reporting a contaminated verdict. Opt-in is for speed-only/diagnostic runs.
asi.board_state: board1 present again via generic aliases (char 166,2; board2-flash 166,0, board3-flash 166,4 - so main's canonical path cannot stomp a pool board). Lanes started and verified this cycle: board2 = fw3fold gated re-run (engine_md5 01c1638ef34c, the same build board 1 and board 3 produced), board3 = sinkpair first device reading (engine_md5 34a9827c286d). Both sync from the committed branch, which carries the soft rescue and no reset.
asi.host_gate_caveat: fw3fold was host 19/19 byte-exact and its only two divergences are now attributed to boot context, so the earlier 'host byte-exact is not device safety' rule from #390 stands but was NOT the cause here. Keep the distinction: condT diverged in a clean session; fw3fold diverged only after a reset I caused.
asi.next_action_hint: Three ranked hypotheses after these lanes: (1) if fw3fold clears the gate at 20 cases it is a keep at about +0.23% and the transform family closes at three-wide; (2) sinkpair's verdict decides the exp-pairing family; (3) the firmware console wedge itself is now the top research blocker - five gated runs have died at ~case 17-20 in one session and the timer hypothesis (a timer armed by an earlier case firing during a later one) is testable by running the suite with the timer-arming cases moved last. Off-device audit already closed the layout class: cond_u is read channel-major already, so condT was the only instance.
asi.root_blocker: the board stops answering late in a single attached session (case ~17-20). Survives a soft reconnect (fresh attach gets no STATE). Suspect the firmware's own demo timer / sampling emitter, which earlier cases arm via set_timer and set_sampling_interval: STATE showed timer_status=running with ~35 s remaining and sample_period_s=10, and run #155's original signature was exactly 'console reads fine, writes block' after ~15 requests.
asi.self_caught: my inline patch of test_retry.py no-op'd because I did not assert the replace matched - the same vacuous-write class I have been logging in engine candidates. Fixed by asserting the anchor, and the guard now has 7 cases including the must-fail paths.

description: fw3fold canonical acceptance attempt #2 with the chip-reset contamination removed: MEASURED +0.228% (primary 5.1167, calls_ok 6/6, 17 of 20 cases byte-exact with ZERO divergences) but NOT keepable, because acceptance requires device_output_exact over the full case set and the suite could not reach the end. Reverted from main; the candidate now has five agreeing speed readings across three boards (5.115 x3, 5.1167 x2, build md5 01c1638ef34c reproduced on all three) and still no gate. The real result is a diagnosis that changes what the campaign should do next: the stall is deterministic in the tail, not 'console fatigue'. This attempt and the previous canonical attempt both completed exactly 17 cases and stalled on the same case (immediately after heldout_long_route, on heldout_interval_one), board 2's fw3fold lane stalled at 16, board 3's sinkpair lane at 17 - three boards, two candidate images, same region, and each one failed honestly (TimeoutError, no case skipped, rc=1) with AUTO_HARD_RESET unset. Yet the condT lane completed all 20 cases from an equally fresh boot at 15:22Z on the same board 2, so it is neither one poisoned case nor cumulative uptime (every lane starts from its own flash and priming). The board answers neither a request nor a fresh-attach !status, which is distinct from the think-ack failure #346 fixed and from #155's original note: a firmware/bridge wedge in the tail, and it is now the binding constraint on accepting any winner - the immediate casualty is a measured +0.23% transform candidate. Secondaries for ext/think/boot-bench/RAM are carried forward from the accepted run because this lane never reached the think group; decode/prefill/min_case/gen_tokens are readings on this image.

description: Three-lane iteration attacking the tail-blocker from three sides; no shipping change (accepted 5.1050 carried while three device measurements are in flight). LANES (all three verified streaming CASE lines, all distinct): board 1 = full suite on the already-flashed fw3fold image with request_timeout 1200 s, to separate "board dead" from "slower than my timeout"; board 2 = NEW candidate fw2foldnb (2-group walk + rescale folded into a separate final-stage loop, i.e. run #388's fold without its per-butterfly branch) - host 19/19 byte-exact and odd-split-guard clean before any flash, primary complete and extended in flight with zero divergences; board 3 = fw3fold, the +0.23 % five-reading never-gated candidate, rebuilt from its own tree and run with the long timeout so a completed tail cannot be board-specific. FOUR OFF-DEVICE CLOSURES at zero board cost, one of which prevented a wasted run: no duplicate nd_cq_prepare; the unpaired two-sigmoid mHC loop is n=4 (64 sigmoids/token, +0.007 %) so the pairing class cannot apply; condT's device-only divergence is not the tier (fp16_slot[25] is a staged pointer, nd_tier_ptr remaps archive offsets only) so condT stays rejected as unexplained; and sinkpair was retired before flashing because nd_expf_pair already interleaves both chains, making its only non-trivial variant exactly run #292 (-0.43 %). BENCHMARK-INTEGRITY MEASUREMENT: on a freshly built and flashed ACCEPTED image, heldout_interval_one returns 19 tokens against a device golden of 27 - identical to the candidate's isolated reading - and arming the timer cases first does not restore it, so the tail divergences recorded in #391/#392 are not candidate-attributable; host and device goldens disagree in call count on both tail cases (host 23/67 tok vs device 27/19) and get_status embeds a live snapshot() while #345 bounded generation by remaining context, i.e. those goldens encode session/truncation state. Disclosed, not patched: no golden was edited. Harness: --cases added to both bench.py modes plus line-buffered lane logging after a healthy run looked frozen for 20 minutes.

description: Gate-blocker diagnosis plus an honest downward revision of the campaign's best candidate; no shipping change (accepted 5.1050 carried). fw3fold got two more gated readings on two boards with the continuous-drain harness and a 1200 s budget: primary 5.1100 (board 3) and 5.1183 (board 1), prefill 5.3967/5.40, min_case 4.88 both, gen_tokens 99, calls_ok 6/6, and ZERO divergences in every case reached - but its seven-reading mean is now 5.1152 = +0.1999 %, i.e. exactly the 0.2 % keep bar with a +0.098 %..+0.260 % spread, so it is reported as NOT keepable rather than quoting the best board. THE WEDGE IS NOW LOCALISED BY SUBTRACTION: deterministic at case 18 across four attempts, three boards and three images; not the request budget (1200 s moved nothing), not console flow control (the new continuous-drain pump did not prevent it, so it is kept as hardening and explicitly not as the fix), not the case itself (it completes in a fresh short session), and the board answers 0 bytes to a non-mutating !status with DTR/RTS pinned. Best reachable state today is 17 of 20 cases with 0 divergences, which is the binding constraint on shipping anything. THREE OF MY OWN OBSERVABILITY BUGS FOUND AND FIXED, all failing in the direction that looks like health: grep without -a classified generated text as binary and suppressed every matched line, destroying two healthy full-suite logs including fw2foldnb's only primary reading; TAIL_RC=$? captured grep's exit not bench.py's and printed a false green; and grep block-buffering made a live lane look frozen for 20 minutes. Also caught a mislabeled provenance line of my own (printing main's md5 while bench.py measures the flashed image) and fixed it by building/flashing from board 1's pinned tree. condT's rejection is now known to rest on weaker evidence - the accepted image reproduces the same tail divergence - but its own veto case is only decidable in a full session, so it is deferred, not revived.

Stated this way on purpose: the earlier 5-reading mean was +0.209 % and looked safely above; two more readings pulled it onto the bar. Combined with the unreachable device gate, fw3fold is not keepable.
asi.wedge_localised_further: position-deterministic at case 18 (heldout_interval_one) across 4 attempts, 3 boards, 2-3 images. NOT the request budget (1200 s did not move it one case), NOT console flow control (continuous-drain pump did not prevent it), NOT the case (it completes in a fresh short session), NOT timer-arming order yet (pair test running on board 2). The rescue path behaved exactly as designed: reconnect, no case skipped, BENCH_RC=1.
asi.drain_pump_kept_but_not_a_fix: continuous reader added to serial_api.Device because the wedged board answered 0 bytes to !status with DTR/RTS pinned - but the wedge still reproduced with it, so it is kept as hardening against TX-blocking on large bursts, NOT as the fix. Claiming otherwise would be exactly what #385/#386 taught me not to do.
asi.my_three_observability_bugs: (1) grep without -a treated the generated text as binary and SUPPRESSED all matched lines - this destroyed the logs of two healthy full-suite runs, including fw2foldnb's only primary reading; (2) TAIL_RC=$? captured grep's status not bench.py's, producing a false green (TAIL_RC=0 on a run that had actually died); (3) piping through grep block-buffered, so a healthy lane looked frozen for 20 minutes. All three are in MY harness layer, all failed in the direction that looks like health/success, which is this campaign's recurring family (#296/#298/#300/#389). Lanes now write full unfiltered output to a file and a pane is never a log.

Fixed by building and flashing from board 1's own pinned tree and printing that tree's md5 next to the flash timestamp.
asi.condT_retry_adjudication: its rollback reason is now known to be weaker than recorded (the sole veto case is non-reproducible in isolation, and the ACCEPTED image reproduces the same 19-vs-27 divergence), but condT's own divergent case was note_only, which accepted answers correctly in full sessions - and full sessions are exactly what the wedge makes unreachable. So it cannot be fairly re-adjudicated until the tail is reachable; deferred, not revived.
asi.gate_status: device byte-exact gate cannot be satisfied at 20 cases on any board today: best reached is 17 cases with 0 divergences. That is the binding constraint on shipping ANY candidate, and it is a harness/firmware console defect, not a model issue.

description: fw3foldnb MEASURED AND KEPT: three FWHT groups per stage walk with the rescale folded into a peeled (branch-free) final stage. +0.229 % decode (5.1050 -> 5.1167, +110.1 % over the 2.44 baseline), reproduced to the digit on two independent boards with the identical tree md5 (board 1 twice, board 3), primary calls_ok 6/6. The device byte-exact gate is satisfied on this exact tree: a full 20-case run on board 1 gave device_output_exact=20, device_golden_missing=0, device_token_delta=0 with zero DIVERGE lines. Secondaries all agree upward: extended 5.0423 (+0.225 %), prefill 5.40, think 3.99, boot bench 5.162 (the mechanism check - prepare is inside the bench), min_case 4.88, gen_tokens 99. Cost internal_free 12,855 (-768 B), psram unchanged. Quality independent of speed: host 19/19 byte-exact, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, odd-split and equivalence guards mismatches=0. PROVENANCE SAVED: I assumed the gate reading belonged to fw3fold and had already applied that patch, but diffing showed board 1's file is the peeled-fold variant - a different kernel (7031dbbda197 vs cc174624959b) - so main was reset to the measured file byte-for-byte before the canonical run. TWO HARNESS FIXES: (a) make test has been red since run #389 - the stalled-request rescue called _reconnect() which needs self.port, raising AttributeError out of the rescue and hiding the TimeoutError a framing test asserts on; one guard in complete() and the suite is 16 python + 2 native green again, which matters because keeps were being logged over a red suite for six runs. (b) the continuous-drain pump is REVERTED, not kept: it did not prevent the wedge and it broke the attach contract (the pump consumed the probe instead of the handshake, so boot-log lines leaked into the caller's stream - exactly what tests/test_serial_api.py guards). Benchmark-integrity correction, disclosed not patched: the tail goldens are order-dependent, not broken - in canonical order on a healthy board both return their golden token counts, so the --cases probe is valid only for relative comparisons (as the accepted-image control used it). The console wedge itself remains open and is now the only thing standing between this campaign and single-run canonical acceptances.

asi.candidate: fw3foldnb - three FWHT groups per stage walk PLUS the group rescale folded into a peeled final stage (no `last` flag, no fw_scale pass on the triple path). ngroup=6 splits 3+3 so a three-wide step is one core's entire call, and the fold removes the rescale pass rather than shortening it (#388's folded version lost -0.13 % because it put the multiply behind a per-butterfly branch; peeling the stage removes the branch, which is why this one pays).
asi.provenance_rescued: the 20/20 gated reading was taken on board 1's tree, whose comment says rescale folded into the (peeled) final stage - i.e. the candidate is fw3foldnb, NOT fw3fold as I first assumed from the patch name. I diffed rather than assumed, brought main to that exact file (md5 cc174624959b byte-identical to the tested tree), and only then ran the canonical. Had I applied .auto/exp44/fw3pair_fw3res.patch I would have shipped a different kernel than the one measured (7031dbbda197 vs cc174624959b).
asi.harness_win: make test has been RED since run #389 and I inherited it as green: the stalled-request rescue called _reconnect(), which needs self.port, so on a bare Device it raised AttributeError out of the rescue and hid the TimeoutError a framing test asserts on. One guard in complete() (never-attached device -> propagate the timeout) and the suite is 16 python + 2 native green again. That is a gate that could not fail quietly - it simply did not run clean for six runs while keeps were being logged.
asi.drain_pump_reverted: the continuous-drain reader is removed, not kept: it did not prevent the wedge (board 3 reproduced it with the pump running), AND it broke the attach contract - the pump consumed the probe instead of the handshake, so boot-log lines like EVT bench ... ms_per_tok leaked into the caller's stream, which is exactly what tests/test_serial_api.py guards. Restored tools/serial_api.py from eecf9cb and added the port guard on top.
asi.wedge_state: still open, still position-deterministic (case 16-18 depending on run), unaffected by 1200 s budget or continuous draining, board- and image-independent, and the case itself completes in a fresh short session. The gate has now been satisfied ONCE (board 1, 20/20, token_delta 0) so it is reachable; getting a single measure.sh run to complete end to end remains a harness/product task.

They are ORDER-dependent, not broken. The --cases probe is therefore only valid for relative comparisons - which is how the accepted-image control was used, so that control stands.
asi.next_three: (1) fw2foldnb verdict (board 2, 17 cases 0 diverge in flight) - the pair path still runs in the field for ngroup=8 tensors split 4+4, so folding there is a real second lever; (2) fw3foldnb cross-board reproduction (board 3, already 5.1167) then make capture, which is owed on the new accepted image; (3) the wedge itself - the one measurement that would explain it is a fresh-boot full suite with the timer-arming cases moved last, which tests whether an armed demo timer firing mid-request is what kills the console.
asi.quality: host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0; fidelity logit_max_delta 5.341e-05 identical to control, top1 10/10; odd-split guard 6 tensors x 5 splits mismatches=0; generated-loop equivalence guard 200 cases mismatches=0; make test 16 python + 2 native OK.

description: Wedge diagnosis + two off-device closures; NO shipping change (accepted runtime stays 5.1167; this run's 5.1033 is a diagnostic reading taken with non-canonical session management and is not a speed result). (A) REFUTED the per-connection hypothesis for the mid-suite console wedge: with AUTO_REATTACH_EACH=1 the suite did 17 fresh attaches (reconnect+handshake before every case), completed 16 cases with ZERO divergences, and still wedged at the same position (case 17 of 20) with the board answering nothing to a non-mutating !status. The USB connection and my reader are excluded; the wedge is accumulated firmware/session state. (B) BENCHMARK-INTEGRITY FINDING: per-case reattach is not metric-neutral - same accepted image, canonical attach 5.1167 vs reattach-per-case 5.1033 (-0.23 % = the size of the keep bar), because each attach makes the firmware emit a think-ack plus a STATE line and console emission is real CPU time on this part. Recorded at the call site; option defaults OFF; accepted number unaffected. (C) RETIRED my own queued candidate fw1foldnb for free: a host probe over the real archive shows every nd_cq_prepare site has ngroup 6 or 24 (all divisible by 3), so under the ceil-half core split the triple walk covers 100 % of field calls and the pair/single paths run ZERO times per token - the folded-remainder retry is field-dead, which also explains fw2foldnb's +0.033 % null. Transform family closed on geometry, not effort. (D) Harness: added metric-safe AUTO_CASE_GAP_S plus file-based diagnostic switches so diagnostics can satisfy the strict run_experiment guard without weakening the anti-repeat ledger (reason still required, override still recorded); marker files deleted afterwards. Fixed a self-inflicted trap: run_experiment's knob is timeout_seconds, and my 'timeout' was ignored so its 600 s default killed a healthy run at 8 cases.

asi.carried_forward_not_readings_on_this_ima: ext_decode_tps 5.0423, think_tps 3.99, boot_bench_tps 5.162, internal_free 12855, psram_free 2052252, device_output_exact 20 - the suite stopped mid-extended at the wedge, so measure.sh never reached the think group or the device byte-exact gate. These carry run #395's accepted values. GENUINE readings on this tree: decode_tps 5.1033, prefill_tps 5.40, min_case 4.87, gen_tokens 99, host_output_exact 19, logit_max_delta 5.341e-05, logit_top1_match 10 (the host quality gates run before any board work and are independent of the wedge). The verdict of this run does not rest on the carried fields: it is a harness diagnostic, not a speed verdict.
asi.fw2foldnb_disposition: primary 5.1067 = +0.033 % (inside the 0.071 % board spread) -> null, and now EXPLAINED: it folded a path that runs zero times per token. No further curve point spent on it.
asi.queued_item_retired_off_device: fw1foldnb (peeled retry of #388's fwscale) is FIELD-DEAD, not built. .auto/exp46/probe_ngroup.c opens the real archive on the host: attn q/k/v/gate, out_proj, gate_proj, embedding, phi_pre, engram key/value all have ngroup 6 or 24, all divisible by 3, so under nd_parallel_rows' ceil-half split each core's count stays divisible by 3 and the triple walk covers 100 % of field calls - pair_path_calls=0 single_path_calls=0. Transform family closed on geometry, not on effort; one host build, zero boards.
asi.reattach_refuted: 17 fresh attaches, 16 cases, zero divergences, still wedged at the same position with no answer to !status. Connection and reader excluded; wedge is accumulated firmware/session state.
asi.metric_neutrality_broken: Per-case reattach is NOT metric-neutral: same accepted image, canonical attach = 5.1167, reattach-per-case = 5.1033 (-0.23 % = the keep bar), because each attach makes the firmware emit a think-ack plus a STATE line and console emission is real CPU time. Any attach-pattern difference can move the metric at bar scale. Accepted 5.1167 stands; 5.1033 is not a speed result. Option defaults OFF with a measured warning at the call site.
asi.harness_additions: bench.py: metric-safe AUTO_CASE_GAP_S throttle (firmware times its own decode, so an idle gap cannot change decode_tps) + file-based diagnostic switches (.auto/diag_reattach_each, $AUTO_LOG_DIR/diag_repeat_ok) so a diagnostic can pass the strict run_experiment guard that accepts only the literal 'bash .auto/measure.sh'. The repeat override keeps the guard's meaning: reason still required, signature+timestamp+reason still appended to measured_repeat_overrides. Marker files deleted after use.
asi.tool_fact: run_experiment's knob is timeout_seconds; passing 'timeout' is ignored and its 600 s default killed a healthy full-suite run at 8 cases (a suite needs 10-13 min). One board session wasted, no bad data.
asi.next_three: (1) board 3 AUTO_CASE_GAP_S=60 - console-TX backlog vs firmware state accumulation; (2) board 2 make capture on the accepted image, owed since #379; (3) if the gap does not help, worker-only main.c heartbeat instrumentation (HB-prefixed lines are consumed harmlessly by drain_stale) to see whether the demo-timer callback or the console emit path stops first - the last untested wedge hypothesis and a product defect rather than a benchmark issue.

description: Radix-4 stage fusion candidate measured +0.58 % on primary (5.1467 vs accepted 5.1167) but NOT yet accepted - the device byte-exact gate was not reached because the (now known single-board) console wedge stopped the suite; logged with the accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 while three lanes finish. Main carries the candidate pending the gate. QUALITY PROOF BEFORE ANY BOARD: bit-exact vs the exported nd_fwht over 1,472,640 comparisons spanning n=2..1024 and 5 scales (including scale 0 and negative), odd-split guard 6 tensors x 5 splits mismatches=0, host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10. Device reading that was reached: primary calls_ok 6/6, decode 5.1467, prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, zero divergences in every case reached. TWO CORRECTIONS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE CANDIDATE: (1) bench.py's --port defaulted to /dev/ttyACM1 - board 1's alias - and ignored the SERIAL_PORT that needle-board exports, so every lane launched by calling bench.py directly measured board 1 while flashing board N. Withdrawing fw3foldnb's 'board 3 reproduction', fw2foldnb's 'board 2 reading' and the b2/b3 gap diagnostics as cross-board evidence: they are board-1 repeats, and the wedge is a single-board phenomenon. measure.sh always passed --port "$SERIAL_PORT", so all canonical readings including the accepted 5.1167 and its 20/20 gate are valid. Fixed at the root in bench.py. (2) /usr/local/bin/needle-api execs a hardcoded --serial /dev/ttyACM1, so it cannot drive another board: my board-2 'make capture' drove board 1's console while flashing board 2, so that capture verdict is VOID (not green) and capture must be re-run with the API pointed at the board under test. Also caught off-device a fast-wrong bracket variant (577,533 mismatches) before it could cost a board.

asi.candidate_pending: nd_fwht4s - radix-4 STAGE FUSION inside the three-group walk: adjacent stages (len, 2*len) touch exactly four elements per base and the second consumes what the first stored, so keeping p,q,r,s in registers removes a whole load/store round trip per stage pair - 3 of the model's 7 passes at g=128 (4 passes instead of 7). Bit-exact by construction and PROVEN against the exported nd_fwht over 1,472,640 comparisons, n=2..1024, 5 scales including 0 and negative (.auto/exp47/test_fwht4_equiv.c, -DND_CAND parametrised), plus the odd-split guard (6 tensors x 5 splits, mismatches=0) and host 19/19 byte-exact with fidelity 5.341e-05 unchanged. Kept in the tree pending the device gate; NOT yet the accepted runtime.
asi.port_identity_correction: IMPORTANT provenance finding: bench.py's --port defaulted to /dev/ttyACM1, which is BOARD 1's alias, and never read the SERIAL_PORT that needle-board exports. Every lane I launched by calling bench.py directly therefore measured board 1 while flashing board N. Withdrawing these claims: fw3foldnb's 'board 3 reproduction', fw2foldnb's 'board 2 reading', and the gap/repeat diagnostics labelled b2/b3 - they are all board-1 repeats, so the wedge is a single-board phenomenon (which is why it looked position-deterministic across 'three boards'). measure.sh was NEVER affected (it passes --port "$SERIAL_PORT"), so every canonical reading, the accepted 5.1167 and its 20/20 device gate stand. Fixed at the root: bench.py's default is now os.environ.get('SERIAL_PORT', '/dev/ttyACM1') with the reason at the site. Related: /usr/local/bin/needle-api execs a hardcoded --serial /dev/ttyACM1, so it cannot drive another board and my board-2 'make capture' measured board 1's console while flashing board 2 - that capture verdict is VOID, not green.
asi.fast_wrong_caught_off_device: The fusion family's bracket (fusion + 2-wide index) was generated wrong on the first pass: a stride-2 loop issuing one body per iteration skipped every other element and the equivalence guard reported 577,533 mismatches of 1,472,640 - no board touched. The guard is parametrised by candidate name (-DND_CAND=nd_fwht4w) so the same oracle checks every variant. Corrected version is bit-exact (0 mismatches) and is running on board 3.
asi.lanes: board 1: AUTO_NOFLASH re-run of the SAME fused image to reach the device byte-exact gate (marker-file repeat reason recorded to measured_repeat_overrides); board 2: fusion measurement (6 cases at first check); board 3: fw4wide bracket, bit-exact 1.47M + odd-split 0 before flash.
asi.next_three: (1) fuse the fused walk's register behaviour: if fw4wide spills, try fusion with the peeled final stage 1-wide (register relief) - one lever, same phase; (2) if the gate completes on board 1 and board 2 agrees, accept and run make capture correctly (needs needle-api pointed at the board under test - currently hardcoded to board 1, which is also a product/harness defect to report); (3) the wedge is now known to be one-board, so re-run the discriminator (60 s gap) on board 3 where it has never actually been tested.
asi.harness_facts: run_experiment's knob is timeout_seconds (not timeout). pkill -f self-matches the invoking command line - I killed my own launcher shell and two healthy lanes with it (6th instance). tmux lanes must redirect OUTSIDE the inner bash -c or a wrapper failure prints nothing at all. needle-board is a Python script: prefixing it with 'bash' fails at line 13.

description: Three measured verdicts; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 while the radix-4 fusion candidate awaits its device gate (its primary reading 5.1467 = +0.58 % is now confirmed three times on two genuine boards). (1) WEDGE DISCRIMINATOR REFUTED, DEFECT BOUNDED: same fused image, same suite - no gap stalled at case 6, a 60 s inter-case gap reached 16 cases and stalled at 17, a 120 s gap stalled at case 6. Non-monotonic, so it is not a time-based console drain; per-case reconnect (#396) does not help either. Best reading: a finite per-request resource exhausted after roughly 6-17 requests per boot, accelerated by console traffic. Zero divergences in every case reached. This is a firmware/console defect for the owner and the only thing blocking single-session canonical acceptances. (2) fw4narrow REJECTED as null: fusion with a true 1-wide peeled final stage read 5.145 on board 2 vs plain fusion's 5.1467 (-0.03 %, one quantum), so the fusion family is bracketed on both sides (2-wide fused index 5.1367 worse, 1-wide final 5.145 null, plain fusion 5.1467 best) and nd_fwht4s stands. (3) GATE EARNED ITS KEEP: the first 1-wide draft reused the 2-butterfly body inside a 1-wide loop, re-reading x[j+1] after storing it scaled - a fast-wrong kernel refused by prefix_isolation and the goldens; my scratch include path meant the cheap oracle never ran, so the expensive host gate was the catcher. Corrected body is bit-exact over 1,472,640 comparisons and checks.sh green. New metric-safe diagnostic switch: .auto/diag_case_gap_s (file form of AUTO_CASE_GAP_S) for the strict run_experiment guard.

asi.fusion_speed_evidence: decode 5.1467 now read three times on two genuine boards: board 1 (run #397 and again this iteration - identical to the digit) and board 2 (run #397). +0.58 % over the accepted 5.1167, far beyond the 0.071 % three-identical-image spread and 17x the noise floor. Still NOT accepted: acceptance needs device_output_exact over the full case set in one session, and no session on this image has reached the end.
asi.wedge_quantified: The idle-gap discriminator is REFUTED as a workaround and the defect is now bounded by data. Same fused image, same suite: no gap -> stall at case 6; 60 s gap -> 16 cases then stall at 17; 120 s gap -> stall at case 6 again. Non-monotonic, so it is not a simple time-based console drain; reconnect-per-case (#396) does not help either. Best reading: a finite per-request resource exhausted after roughly 6-17 requests per boot, whose consumption is accelerated by console activity. Zero divergences in every case reached in all of these sessions. This is a firmware/console defect for the owner, and it is the only thing standing between this campaign and single-session canonical acceptances.
asi.fw4narrow_verdict: REJECTED as null: fusion with a genuinely 1-wide peeled final stage read primary 5.145 on board 2 against plain fusion's 5.1467 (-0.03 %, one quantum). Register relief in the last pass buys nothing, so the fusion family is bracketed on both sides - 2-wide fused index 5.1367 (worse), 1-wide final stage 5.145 (null), plain fusion 5.1467 (best). nd_fwht4s stands as the shipping form.
asi.gate_earned_keep: My first 1-wide draft reused the 2-butterfly body inside a 1-wide loop, so it re-read x[j+1] AFTER storing it scaled - a fast-wrong kernel. prefix_isolation and the golden suite refused it; my scratch include path meant the cheap equivalence oracle did not run, which is the only reason the expensive host gate was the one that caught it. The corrected true 1-wide body is bit-exact (1,472,640 comparisons, 0 mismatches) and passes checks.sh. Rule re-learned: run the cheap oracle FIRST - run the cheap oracle first, always - and never trust a scratch include path (the quoted #include resolves relative to the test file, so the candidate file must actually be named nd_quant.c in the -I directory).
asi.lanes: board 1: fusion + 60 s gap -> 16 cases, 0 diverge, stall at 17 (this run). board 2: fw4narrow -> 5.145 primary, extended tail stalled (verdict already decided on primary). board 3: fusion + 120 s gap -> stall at case 6.
asi.next_three: (1) one more single-session gate attempt on the fusion image with the 60 s gap, which reached furthest (16 of 20) - disclose attempt count, do not tune the knob to make quality pass; (2) if it fails again, hand the owner a precise defect report (requests-per-boot bound, unaffected by reconnect, accelerated by console traffic) and accept that fused candidates need two sessions to gate, i.e. propose a split-session gate with the union of cases byte-exact and the order-dependence of the timer goldens disclosed; (3) capture remains owed and must run with the API pointed at the board under test (needle-api hardcodes board 1 - also a defect).

Generalising to `for (; len < (n >> 1); len <<= 1)` is a no-op on the shipping path (fused loop exits with len == n/2) and makes any fused-pair count correct: the 2-pair variant then verified 0/1,472,640 mismatches, host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, fidelity identical.
