description: Stall-attribution iteration: the console wedge is NOT candidate-attributable, and the fusion candidate is exonerated. Three same-window full-suite runs with runner-asserted provenance: ACCEPTED engine cc174624959b (board 2) 16 cases / 0 divergences / RC=1; FUSION engine 8667e160a278 (board 3) 16 cases / 0 divergences / RC=1; FUSION on board 1 (this run) 17 cases / 0 divergences, decode 5.1467 (+0.58 %, fourth reading, prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99). The accepted image reproduces the tail stall at the same position, so the blocker is a firmware/console defect, not my kernel - and the fusion is still NOT accepted because the device byte-exact gate needs all 20 cases in one session. New synthesis: stall position tracks concurrent console traffic (20/20 was reached by run #395 with board 1 alone; the pathological 6-case stalls happened with three lanes plus the capture API on one USB hub; 60 s and 120 s inter-case gaps were both measured and neither helped, so the knob is concurrent emitters, not idle time). Added metric-safe .auto/diag_request_timeout_s so a wedged session reports in 27 min instead of 2 h (a timed-out case fails the run, so it can never create a false pass). Off-device closure: folding prepare's copy into the first fused pass is dead - stage 1 must read zeros over the padded tail, so removing the copy puts a bounds test in the hottest loop, the trade #292/#231 measured as a loss.

asi.candidate_exoneration: Same window, same suite, same fail-fast setting, provenance asserted by measure.sh: ACCEPTED engine cc174624959b on board 2 reached 16 cases with ZERO divergences then RC=1 (TimeoutError); FUSION engine 8667e160a278 on board 3 reached 16 cases, zero divergences, RC=1; the FUSION on board 1 reached 17 cases, zero divergences. The tail stall is therefore NOT candidate-attributable - the accepted image reproduces it at the same position - and the fused kernel reaches exactly as far as the accepted one.
asi.stall_traffic_hypothesis: Stall position tracks total console traffic across the pool, not the image: 20/20 was achieved by run #395 when board 1 was the ONLY active board; the pathological 6-case stalls happened while three lanes plus the needle-api capture held the same USB hub; a 60 s inter-case gap did not help and a 120 s gap did not help (both measured) because the knob is not per-case idle time but concurrent emitters. Next test (queued first): kill every other lane and API, then run one sole-board full suite - if it reaches 20/20 the defect is USB/console contention and the campaign can accept candidates again.
asi.fusion_reading: Fourth independent reading of radix-4 fusion engine 8667e160a278: decode 5.1467, prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, calls_ok 6/6, ZERO divergences in all 17 cases reached. Spread across four sessions/two boards is one tick. +0.58 % over the accepted 5.1167. Still not accepted: the device byte-exact gate needs all 20 cases in one session.
asi.fail_fast: Added .auto/diag_request_timeout_s (file form of AUTO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S, applied after parse_args so it reaches serial_api.Device). It only shortens how long a stalled request is waited for, and a timed-out case FAILS the run, so it cannot turn a failure into a pass: a wedged 20-case session now reports in ~27 min instead of ~2 h. Verified by this run: 1621 s.
asi.off_device_closure: Folding nd_cq_prepare's copy into the first fused pass is dead on code reading: stage 1 must read zeros over the padded tail, and once the copy is gone those reads would have to become a bounds test inside the hottest straight-line loop - exactly the trade runs #292/#231 measured as a loss (a data-independent branch in that loop costs more than the work it removes). Not built.

(2) If it reaches 20/20: accept the fusion (+0.58 %), run make capture on the accepted image, then re-derive the phase map with AUTO_PROFILE=1 on the new denominator. description: Console-contention theory REFUTED by the sole-board test. With every other lane stopped, the capture API killed, and no process holding any needle-pi handle, the radix-4 fusion image answered 16 requests in a 530 s run (all fast - the earlier 1621 s sessions were simply 200 s timeouts on the already-dead tail) and then stopped answering at case 17, exactly as it did with three lanes and an API running. Pool traffic is not the wedge mechanism. Reading reproduced again: decode 5.1467 (+0.58 % over the accepted 5.1167), prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, zero divergences in every case reached. Case map now pinned: 20 cases (6 primary, 13 extended, 1 think) and four attempts died at case 17 or 18 - heldout_long_route / heldout_interval_one - deterministic within one case across engines, gaps and traffic levels; run #395 once reached 20/20, so the per-boot budget is 16-20 requests and the campaign cannot count on 20. Next experiment is a dependency-compressed tail session: #393's tail-only divergence had NO arming predecessors, so carrying sampling5/timer60/heldout_sampling15/heldout_interval_over_max plus the tail cases (~7 requests) may reproduce the canonical generations and let the device gate be satisfied as a disclosed union of a prefix session and a tail session. If it still diverges, the fusion goes to the owner as gate-blocked plus a firmware defect report.

asi.case_map: The suite is 20 cases: 6 primary, 13 extended, 1 think. Four attempts completed exactly 16 (dying on #17 heldout_long_route) or 17 (dying on #18 heldout_interval_one): the wall is in the tail region 17-18, deterministic within one case, and independent of engine, inter-case gap, and pool traffic. #395 once completed all 20, so the budget is 16-20 requests per boot and the campaign cannot rely on reaching 20.
asi.next_experiment: Dependency-compressed tail session. #393's tail-only probe returned 19 tokens against a 27-token golden for heldout_interval_one - but that probe ran the tail cases with NO predecessors, and the tail's timer/sampling cases are armed by earlier ones (sampling5, timer60, heldout_sampling15, heldout_interval_over_max). Hypothesis: a session carrying the arming predecessors + the tail (6-7 requests, well inside the budget) reproduces the canonical generations, in which case the device byte-exact gate can be satisfied as the UNION of a prefix session (cases 1-16) and a dependency-compressed tail session, disclosed as such. Falsifiable immediately with bench.py --cases on the already-built image. If it still diverges, the tail is unreachable and the fusion (+0.58 %, bit-exact everywhere it can be measured) goes to the owner as gate-blocked with a defect report.
asi.refuted: SOLE-BOARD refutes the console-contention theory: with every other lane, the capture API, and all console handles closed, the same fusion image answered 16 requests in a 530 s run (everything fast - the earlier 1621 s runs were just 200 s timeouts on the dead tail) and then stopped answering at case 17, exactly as it did with three lanes running. Concurrent pool traffic is not the mechanism.
asi.state: Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167. The radix-4 fusion (engine 8667e160a278) is at +0.58 % with four agreeing primary readings on two boards, host 19/19 byte-exact, zero device divergences in 49 case-comparisons across four sessions, and is now exonerated from the stall; it remains NOT accepted solely because the device gate needs 20 cases in one session.
asi.honesty: The traffic hypothesis was mine, it was plausible, it explained the 6-case stalls and #395's 20/20 - and one cheap sole-board run killed it. Worth recording because the run cost 9 minutes and settled a question that had already consumed several hours of interpretation.

description: Fusion candidate's own monitor set measured at last (7-request primary,think session fits the measured 16-20 request per-boot budget, so it completes): decode 5.1467 (+0.58 % over the accepted 5.1167), think_tps 4.01 (+0.50 % - the monitor that guards the 4-bit/vocabulary path, so the win is not paid for there), boot_bench 5.194 = 193 ms/token (+0.62 %, the mechanism check), prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, token_delta 0, device byte-exact 7/7 with golden_missing 0, psram unchanged - AND A NEW COST: internal_free 11,831 vs the accepted 12,855, i.e. the fused kernel costs 1,024 B of internal heap, the largest RAM price of any live candidate, invisible until now because every earlier fusion session died in the extended tail and carried the accepted RAM figure. Also settled: the wedge's position is a function of both accumulated requests and concurrent console traffic (three lanes -> case 6, sole board -> 16-17), so runs #400 and #401 were each half right and full-suite attempts must run with the pool idle. Transform family CLOSED on every axis: width 4 = exactly null (its guard is false for the dominant ngroup=6 tensors), radix-8 x3 groups = exactly null (4->3 passes absorbed by registers), radix-8 x2 groups = -0.19 % rejected. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167: the fusion is still NOT accepted because device_output_exact_min is 20 and four full-suite attempts on two engines reached 16-17 cases with zero divergences, the accepted image reproducing the same tail.

asi.cost_decision: The 1 KiB is affordable but not free: 11,831 B is the lowest internal heap in the campaign, and the RAM-blocked family (phi row residency wants ~18 KB/core) is priced against exactly this pool, so the fusion makes that idea strictly further away. If the owner ever takes #293's assertion-level option (+8,248 B) the trade is trivially worth it; without it, this is a real -8 percent reduction in the remaining RAM headroom that buys +0.58 percent speed.
asi.gate_status: STILL NOT ACCEPTED. device_output_exact_min is 20 and this session ran 7 cases by design, so measure.sh correctly skipped the device gate. Four full-suite attempts on two engines reached 16/16/17/17 cases with zero divergences; the accepted image reproduces the same tail stall, so this is an engine-independent firmware/console defect, not a candidate property. Acceptance needs either one lucky 20-case session or an owner decision to accept 7/7 + 19/19 host + 49 device case-comparisons with zero divergences as the quality evidence for a bit-exact change.
asi.finding_cost: MEASURED COST, new fact: internal_free 11,831 against the accepted 12,855, i.e. the fused kernel costs 1,024 B of internal heap - the largest internal-RAM price of any candidate still under consideration, and internal heap is the campaign's scarcest resource (#292's IRAM-text/heap coupling). psram_free unchanged. Every prior fusion reading carried the accepted RAM figure because those sessions died in the extended tail; the cost was invisible until now.
asi.finding_secondaries: MEASURED on the fusion image itself (previously carried): think_tps 4.01 vs 3.99 (+0.50 %, so the 4-bit/vocabulary path is not harmed - the monitor that exists to catch exactly that), boot_bench 5.194 vs 5.162 (+0.62 %, 197 -> 193 ms/token, the mechanism check since prepare is inside the bench), prefill 5.435, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, token_delta 0, device byte-exact 7/7 with golden_missing 0.
asi.method: A 7-request session (primary,think) fits inside the measured 16-20-request per-boot budget, so it completes reliably and yields decode, prefill, min_case, think, boot bench and both heaps - the whole monitor set except ext_decode_tps. Added .auto/diag_groups (file form of AUTO_GROUPS, consulted only when the env var is unset, and measure.sh skips the device gate for restricted runs, which is why this must never be used for acceptance). Runtime 216 s instead of 27+ min.
asi.stall_synthesis: Position of the wedge is a function of concurrent console traffic AND accumulated requests: three lanes running -> stall at case 6; sole board -> 16-17. So run #400 ('accelerated by traffic') and run #401 ('traffic is not the mechanism') were each half right: traffic is not the cause but it is an accelerator. Consequence for the campaign: full-suite attempts should be run with the pool otherwise idle, and three-lane batches can only be trusted for primary-group speed verdicts.
asi.next_three: (1) One more sole-board full-suite acceptance attempt on the fusion, pool idle, no other emitters - the only remaining route to the formal 20/20, and if it lands 16-17 again the candidate goes to the owner as gate-blocked with the defect report rather than being re-attempted further. (2) ext_decode_tps for the fusion via diag_groups=extended in its own session (13 requests, from a fresh boot) - speed-valid even though restricted sessions cannot serve as the byte-exact gate. (3) The transform family is closed on every axis (width 1/2/3/4, stage fusion 2/3/radix-8, passes 4 vs 3, rescale placement, stage order), so the remaining above-bar items are owner decisions: phi residency vs 11,831 B, 120 MHz vendor-blocked, and the 0.2 % bar.
asi.transform_closure: Three screens logged this window, all bit-exact before any board: width-4 quad = 5.1467 (exactly null; its guard is false for the dominant ngroup=6 tensors so it never executes there), radix-8 x3 groups = 5.1467 (exactly null: the 4->3 pass removal bought nothing, registers absorbed it), radix-8 x2 groups = 5.1367 (-0.19 %, rejected). The run #399 dose-response (+0.16 % per removed pass) correctly predicted the SIGN of the lever and over-predicted its size at the third pass - the measured +0.16 % stops paying once the loop is register-bound.

description: Cost-axis retry of the 2-pair fusion (c9507112b7e2) - REFUTED, and the refutation is the useful part. Rejected by run #399 on speed alone, it was reopened because run #402 introduced a new scarce dimension (the 3-pair fusion costs 1,024 B of internal heap) that could have inverted the ranking if less fusion meant less code. Measured on its own session: decode 5.1383 (+0.42 %, reproducing #399 to the digit), think 4.00, boot bench 5.186, min_case 4.90, token_delta 0, device byte-exact 7/7 golden_missing 0 - and internal_free 11,831, EXACTLY the 3-pair fusion's figure. So the 1 KiB is not per-fused-pair: nm on the ELF shows no separate symbols for the walk variants (all inlined into fwht_rows, 0x837 = 2,103 B), i.e. it is the fixed cost of the fused kernel existing. The 3-pair form therefore dominates outright and the assumed speed-for-RAM trade does not exist. This also points at the real lever: fwht_rows carries inlined fallbacks the field never runs (the g<8 branch, and the pair/single tails that run zero times per token per run #396), so making those cold paths noinline should refund part of the 1,024 B at neutral speed - keeping the fallbacks present, since deleting an unused tail is exactly run #333's silent-drop class.

asi.finding: internal_free 11,831 for the 2-pair form = EXACTLY the 3-pair fusion's 11,831. So the 1,024 B is not proportional to the number of fused pairs; it is the fixed cost of the fused kernel existing (nm on the current ELF shows no separate symbols for nd_fwht4s/nd_fwht3s/nd_fwht3p - they are all inlined into fwht_rows, which is 0x837 = 2,103 bytes). My 'fewer fused pairs costs less RAM' premise for the retry is REFUTED, cheaply, by one 218 s session.
asi.invalidation_check: This is the answer to 'does #402 invalidate a previous discard?' - it reopened the 2-pair fusion on a changed assumption (cost axis) and the answer is no: strictly dominated, same RAM, slower. Rejected on both axes now, and the retry took one restricted-group session rather than a full suite.
asi.next_three: (1) Refund the RAM: nm shows the transform family is inlined into fwht_rows (2,103 B) including fallbacks the field never runs - the g<8 branch and the pair/single tails, which run ZERO times per token (measured in run #396: every nd_cq_prepare site has ngroup 6 or 24, so the 3-wide walk covers 100 percent of field calls under the ceil-half split). Marking those cold fallbacks noinline - or routing g<8 through the fused kernel, which the oracle already proves exact for n=2..1024 - should give back part of the 1,024 B at neutral speed, and run #375 independently measured NOT inlining as slightly better. That converts the fusion's cost from -1,024 B toward neutral without touching arithmetic; off-device proof first with nm -S, then one session. Keep the fallbacks present (do not delete them): deleting a tail for an ngroup the field does not produce is exactly run #333's silent-drop class. (2) Sole-board full-suite acceptance attempt with the pool idle - the only route to the formal 20-case device gate. (3) ext_decode_tps for the fusion in its own 13-request session (speed-valid, never a gate).

description: Cold-path IRAM refund: the fusion candidate's cost objection is RETIRED. The helpers stay present (deleting an unused tail is run #333's silent-drop class) and the oracle still proves bit-exactness over 1,472,640 comparisons plus host 19/19 and odd-split 0/30. Device: decode 5.1467 (+0.58 % over the accepted 5.1167, fusion speed fully preserved), think 4.01, boot_bench 5.194 (193 ms/token), prefill 5.4367, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, token_delta 0, device byte-exact 7/7 with golden_missing 0, psram unchanged - and internal_free 12,855, i.e. EXACTLY the accepted figure, so the fusion's 1,024 B price is now zero. asi.finding: Fusion + noinline-cold-fallbacks measured: decode 5.1467 (+0.58 %), think 4.01 (+0.50 %), boot_bench 5.194 = 193 ms/token (+0.62 %), prefill 5.4367, min_case 4.91, gen_tokens 99, token_delta 0, device byte-exact 7/7 golden_missing 0, psram unchanged, and internal_free 12,855 - the accepted value to the digit. So the fusion now ships at ZERO internal-RAM and ZERO PSRAM cost, and every measured monitor is up. The off-device prediction (.iram0.text -1,116 B) over-shoot the observed 1,024 B refund slightly (alignment/other sections), which is worth remembering when pricing RAM from size(1).
asi.mechanism: The cold-path class is general, not transform-specific: any ND_HOT static single-call-site helper whose path the field never takes is paying internal heap twice over - first because GCC inlines it into the hot caller whatever its section attribute says, second because the surviving out-of-line body still lands in IRAM. The fix is the attribute pair (drop ND_HOT, add noinline), and run #385 already proved the resulting IRAM-to-flash crossing costs zero cycles, which is free here anyway since the path is never executed.
asi.off_device_first: The refund was measured before any board: .iram0.text 73,551 -> 72,435 (-1,116 B) and .flash.text 148,612 -> 149,612 (+1,000 B, i.e. the bodies moved rather than vanished) from two builds and size(1). That is a 4-minute build and zero board time to establish a candidate's cost axis, and it is the cheapest decisive measurement of this window.

asi.phi_residency_closed: The campaign's last RESERVED above-bar speed item - phi 4-bit row residency, ceiling ~+0.39 %, 'gated on the owner's assertion-level RAM' - is CLOSED OFF-DEVICE for the price of reading two functions, and on a stronger basis than RAM. gemv_rows_generic walks each row exactly once (row = packed + r*rowbytes, inner loop advancing gi*g*bits) and each phi tensor is called once per layer per token, so a phi weight byte's reuse count is 1. Staging therefore cannot save the PSRAM read it would have to perform to arrive: copy-in reads the bytes once, compute reads them from internal RAM, total traffic is unchanged while the copy adds a full write. The measured '+9.3 % when weights are in internal RAM' ceiling silently assumed free arrival. Three independent measurements already agree with this consequence: #287's copy/GDMA attempts (-17.9 % and -67.8 %), #330's flat 13.90 % delivery tax on every cold 2-bit pass, and #295's residency-vs-cold equivalence. Corollary with real value: the streaming-once principle means assertion-level RAM has NO speed buyer at all, so #293's +8,248 B is a pure diagnostics-vs-RAM decision for the owner, not a route to tokens.
asi.queued_third_idea_note: Also closed on the same reading pass: any 'stage the weights into internal RAM' family member for the 2-bit path, for the same reuse-1 reason. asi.defect_sharpened: THE WEDGE, LOCALISED BY EXCLUSION. With the instrument running, the failing state was captured directly: the app had finished priming, opened the model (internal_free 16,779, psram_free 697,356) and was printing TDIAG every 5 s at the moment bench.py reported 'ESP32 did not become ready'. description: Two device screens launched + a provenance gate hole closed + one off-device closure; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (metric and all secondaries are the accepted fw3foldnb run's values carried forward - nothing ran to completion this iteration, the two screens are mid-flight). OPERATOR REDIRECT FOLLOWED: harness expansion and gate re-attempts stopped; three distinct screens against pinned baselines, live processes and growing non-empty logs verified within ~16 s. (1) DEVICE SCREENS (boards 2+3): the two most anomalous map entries, both priced from assumptions and never split. `mhc-mix` = 4.7 ms aggregate over four small loops, ~10 cycles per element-op against the 1-2 cycles a resident elementwise loop measures elsewhere (5x anomaly); `engram` = 16.1 ms while its own 2-bit GEMVs account for ~14.2 ms and its slot gathers were priced at ~0.02 ms - a ~1.9 ms gap with no accounting. The image adds six additive sub-phase timers (of-mix:lane_rms/bias/lanew/sub, of-eng:slot_row) and touches no arithmetic, so the byte-exact and fidelity gates still bind; board 2 runs the full 20-case suite as the quality gate, board 3 independently reproduces the attribution on a second board. Timer overhead makes decode non-comparable to the pinned baseline, so these are attribution screens, not speed claims - run #355's prepare split is the precedent and it produced two shipped wins. (2) GATE HOLE CLOSED: the runner's `engine_md5` hashed only nd_quant.c + the .S files, so an nd_model.c-only candidate was never covered by EXPECT_ENGINE_MD5 - this candidate and earlier lanes (condT, silu4, cond2, cond4) were unprotected. Now hashes engine/src/*.c + *.S + engine/include/*.h + esp32/main/*.c; both boards now report a59990aa84e2. Separately: `needle-board run N --` executes with a cwd that is NOT the checkout, so relative-path candidate copies patch the wrong tree - the cause of my four PROVENANCE_MISMATCH exits, which were the gate refusing a wrongly-computed expectation. (3) OFF-DEVICE: condT's device-only divergence re-investigated; tier-overwrite and in-place-write-through-a-flash-pointer both excluded by code ordering (staging at nd_model.c:387 precedes the tier build at 436+; the tier is a separate PSRAM buffer reached via nd_tier_ptr at each GEMV site while fp16_slot[li][25] is read through the raw archive pointer). Stays rejected as unexplained. (4) BOARD 1 concrete blocker named: console/flash nodes re-created 00:23, 01:00, 01:34 (boards 2/3 stable since 00:22), 4,822 log bytes but no STATE, last two runs died at the readiness handshake; the console is a USB-UART bridge on UART0 so it can leave USB while the ESP32 keeps computing - rig fault, operator-side reseat, and the new ATTACH_DEVICE / WARN stalled_device_identity lines will prove it in one run.

asi.gate_hole_found: measure.sh's provenance field hashed ONLY engine/src/nd_quant.c + engine/src/*.S, so every nd_model.c-only candidate (this one, condT, silu4, cond2, cond4) was NOT covered by EXPECT_ENGINE_MD5. Now hashes engine/src/*.c + *.S + engine/include/*.h + esp32/main/*.c. The four PROVENANCE_MISMATCH exits I hit were the gate correctly refusing my own mis-computed expectation - a gate refusing a wrong claim is the gate working.
asi.hypothesis: mhc-mix (~10 cycles per element-op, 5x any equivalent resident loop) and engram (1.9 ms unaccounted) are the two map entries priced from assumptions rather than measurement; the run #355 prepare split is the precedent where splitting a phase aggregate produced two shipped wins.

Both verified live: PROVENANCE engine_md5=a59990aa84e2, 4 build processes, logs growing within 16 s. Secondaries here are the ACCEPTED run's values carried forward, not readings on the profiled image.
asi.next1: Read both lanes: which sub-timer owns mhc-mix's 4.7 ms, and whether of-eng:slot_row explains engram's ~1.9 ms gap. Each winner becomes ONE bit-exact lever (fuse the sweeps over the same resident 3 KB lane buffer / dequant fewer bytes per slot) measured against pinned 5.1167 with the full gate.
asi.next2: Price Sinkhorn's logf. The banked logf(1.0f) skip was refused against an ASSUMED 150-250 cycle logf and a 787-cycle break-even; the map's 3.8 ms over ~2,560 transcendental calls implies ~356 cycles/call. One kbench bench_log() on field-realistic arguments plus a host call count settles it, no engine change.
asi.next3: attn-stage on a real request by subtraction: attn-stage 99.1 ms vs named children summing to 40.1, remainder assumed to be the q/k/v/gate GEMVs (also counted by proj2bit). Verify with a request-path diff of two prof_dump snapshots instead of trusting overlapping cumulative timers (#344's rule).

asi.warning: nd_prof reads cost ~4-10 cycles each and of-eng:slot_row brackets a per-call dequant, so its absolute value is inflated on small calls. Judge it as a share of ND_P_ENGRAM, and re-measure at lower bracket overhead before pricing a lever from it.

description: Attribution screens MEASURED on two boards (identical tables, zero spread) + Sinkhorn priced exactly off-device and refused + two stale map numbers corrected; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries are the accepted fw3foldnb run's; the 5.1367 shown is the PROFILED image and is explicitly not a speed claim - see asi.warning). THE SCREEN: six additive sub-phase timers splitting the two map entries whose per-element costs looked 5-10x off, boards 2 and 3, provenance asserted (a59990aa84e2), full suites running. RESULT (1) `mhc-mix` is 2.5 ms, not the ledger's 4.7 ms (stale), and it is now fully attributed: lane_rms 1.2 + lanew 0.6 + bias 0.2 + sub 0.2 = 2.2 of 2.5 ms. Its dominant term is a SINGLE-accumulator reduction over the whole lane buffer, so the only ILP that preserves bits would reassociate it - the lever the byte-exact gate refuses. So the anomaly was arithmetic built on the stale 4.7 ms: recomputed, the loop sits at the latency-bound floor of a serial sum. No candidate. (2) `engram`'s slot-row dequant is 0.6 ms/token, 30x the ~0.02 ms it was priced at - real work, still only 0.3 % of the token, and it raises a specific new question (does dequant_row materialise 768 weights to consume sub=128?), which is the next experiment. (3) OFF-DEVICE, no board: Sinkhorn exp-pairing priced with counters on the real engine - 8 sinkhorn calls/token, 5,120 gross exp terms, 1,334 already skipped by #291, 3,786 reaching nd_expf, 1,280 logf, 2,560 adjacent pair slots, 0.6131 pairable -> 1,570 x 49.4 cycles = 0.323 ms minus 0.043 ms of eligibility tests = +0.145 % at full realisation, i.e. sub-bar after the family's measured 25-70 % band. Not built. This also reconciles the two ledger figures that looked contradictory (1,280 vs 5,120 exps - different scopes, both right) and re-confirms the logf(1.0f) skip is closed on measured counts, not arithmetic in a comment. (4) Harness: the provenance assertion covered only nd_quant.c + asm, so no nd_model.c-only candidate was ever checked - now hashes the whole engine plus app; and `needle-board run N --` executes with a cwd that is not the checkout, which is how my relative-path candidate copies patched the wrong tree while agreeing with their own relative md5sum. Instrumentation reverted from the engine tree.

Sinkhorn's 3.8 ms is fully explained by measured per-call costs, so it carries no anomaly.
asi.lanes: board2 + board3 = the six-timer attribution image, full suites, provenance engine_md5=a59990aa84e2, primary group completed on both (decode 5.1367 each). The split itself (engine + header + main.c) is REVERTED in main; only harness changes remain.
asi.next1: engram slot_row is 0.6 ms/token, 30x the ledger's ~0.02 ms estimate, and the tables use sub=128 columns while nd_cq_dequant_row materialises a full row. Read whether it dequantises 768 weights to consume 128 - if so that is a 6x over-dequant and a bit-exact 'dequant only the sub columns' candidate worth up to +0.3 %. Host-side code read first, cheap.
asi.next2: attn-stage is 99.1 ms while its named children (heads 35.2 + taps 3.3 + norms 0.5 + rope 0.2 + kv 0.9) sum to 40.1; the ~59 ms remainder is ASSUMED to be the q/k/v/gate GEMVs (also counted by proj2bit). Verify with a two-snapshot request-path diff instead of trusting overlapping cumulative timers (#344's rule).
asi.next3: phi is 10.0 ms (5.2 %); its only measured headroom is the 9.3 % delivery ceiling (= +0.47 %) gated on internal RAM (#293 owner decision). Before asking the owner again, check whether the same delivery share is collectable another way: phi rows are read once per token, so any residency needs a mechanism that avoids the read it must perform (#407's closure) - i.e. only a smaller per-token footprint counts, which is a quantisation change (frozen).
asi.stale_numbers_corrected: mhc-mix 4.7 -> 2.5 ms; engram slot-row dequant 0.02 -> 0.6 ms; Sinkhorn exp count 1,280 -> 3,786 reaching nd_expf (5,120 gross).
asi.warning: the profiled image reads 5.1367 = +0.39 % over the accepted 5.1167 on two boards. That is a codegen side-effect of the timer insertions, NOT a speed claim, and it disproves the implicit assumption that ND_PROFILE images always read slower. Never read a profiled decode as a delta in either direction.

description: Third screen (off-device, zero board time): the engram slot-row dequant measured at 0.6 ms/token is geometry-CONFIRMED and closed without a candidate; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries are the accepted fw3foldnb run's - this iteration ran no shipping image, only host diagnostics while the two diagnostic lanes finish). HYPOTHESIS: run #410's split put the engram's per-slot row dequant at 0.6 ms, 30x the ~0.02 ms it had been priced at, and if the kernel dequantised 768 weights to consume sub=128 that would be a 6x over-dequant worth ~+0.26%. TESTED, three ways, all off-device: (1) the engram tables are [slots][128], so sub=128 IS the whole row - no over-dequant, hypothesis dead from the tensor shape; (2) counted the real call rate with -DND_ENG_STATS on the host engine over a real frozen primary prompt: 2,154 dequant calls over 181 forward steps = 11.9 ~ 12 rows per step, exactly the ledger's 12 rows x 128 weights, so the geometry the phase map rests on is now measured, not derived; (3) checked the obvious residency lever - m->row and m->tmp2 are already ND_ALLOC_FAST (internal SRAM), so the 'FWHT thrashes a PSRAM scratch row' explanation does not exist. RESIDUAL, stated as a residual: 12k cycles per 128-element row (~94 cycles/element) against a modelled 2.5-5k, so 2-5x remains unexplained - but the whole phase is 0.3 % of the token, and the one bit-exact lever I can name (the nibble loop's `if (sh + bits > 8)`, a ~50 % mispredicting branch on 64 of 128 nibbles) prices at +0.017-0.034 %. Below the bar, so not built; the phase is left measured with an honest gap rather than priced on a guess. Combined with #410's engram GEMV arithmetic (13.3 ms of the phase at the measured 2.695 cyc/weight + 0.6 ms slot rows = 13.9 vs 16.2 measured), the engram family is closed: no board should go there. Diagnostic instrumentation reverted from the engine tree (git diff over engine now covers only the harness-side header, and the accepted code paths are byte-identical to a6e7454). LANES: boards 2 and 3 each completed 6/6 primary cases on the timer image (route_translate 4.900, heldout_timer45 5.190) with extended in flight; the timer image is diagnostic-only and cannot ship, so its device gate is not an acceptance path - the attribution payload was already delivered and was identical on both boards.

asi.branchless_nibble_priced: the mixed-byte-boundary branch costs a 50% mispredict on ~64 of the row's nibbles = ~640-1280 cycles/row; removing it entirely = 7.7-15.6k cycles/token = +0.017-0.034%, sub-bar. So even though it is the textbook fix, it cannot clear 0.2% here.
asi.geometry_confirmed: ENGSTATS dequant_row_calls=2154 over 181 forward steps (158 prefill + 23 decode, real primary prompt 'Sample telemetry every 5 seconds') = 11.9 ~ 12 rows per step, exactly the ledger's 12 rows x 128 weights = 1,536 weights/token. The phase map's engram geometry entry is validated, not assumed.
asi.lanes: boards 2+3 on the diagnostic image: 6/6 primary cases each (route_translate 4.900, heldout_timer45 5.190), extended in flight. The timer image is diagnostic-only and cannot ship, so its 20-case device gate is not the acceptance path for anything; the attribution payload was already delivered from the boot-bench table, identical on both boards.
asi.measured_residual: 0.6 ms/token / 12 rows = ~12k cycles per 128-element row = ~94 cycles/element, against a modelled ~2.5-5k (bit-extract + FWHT(128)=448 butterflies + scale + 128-float copy). 2-5x still unexplained. Whole phase is 0.3% of the token, so even deleting it pays +0.31% and no mechanism for that is identifiable.
asi.next1: attn-stage is 99.1 ms while its named children (heads 35.2, taps 3.3, norms 0.5, rope 0.2, kv 0.9) sum to 40.1; the ~59 ms remainder is ASSUMED to be the q/k/v/gate GEMVs which proj2bit also counts. This is the largest unexamined number in the token. Measure it by differencing two prof_dump snapshots on a real request (#344's rule against cumulative timers) rather than by subtraction of overlapping phases.
asi.next2: qkv taps: 3.3 ms (1.7%) is now the largest non-GEMV phase with no internal split, after mhc-mix (2.5 ms, fully attributed this session) and sinkhorn (3.8 ms, priced to the transcendental and closed). 9 taps x 768 columns x 32 B = 221 KB/token read. Screen its internals before theorising: taps-vs-write vs gather, one profiled build.
asi.next3: engram's remaining 15.6 ms checks out arithmetically against the measured 2.695 cyc/weight: 2 sites x 2 x 589,824 = 2.36 M weights, two-core = 3.18 M cycles = 13.3 ms, plus the 0.6 ms slot rows = 13.9 vs 16.2 measured; residual 2.3 ms is prepare and pointer math inside the same bracket. So the phase is essentially closed and no board should go there.
asi.owner_only: phi row residency (10.0 ms, 9.3% delivery ceiling = +0.47%, needs ~18 KB/core vs 12,855 B free, gated on #293's assertion-level RAM) and 120 MHz (vendor-blocked #331). Nothing else above the bar is in-rule.
asi.residency_dead_on_inspection: m->row and m->tmp2 are already ND_ALLOC_FAST (internal SRAM, nd_model.c:675 and :654), so the 'FWHT thrashes a PSRAM scratch row' explanation is false and a residency candidate does not exist. This is the cheap kind of negative result: one grep, zero board time.

description: Lane diagnosis + three distinct screens put on three boards + a near-duplicate avoided; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries are the accepted fw3foldnb run's; none of this iteration's images can ship - two are timer-instrumented diagnostics and one is a kbench screen - so no speed claim is made). LANE DIAGNOSIS (within locks, from the logs themselves): the two split-timer lanes were not frozen-polling - each ended rc=1 with 'TimeoutError: board did not answer after one reconnect; case was not skipped, and no chip reset attempted', after b2 completed 16 device cases and b3 17, with ZERO divergences in every case reached; the failing raise is the #346 STATE/ack gate path, not the per-case request loop, which is why my WARN stalled_device_identity line never printed. IDENTITY TEST REFUTES MY OWN THEORY: b2 died at rdev 166.3 and b3 at rdev 166.5, path==real, both nodes unchanged since 00:22 - so the console leg did NOT re-enumerate on the healthy boards, and the wall is a per-boot request ceiling of 16-20 requests, engine-independent, exactly as #392/#401 measured. Board 1's node re-creations (00:23/01:00/01:34) are a separate rig fault, not this phenomenon. NEAR-DUPLICATE AVOIDED: Experiment 31's lanes still sat in .auto/ideas.md marked ACTIVE and 31B (attention P.V accumulate order) had a single stray log mention, so I nearly flashed it - run #354 had already measured it (position-major 9.587 cyc/update vs dim-major 17.164 = 44.1 % WORSE, bit-exact reorder verified first). The stale list is pruned with dispositions inline. SCREENS NOW RUNNING: board 1 = KB LOG, a kbench microbenchmark that prices libm logf on field-shaped operands (1,280 calls/token, 13.58 % exactly 1.0f, min over 12 rounds, operands built as the kernel builds its sums, mixed/non-one/mul-floor modes) - this settles the banked logf(1.0f) skip against a measured cost instead of the assumed 150-420 cycles that run #294's 787-cycle break-even used, and it is shippable iff logf >= ~560 cycles. Board 2 = request-path attribution harvest on the profiled image (attn-stage is a 99.1 ms parent against 40.1 ms of named children - the largest unexamined number in the token). Board 3 = ND_P_TAPS split three ways (of-taps:q/k/v), the last unsplit phase at 3.3 ms (1.7 %), full 20-case suite running with provenance verified from the applied tree (ad56ea43a34d). OWN BUGS CAUGHT: (1) my pre-launch check on the kbench candidate was vacuous - it asserted the macro name appeared before the first occurrence of the function name, which matched my own comment while the macro was undefined at the use site, so the build failed at line 915; the fix uses __attribute__((noinline)) directly, and the positive control is that the build had to fail, which it did. (2) my first hand-computed EXPECT omitted a second header in engine/include and would have false-aborted a correct tree, so provenance values are now computed from the applied worker tree with measure.sh's own glob. RETRY CONSIDERED, NOT TAKEN: condT's veto looked stale after #393/#394, but #392 records that condT's lane completed all 20 cases in canonical order, so its single divergence was not a stall or ordering artefact - rejection stands, no board spent.

description: Three screens landed; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries are the accepted run's - all three images were diagnostic: two profiled, one kbench, so no speed claim). BOARD 1, KB LOG (device microbenchmark, and first its own control: it reproduced KB EXP 246.02/198.03 = +19.51% against #229's 247.42/198.04, KB DOT 138/403/213 exactly as #230, KB DIV 7.95/30.92 exactly as #338, cycles/us 23999). RESULT: libm logf costs 23.13 cycles/call in the field-mixed set and 22.63 excluding exact ones, against a 1.09-cycle multiply floor - i.e. ~22 net, not the 150-420 the ledger assumed when it banked the logf(1.0f) skip. With the host-measured 1,280 logf/token and a 0.1361 exactly-one share (my own counter, confirming the inherited 13.58%), the skip buys 174 x (22.6-4) = 3,236 cycles = +0.007%. CLOSED on measurement, and run #294's conclusion stands even though its cost figure did not. THE GENERAL FINDING is the third in a row and it retires a whole family: measured per-call costs here are ~8 cycles (__divsf3, #338), ~22 (logf, now), 0 for an IRAM-to-flash callee crossing (#385) - so no call-removal lever in this model can exceed ~0.03%, which closes the 'replace or hoist a libm call' line for good (#294, #336, #338, #368 all sized it from assumption). My own printed summary line on that bench was wrong twice over (a whole-run count used as a per-token divisor, and a threshold 4x too large: 0.2% of a 193 ms token is 92,640 cycles at 240 MHz, not 386,000); decisions were taken from the per-field cycle columns and the error is disclosed, not edited away. BOARD 3: ND_P_TAPS split three ways - of-taps:q 2.4 ms, k 0.4, v 0.5, so q is 73% of the phase, and q's 0.3 ms/layer over 9 taps x 288 columns is 27.8 cycles per MAC, which matches cold-line delivery almost exactly (10,368 B of staged tap table = 162 lines x ~300 cycles = 48,600 of 72,000 cycles); the tables are 221 KB/token against a 64 KB cache so they cannot be made resident - #302's 'scattered-read floor' claim now has a number on it, and the next step is a resident-tap-table control to prove the diagnosis rather than argue it. BOARD 2: request-path harvest rc=0, whole block 157.1 (bench) / 174.1 (tools) / 206.0 (route) ms with attn-stage 99.1/107.5/131.5 and proj2bit 86.3/99.0/110.9 - this kills my own queued '59 ms unexplained inside attn-stage' worry, because attn-stage contains the q/k/v/gate GEMVs that proj2bit also counts, so the phases overlap and subtracting them is meaningless (#344's rule); route's extra attention is the longer context (#145). Also recorded: the sampler's request-path logits4 is 3.8/7.0 ms against a 0.23 ms projection, the largest remaining unattributed per-request block.

asi.board1_reproduced_published_numbers: before trusting its new number: KB EXP pair 246.02/198.03 = +19.51% (vs #229's 247.42/198.04, +19.96%), KB DOT 138/403/213 = #230 exactly, KB DIV 7.95/30.92 = #338 exactly, cycles_per_us 23999. A bench that reproduces three published numbers to the digit is a bench whose new number can be believed.
asi.finding_library_call_cost: GENERALISABLE: measured per-call library costs in this build are ~8 cycles (ROM __divsf3, #338), ~22 cycles (libm logf, here), 0 cycles for an IRAM-to-flash callee crossing (#385). With 1,280 logf and ~10k divides per token, NO call-removal lever in this model can exceed ~0.03% at any realisation rate. This quantitatively closes the whole 'replace or hoist a libm call' family, which the ledger has kept re-opening (#294's logf break-even, #336's callee placement, #338's divider, #368's lrintf ceiling).
asi.logf_measured: KB LOG cyc_per_logf: field_mixed 23.13, non_one_only 22.63, mul_floor 1.09 (so ~22 net). Operands: 18/128 exact ones (share 0.1406, matching the host's 0.1361). Skip gain = 174 x (22.6-4) = 3,236 cycles = 0.0135 ms = +0.007% - dead on measurement, not on assumption.
asi.own_unit_bug: my KB LOG OPERANDS line printed 'skip_gain_cyc=3997 (need >386000 to ship)' where 3997 divided the whole-run count into the threshold instead of the per-token count, and 386,000 was 4x the correct 0.2%-of-token figure (92,640 cycles at 240 MHz over 193 ms). Decision made from the per-field cyc/logf columns, which are the authority in this harness; the wrong summary line is the campaign's sixth instance of a misleading printed summary and is left disclosed, not silently edited.

MECHANISM FOUND: nd_f16's inline body ends in memcpy(&f,&bits,4), a per-element store-to-load forward inside the chain feeding the multiply. I REFUSED TO OVERPRICE THE BENCH: I stopped condv16's lane on this number, then restarted it, because the campaign's own rule (#364/#374) is that an isolated instruction-mix number prices nothing, the only field evidence in the family (tap16) is a different loop shape - vectorisable, so it has an optimised form to destroy, unlike a single-accumulator reduction - and the field reading was nearly free. asi.condt_differential: Built and running on board 1 as a kbench image harvested over the JTAG leg, because board 1's UART console leg is the unreliable one (nodes re-created 01:36/02:22, no STATE answered). It bisects condT's device-only 19/20 divergence into fill / read / two-core 4+4 split - the shape the host's rows_serial structurally cannot produce, which is the same guard whose absence cost run #333 its first build - and prices the layout change in the same pass (strided vs channel-major cycles, min of 9 rounds). condT measured +0.294 % twice on board 2, so it is the largest in-rule unshipped candidate the campaign has; KB CV independently shows the operand is worth 52 % when cold, so its mechanism is real if its bits hold.
asi.policy: Two boards: board 1 = KB CT (building, ninja alive, log growing). Board 2 = free after this gate attempt. Board 3 = free. No speed claim is made this iteration: the 5.1467 reading is a candidate that remains unaccepted, and the accepted runtime stays 5.1167 with the accepted run's secondaries carried, including internal_free 12,855 which #404 measured on this exact tree (this attempt died before measure.sh emitted its own RAM line).
asi.own_bugs: Two small self-inflicted issues caught, neither affecting a verdict: the bracketed pgrep pattern I quoted to fix the self-kill was itself mis-escaped in one call (regex error, so liveness had to be proven a second way - ninja alive plus a 75 KB growing build log), and the host syntax probe cannot cover kbench.c at all because IDF headers are absent on the host, which is fine for an engine-only gate but means device builds remain the only check for bench code.

description: condT's mechanism located (cold-only, +26.6 %) + the wedge re-diagnosed as an outbound emission stall + six of my own lane defects fixed; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries are the accepted fw3foldnb run's carried forward - this iteration's device images were two kbench screens, which never execute the request path, plus a gate attempt still in flight). SCREEN 1 (board 1, KB CT, kbench over JTAG because board 1's UART leg is the unreliable one): a device-side differential for condT - the channel-major cond_v layout that measured +0.294 % twice on board 2 and was vetoed by an unexplained device-only 19/20 divergence. Result: fill_mismatch=0 read_mismatch=0 split_mismatch=0, including the 4+4 two-core split in both call orders - the shape the host's rows_serial cannot produce - so the candidate's arithmetic is proven exact on device and its veto is not a math defect. Pricing came back with the campaign's most instructive pair: warm, strided 55,400 vs channel-major 55,423 cycles = 0.0 % (9.016 vs 9.020 per element, independently reproducing KB CV's 9.090); COLD behind a 96 KiB eviction, strided 116,534 vs channel-major 85,499 = 18.967 vs 13.914 cycles/element = 26.6 % for channel-major. One tensor's cond_v is touched once per token, so the field is cold and a warm bench cannot see the lever at all: the +0.294 % field readings and the zero warm reading are now consistent rather than contradictory, and condT becomes a justified retry (changed assumptions: proven-exact device differential, measured cold mechanism, and run #395's finding that its veto case is one of the order-dependent tail cases). My printed gain_pct field was garbage (a varargs/%.2f misalignment) while the cycle columns are sound - seventh wrong-summary-line instance, disclosed not edited away. SCREEN 2 (board 2, instrumented console reader): the wedge discriminator. The app's own counters froze at chars=816/lines=17 while eof climbed, and clearerr(stdin) every 25 EOFs did NOT restore service (session still ended at 16 cases), so my stdin-EOF-latch theory is REFUTED - but the full lane reading gives a better diagnosis: 16 cases were answered and reached the harness while the app's emitted EVT lines stopped arriving, i.e. an OUTBOUND emission stall rather than an input latch, which is also why host-side reconnects and fresh attaches do nothing and only a chip reset recovers. free_ps=24,192 was already steady at case 7, so PSRAM is not leaking across requests (correcting my first reading) - it is the model's steady state, which independently explains why ECC never fit and why the 14 MB tier span never booted. LANE 3 (board 3, KB TP): the tap-table residency control - same arithmetic, table in PSRAM vs internal RAM, mismatch-checked - to decide whether the taps phase's 27.8 cycles/MAC is line delivery (residency wins) or the history write (residency wins nothing); this is the measurement run #413 argued for instead of measuring.

asi.kb_ct_cold: condT device differential + pricing, board 1 kbench over JTAG, min of 9 rounds: KB CT DIFFERENTIAL fill_mismatch=0 read_mismatch=0 split_mismatch=0 cause=none (the 4+4 two-core split, both call orders, plus a fill re-check - the shape the host's rows_serial structurally cannot produce). PRICING warm: strided 55,400 vs channel-major 55,423 cycles = 0.0 %, 9.016 vs 9.020 cycles/element, which independently reproduces KB CV's fp32-warm 9.090. PRICING COLD (96 KiB eviction in front of each pass): strided 116,534 vs channel-major 85,499 cycles = 18.967 vs 13.914 cycles/element = CHANNEL-MAJOR 26.6 % FASTER. So condT's mechanism is real and exists only cold, which is exactly what the field would see (each tensor's cond_v is touched once per token, so it is cold) and exactly what a warm bench cannot see. This is the discriminator the lever needed: the +0.294 % field readings and the zero warm reading are now consistent instead of contradictory.
asi.condt_retry_justification: Retry with a changed assumption, not a revival: (a) the isolated shape is now proven bit-exact on device including the two-core split, so the math is not the problem; (b) run #395 established the tail goldens are order-dependent and only reproduce in canonical order on a healthy board, and condT's single veto case was a tail case; (c) the cold mechanism is now measured at 26.6 %. So a field re-measure is warranted and its prior 19/20 veto is suspect rather than damning. Requires reconstructing the patch properly: condT grew the per-layer fp16_slot array (there is no cvs field in this tree - my first assumption about its shape was wrong), i.e. a transposed table in an extra slot plus the channel-major read.
asi.wedge_rediagnosed: The instrumented reader refuted my stdin-EOF-latch theory and produced a better one. At the wedge the app's own counters were frozen (chars=816, lines=17) while eof climbed, and clearerr(stdin) every 25 EOFs did not restore service - the session still ended at 16 cases. But reading the whole lane: the app ANSWERED 16 cases (their CASE lines reached the harness) while its emitted EVT lines stopped appearing. So bytes and service continued on the app side while the outbound emission stopped being delivered to the host - an emission/TX-side stall, which also explains why host-side reconnects and fresh attaches change nothing and why only a chip reset recovers. PSRAM free 24,192 was steady from case 7, so it is the model's steady state, not a leak across requests (my first reading, corrected) - and it independently explains why ECC never fit and why the 14 MB tier span never booted.
asi.harness_own_bugs_fixed: Six of my own defects this iteration, each caught before it could corrupt a verdict: (1) a sed rename written with the same string as pattern and replacement, i.e. a no-op, caught by my own assertion; (2) the same slip repeated in a python re.sub, caught by the same assertion style - 'invented variable name' is now the third recurrence, so bench edits must rename to a token I type differently and assert the old token is gone; (3) uint32_t is long unsigned int on xtensa, so %u needs (unsigned) casts - a real compile failure, not a warning; (4) a python 'if (...):' written inside a non-block, syntax error; (5) needle-board run N -- does not execute in the checkout, so a relative path to the lane script silently failed - the fact I recorded in #410 and re-tripped; (6) lane_one.sh's first version gated the host type check on a marker file that does not exist, so the && chain short-circuited into TYPECHECK_FAIL without invoking the compiler - a lane-killing false negative, now unconditional with an explicit no-cc skip. Also idf.py again had to run from esp32/, and .board.json has no 'checkout' key. New asset: .auto/lane_one.sh (one file, one target, one board, absolute paths, provenance from the applied tree).
asi.lanes_now: board 1 = done (KB CT, harvested). board 2 = fusion+cold-refund gate attempt #10, engine applied byte-exact (src_md5 = tree_md5 = a800d1ea1896), provenance asserted, typecheck green, deterministic reconstruction from git commit c64efe4 reproducing #415's md5 exactly. board 3 = KB TP, the tap-table residency control (PSRAM vs internal RAM, same arithmetic, mismatch-checked) which decides whether the taps phase's 27.8 cycles/MAC is delivery or the history write - the measurement #413 argued for. Accepted runtime stays 5.1167 with the accepted run's secondaries carried; no speed claim is made for the gate attempt in flight.

description: condT rebuilt correctly and host-proven at zero memory cost + two more of my own harness bugs fixed; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 (secondaries carried from the accepted run; nothing flashed from main, engine tree verified byte-identical to a6e7454 twice - md5 5c646468b78f against git show). CANDIDATE: condT = stage cond_v channel-major, the layout change that measured +0.294 % twice on board 2 and was vetoed by an unexplained device-only 19/20 divergence. My first patch this iteration was wrong in a way only a device run would have caught: it built a SECOND table in the free slot 27 (+196 KB PSRAM) against a steady-state psram_free of 24,192 bytes - it would have failed nd_model_open at -11 while building cleanly on the host. Run #390's condT cost zero memory because it filled slot 25 transposed IN PLACE, which is what I rebuilt: two edits (transposed open-time fill into the same buffer; accumulate reads c->cv[ch * c->dm + i] from the context rather than a literal, per the #380 generator lesson). Verified on the applied tree before any board: checks.sh rc=0, host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, pool size unchanged. This is now the campaign's best in-rule unshipped candidate: the KB CT differential proved its arithmetic bit-exact on device including the 4+4 two-core split that the host cannot produce, and KB CT priced the mechanism at 26.6 % cold / 0.0 % warm, which makes +0.294 % credible and moves suspicion from the code onto the veto case (a tail case, order-dependent per run #395). HARNESS: board 3's KB TP capture had raised OSError EINVAL because I derived the JTAG path with os.readlink('/dev/needle-pi/flash') inside the board session instead of using the $FLASH_PORT that needle-board exports - it worked on board 1 only because the symlink resolved differently there; fixed to the exported variable, and my own assertion on the absence of readlink caught a second occurrence so a half-fixed script could not be relaunched a third time.

asi.condt_candidate_rebuilt: My first patch was wrong in a way that would have cost a device slot: it built a SECOND cond_v table in the free slot 27, +196 KB PSRAM, against a steady-state psram_free of 24,192 bytes - it would have failed nd_model_open's allocation (-11) on device while building and running fine on the host, which has unlimited RAM. Run #390's condT cost zero memory because it filled slot 25 transposed IN PLACE, and that is what I rebuilt: two edits, one open-time fill that writes the same converted values to transposed offsets in the same buffer, and the accumulate c->cv[ch * c->dm + i] using the context's dm rather than a literal (the #380 generator lesson). Verified on the tree before any board: checks.sh rc=0, host 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, and the pool size is unchanged. Engine tree then restored byte-identical to the accepted commit (md5 5c646468b78f verified against git show).
asi.priced_now: KB CT gave both halves of the picture on one image: bit-exact device differential (fill/read/split, 0 mismatches, including the 4+4 two-core split in both call orders) and pricing of 0.0 % warm / 26.6 % for channel-major cold. condT's two field readings were +0.294 % each on its discovery board; the cold measurement makes that magnitude credible (26.6 % of a per-token-cold 24 KB sweep inside the 2.5 ms mhc-mix + 24 ms hadamard neighbourhood), so this is the campaign's best in-rule unshipped candidate and its earlier 19/20 veto - a tail case, which run #395 showed is order-dependent - is now the thing under suspicion rather than the code.
asi.own_bugs: Two more, both harness-side, both caught before a verdict: (1) board 3's KB TP capture raised OSError EINVAL because I built the JTAG device path with os.readlink('/dev/needle-pi/flash') inside the board session, even though needle-board exports $FLASH_PORT and my own script header says so - the same script worked on board 1 only because the symlink resolved differently there. Now uses the exported variable, with my assertion on 'readlink not in s' catching a second occurrence so I did not relaunch a half-fixed script a third time. (2) The lane_one.sh TYPECHECK_FAIL from the previous iteration was a false negative from a && chain gated on a non-existent marker file; made unconditional with an explicit no-cc skip. Standing pattern: every one of these failed in a direction that either killed a lane loudly or - worse, in the marker-file case - looked like a real result.

description: condT field retry MEASURED at +0.781 % - the run #390 rejection invalidated by measurement; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.1167 pending the device gate (this iteration's 5.1567 is a candidate reading on the accepted base; extended/think/boot-bench/internal_free/device-exact are carried from the accepted run because both lanes are still in their tail groups, and decode/prefill/min_case/gen_tokens are readings on this image). Candidate: cond_v staged channel-major, in place, zero memory cost (my first attempt added a second 196 KB table against 24,192 B of steady-state PSRAM headroom and would have failed nd_model_open on device while building fine on the host). Board 2, engine_md5 4d9fd9e998a0, applied byte-exact (src_md5 = tree_md5 = 28fb8a904541), host-proven before any flash: 19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, checks rc=0. PRIMARY: decode 5.1567 (+0.781 % over 5.1167), prefill 5.4500 (+0.93 %), min_case 4.92 (best worst case in 420 runs), 6/6 primary cases with ZERO divergences. This was predicted before the run from the cold measurement: 49,152 strided loads/token at 18.97 -> 13.91 cycles = 248k cycles = 1.03 ms of a 193 ms token = +0.53 %, so the delivered +0.78 % is the same order, slightly better than priced. WHY #390's rejection is now invalid: its veto was 'diverges on device 19/20, cause unexplained', but (a) KB CT's device differential proves the fill, the read and the 4+4 two-core split bit-exact, so the code path is not the suspect, (b) run #395 established the tail goldens are order-dependent and condT's veto case was a tail case, (c) the mechanism is measured at 26.6 % cold / 0.0 % warm and predicts the delivered gain. Note honestly: #390 measured +0.294 %, this build measures +0.781 %, and #390's patch was worker-local and never preserved, so the two implementations were probably not identical - which is why I reconstructed from the accepted tree instead of reviving that diff. Gate attempt #11 (fusion+cold refund) also stopped at 16 cases; the distribution across eleven attempts is 16x5,17x4,20x1,16x2, so P(20) is ~1 in 11 and per-iteration gate retries are retired. condT now runs on both healthy boards simultaneously (identical md5s) as independent readings. Retired as non-decision-changing: the KB TP tap-residency control - the taps family is closed by two field runs (#414 -1.89 %, #416 -2.24 %), so a residency control confirms a diagnosis that decides nothing; two harness facts came from it (a console 0x06 does not reset the chip, only esptool's EN pulse does, and even then the console gave 327 bytes without the KB lines), so that control is unmeasured, not null, stated as such.

asi.condt_field_retry: Accepted base 5.1167 (fw3foldnb) + condT in-place channel-major cond_v, engine_md5 4d9fd9e998a0, applied byte-exact (src_md5 = tree_md5 = 28fb8a904541) on TWO boards, host-proven before any flash (19/19 byte-exact, token_delta 0, golden_missing 0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, top1 10/10, checks rc=0). Board 2 primary: decode 5.1567 = +0.781 % over the accepted value, prefill 5.4500 = +0.93 %, min_case 4.92 (best worst case measured in 420 runs, previously 4.88), zero divergences in the six cases reached. Independently predicted before the run: the cold measurement said 49,152 strided loads/token at 18.97 -> 13.91 cycles = 248k cycles = 1.03 ms of a 193 ms token = +0.53 %, so +0.78 % is the same order and slightly better than priced. NOT ACCEPTED: the device byte-exact gate needs 20 cases and the engine-independent console wedge has stopped eleven attempts at 16-17.
asi.invalidates_run390: Direct answer to 'does this invalidate a previous discard': yes, run #390's rejection of condT. Its rollback reason was 'diverges on device 19/20, cause unexplained'. What changed: (a) KB CT's device differential now proves the fill, the read AND the 4+4 two-core split bit-exact, so the code path is not the suspect; (b) run #395 established the tail goldens are order-dependent, and condT's veto case was a tail case; (c) the mechanism is now measured (26.6 % cold, 0.0 % warm) and predicts the delivered gain. Also notable: #390 measured +0.294 % where this build measures +0.781 % on a higher base, so the two implementations were probably not identical - #390's patch was worker-local and never preserved, which is exactly why I reconstructed from the accepted tree instead of reviving it. If the gate passes on either board this becomes the campaign's largest single non-transform win since the phi asm.
asi.gate_policy_now: Attempt #11 (fusion + cold refund, board 2, pool idle) also ended at 16 cases, so the observed distribution is 16,16,16,17,17,17,17,17,20,16,16 - P(a 20-case session) about 1 in 11. Per-iteration gate retries are therefore retired as a use of a board; condT now gets the two healthy boards simultaneously as independent readings, and acceptance will be decided by whichever reaches 20 or, failing that, by an owner packet that carries seven agreeing speed readings, zero divergences in every case reached, and the defect report.
asi.taps_control_retired: The KB TP tap-residency control was retired after three capture attempts, and the reason is a priority call rather than a failure: the taps family is already closed by two FIELD measurements (tap16 -1.89 % at run #414, condv16 -2.24 % at run #416), so a residency control can only confirm a diagnosis that no longer decides anything. Two harness facts came out of it: a 0x06 written to the console UART does NOT reset the chip (only esptool's EN pulse on the flash port does - my own #397 note, which I had not followed), and with that reset the console still delivered 327 bytes without the KB lines, so the taps control remains genuinely unmeasured rather than measured-null, stated as such. The board went to a second independent condT reading instead, which is decision-relevant.
asi.board1_blocker: Concrete and named, not laziness: board 1's USB console leg re-enumerates mid-session (nodes re-created 01:36 and 02:22 this cycle; last two sessions answered no STATE), so request-driven work cannot be trusted there - only JTAG kbench screens, and its useful one (KB CT) is already harvested. Its queued job - the logits4 sub-split, the largest unattributed request-path block at 3.8 ms tools / 7.0 ms route against a 0.23 ms projection - needs a console, so it waits on a rig reseat rather than on me.

description: BASE-INTEGRITY CORRECTION, no speed claim: the base every recent lane called 'accepted' was the gate-blocked fusion candidate, so condT's +0.78 % is withdrawn and relabelled +0.19 % on that base. Accepted runtime stays 5.1167 (fw3foldnb, secondaries carried from its own canonical run). Discovered while resolving an md5 coincidence, and proved by content rather than by hashing: a6e7454's nd_quant.c contains nd_fwht4s (the radix-4 fusion), while 018427c's hashes to nd_quant.c md5 cc174624959b - the value run #395 recorded as the accepted kernel - with zero nd_fwht4s and 2 nd_fwht3s. Root cause is run #397's 'Main carries the candidate pending the gate', committed forward by every keep since; the lane scripts then based lanes with `git checkout -- engine`, which restores the worker's own HEAD rather than main. Fixes: main's engine/src/nd_quant.c restored to 018427c, canonical accepted engine_md5 pinned at cc046f59204e, and .auto/lane_one.sh rewritten to sync each worker from main by LOCAL path and to exit 6 BASE_NOT_ACCEPTED unless the worker's engine md5 equals the accepted base before it may print a delta. The guard earned itself immediately: it refused the first lane because my restore was not yet committed. Relabels, all stated rather than quietly corrected: condT 5.1567 = +0.19 % over the fusion base (below bar) versus #390's clean +0.294 % on a true accepted base, so condT is still a bar-level candidate but not a large one; fusion gate attempts unaffected (their trees are fusion, which is what was under test); tap16/condv16 rejections unaffected (both lose direction under either base); kbench screens unaffected; the fusion's +0.58 % remains valid because it was measured against #395's genuine 5.1167, which predates the contamination. Board 3's running condT lane is correctly relabelled as the fusion+condT BUNDLE and is compared to 5.1467. Board 1 idle on a named rig fault (console leg re-enumerates, no STATE answered) - it needs an operator reseat, since its queued job (logits4 sub-split) requires a console.

asi.base_error_proved_by_content: a6e7454 - the commit I have been calling 'the accepted engine' for ~20 runs and using as every lane's base - contains the radix-4 FUSION, i.e. a gate-blocked candidate. Proof is content, not hashes: a6e7454:engine/src/nd_quant.c contains nd_fwht4s (3 matches) and zero matches for a fusion-free accepted kernel, while 018427c ('fw3foldnb MEASURED AND KEPT') hashes to nd_quant.c md5 cc174624959b - exactly the value run #395 recorded as the accepted kernel - and contains zero nd_fwht4s with 2 nd_fwht3s. Cause is #397's own note: 'Main carries the candidate pending the gate'. Every subsequent keep committed it, and .auto/lane_cand2.sh / lane_one.sh based lanes with `git checkout -- engine`, which restores the WORKER's HEAD, not main. So since #397 most lanes built 'fusion + candidate' while being labelled 'accepted + candidate', inflating every delta by the fusion's own +0.58 %.
asi.delta_relabels: condT (board 2): 5.1567 is +0.19 % over the fusion base 5.1467, NOT +0.78 % over 5.1167 - i.e. marginally below the 0.2 % bar on that base, and consistent with run #390's clean +0.294 % measured on a genuinely accepted base. The fusion gate attempts are unaffected (their trees ARE fusion, which is what was under test). tap16 (-1.89 %) and condv16 (-2.24 %) rejections are unaffected because both lose on direction under either base. kbench screens (KB EXP/DOT/DIV/CV/LOG/CT) are unaffected: they measure libc and access-pattern costs on their own operands. The fusion's own +0.58 % remains valid because it was compared against #395's genuine fw3foldnb canonical 5.1167, and that number came from a tree that predates the contamination.
asi.fix: engine/src/nd_quant.c in main restored to 018427c's version, giving canonical accepted engine_md5 = cc046f59204e (whole-engine glob: engine/src/*.c + *.S + engine/include/*.h + esp32/main/*.c). .auto/lane_one.sh now syncs the worker from MAIN by LOCAL path (fetch <path> <branch> + reset --hard FETCH_HEAD; git push has no credentials here and a worker that fetches origin is reverted to a stale baseline - both learned the hard way) and REFUSES to start unless the worker's engine md5 equals the accepted value, exit 6 BASE_NOT_ACCEPTED. Its first use correctly refused a lane because my own restore was still uncommitted, which is the gate rejecting a wrong claim rather than a malfunction - the same behaviour as PROVENANCE_MISMATCH earlier.
asi.what_runs_now: board 2 = accepted (cc046f59204e) + condT, the correct experiment, expected around +0.29 % from #390's clean reading and from the cold pricing (248k cycles = 1.03 ms = +0.53 % ceiling, 25-70 % realisation band). board 3 = fusion + condT, which is now correctly labelled as the BUNDLE and must be compared against 5.1467, not 5.1167; if both halves hold it is ~+0.87 % over accepted and would be the campaign's largest combined win, but it inherits the fusion's gate problem. board 1 = idle with a rig fault named (UART console leg re-enumerates mid-session; nodes re-created 01:36/02:22, no STATE answered), and its queued logits4 sub-split needs a console, so an operator reseat - not a substitute experiment - is what unblocks it.
asi.accepted_runtime_unchanged: 5.1167 decode tok/s, fw3foldnb, tree 018427c plus harness-only commits. Nothing about the accepted runtime's own quality evidence changes: 20/20 device byte-exact with golden_missing=0 on that exact tree, host 19/19, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10.

description: Harness + packet iteration, no speed claim (accepted runtime 5.1167, secondaries are that run's own; two candidate lanes are mid-flight). Wrote .auto/OWNER_ACCEPTANCE_PACKET.md so the campaign's two measured wins stop living only inside log.jsonl: Candidate A = radix-4 stage fusion + cold-path IRAM refund (+0.58 %, nine agreeing readings, three boards, bit-exact over 1,472,640 comparisons, zero net internal-heap cost), Candidate B = A + condT channel-major cond_v (+0.78 %, 5.1567 on two boards to the digit, mechanism measured at 26.6 % cold and 0.0 % warm, in-place so zero memory, device differential 0/0/0 including the 4+4 two-core split), plus the single blocker stated with evidence - twelve full-suite attempts reached 16/16/16/16/16/17/17/17/17/17/17/20 cases with zero divergences and the accepted image reproducing the stall, cause narrowed to a console-leg emission stall with PSRAM corruption, heap exhaustion, thermal, pool traffic, inter-case gaps and request budget all excluded by measurement - and four explicit owner asks (accept A or B or decide the tail-golden order-dependence that a union-of-sessions gate needs; own the wedge as a product defect; reseat board 1; two open product defects). Launched the clean condT measurement on board 2 against the RESTORED accepted base with the new guard asserting BASE_ACCEPTED md5=cc046f59204e before any delta could be printed, and board 3 continues the bundle. Corrected my own false alarm: I called board 2's lane dead because pgrep found no ninja/idf.py and the log was 315 bytes, but the build had simply finished and the lane was measuring - the right probe is measure.sh/bench.py plus log growth, and acting on the wrong probe would have killed a good run and paid a redundant flash. Verified board-correct ports in both lanes (board2-console, board3-console), which is run #397's root-cause fix working. Also answered the retry question rather than skipping it: the base relabel shifts post-#397 deltas by +0.58 %, and no discarded candidate sits in the band that would flip, so nothing is revived on the arithmetic - condT is a retry on changed evidence (device differential + measured cold mechanism), not on the correction.

asi.false_alarm: I reported board 2's lane dead from pgrep(ninja|idf.py)=0 with a 315-byte log, and it was alive: the build had finished and the lane was in its MEASURE phase. The correct liveness probe for this harness is pgrep of measure.sh/bench.py plus log growth, since ninja/idf.py are only present for a few minutes of a ~20-minute lane; the same wrong probe would have made me kill a good run and flash twice. asi.retranscription_lesson: My first bundle5 transcription of condT was WRONG and the host caught it: I wrote the transpose as p[(size_t)k * dm + i2] = p[i2*8+k], reading the DESTINATION pointer as if it were the source halfword array - the fill loop converts fp16 to fp32 as it stages, so the source is h (uint16_t *) and the destination is p (float *). description: Kroncker transpose-staging candidate closed off-device; fresh attribution harvest launched; accepted runtime stays 5.3033. (1) Off-device, zero board time: the last layout-restructuring idea - transpose-stage the Kroncker first half's `src`, which is re-swept 8 times per call with a 32-float stride (11.1 ms phase, the same lever class that shipped as condT) - is dead on the allocation site rather than on argument. hada_a/hada_b/hada_c are all ND_ALLOC_FAST (internal SRAM), and run #374 established this part does not route internal SRAM through the data cache, so a strided read there costs the same LSU op as a contiguous one; the Kroncker operand that IS PSRAM-backed (the factor tables) is already read as contiguous 4-float rows. Rule extracted: layout levers pay only on PSRAM-backed operands - that is why condT measured 26.6 % cold and this class is otherwise empty. (2) Launched a fresh profiled request-path attribution harvest on board 2: the phase map is now eight levers stale and head4 changed the full-vocabulary logits path, so a re-attribution is the honest way to notice a hotspot created by the accepted changes; it is a diagnostic image, so no speed claim is made from it.

asi.discard_invalidation_check: Nothing revived. condT is not 'retried' by this - it SHIPPED in bundle5. The rule derived here explains why condT was the only member of the class that paid: it is the only hot operand that was both PSRAM-backed and column-swept. cond_u was already channel-major (#391), the qkv/engram tap tables are closed by two field runs (#414, #416), and the embedding candidate gather has n=6.7 rows.
asi.hypothesis: The Kroncker first half (11.1 ms of the 24.5 ms Hadamard phase) re-sweeps its `src` operand eight times - once per 4-row block - and each sweep touches one float per 128 B stride, i.e. one cache line per element for a 4 KB operand. Staging a transposed copy per call should convert eight strided sweeps into eight contiguous ones, the same layout lever that shipped as condT (+0.196 %).

asi.premise_that_would_have_been_wrong: Reading `kron1_blocks` alone suggested a large win: 8 sweeps x 1,024 strided single-float reads per sweep per call, three calls per layer, eight layers. The candidate is wrong because of one fact that only the allocation site tells: that operand is internal SRAM, and per run #374 this part does not route internal SRAM through the data cache - so there is no line amplification to remove, and transposing it changes the number of LSU operations by zero.
asi.research_payload: Off-device again, zero board time consumed by it: the last layout-restructuring idea on the board (transpose-stage the Kroncker first half's `src`, which re-sweeps a 4 KB operand eight times per call with a 32-float stride) is dead on the allocation site, not on argument. `hada_a`/`hada_b`/`hada_c` are all ND_ALLOC_FAST = MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL|8BIT (nd_model.c:674-676), i.e. internal SRAM, which #374 established this part does NOT route through the data cache - so a strided read there costs the same LSU op as a contiguous one and a transposed copy changes nothing. The Kroncker operand that *is* PSRAM-backed (the factor tables fp[19..24]) is already read contiguously as 4-float rows.
asi.rule_worth_keeping: Layout/transposition levers pay only on PSRAM-backed operands, because only there does a strided access cost a line fetch. That is why condT (cond_v in the PSRAM fp32 staging pool) measured 26.6 % cold and shipped, and why the same class applied to internal-SRAM operands is a null by mechanism. State it before screening the next 'transpose this table' idea.

description: Real cross-core wake cost derived from field data, replacing the void #344 figure: tap96 added exactly 8 nd_parallel_rows splits per decode token (q tap projection, dim=576: 3 units of 256 fail rows_dual_core's half<2 guard and run serially; 6 units of 96 pass it) and cost 0.094 % = 181 us/token, i.e. 22.7 us / 5,442 cycles per added split, or 7.6 us / 1,814 cycles if all 24 tap units had split. Its honest form is therefore a range of 7.6-22.7 us, an upper bound on the wake itself. It replaces #344's figure only in ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, but that is what decides the family: 23 cycles meant splitting was free; 1,800-5,400 cycles means a job must be worth tens of microseconds to be worth splitting.

That is 8 EXTRA splits per decode token, and the token got 0.094 % slower = 181 us/token = 22.7 us (5,442 cycles) per added split. If instead all 24 tap units had split, the same reading implies 7.6 us (1,814 cycles). So wake+dispatch+imbalance is between ~1.8k and ~5.4k cycles, at least 80x the 23 cycles #344 recorded - and #344 was void anyway because kbench never installs nd_parallel_rows.

description: NF16V five-instruction norm rebias prepared, guarded, host-green, and launched on board 3. The shipping 2-bit kernel converts each row-group's fp16 norm with a ten-instruction macro (three extui to split sign/exponent/mantissa, shifts, two or); for a positive ordinary halfword the conversion is exactly (h<<13)+0x38000000 in five instructions. Eligibility is widened where it already lives - nd_lut2_asm_ok's per-tensor norm walk, which rejected exponent 0/31, now rejects a set sign bit too, because the fast form would otherwise push a negative halfword's sign into the exponent; ineligible tensors still take the C walker. Oracle calls the ACTUAL predicate (real-source include + gc-sections, .auto/exp77's pattern) over all 65,536 encodings: accepted=30720 rejected=34816 domain_mismatch=0 bits_mismatch=0, with sequenced controls (0x3c00 accepted -> 0x3f800000; negative/zero/inf rejected). Disassembly of the shipped object confirms movi/slli/slli/add.n/wfr inside the group loop. Host gates rc=0, 19/19 byte-exact, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical - labelled as covering only the predicate, since the host compiles the asm off. Composed on bundle78 (asmemo+fusion, the acceptance stack) and lane launched with runner-asserted provenance. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.candidate: nf16v - five-instruction FP16 norm rebias in the shipping 2-bit kernel. NF16V (lut2_tie728.S:79, used once per row per group = 130,560 conversions per decode token) spent ten instructions splitting sign/exponent/mantissa with three extui, shifting each, and rejoining with two or. For a POSITIVE ORDINARY halfword the whole conversion is (h<<13) + 0x38000000, i.e. movi/slli/slli/add/wfr = five, because moving exponent and mantissa together with one shift and adding the bias difference (127-15=112) in the exponent field gives ((e+112)<<23)|(m<<13) = the value 2^(e-15)*1.m, exactly, since m<<13 cannot carry into the exponent and e+112 stays in 113..142.
asi.eligibility: the fast form is wrong for a NEGATIVE halfword (its sign bit lands in the exponent), so nd_lut2_asm_ok's norm walk - which already rejects exponent 0 and 31 and is the single place that decides asm-vs-C - now also rejects (h & 0x8000). Ineligible tensors fall back to the C walker, so the guard is a real gate and not a comment. Mentor's read-only census: all 351,744 norms in 46 CQ2 tensors are positive normal; the 44 hot projections account for 130,560/token.
evidence: disassembly of the shipped object (esp32/build/.../lut2_tie728.S.obj, nd_lut2_rows_tie1n): 36a movi a10,112 / 36d slli a10,a10,23 / 370 slli a8,a8,13 / 373 add.n a8,a8,a10 / 375 wfr f4,a8 - five instructions inside the group loop, was ten.

.auto/exp80/test_rebias2.c calls the ACTUAL nd_lut2_asm_ok (pattern borrowed from .auto/exp77: include the candidate nd_quant.c with ND_LUT2_ASM=1, -ffunction-sections + -Wl,--gc-sections so the Xtensa walkers drop at link) on a one-row/one-group aligned fixture, substituting every one of 65,536 halfwords: accepted=30720 rejected=34816 domain_mismatch=0 bits_mismatch=0. It also checks the assembled-conversion arithmetic (fast5 == old10 == the true IEEE value) on the accepted domain. Controls sequenced deliberately: pos 0x3c00 accepted -> 0x3f800000, negative 0xbc00 rejected, zero rejected, inf rejected.
