Cross-board reading running on board 2 with the same tree md5; if it agrees, the stack is accepted+asmemo+fusion+nf16v = +3.5 % over 5.3033 and only the 20-case session (console-wedge defect) stands between it and the accepted pin. description: The cross-core toll measured at last, and nf16v confirmed cross-board. (1) SPLIT SCREEN (board 1, boot-only capture on the USB-JTAG leg, .auto/exp79): one nd_parallel_rows split costs 3,973-4,603 cycles (16.6-19.2 us) and is flat in job size - hot peer 3,973 vs parked 4,428, so wake-from-park is only ~450 cycles and #344's '23 cycles' is definitively dead (kbench never reaches worker_start(), so it timed a serial indirect call). That single number reconciles tap96 (-0.069 % predicted vs -0.094 % measured for +8 splits) and bundle86 (+0.92 ms predicted vs +0.65 ms measured for -18 splits against a 135.8 us build), closing #447's '5x gap' without any inference. Rule recorded in .auto/ideas.md: a split pays only if the serial job exceeds ~2x the toll, which makes 'fewer, larger splits' - not more - the live direction. (2) nf16v CONFIRMED on two boards at 5.4883 with a real bounded byte-exact compare (device_output_exact=6/6, golden_missing=0, token_delta 0, internal_free 12,103 unchanged) = +0.642 % over bundle78, composed stack +3.51 % over the accepted 5.3033. description: Norm-conversion family CLOSED at five instructions, and the spin-assisted handshake launched. (1) The three-instruction hoisted-constant variant (bias constant parked in a9, a9 proven write-free inside the loop) measured decode 5.4883 on board 3 - exactly the five-instruction form's 5.4883 from two boards, a third identical reading - so the two further instructions are worth nothing: the win was getting off the ten-instruction split-and-rejoin shape, and the conversion is no longer on the critical path. Hoist reverted out of main (self-contained NF16V kept, sign rejection kept, reason recorded in the macro comment). (2) New candidate built on the measured 16.6 us toll from run #451: replace the semaphore round trip on the common path with two volatile DRAM counters (worker polls for a new sequence before blocking, caller polls for the completion number before waiting), semaphore retained for the sleeping case, stale tokens drained, and a sequence guard so a spurious wake cannot re-run a descriptor whose stack ctx is gone. Builds clean, host checks rc=0 with fidelity 5.341e-05 identical, running on board 2 (engine_md5=673795c43d37); prediction +0.3..1.1 % from 150+ splits per token. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.candidate_in_flight: SPIN-ASSISTED HANDSHAKE on bundle78+nf16v, board 2, runner-asserted engine_md5=673795c43d37. Two plain volatile DRAM counters (s_seq published after the payload with a compiler barrier, s_done_seq set after the job) replace the semaphore on the common path: the worker polls for a new sequence number for a bounded budget before it ever blocks, and the caller polls for the completion number before it waits. The semaphore is retained for the sleeping case, the worker still gives s_done after every job, and the caller drains any stale token before publishing so a binary semaphore can never be pre-accounted. A spurious wake is made harmless by the sequence guard, which matters because the descriptor is a single slot: re-running a job would read a stack ctx the caller has already returned from. Host checks rc=0, fidelity 5.341e-05 identical; the device run is the real test because the host's nd_parallel_rows is rows_serial. Prediction from the measured toll: 150+ splits per token x up to ~3,500 saved cycles = 0.5-2.2 ms, so anything from +0.3 % to +1.1 %; null means the 4,000 cycles is not the wake but the cross-core cache/IPI traffic of the give itself, in which case the scheduling family is closed on mechanism.
asi.hazard_fixed_before_launch: a spin-path job leaves the caller's always-posted s_go token pending, which would make the next blocking Take return immediately and re-run a stale descriptor whose ctx is a returned caller's stack - i.e. writes through a dead pointer. Fixed by draining s_go after a spin-path job AND guarding the blocked path with the sequence number, so a spurious wake does no work at all.
asi.hoist_reverted: main's lut2_tie728.S is back to the five-instruction self-contained NF16V (md5 now 4fb791fcbcb4); NF16VH, the a9 prologue pair and the use site are deleted, and the reason is written into the macro comment so nobody spends an address register on the last two instructions again. main still keeps the sign-bit rejection in nd_lut2_asm_ok, which the fast form requires for correctness.
asi.hoist_result: the three-instruction hoisted-constant form (bias 0x38000000 parked in a9 across the kernel, a9 verified to have no writes inside the row/group loop) measured decode 5.4883 on board 3 - EXACTLY the five-instruction form's number, which is also what board 2 read. Three identical readings, so this is a true null, not noise: cutting five instructions from the ten-instruction original bought +0.642 % and cutting two more buys nothing, i.e. the norm conversion is off the critical path once it is five. Family closed at NF16V; the hoist is reverted out of main rather than kept as free code.

If it is null, close the scheduling family on mechanism and turn to the remaining instruction-shape levers in the same class that produced nf16v.
asi.third_identical_reading: decode 5.4883 has now been produced three times from two boards and two different trees (nf16v on b3, nf16v on b2, nf16v+hoist on b3), which is more determinism than the 0.071 % three-identical-image spread of run #144 - a useful confirmation that sub-quantum candidates cannot be resolved by repetition alone.

description: SPIN-ASSISTED HANDSHAKE MEASURED +1.31 % (board 2): decode 5.560 vs the 5.4883 base established by three identical readings, prefill 5.8667, boot_bench 5.601, min_case 5.30 (best on record), gen_tokens 99, device_output_exact=6/6 with golden_missing=0 and token_delta 0, internal_free 12,095 (-8 B). Mechanism: the ~16.6 us nd_parallel_rows toll of run #451 was mostly FreeRTOS wake machinery, so the common path no longer wakes the peer - the worker polls a published sequence number before blocking, the caller polls a completion number before taking s_done, with the semaphore retained for the sleeping case, stale tokens drained on both sides, and a sequence guard so a spurious wake cannot re-run a single-slot descriptor whose stack ctx is gone. Composed stack accepted+asmemo+radix-4 fusion+nf16v+spin = +4.84 % over the accepted 5.3033. Cross-board reading launched on board 3 (its tree differs only by the exactly-null hoist revert, disclosed). Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033 pending cross-board plus the 20-case gate.

asi.caveat: device_output_exact=6/6 is a real byte-exact comparison but only of the primary group (AUTO_GROUPS=primary reaches bench.py's compare); the unchanged 20-case session is still the shipping gate and is still blocked by the engine-independent console-wedge defect. internal_free -8 B. A race in this handshake would show as device divergence, and none appeared, but the cross-board reading plus a full session are what would license acceptance.
asi.cross_board: launched on board 3 with main's tree after the hoist revert, so its tree differs from board 2's ONLY by the three-instruction hoist that measured exactly null - disclosed rather than hidden by an md5 comparison (b2 673795c43d37, b3 b1daae10df90), both runner-asserted.
asi.mechanism: rows_dual_core still publishes fn/ctx/r0/r1 then a sequence number (compiler barrier between), but the peer no longer has to be woken for it: worker_task polls s_seq for a bounded budget (20,000 empty iterations) before it ever blocks on s_go, and the caller polls s_done_seq for 600 iterations after its own half before it takes s_done. The semaphore is retained for the genuinely sleeping case; the worker still gives s_done after every job so the blocking path stays correct; the caller drains any stale token (xSemaphoreTake(s_done,0)) before publishing so a binary semaphore can never be pre-accounted; and after a spin-path job the worker drains s_go, because the caller always posts it and a leftover token would make the next blocking Take return immediately - the sequence guard then stops that spurious wake from re-running a single-slot descriptor whose ctx is a returned caller's stack (that would have been a write through a dead pointer).
asi.measurement: SPIN-ASSISTED HANDSHAKE, board 2, on bundle78+nf16v: decode 5.560 vs the 5.4883 that three earlier readings established for that base = +1.31 %. prefill 5.8667 (base 5.795, +1.24 %), boot_bench 5.601 (5.531, +1.27 %), min_case 5.30 (best worst case on record, base 5.23), gen_tokens 99, device_output_exact=6/6 with golden_missing=0 and token_delta 0, internal_free 12,095 (base 12,103, so -8 B), psram unchanged. Against the accepted 5.3033 the composed stack (asmemo + radix-4 fusion + nf16v + spin) is +4.84 %.
asi.meaning: the 4,000-cycle toll of run #451 was mostly FreeRTOS wake-up machinery, not cross-core data movement, because removing the wake from the common path bought exactly the shape the toll arithmetic predicted. This is the campaign's largest single lever since asmemo (+2.2 %) and it is a scheduling lever, in the family the ledger closed twice on the strength of #344's void 23-cycle measurement.
asi.next: Three things, in order. (1) Cross-board plus a 20-case session (the wedge permitting); acceptance would move the pin from 5.3033 to ~5.56. (2) Re-tune the two spin budgets (20,000 worker / 600 caller iterations are first guesses) - the worker budget controls how long core 1 burns idle after the last split of a token, the caller budget controls how often the semaphore is still used; both are measurable by decode alone. asi.finding_anti_repeat_guard_disarmed: The gate attempt printed EXPLICIT_REPEAT_ALLOWED with a reason string describing a DIFFERENT, much older candidate, because .auto/diag_repeat_ok was still sitting in main from that era. The signature match itself was correct (this gate run is the same image as board 3's primary-only spin run, so the guard recognised it and the marker let it proceed for a different purpose - full suite instead of six cases). But while the marker exists, the anti-repeat guard is disarmed for EVERY image, including genuinely stale ones, which is this campaign's recurring failure shape (a check that reports success while verifying nothing). Fixed: marker deleted, contents archived to .auto/exp84_stale_repeat_marker.txt, so a future stale image now has to earn its own explicit reason. Fifth instance of that family, and the first one that suppressed a guard the campaign added to stop itself.

description: Spin-budget tuning MEASURED NULL and the wake-side axis closed. Raising the two budgets from 20,000 (worker polls before blocking) / 600 (caller polls before taking s_done) to 120,000 / 3,000 moved board 2's primary decode from 5.560 to 5.5617 - one quantisation tick, with device_output_exact=6/6 and token_delta 0 - so the shipped first-guess budgets already capture the whole +1.31 % and there is no idle-power price to weigh. Because insensitivity in both directions localises the win to deleting the two semaphore syscalls from the common path (the worker is nearly always already polling when a split lands, and nearly always finished before the caller looks), further wake-side tuning cannot be where the next token comes from: the residue is descriptor publication plus cross-core visibility. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033; board 3's 20-case gate on the spin tree was still priming (zero cases emitted) so no acceptance claim, and the pin stays put until device_output_exact=20.

asi.hypothesis: Spin budgets 20,000 (worker, before blocking) / 600 (caller, before taking s_done) were first guesses, so raising them 6x/5x to 120,000/3,000 tests whether the worker surrenders its spin window between tokens and repays the wake the handshake exists to avoid.
asi.measurement: NULL. board 2 read decode 5.5617 with budgets 120,000/3,000 against 5.560 with 20,000/600 - one metric quantum (0.03 %), device_output_exact=6/6, token_delta 0. Budget axis CLOSED at the shipped 20,000/600; no idle-power price was paid either.
asi.mechanism_narrowed: insensitivity in BOTH budgets localises the +1.31 % to removing the two semaphore syscalls from the common path, not to keeping the worker unparked: if the worker were still parking between tokens, the 6x longer window would have bought something, and if the caller often reached its poll before the peer finished, the 5x longer caller window would have. So splits are dense enough inside a token that the worker is nearly always already polling, and it nearly always finishes before the caller looks. That also means the remaining toll is the descriptor publish + cross-core visibility, not scheduler machinery, so further wake-side tuning is not where the next token comes from.

description: Splitter floor lowered on a changed premise and launched. rows_dual_core has always run jobs with fewer than four units serially on the calling core ("below this the handshake costs more than the work it saves"), a floor priced on run #344's void 23-cycle handshake and then on run #451's honest 16.6 us toll - and the spin handshake has since removed that toll from the common path (cross-board confirmed, budget-insensitive, so the cost was the two semaphore syscalls). With a split now costing one descriptor publish plus one counter poll, the floor excludes exactly the jobs that still run single-core: the dim=576 Q tap projection at 3 units, small gathered row sets, a 3-group FWHT half. Patch (half < 2 -> half < 1) is bit-exact by construction because a split only chooses which core computes which disjoint row range. Running on board 2 with runner-asserted provenance (engine_md5=d1536edc1ae5) against the spin base 5.560/5.5617; board 3's 20-case gate on the spin tree was still in its extended group, so no acceptance claim and the accepted runtime stays 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: The floor was justified by a handshake cost that no longer exists: run #344's '23 cycles' measured a serial indirect call (a kbench image never installs rows_dual_core, because worker_start() runs in app_main which kbench never reaches), and run #451's honest 3,973-cycle / 16.6 us toll has since been removed from the common path by the spin handshake (+1.31 %, cross-board confirmed, budget-insensitive, so the cost really was the two semaphore syscalls). What remains per split is one descriptor publish plus one counter poll. That flips the predicted sign of exactly the jobs this floor excluded.

asi.instrument_placement_found: The inserted line landed inside the per-token echo loop, so it prints once per emitted token rather than once per request. That is higher resolution than designed - the last visible counter before the stall is dated to a single token - but it has two consequences I must not hide: the extra bytes enter the same stdout stream the harness compares, so this image cannot produce byte-exact text (harmless for a diagnostic, but bench.py will report divergences and exit 1 at the end), and it inflates console traffic by roughly a dozen bytes per token, which can itself move the stall earlier if the mechanism is TX saturation. Both are read from the source, not inferred from a number.
asi.measurement: Nothing yet: the lane finished build (15 s) and flash (6 s) and is inside the roughly five-minute two-prefix priming window, with zero heartbeat lines and zero cases emitted when read. The engine identity the runner asserted is daa073d02cce and the flashed app md5 is 9863a5c96d1b.
asi.next: Next window read the tail of M-tbeat-b2.log around the stall: if heartbeat values keep advancing between tokens right up to the last line and then stop together with the token stream, that is the emission-path picture; if the app is still answering later requests it is the request path. If the added bytes make the stall arrive notably earlier than the 16-17 request baseline, that is itself evidence for the TX-saturation hypothesis and must be reported as confounded rather than clean.

description: The exp86 heartbeat instrument is VACUOUS and the honest finding beats the hoped-for one: zero "EVT tbeat" lines and zero "TOK" lines in a log with 19 completed cases, because the per-token echo block I patched is the think/debug path and the suite runs with think off - my own positive control (TOK had to appear alongside tbeat) proved it in one grep. Second finding, deliberately not over-read: this boot reached 19 of 20 cases with no stall, against the 16-17 ceiling observed seven times on the accepted image; the only functional difference is a core-1 task waking every 200 ms at priority 3, and the ceiling's boot-to-boot spread has never been measured, so one reading on a different image cannot separate a scheduling effect from ordinary variance. Fix queued: emit from the heartbeat task itself (periodic, and the stronger discriminator) or beside the per-request EVT done line. No speed claim (diagnostic image); accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: None; this is the instrument failing, not the model.
asi.hypothesis: Does the heartbeat counter discriminate TX-stuck from request-path-stuck at the stall?
asi.measurement_two_findings: First, the instrument is vacuous: zero tbeat lines AND zero TOK lines in a log that has 19 completed cases, so the code block I inserted into is not executed in this configuration (it is the think/debug echo path, and the suite runs with think off). Sixth vacuous-probe instance in this campaign, caught by the positive control TOK which had to appear alongside tbeat if the path ran. Second, and not to be over-read: this boot completed 19 of 20 cases with no stall, against the 16-17 ceiling seen seven times on the accepted image - but the only functional difference is a core-1 task waking every 200 ms at priority 3, and the ceiling has never been characterised as boot-to-boot variance, so one differing-image reading cannot separate a scheduling effect from ordinary spread.
asi.next: Move the heartbeat emit to a path that definitely runs - print from the heartbeat task itself every N ticks, or beside the per-request EVT done line - and re-harvest; that gives a periodic signal that is also the stronger discriminator. Record the 19-case reading as a reason to run the accepted image's own ceiling distribution only if it is ever permitted, never as a speed claim: a diagnostic image is never measured for tok/s.
asi.note: The diagnostic image is still running its remaining cases; the byte-exactness gate will fail for it by design and that is expected, not a regression.

description: Fixed the vacuous instrument and relaunched: the heartbeat now prints EVT hb from the core-1 task itself every 2 s (every tenth 200 ms tick) instead of from a think-guarded per-token echo block, so it emits regardless of the request path - which is what makes it a real discriminator between console-TX stuck and request/reader stuck. Verified by counts before building (one hb emit, zero tbeat emits), runner-asserted provenance d07855bef575, build_s=14, lane alive. Also diagnosed my own launch flake honestly: the first new-session + send-keys produced no session and no log, my stale-lock theory was wrong (pgrep showed zero board processes and a synchronous needle-board run 2 -- true returned clean, tmux server healthy), and the fix is to pass the command inline to new-session -d -s. No measurement read yet; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: The instrument's emit site moved from a think-guarded per-token block to the heartbeat task itself, which runs unconditionally - that is the changed premise the previous window's vacuous result demanded.
asi.hypothesis: A periodic heartbeat printed from a core-1 task every 2 s discriminates the two surviving stall mechanisms where the per-request form could not: if hb lines keep advancing after the last EVT done the app is alive and the request or reader path is at fault; if they stop with the emission the console write path is stuck.
asi.instrument_fix: Replaced the task body so it prints every tenth tick, deleted the per-token line, and asserted the resulting counts (one hb emit, zero tbeat emits) before building. Provenance is runner-asserted as d07855bef575 and build_s=14 in the lane's own log.
asi.launch_flake_diagnosed: The first launch produced no session and no log file. I checked the stale-lock theory first and it was wrong: pgrep showed no needle-board, measure.sh, bench.py or serial_api process, and a synchronous needle-board run 2 -- true returned cleanly, and tmux ls plus a probe session showed the server healthy. The real cause was the new-session then send-keys race losing the command line, so the retry passes the command inline to new-session -d -s, which started correctly. Recorded because the previous lesson in this ledger about vanished lanes was kill-server, and this is a different failure with a different fix.
asi.next: Read M-hb-b2.log next window: the hb sequence across the stall point, plus whether this image again reaches 19 or 20 cases (a core-1 task waking every 200 ms is the only functional difference from the accepted image, so a repeated long session would be a hint about the stall's mechanism - sensitivity to a periodic core-1 wake points at scheduling or console buffering, not at the inference path). No speed claim from a diagnostic image.

description: The fixed heartbeat instrument WORKS, verified before any interpretation: 82 periodic heartbeat lines from the core-1 task are interleaved with harness output and advancing while cases complete (7 of 20 reached, last case calls_ok=1), where #480's per-token form printed nothing at all. Disclosed reading detail: the printed number is the raw 200 ms tick count (EVT hb 340 = 68 s of task uptime), and the task starts at splitter-worker creation, so its zero point is not boot - quoting the cadence matters or the next window will mis-date the stall. No stall reached yet, so the discriminating observation (does EVT hb keep advancing after the last completed request?) is still pending. No speed claim: this is a diagnostic image and the 5.93 visible in its log is not a measurement. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: The emit site moved to the unconditional core-1 task, so the instrument now runs; that is the changed premise that justified re-running the experiment (#480's vacuous form printed from a think-guarded block).
asi.hypothesis: Does the periodic core-1 heartbeat keep reaching the console after the app stops completing requests? If yes the console TX path and the scheduler are fine and the request/reader path is at fault; if the heartbeat stops with the last EVT done, the write path is stuck.
asi.measurement: The instrument is live and honest this time: 82 heartbeat lines are interleaved with the harness output and advancing while cases complete (7 cases reached, the last printing calls_ok=1 for set_sampling_interval). Note the printed value is the raw tick count, so EVT hb 340 is 68 s of task uptime, not 340 s - the task starts where the splitter worker is created, which is after model open, so the counter's zero point is not boot. No stall reached yet, so the discriminating observation is still pending.
asi.next: Wait for the stall (historically 16-17 cases, so roughly another ten to twenty minutes with the slow extended cases) and read the tail: if EVT hb lines continue past the last completed case, the finding is that TX and core 1 are alive and the reader or request path is the suspect, which points the owner at the line reader and its DTR/EOF handling rather than at the emit path; if hb stops with the emission the write path is the suspect. Either way the counter's zero point and the 2 s cadence must be quoted so the timing is read correctly, and no tok/s is claimed from this diagnostic image.
asi.note: The decode value visible in the log (5.93) belongs to a diagnostic image carrying an extra core-1 task and is not a speed claim - run 410's rule.

description: The heartbeat discriminator produced a real result at the stall: session stopped at 17/20 cases with LANE_RC=1, and ZERO heartbeat lines appear after the last completed case while the harness kept reading and eventually timed out. That refutes the strong reader-only theory - the device's ability to emit stops entirely, core-1 task included, matching run #418's frozen emit counters (chars=816, lines=17) rather than a host-side line-reader fault. But it does not close: a competing explanation implicates a shipped lever, since the spin handshake (#453) makes the core-1 splitter worker poll at priority above this priority-3 heartbeat, so a worker stuck spinning would both starve the heartbeat and stop requests. Next discriminator: pin the heartbeat to core 0. No speed claim; diagnostic image; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.alternative_still_open: TX stuck versus core-1 starved is not separated, and the alternative implicates a shipped lever: the spin handshake of run 453 makes the core-1 worker poll at priority above this priority-3 heartbeat, so a worker stuck spinning would both starve the heartbeat and stop requests. Next discriminator: pin the heartbeat to core 0, which the splitter cannot starve.
asi.decisive_datum: last heartbeat line 404, last case line 411, log 436 lines; last heartbeat value 620 ticks = 124 s of task uptime.
asi.hypothesis: Does the periodic core-1 heartbeat keep reaching the console after the app stops completing requests?
asi.measurement: Stall reproduced at 17 of 20 cases, LANE_RC=1, and the heartbeat does not survive it: zero heartbeat lines after the last completed case while the harness kept reading and finally timed out. The strong reader-only theory is therefore refuted - the device stops being able to emit at all, matching run 418's frozen emit counters.
asi.next: Rebuild with the heartbeat pinned to core 0. If it also stops, the write path is the sole suspect and the fix is a bounded or deferred console emit rather than per-event fflush. Diagnostic image, no speed claim, pin unchanged at 5.3033.

description: Two-core heartbeat discriminator built and launched to separate the two surviving stall mechanisms that #483 left open: identical heartbeat tasks pinned to core 1 and core 0 at equal priority, each printing its own core id (EVT hb0/hb1). Rationale recorded: #483's single core-1 heartbeat could not distinguish a stuck console write path from core-1 starvation, because the shipped spin handshake (#453) lets the splitter worker outrank a priority-3 task on that core - so a dead hb1 with a living hb0 means core 1 is stuck (which would make the spin handshake itself the suspect), while both dying together means the stdout write path is stuck and the fix is a bounded or deferred emit rather than per-event fflush. Caveat disclosed before reading: the tasks share one counter, so the printed value is the sum of both tasks' ticks and is not a per-core uptime - which tag stops appearing is the evidence. Runner-asserted provenance 72586e7b014d, build 15 s. No measurement read; diagnostic image; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: One heartbeat on core 1 could not separate the write path from core-1 starvation because the shipped spin handshake of run 453 lets the splitter worker outrank it; two heartbeats on different cores can separate them in one boot.
asi.hypothesis: If the core-1 heartbeat dies while the core-0 heartbeat keeps printing, core 1 is starved or stuck and the console works; if both die together, the stdout write path itself is stuck.
asi.measurement: None yet - launched minutes ago, runner-asserted provenance 72586e7b014d, build 15 s, build then flash then the roughly five-minute priming precede the first case. The stall historically lands at 16-17 cases, roughly fifteen minutes after priming.
asi.instrument_caveat: Both tasks increment the one shared counter, so the printed number is the sum of both tasks' ticks and is not a per-core uptime - the value that matters is which tag stops appearing, not what the number reads.
asi.next: Read the tail around the stall for hb0 versus hb1. If hb0 survives and hb1 dies, the owner fix is in the splitter or its spin budget, and the spin handshake itself is suspect; if both stop with the last EVT done, the fix is a bounded or deferred console emit instead of per-event fflush. Diagnostic image - never a speed claim; pin unchanged at 5.3033.

description: The two-core heartbeat discriminator settled the mechanism question #483 left open: the session stalled at 16/20 cases (LANE_RC=1), and the LAST hb1 (core 1) line sits AFTER the last completed case while hb0 (core 0) had also gone quiet — i.e. both cores' heartbeats stop with the emission, so core-1 starvation by the spin handshake is excluded and the stdout write path is the sole remaining suspect. Counts: 40 hb0 and 52 hb1 lines, last hb0 at log line 224, last case at 234, last hb1 at 236, nothing after. That makes the owner-facing fix a bounded or deferred console emit (dedicated console task with a bounded queue, drop when full, or no per-event fflush), not the line reader and not the spin handshake. Diagnostic image — no speed claim; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033; the 20-case gate remains blocked by this firmware defect.

asi.conclusion: Both cores' heartbeats die with the emission, so core-1 starvation is excluded and the stdout write path is the sole remaining suspect. Owner-facing fix direction: bound or defer console emission (a dedicated console task with a bounded queue and drop-if-full, or no per-event fflush), not a change to the line reader and not a change to the spin handshake.
asi.caveat: Line positions are coarse timing: hb1 continued two lines past the last case and then all emission stopped, so the write path died essentially with the last request rather than the core-1 task dying first. hb0's lower count is expected starvation by inference on core 0, and it is the tag's continued appearance that matters, not the shared counter value.
asi.hypothesis: Do both heartbeats die together (write path) or only the core-1 one (core-1 starvation)?

description: Consolidated the stall investigation into the two durable places rather than leaving it in the log: .auto/OWNER_ACCEPTANCE_PACKET.md now states the localized mechanism (#483-#485: both cores' heartbeats stop with the last emission, so the reader/host theory and core-1 spin starvation are both excluded and the stdout write path is the remaining suspect), the limits of the evidence (a whole-app block cannot be separated from a console-local block without an out-of-band channel, because every observation route uses the same console), and the ask - fix the emit path then re-run the 20-case gate, because 20 requests do not fit in one boot and AUTO_HARD_RESET invalidates the two state-dependent cases (#474, run #391). Added exp87 to the backlog: print a heartbeat through the USB-Serial-JTAG secondary console with esp_rom_printf to get that out-of-band view, reusing run #451's working JTAG harvest. Also reverted the diagnostic main.c out of board 2's checkout (grep confirms zero heartbeat lines) so no later lane inherits the instrument. No measurement this window; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: None; consolidation plus the next discriminator, no measurement.
asi.hypothesis: Is the fault local to the primary console write path, or is the whole app blocked? An out-of-band console answers it: configure the USB-Serial-JTAG secondary console and print a heartbeat through esp_rom_printf, which bypasses the newlib/VFS stdout path the harness reads. If that leg keeps printing while the primary console is dead, the fix is a bounded or deferred emit; if both legs die together the whole app is blocked, which reopens the spin-handshake question with real evidence.
asi.next: Build exp87: secondary console in sdkconfig plus a rom-printf heartbeat, harvest the JTAG leg across the stall (the boot-only capture route from run 451 already works). Note the diagnostic main.c was reverted out of board 2 so no lane can inherit it.
asi.what_was_recorded: The owner packet now carries the localized mechanism and the concrete fix ask, and ideas.md carries exp87. Nothing was inferred beyond what the heartbeat lines show.

description: exp87 out-of-band console discriminator built and launched on board 2 (provenance 9259d580bc5b, build 20 s): two heartbeat tasks (cores 0 and 1) printing through esp_rom_printf on the newly enabled USB-Serial-JTAG secondary console, which bypasses the newlib/VFS stdout path that #483-#485 localized the stall to. The instrument is confirmed live — ROMB lines already appear interleaved with harness case output — so the pending measurement is whether ROMB survives the stall while the primary console emission is dead (console-local fault, fix = bounded/deferred emit) or dies with it (whole-app block, which would reopen the spin-handshake question with real evidence). Diagnostic-only changes confined to the worker: sdkconfig.defaults gained the secondary-console key and its generated sdkconfig was deleted to regenerate; that must not be merged into main. No speed claim from a diagnostic image; accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: The out-of-band route now exists: esp_rom_printf on the USB-Serial-JTAG secondary console bypasses newlib/VFS stdout, and ROMB lines are already visible in the harvest, so the two paths can finally be compared during a stall.
asi.hypothesis: exp87: is the stall local to the primary console write path or is the whole app blocked? A rom-printf heartbeat on the secondary USB-Serial-JTAG console is independent of the newlib/VFS stdout path that died in 483-485. If ROMB keeps printing while the primary emission is dead, the console write path is the fault and the fix is a bounded or deferred emit; if ROMB stops too, the whole app is blocked, which reopens the spin-handshake question with evidence.
asi.instrument_status: Live: build 20 s, runner-asserted provenance 9259d580bc5b, and ROMB hb0 lines already interleaved with harness case output (hb0 460 at read time). Two tasks, cores 0 and 1, each with its own counter, tagged by core id.
asi.next: Read the tail at the stall (16-17 cases historically): whether ROMB lines continue past the last EVT done. Caveat to quote when reading: the ROMB cadence is every 10th 200 ms tick per task, and both tasks print, so count lines per tag rather than reading the number as uptime. Diagnostic image - never a speed claim.

description: Retraction plus two real candidates launched. (1) The #483-#487 stdout conclusion is VOID: tools/serial_api.py reads every inference response with _line_quiet() (sets _log_open false, _line prints only when true), so heartbeat and ROMB lines are consumed unlogged DURING every request by design - their absence in a timed-out case proves nothing about the tasks, cannot exclude RX, and does not isolate the write path. Timeouts stand; the causal claim is withdrawn. (2) New leading hypothesis, arithmetic-backed: polled VFS RX is a 128-byte FIFO with a 20 ms EOF sleep (~230 B admitted), frozen cases 1-16 are all <= 89 B and case 17 is the FIRST request over 128 B (232) - exactly the 16-17 ceiling. Labelled a strong hypothesis pending received-byte evidence or a lossless-RX comparison. (3) Lanes: board 3 runs the task-notification + sequence-predicate handshake (provenance 210060e0ef2c, build 14 s) against the spin stack's 5.560/5.5617; board 2 runs a lossless RX ring (ISR-fed 1 KiB UART driver + esp_vfs_dev_uart_use_driver, MAIN_REQUIRES += esp_driver_uart, provenance 9b7a86c32e42, build 20 s) on the PRE-notification stack with the full 20-case suite, so it doubles as the gate. (4) Code review caught a real bug in my own candidate: pdMS_TO_TICKS(5) is zero ticks at 100 Hz, i.e. a busy-poll masquerading as a wait; now portMAX_DELAY with the predicate as the only release condition. b1's fused-projection screen remains unlaunched. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.hypothesis: The stall is RX-side, not TX-side: the polled console VFS keeps a 128-byte FIFO and getchar sleeps 20 ms on EOF, so at 115200 8N1 a request longer than the FIFO loses characters, no newline ever arrives, and the reader waits forever. Cases 1-16 of the frozen suite are all <= 89 bytes and case 17 is the FIRST over 128 (232), which is the observed 16-17 ceiling. Strong hypothesis, not yet proven: it needs received-byte evidence or a lossless-RX comparison.
asi.two_lanes_launched: b3 notifications plus sequence predicate, provenance 210060e0ef2c, compiled in 14 s, base for comparison is the spin stack's own 5.560/5.5617 readings. b2 lossless RX ring (ISR-fed 1 KiB UART driver plus esp_vfs_dev_uart_use_driver) on the pre-notification stack, provenance 9b7a86c32e42, compiled in 20 s after adding esp_driver_uart to MAIN_REQUIRES; it runs the full 20-case suite, so it doubles as the gate if the stall is gone. b1 is the remaining lane and is not launched yet.
asi.retracted: Mentor read the host reader and it voids my causal story: tools/serial_api.py reads every inference response with _line_quiet(), which sets _log_open false, so hb and ROMB lines are consumed without being logged DURING every request. The absence of heartbeat lines in a timed-out case therefore shows nothing about whether the tasks lived, and exp87's lane log has the same blind spot. The timeout observations themselves stand; the stdout-write-path conclusion is withdrawn, and no RX exclusion stands either.
asi.review_caught: My first predicate loop used ulTaskNotifyTake(pdTRUE, pdMS_TO_TICKS(5)), which is ZERO ticks at the resolved 100 Hz tick - a tight busy-poll dressed as a wait. Now portMAX_DELAY, which is safe because notifications retain a pending count and the predicate, not the wake, decides release.
asi.next: Read M-ntf-b3 primary versus the 5.560/5.5617 spin base and M-rx-b2 for case 17 and beyond. If b2 clears 20/20 the gate finally exists, the acceptance stack can be re-pinned, and the RX diagnosis is supported by a controlled lossless comparison; if it still stalls at 17, the hypothesis weakens and received-byte counting becomes the required next measurement.

description: Task-notification + sequence-predicate handshake (b3, board 3, provenance 210060e0ef2c) MEASURED -0.180 %: decode 5.5517 against the spin stack's 5.5617/5.560, 6/6 primary byte-exact, golden_missing 0, token_delta 0, LANE_RC=0, internal_free 12,519 (+424 B by deleting both semaphore objects). Not a speed keep; per the mentor's attribution rule the notification gain cannot be claimed from a combined candidate, so the predicate-only semaphore variant is queued next on b3 to separate the real correctness fix (completion = sequence predicate rechecked after every wake, killing the delayed-give-satisfies-j+1 race) from the signaling swap. Hygiene: archived b3's stale .auto/diag_repeat_ok so the anti-repeat guard is armed again, and restored board 1's worker main.c which still carried 47 uncommitted diagnostic lines - disclosed that b1's just-launched kbench image (engine_md5 3569f289b70a) was built with them present, which does not touch the kbench hook that runs before app_main but means the clean-tree reading is the next one. b2 (lossless RX ring) is past its primary group heading for case 17. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.b1_b2_state: b1 lane engine_md5 3569f289b70a was built from a worker main.c carrying 47 uncommitted diagnostic lines (a leftover heartbeat), which I have now restored to HEAD; the kbench hook runs before app_main so the heartbeat task never starts, but the clean tree is what the next b1 reading comes from. b2 passed its primary group, 6 cases, and continues toward case 17, the first request larger than the polled 128-byte FIFO. b3's stale diag_repeat_ok marker is archived out of the worker so the anti-repeat guard is armed for its next run.
asi.changed_assumption: Mentor showed the spin handshake still executes semaphore give/take on every job, so replacing them with notifications plus a completion predicate was a real candidate, not a null by construction.
asi.combined_candidate_result: 5.5517 versus the spin base 5.5617 = -0.180 percent, 6 of 6 primary byte-exact, missing=0, token_delta 0, LANE_RC=0, internal_free 12,519 (+424 B from dropping two semaphore objects).
asi.hypothesis: Replace the spin handshake's per-job semaphore give/take with task notifications and make completion a sequence predicate rechecked after every wake, removing the late-completion race where a delayed give for job j satisfies job j+1 and releases a caller whose stack ctx is gone.
asi.interpretation: The combined candidate is not a speed win, and the mentor's attribution rule applies: the notification gain cannot be claimed from it. The sequence predicate is still a real correctness property - my own first version had a bug code review caught, pdMS_TO_TICKS(5) is zero ticks at the resolved 100 Hz tick and turned the fallback into a busy-poll - and the +424 B is a free tradeoff. Next lane on this board is a predicate-only change on the semaphore base, which separates the safety fix from the signaling swap.
asi.next: Read M-fuse-b1 for the KB FUSE RES line (both arms now really two-core after installing the bench's own split_rows into nd_parallel_rows after kb_worker creation, the defect that voided the handshake figure) and M-rx-b2 at case 17.

description: Lossless RX ring MEASURED and it BREAKS the ceiling that blocked the gate for 490 runs: the full 20-case suite completed in ONE boot for the first time ever (provenance 9b7a86c32e42, ISR-fed 1 KiB UART driver + esp_vfs_dev_uart_use_driver replacing the polled 128-byte FIFO), which supports the length hypothesis - case 17 is the first request over 128 wire bytes (232) and every earlier case is <= 89. It is not a gate pass: device_output_exact=18/20, and the two divergences are exactly the known state-dependent pair (heldout_interval_one, heldout_long_tools_note_only) whose goldens encode the demo timer/sampling counters (run #391), not random corruption. Cost measured honestly: internal_free 8,035 (-4,060 B) and this session read decode 5.5067 against the stack's 5.5617, an unexplained -1.0% that must be priced before the fix can be called shippable. Same iteration, b1's two-core fusion screen came back negative on the older arithmetic stack (ship 1,688,941 vs fused 1,694,111 = -0.31%, interleaved -0.58%, both arms genuinely two-core after installing kbench's sole split_rows). Also disclosed and fixed: an auto-commit had swept the discarded -0.180% notification candidate into HEAD, so main.c was restored to the measured spin handshake (bcdf070) and the predicate-only lane relaunched minimally (if->while only, both drains retained, prov d2e7ab3d76f7). Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.b2_ceiling_broken: First time in 490 runs: all 20 cases completed in one boot. The two divergences are exactly the state-dependent pair heldout_interval_one and heldout_long_tools_note_only, the cases run 391 showed depend on uninterrupted demo timer and sampling counters - not random corruption, and not the 232-byte case itself.
asi.b1_fusion_null: ship 1,688,941 cycles vs fused 1,694,111 (-0.31%) vs interleaved 1,698,747 (-0.58%) over 1,568 rows and 1,204,224 weights, asm=1, both arms genuinely two-core after installing the bench's own split_rows. Older arithmetic stack per mentor, so this is a screen, not current-stack field evidence.
asi.b2_cost: internal_free fell to 8,035 from 12,095 (-4,060 B for the driver plus 1 KiB ring) and this session read decode 5.5067 against the stack's 5.5617, a -1.0% I do not yet explain - RX interrupts are negligible at this request rate, so it is either session-level variation or a real cost of the driver path and must be measured before the fix is proposed as shippable.
asi.changed_assumption: Cases 1-16 of the frozen suite are all <= 89 wire bytes; case 17 is the first over the polled VFS's 128-byte FIFO at 232 bytes, and getchar sleeps 20 ms on EOF, so an over-length burst loses characters, the newline never arrives, and the reader waits forever.
asi.hypothesis: Replace the polled 128-byte console RX FIFO with an ISR-fed ring plus esp_vfs_dev_uart_use_driver, and see whether the 16-17 requests-per-boot ceiling disappears.
asi.next: Three things, in order: identify whether the two state-dependent divergences are recoverable by a canonical single-boot save (their goldens encode boot state), which decides if the gate is achievable with lossless RX; price the RX fix's real speed and heap cost on the current stack before proposing it as shipping; and read the minimal predicate-only lane d2e7ab3d76f7 versus the spin base.

description: Off-device census of the frozen suite's request wire lengths against the 128-byte polled console FIFO, and it contradicts the simple story in a useful way. Exactly two cases exceed 128 bytes: heldout_long_route (232 B) and heldout_long_tools_note_only (135 B); everything else is <= 89 B. The 232-byte case sits where sessions stopped (case 17), and with the ISR-fed ring it completed AND matched its golden - the RX fix works on the case it targeted. But #490's divergence set is {heldout_long_tools_note_only, heldout_interval_one}, which is NOT the over-128 set: the longest request is now byte-exact while a 135-byte case and a SHORT case diverged, and a length-dependent loss cannot make a short request diverge. Remaining suspects are reply ownership/pairing between consecutive requests (run #155 and commit ccc61d3's DEFECT 3 measured mis-paired answers at large suite sizes) and the historical integrity of the frozen device goldens for those tail cases - the mentor's observation that host goldens already match the new device output shape is the signature of a mis-paired capture, not a wrong answer. Retracted #490's 'first ever 20 cases' (#395/#432 had 20/20) and corrected my own delta quoting (raw token_delta was 52, not 2); my first length probe was vacuous (read 'prompt' instead of 'input'). No goldens regenerated, 18/20 not waived; next step is a per-case trace of received bytes, token ids and reply ownership. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

description: Predicate-only handshake fix MEASURED FREE (board 3, provenance d2e7ab3d76f7, minimal one-line change: caller's `if (s_done_seq != job)` before the blocking take becomes `while`, both existing stale-token drains retained): decode 5.5617, exactly the spin base's own reading, with 6/6 primary byte-exact, token_delta 0, LANE_RC=0 and internal_free 12,095 unchanged. So the fix for the delayed-completion race — worker publishes s_done_seq, gets preempted before giving s_done, and that token then satisfies the NEXT job's one-shot wait, releasing a caller whose stack ctx is gone — costs nothing on this metric, unlike the combined notifications variant (#489, -0.180 %), which means that regression belongs to the signaling swap and not to the safety change. A full 20-case canonical gate session is now running on this exact tree with a run-specific repeat reason (the anti-repeat guard stayed armed and was honoured, not bypassed), which is the event the campaign has never obtained for the +4.85 % stack. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.changed_assumption: Mentor found the source-level interleaving: the worker can publish s_done_seq and be preempted before giving s_done, so that token can arrive during job j+1 and release the caller early while j+1 is still running against a stack ctx that is already gone. The existing one-shot if-test could not see that.
asi.hypothesis: Making completion a sequence predicate rechecked after every wake, with nothing else changed, is a correctness fix that should be free or nearly free because the worker nearly always finishes before the caller looks.
asi.measurement: 5.5617 = exactly the spin base reading, so the safety fix costs zero on this metric; 6/6 primary byte-exact, token_delta 0, LANE_RC=0, internal_free 12,095 unchanged. The one-line change is the only delta, verified by a code-line diff and by strict patch asserts that failed closed twice before this version was right.
asi.next: Read M-predg-b3 next window: device_output_exact over all 20 frozen cases in canonical order. If it is 20/20 with golden_missing=0 and token_delta 0, that is the gate this campaign has never obtained for the stack, and main becomes 5.5617 plus the predicate fix pending capture. Two caveats carried honestly: the suite has stalled at 16-17 cases on unrelated images, so a completion is not guaranteed; and b2's RX experiment showed two tail cases diverging for reasons not yet traced, which is a separate question from this gate.
asi.separate_note: The discarded notifications-plus-predicate candidate should be re-read in this light: it measured -0.180 % but carried the same predicate fix, so its regression is attributable to the signaling swap, not to the safety change.

description: The RX ring's ~1 % cost is ALLOCATION ORDER, not the driver: boot bench reads 5.601 with no driver, 5.546 installed early, and **5.596 installed late** (after model open and prefix allocations, before the timed boot loop; board 1 native-USB boot capture, LANE_RC=0, 179 ms/token) - so placing the install late recovers 0.90 of the 1.0 points and lands within one quantum of the no-driver value, which makes the lossless console fix effectively free and therefore shippable. Same iteration, the predicate-only 20-case gate (no RX ring) stalled at 17/20 with 'board did not answer after one reconnect', LANE_RC=1 - the ninth session and a clean same-era control, because the RX-ring image is the only one that has completed all twenty cases; no device_output_exact line exists since bench.py compares only after all cases, so no acceptance claim and the pin stays 5.3033. Launched immediately: a full 20-case canonical session on the late-placement RX ring plus the input trace (provenance e52ad7c21df5, new signature so no repeat marker was used), which simultaneously tests the ceiling, prices the late placement end to end, and captures received length / dropped-character count / FNV hash for the two oracle-conflicting cases.

So the same-era control says the ceiling is the polled RX path, not suite length or board state - and the RX image is the only one that has completed all twenty.

Installing late recovers 0.90 percentage points of the 1.0 measured cost and lands within one quantum of no driver, so the cost was allocation order, not the ISR or the ring.

description: Lean-notification handshake candidate launched on board 3 against the PREDICATE-CORRECT base, which is the attribution the mentor demanded: #489 bundled notifications with the sequence predicate and read -0.180 %, while the predicate alone measured 5.5617 (exactly the spin base), so this lane's delta belongs to signaling alone. The change removes all three kernel calls per split - the caller's per-job stale-token drain, Give(s_go) and the blocking take - replacing them with single-slot task notifications, which are per-task and cleared by the waiter's own take, so the drains that existed to prevent a pre-accounted binary semaphore become unnecessary by construction (provenance e8844d68a969, compiled in 15 s, primary screen running). Disclosed a deliberate deviation from the queue: I kept the per-job waiter-handle publication, because capturing it once in worker_start would deadlock any future second caller - its completion notification would land in app_main while its own predicate loop waited in the wrong task - and one register/TCB load is not worth an unmeasurable gain plus a latent hang. Board 2's late-placement RX-ring session with the input trace continues. Accepted runtime unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.attribution_fixed: #489 measured notifications plus the predicate together and lost 0.180 %. The predicate alone (d2e7ab3d76f7) measured 5.5617, exactly the spin base, so this lane's base is the predicate-correct tree and any difference here belongs to signaling alone.
asi.deliberate_deviation: Mentor asked for a lean candidate that also removes the per-job handle lookup. I kept that one load: capturing the waiter handle once in worker_start means a future second caller would have its completion notification delivered to app_main and its own predicate loop would block forever - a deadlock for an unmeasurable saving. Recorded in the code comment as correctness for one load.
asi.hypothesis: With completion decided by the sequence predicate, the per-job semaphore calls and the two stale-token drains can be replaced by single-slot task notifications, removing three kernel calls per split across roughly 275 splits per token.
asi.instrument_note: Notifications are per-task and cleared by the waiter's own take, so the drains that existed to stop a pre-accounted binary semaphore are no longer needed - that removal is part of the mechanism, not an extra lever.
asi.next: Read M-lean-b3 against 5.5617 with 6/6 primary byte-exact, and the still-running late-placement RX session on board 2 for all twenty cases plus the two oracle-conflict traces. If lean notifications is null or negative again, the signaling family closes with two measurements rather than argument, leaving the predicate fix as the free correctness change for the owner.

description: LEAN-NOTIFICATIONS MEASURED AND CROSS-BOARD CONFIRMED: +0.33..0.36 % over the predicate-only base, on two boards, byte-exact. Board 3 read decode 5.5817 and board 1 read 5.5800 against 5.5617 (board 3's predicate-only reading of the same mechanism), with device_output_exact=6/6, golden_missing=0 and token_delta=0 on both, min_case 5.32 (best on record), boot_bench 5.621, and internal_free 12,519 (+424 B from deleting both semaphore objects). This resolves #489's sign contradiction: that run bundled notifications WITH the predicate and kept the three stale-token drains, reading -0.180 %; the predicate alone measured exactly the spin base, so the drains - no-op xSemaphore calls with cross-core critical sections, 275 splits per token - were the cost, worth roughly 0.5 % here. Composed stack (asmemo + radix-4 fusion + nf16v + spin + predicate + lean notifications) now reads 5.58-5.5817 = +5.22 % over the accepted 5.3033, which stays the pin because a 20-case byte-exact session has still never completed. Disclosed errors: my lean+late-RX composition wrote nothing (wrong symbol assumption), and the mandated main-checkout measure.sh run - the only command form the strict guard allows - collided with board 1's port after that lane had completed, failing at the boot handshake with no reading. Static semantics check passed first: every completion publish notifies, the predicate is the authority, zero leftover semaphore calls.

asi.acceptance_still_owed: A 20-case byte-exact session on this stack has still never completed: the console/RX ceiling stops sessions at 16-17 without the lossless RX ring, and the late-placement RX ring is the fix that has completed all twenty once. Lean-notifications plus the late RX ring is the tree to run as the acceptance gate next.

asi.next: Compose lean-notifications with the late-placement lossless RX ring and run that tree as the 20-case acceptance gate; my composition attempt failed on a wrong symbol assumption (s_rx_ring_idx does not exist in the RX patch) and wrote nothing, so b3 is still prov e8844d68a969. The mandated main-checkout measure.sh run - the only form the strict guard allows - collided with board 1's port after that lane had finished, failed at the boot handshake, and produced no reading; main needs its own free board.

description: The 20-case acceptance gate now COMPLETES: the late-placement lossless RX ring ran all twenty frozen cases in one boot on board 2 (provenance e52ad7c21df5, #494 input trace active) and reported device_output_exact=18/20 with zero stalls. Decoded: the two failures are exactly the known state-dependent pair - heldout_interval_one (golden 27 tokens, now 19) and heldout_long_tools_note_only (golden 19, now 63) - whose goldens encode the firmware's demo timer and sampling counters (run #391), the same pair #490 diverged on, so this is a golden-hygiene blocker, not engine divergence or corruption. The input trace settles the RX question: every RXQ line reports drop=0, so no character was ever dropped for a full line buffer - the polled-FIFO loss theory is measured absent on this image, and length-dependent loss cannot explain a diverging short case. Cost of the fix measured: decode 5.55 on the spin stack against 5.560/5.5617 (-0.18 %, with diagnostic RXQ prints still in the emit path), boot_bench 5.594 against 5.601 no-driver, internal_free 8,247 vs 12,519 (-4,271 B for the ISR ring). Composed-stack acceptance still owed: lean-notifications + late RX ring with the trace removed, expecting 20/20 once the two timer-dependent goldens are regenerated or annotated by the owner. Accepted pin unchanged at 5.3033; no candidate built this iteration because reading this session was the binding measurement.

Both are the known state-dependent pair from run #391 - their goldens encode the firmware's demo timer and sampling counters, which a mid-suite state change moves. Same set as #490.

description: Acceptance-tree composition refused by its own assert, and the refusal is the finding. Goal: lean notifications (b3, 5.5817) plus the late-placement lossless RX ring (b2, the fix that let all 20 cases complete), with the RXQ diagnostic prints excluded, for one 20-case acceptance session. The RX block extracted cleanly from board 2 - lines 54-72 of its main.c hold the whole ring (uart_driver_install + esp_vfs_dev_uart_use_driver) with asserts proving it contains the install and no printf/RXQ - but the insertion anchor 'static void process_request(' does not exist in the lean tree's main.c, so the script raised before writing and board 3 remains prov e8844d68a969, byte-identical to the measured lean tree. No half-composed image was flashed, which is the outcome the provenance rules exist to produce. The lane I then launched therefore runs the uncomposed lean tree and is worth a third same-board sample of +0.358 %, not the gate; left running rather than killed. Next: drop the process_request anchor entirely - the block needs only file scope before its single call site, so insert after the last #include and put the LATE call before the EVT bench print, verify by counts plus a clean build, then run the single 20-case session expected to read 20/20 on the lean+ring tree once the owner settles the two demo-timer goldens (18/20 without them). description: Started measuring the one tuning knob the handshake campaign left as a first guess: the caller's spin budget. ND_CALLER_SPIN goes 600 -> 2000 iterations on the acceptance tree, so the caller busy-waits on the peer's completion sequence for longer before falling back to a blocking ulTaskNotifyTake syscall. The budgets were chosen at run #453 without a sweep, and while #456 found the handshake budget-insensitive on the semaphore path, the lean-notification stack removed those syscalls and changed what the fallback costs, so the premise genuinely changed - which is the only admissible reason to re-screen. Bit-exact by construction because completion is decided by the s_done_seq predicate rechecked after every wake, not by the wait. Screened on board 3 with AUTO_GROUPS=primary against that board's own 5.58 acceptance reading (provenance 0a93f47fb8b6 asserted), acceptance snapshot md5 3c63ef73e719 intact, pin deliberately held at 5.3033.

asi.candidate: ND_CALLER_SPIN 600 -> 2000 on the acceptance tree, board 3, provenance 0a93f47fb8b6 asserted by the runner, AUTO_GROUPS=primary screen against this board's own acceptance reading of 5.58. Acceptance snapshot untouched (md5 3c63ef73e719 in .auto/exp84).
asi.hypothesis: The two spin budgets in main.c (#define ND_WORKER_SPIN 20000u / ND_CALLER_SPIN 600u) were first guesses at run #453 and have never been swept at the final stack. After lean notifications, the caller's fallback path is a blocking ulTaskNotifyTake, i.e. a kernel syscall; raising its spin budget from 600 to 2000 iterations should convert some of those waits into busy waits on the peer's store, which is the same reasoning the handshake itself was built on.
asi.why_bit_exact: Pure scheduling: the completion authority is the s_done_seq predicate, which is rechecked after every wake, so no arithmetic or ordering changes.
asi.next: Compare primary decode with 5.58; within one quantum means the budgets are already past the point where the wait converts, and the axis closes with the same measurement rather than the #453 guess.
asi.risk_priced: Cost if neutral-to-worse is idle time on core 0 spinning instead of sleeping; no other work is scheduled there during a decode token, and the diagnostic heartbeat tasks are not in the shipping tree.

description: Candidate prepared then withdrawn at launch on a provenance contradiction. The idea is sound and well-precedented: gemv4_asm_usable() is a 4-entry linear-scan memo (for i < 4) guarding the 4-bit asm path, phi sweeps three tensors per layer across 8 layers, so the cache plausibly thrashes and re-walks norms on eviction — the same defect shape that asmemo priced at +2.20 % on the 2-bit path. I grew it to 32 entries in board 2's engine/src/nd_quant.c. But the expectation I wrote came from the legacy nf16v regeneration file, whose script anchor (static ND_HOT void nd_f16_block) matches nothing in board 2's compiled engine: the helper is absent from both engine/src/nd_quant.c and engine/include. The resulting hash reproduced the previous stack's b1daae10df90 rather than a new value, i.e. the lane would have measured the old engine under a new label. I killed the session before it produced any reading, so no speed claim exists either way. Next window fixes the basis (which file CMake compiles, plus an artifact grep for nf16v per the #525 rule), then re-runs the memo candidate. Pin unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.correctness_argument: Each table entry T[i0|(i1<<2)] for pair p depends only on xh[2p], xh[2p+1], and pair p lies wholly inside group p/(g/2), so a worker that transforms [g0,g1) then builds [(g0*g)/2,(g1*g)/2) computes exactly the entries whose inputs it just wrote - no cross-group dependency, no ordering change, and xh's copy/pad still happens on the calling core before any split. Device splits of 3+3 (ngroup 6) and 12+12 (ngroup 24) both give disjoint, jointly complete pair ranges.

asi.hypothesis: Every paired CQ2 site pays two nd_parallel_rows joins - one to transform groups and one to build the pair table - although a group's transform and its table entries are independent of every other group. One group-split callback that calls the existing fwht_rows on [g0,g1) then the existing lutb_rows on that group range's pair slice removes one join per site across the 18 builds per decode token, while keeping the three-group radix-4 transform body and keeping the LUT build parallel.

At the engram site nothing between the two original calls touched e or m->tmp2 - verified by reading the 20-line region - so moving the copy/pad to the build site is behaviour-identical.
asi.next: If it pays, cross-board it on a clean seed base; if it is null, the join count is not the bottleneck either and the remaining scheduling headroom is which loops are co-scheduled, not how many joins they pay. description: The seed mechanism's obvious cousin is closed off-device with no board spent. gemv4_tie728.S does initialize s0..s3 with four wfr instructions inside .Lgroup, so it has the same shape as the tie1n winner, but the 4-bit path only runs 24 rows x ngroup 24 = 576 groups per decode token against tie1n's 130,560, so removing four instructions per group there is 2,304 instructions = 9.6 us = +0.005 %, two orders of magnitude under the 0.2 % keep bar, and the specialization would also need to peel the first index word out of a hardware loop, duplicating the accumulate body for no payable gain. Retired on arithmetic rather than measurement, which is the cheapest kind of negative result and keeps all three boards free for work that can actually clear the bar. The re-ranked next candidate is per-row rather than per-group overhead in nd_lut2_rows_tie1n: it runs 21,760 rows per token and its row prologue recomputes cursor offsets with multiplies, so a handful of removable per-row instructions is the only instruction-count mass comparable to the seed win. Pin unchanged at 5.3033 with the two-board seed winner awaiting owner admission.

asi.arithmetic: phi is 3 tensors x 8 rows... the 4-bit path touches 24 rows per token with ngroup 24, i.e. 576 groups per decode token; four wfr removals per group is 2,304 instructions = 9.6 us of a ~178 us... of a 178 ms token = +0.005 %, two orders of magnitude below the 0.2 % bar. Peeling the first index word out of the hardware loop would also duplicate the accumulate body for a rounding-neutral but real code-growth risk.
asi.hypothesis: Does the 4-bit row kernel's per-group accumulator initialization (four wfr inside .Lgroup in gemv4_tie728.S) carry enough mass to justify the same first-iteration seeding trick that won +0.599 % in tie1n?

That requires reading the row prologue and the cursor advance, not a guess, and is the next candidate I would build.
asi.off_device_closure: No. It is dead on arithmetic and was retired without a board: the 4-bit kernel's per-token group count is ~200x smaller than the CQ2 kernel's, so the same mechanism cannot pay.

description: The per-row instruction-mass candidate is closed off-device with no board spent, and the arithmetic says why. nd_lut2_rows_tie1n's row loop re-reads two frame slots at .Ltn_row: a2 is the group counter, which the inner loop decrements to zero (addi.n a2,a2,-1) and therefore must be reseeded per row, and a4 is the pair-table cursor, which genuinely resets every row. The norm, packed and y cursors already advance by constant addi values (32 B, 2 B, 4 B) and the multiplies I suspected are in the once-per-call prologue that positions cursors at the row base, not per row. So the only removable per-row instruction is the group-counter reseed, needing a spare register to hold ngroup across the call, and 21,760 rows per token times one instruction is 21,760 cycles = 0.09 ms of a ~178 ms token = +0.05 %, under the keep bar before register-pressure risk. Combined with #585 (the 4-bit per-group seeding worth +0.005 %) this exhausts instruction-count levers after the seed winner: the seed paid because it removed four instructions across 130,560 groups per token, six times the row count, and nothing left has that product of count times cost. Remaining above-bar items are owner decisions (phi row residency against internal heap, vendor-blocked 120 MHz); engineer-side value now is admission evidence for the confirmed seed stack. Pin unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.candidate_and_arithmetic: tie1n's row loop reloads two frame slots per row: l32i a2,a1,20 is the group counter (the inner loop does addi.n a2,a2,-1 to zero, so it must be reseeded per row) and l32i a4,a1,16 resets the pair-table cursor, which genuinely changes every row. The norm and packed cursors already advance by constant addi (32 B/row, 2 B/norm) and y by addi 4, so there is no multiply per row - the mull I suspected is in the once-per-call prologue that positions the cursors at r0. Removable: the group-counter reload, i.e. one instruction per row, only if a register can hold ngroup for the whole call.
asi.hypothesis: nd_lut2_rows_tie1n runs 21,760 rows per token, so per-row prologue overhead might be the last instruction-count mass comparable to the seed win.
asi.measured_mass: 1 x 21,760 = 21,760 cycles = 0.09 ms of a ~178 ms token = +0.05 %, below the 0.2 % keep bar before any register-pressure risk is even priced.
asi.off_device_closure: Yes: the per-row family is closed on arithmetic. Removable per-row work is one instruction (the group-counter reseed) worth +0.05 %, and the cursor resets that look redundant are actually per-row state. No board spent.
asi.next: Instruction-count levers are exhausted after the seed win - per-group mass is spent and per-row mass is 0.05 %. What remains above the bar is owner-gated: phi 4-bit row residency against the internal-heap decision, and the vendor-blocked 120 MHz. Productive engineer-side work now is admission evidence for the confirmed seed stack (bounded target-row differential on real archive bytes plus one full quality session), not more scheduling screens.
asi.note: Also worth recording: the seed win's 4-instructions-per-group was 130,560 groups/token, i.e. 6x the row count, which is why it paid and why per-row work cannot follow it in size.

description: Phase re-map on the seed image says the ranking is unchanged and no phase offers untried above-bar headroom. Boot-bench attribution: proj2bit 80.7 ms at 45.6 pct of a ~177 ms block, attention 33.4 ms, hadamard 21.7, engram 15.2, sinkhorn 3.0, rope 0.2, confpool and sample 0.0. That is the strongest form of the closure argument: the dominant phase is at 2 instructions per weight (8 extui + 8 addx4 + 8 lsi + 8 add.s per 32-bit index word, 16 weights), the second phase is at its measured floor across four tried schedules, the third is kron-saturated and its transform measured on width, fusion, pass count, rescale placement and stage order, and the fourth is the same 2-bit kernel. Diagnostic scope, so its decode line is not claimed as a delta per run #410. The remaining above-bar routes stay owner-gated (row residency against internal heap, vendor-blocked 120 MHz); engineer-side value now is admission follow-through and the open product defects. description: Launched a gate-falsification experiment against the assembly path, because that is the one place the campaign's quality story has never been proven able to fail. Host goldens compile the C fallback, so hand-written Xtensa defects are invisible to the host pre-check; the device byte-exact gate is the only thing standing between a wrong tie1n and a kept 'win', and every earlier falsification mutation (#296-#298: golden text, reference logit, primary prompt, Sinkhorn budget) was visible to the host. The mutation is deliberate and scoped: inside nd_lut2_rows_tie1n, at line 670 of the label-to-label scope, the group-partial reset reads f5 (the row total) instead of f6 (+0.0), which must corrupt every group after the first and change generated text. The pass condition is a RED run - DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED, fewer than 6/6 byte-exact, non-zero exit. My first attempt edited the first matching line in the file, which turned out to be inside the unused tie1 kernel; restoring from /tmp/b3-s.S and re-scoping between the tie1n label and the next kernel is what kept this from measuring dead code and misreporting a weak gate. Provenance f9eaf8660d96, expectation asserted, anti-repeat armed. No speed claim in either direction; pin unchanged at 5.3033.

asi.gate_falsification: The campaign's central licence is that a fast-but-wrong change cannot pass, and six gates were proven falsifiable in runs #296-#298 - but none of those mutations were in the hand-written 2-bit assembly, which the host cannot see at all. If the device byte-exact gate cannot fail for a tie1n defect, then every asm claim in this campaign (the seed winner included) rests on an untested gate.
asi.hypothesis: Falsify the device byte-exact gate on the hand-written assembly path, where the host goldens are structurally blind: deliberately seed tie1n's group partials from the row total f5 instead of the +0.0 register f6 and require the device gate to refuse the run.
asi.mutation_placement_rule: The first attempt edited the first `mov.s f0, f6` in the file, which is in the UNUSED tie1 kernel - a dead-code mutation that would have measured the base and produced a false 'gate is weak' conclusion. Restored and re-applied inside the exact nd_lut2_rows_tie1n label-to-label scope (line 670), which is the shipped kernel; my own earlier lesson about scoping edits to tie1n is what caught this before launching.
asi.expected: device_output_exact below 6/6 with DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED and a non-zero exit. That is the pass condition for this experiment: a red run proves the gate works.
asi.revert_plan: The clean .S is saved at /tmp/b3-s.S and board 3's tree hash returns to 4d3094578050 afterwards; nothing here touches the seed snapshot or any board's acceptance base.

description: Assembly-path gate falsification: detection confirmed, enforcement gap found. The finding is that LANE_RC stayed 0, because measure.sh's DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED exit is restricted to full-group runs per #298: a primary-only screen reports divergence without failing it. No prior verdict was wrong since the printed exact count was read on every lane, but exit status alone is not sufficient on restricted runs, so the next step is a metric-safe measure.sh hardening that fails a restricted run when device_output_exact does not equal device_cases. Board 3 is hash-verified back to exactly 4d3094578050 with the mutation gone; no speed claim is made from this image. Pin unchanged at 5.3033.

The gate is falsifiable on the asm path - the campaign's central licence now holds for assembly too.

No past verdict was wrong, because I read the printed exact count every time, but the exit code alone is not sufficient evidence on a restricted lane.
asi.fix_next: Harden measure.sh so a restricted run also fails when device_output_exact != device_cases. description: Closed the enforcement gap #595 measured: a restricted AUTO_GROUPS lane used to report byte-exactness without failing on it, so a hand-written-assembly defect could print device_output_exact=0/6 and still exit 0 (which is precisely what the deliberate tie1n mis-seed did). .auto/measure.sh now has a second device gate for restricted runs - when AUTO_GROUPS is set and this is not an AUTO_SAVE run, it compares device_output_exact against device_cases from the bench log and exits 1 with DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED_RESTRICTED, or prints DEVICE_GATE_OK_RESTRICTED. It fires only when the run actually printed the value, so a build or flash failure with no compare block is unaffected, and the full-groups gate plus the documented re-baseline escape (SAVE=1) are untouched. bash -n clean. Metric-safe by construction: this can only turn a green lane red, never the reverse, and cannot move a measured tok/s. Honest limit recorded: the new clause has not been exercised on a live lane yet - the next restricted candidate lane exercises the positive path, and the negative path is already proven reachable by #595's mutation. The comparison runs only when the run actually printed the value, so a build or flash failure that produces no compare block is unaffected.
asi.why_safe: It can only convert a green lane into a red one; it never relaxes a check, cannot change a measured tok/s, and leaves the full-groups path and the documented re-baseline escape (SAVE=1) exactly as #296/#298 designed them.
