The tree comprises: composed attention (B4W paired-head shared-V P.V + DOT8W 8-column QK + SELRES selective rescale), engram[1] staging (EG2), the narrow compact prefix, the amortised group hardware loop, the two-deep codebook schedule, the qk_hd==48 specialization, the sparse Sinkhorn exact fixed-point check, and the interleaved QK accumulator chains. That reads 6.1550 = +16.05% over the owner's accepted 5.3033 and +152.3% over the 2.44 session baseline. B1's own shippable-line tree is preserved in .auto/trees/, so the owner can choose either policy - fastest tree or conservative lineage - with no further measurement. The single outstanding item remains the owner's disposition of the two ring-related held-out cases: keep the lossless RX ring and re-baseline or replace them, drop the ring and lose the >128-byte request fix plus the 20-case suite, or keep them as blockers.

Ran the one experiment that was still genuinely open and decision-relevant: whether the two frozen #647 cases diverge because of console/firmware BACKLOG and per-request arrival timing, or because of persistent state. Tested on the best tree with the harness's own gap diagnostic - AUTO_GROUPS=extended with AUTO_CASE_GAP_S=5, i.e. five idle seconds before every request so any console or firmware backlog is fully drained between cases. Result: device_output_exact 15/17, exactly the same two cases, token_delta 52 unchanged, and heldout_long_tools_note_only still producing its 63-token repeating chain rather than the 67-token golden. So draining the console completely before each request does NOT restore the goldens: the divergence is not backlog, not per-request arrival timing, and not a transient that idles away. Combined with the earlier probes - inputs byte-identical, answers deterministic across repeats, order-independent within an image, and the host agreeing with the device on heldout_interval_one - the surviving explanation is a persistent state the ring establishes at or before priming, which makes it a firmware-state question rather than a harness artefact and squarely the owner's decision: keep the ring and re-baseline or replace the two cases (the ring is what fixed the >128-byte request wedge and made the 20-case suite completable), drop the ring and lose that fix and the suite, or keep them as blockers. What this run contributes to that packet is the removal of the 'it might just be timing' escape hatch: the timing hypothesis is now closed by measurement, not by argument. Nothing about the campaign's performance state changed - the tree is the same d6b8014fd2fb that reads 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, and this run only re-measured a subset of its cases with gaps inserted.

Prepared the decisive diagnostic for the one question the campaign cannot settle for the owner: is the two-case divergence an interrupt-timing RACE in the firmware (a real defect) or boot-time state (a re-baseline decision)? The gap test in #881 closed console backlog and per-request arrival timing - five idle seconds before every request changes nothing - which is itself odd, because an idle console means no ISR fires during the request at all. That leaves two families: persistent state established at or before priming, or an interrupt-timing race in the model's own execution, since the ring installs a UART driver whose ISR can preempt the two-core nd_parallel_rows handshake at arbitrary points. This campaign already found one latent cross-core hazard of exactly that shape (the shared 8 kB codebook table that was byte-exact on three boards by timing luck, reverted at run #162, and the single-job-slot fix at #163), and a race would be invisible to every probe run so far for a specific reason worth stating: inputs would be identical, the output deterministic within an image, and order-independent - because the preemption pattern would repeat on every run of the same image. The diagnostic is one build and no engine change: in a diagnostic image only, bracket nd_model_step_hidden with portDISABLE_INTERRUPTS/portENABLE_INTERRUPTS inside the generation loop and run the extended group. If the two cases return to their goldens, the divergence is a race and the owner's decision becomes a race fix rather than a re-baseline; if they do not, the state is established at priming or model open and the remaining check is a layout comparison - whether the UART driver's installation moves the model's own allocations, which is visible by comparing PSRAM and internal addresses between the two images. Cost about eight minutes; value is that it decides which of the two remaining explanations is true, and both of them change what the owner should do.

Corrected the #647 diagnostic I prepared last run, because it could not actually run, and replaced it with a cheaper non-invasive test that covers the same ground. The flaw: bracketing nd_model_step_hidden in portDISABLE_INTERRUPTS would stop the two-core nd_parallel_rows handshake dead - that handshake is built on FreeRTOS tasks, semaphores and cross-core wakeups, all of which need interrupts - so the image would either hang or silently serialise every split, and any difference in the two cases would then belong to the diagnostic rather than to the ring. Recorded so no future window spends a build on it. The replacement follows from what the ring actually is: its entire footprint is console_rx_ring_enable() plus one esp_driver_uart requirement in main's CMakeLists, with no model code and no model constant changed. So the sharpest question is layout rather than interrupts - does installing the UART driver move where the model's own allocations land? If free_internal_bytes or free_psram_bytes at EVT READY differ between ring and no-ring builds of the SAME tree, then the ring has shifted the heap, and a layout-dependent result means the firmware is reading memory it never wrote: a real defect, of the same family as the shared/uninitialised-state class this campaign already caught once (#159/#162). If the free figures are identical, the ring's effect is elsewhere and the remaining candidate is driver-owned state. The test is two lanes and no engine change: run the extended group on the best tree with the ring (recording the STATE free figures and the two cases' answers), then ablate the ring with a fresh build directory and repeat, comparing both the figures and the answers, and comparing allocation addresses rather than only sizes. Either outcome is decision-relevant for the owner: one produces a defect to fix, the other rules layout out. Campaign state unchanged: best tree d6b8014fd2fb reading 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Closed the #647 layout hypothesis by reading placement rather than by running another two lanes, and stated the honest position on the mechanism. The ring's call site is main.c:560 with its own comment recording the placement: 'LATE (#495): after model open + prefix allocations, before the timed boot loop'. Every model buffer - m->xh, m->lut, the KV cache, the PSRAM tier, the engram staging - is allocated before the UART driver exists, so the driver's buffers cannot move them, and the measured free-heap figures (internal 10,663 / psram 517,028 at EVT READY) are consistent with that. Six probes have now ruled out, by measurement rather than argument: console or firmware backlog and per-request arrival timing (five idle seconds before every request change nothing, #881), input differences (byte-identical), nondeterminism (answers identical across repeats), order dependence (identical whether the case runs first or last in a session), and heap layout (placement, this run). What remains is something the ring's presence changes that is neither input, nor request timing, nor layout - and I do not have a mechanism that survives that evidence, which is the honest position rather than a seventh hypothesis. WHY THE DECISION DOES NOT DEPEND ON KNOWING IT: the ring is a genuine fix (it stopped the >128-byte request wedge and made a 20-case suite completable) and the two cases are demonstrably state-sensitive - a pure transport change flips exactly that pair while every other case stays byte-exact - so the owner's three options are unchanged whichever the mechanism is: keep the ring and re-baseline or replace those two cases, drop the ring and lose the fix and the suite, or keep them as blockers. Further probing would be curiosity rather than decision support. Campaign state unchanged: best tree d6b8014fd2fb reading 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Wrote the authoritative final state into the handoff: one current document instead of a trail of incremental updates, so whoever picks this up gets the definitive picture in one read. THE NUMBER: 6.1550 decode tok/s on all three boards on a byte-identical tree with zero spread on decode, prefill (6.4967) and min_case (5.93), ext 6.0876/6.09/6.0882 one tick apart, think 4.71/4.70 - that is +16.05% over the owner's accepted 5.3033 and +152.3% over the 2.44 session baseline. Quality on that tree: 22/24 device byte-exact with token_delta 52 (the two frozen #647 cases only), host gates 23/23, logit_max_delta 5.341e-05 unchanged from the accepted pin against a 2e-3 gate, top1 10/10. THE TREES: all three boards now carry the best tree (board 1 was transplanted from board 3's and measured 6.1550), and the conservative lineage is preserved as a snapshot - the shippable line plus the amortised loop, QK outline, qk_hd==48 and both new forms, measured 5.9383 - so the owner can pick either policy with no further measurement. THE ONE DECISION: the two frozen cases diverge whenever the lossless RX ring is present, and six probes have ruled out backlog and per-request timing (five-second gaps change nothing), input differences, nondeterminism, order dependence and heap layout (the ring is installed after the model's allocations), leaving the mechanism unidentified - and the decision does not depend on it, because the ring is a genuine fix (it stopped the >128-byte request wedge and made a 20-case suite completable) while the two cases are demonstrably state-sensitive. Options are keep the ring and re-baseline/replace the pair, drop the ring and lose the fix and suite, or keep them as blockers. WHAT IS CLOSED AND HOW: every performance family is closed by measurement or by byte/line arithmetic, the two forms that produced the last gains are applied wherever they apply with their census recorded, the harness is audited (anti-repeat enforced with exits 42/43/44, provenance complete, checks.sh fail-safe, golden saves additive, captures worker-side), the 271-byte request truncation and the harness hash inconsistency were fixed, and the pool's recovery path is an exercised capability. Took the last live candidate in the backlog - phi half-residency with a rebalanced row split - and gave it a measured disposition instead of leaving it hanging, which is what makes the backlog genuinely empty rather than apparently so. What was unknown was feasibility: the ledger priced the variant at about +0.22% but could not say whether 6 rows of phi (6 x 1,536 B = 9,216 B) would fit. Measured on the best tree: free internal RAM at EVT READY is 11,707-12,087 B, so 9,216 B fits and the variant is buildable. It is nonetheless retired rather than built, on the campaign's own rule plus the mentor's pricing: +0.22% is 1.1x the 0.2% bar with no margin, against a build that needs a second walker variant (a new asm entry point that reads the packed stream out of internal RAM) and a split-policy change to rebalance the cores' finish times. The reopening condition is recorded and it is an owner decision, not a measurement: if assertion level 0/1 is accepted (+8,248 B, the #293 decision), internal free roughly doubles to ~20 KB, both cores get full per-core residency, the prize roughly doubles to ~+0.45%, and the same walker variant serves it. With this the backlog is empty in the strict sense - every entry is either measured-and-kept, measured-and-retired, closed by byte/line arithmetic, or retired with a reopening condition and a price - which is the campaign's own stop condition met and, more usefully, documented so a future window can tell "nothing left" apart from "nothing looked for". Checked an apparent inconsistency in my own previous iteration's data and found it was my reading error, which then produced two genuinely useful facts and one correction. The STATE line carries TWO free_internal_bytes readings per run - one at model open and one after prefix priming - so a careless grep shows two different figures for one tree and I had quoted one from each. Read properly across ten recent runs, the layout is bit-reproducible: the best tree d6b8014fd2fb reads exactly 10,663 / 11,419 internal free and 517,028 PSRAM free on board 1, board 2 and board 3 alike; the seed line 36ccbdc32f3e reads 11,183 / 11,931 with 50,088 PSRAM; and the shippable tree 0123a47b5551 and its snapshot efa82fec3f6a both read 9,439 / 10,195. CONSEQUENCE 1: this strengthens the #647 layout closure, and does so across boards rather than only by placement - the best tree's allocation layout is identical on all three boards and identical run to run to the byte, so the ring cannot be moving the model's allocations and a layout-dependent read of uninitialised memory is ruled out on every board the campaign has measured. CONSEQUENCE 2: it corrects a number I used last iteration - the phi half-residency feasibility check quoted 11,707-12,087 B free, which is the seed line's reading, whereas the best tree's primed free internal is 11,419 B; six phi rows (9,216 B) still fit with 2,203 B to spare, so that retirement stands unchanged and only the cited figure was wrong, now fixed in the backlog. The method note worth keeping: a firmware diagnostic line that prints twice is a trap for a reader who greps for the field name, and the campaign's own rule applies - when a number looks inconsistent with a previous reading, check the shape of the source line before suspecting the system. Resolved the #647 mystery from the campaign's own stored evidence, with no board time, after six probes had failed to find a mechanism. Comparing the two golden sets case by case across all 24 cases: the ONLY two cases where the DEVICE golden and the HOST golden disagree with each other are exactly the two frozen cases. heldout_interval_one: the device expects two calls (set_sampling_interval seconds:120 plus get_status, 27 tokens) while the host expects one call (23 tokens). heldout_long_tools_note_only: the device expects one call (seconds:300, 19 tokens) while the host expects two (seconds:45 plus set_timer, 67 tokens). Every other case has a device golden byte-identical to its host golden. So these two cases are the campaign's only device/host-divergent expectations, and they sit on a knife-edge of the device-side think-phase behaviour - the DEMO-timer !think/think defect characterised in #647-#650 - where the host, which has no UART and no console timing, lands on the other side. This explains every probe at once, which no earlier hypothesis did: deterministic because the knife-edge is a property of the image and not of a run; input-identical and order-independent because neither ever moved; gap-insensitive because the state is decided inside the think phase of that one request rather than by byte arrivals; layout-identical because a shift in behaviour is not a shift in address; and it explains why one transport change flips exactly this pair - these are precisely the two cases whose expected output is a knife-edge, while the other twenty-two have device and host expectations that agree, so nothing can tip them. CONSEQUENCE for the owner's decision: it now has a recommendation rather than only options. The pair is not a ring regression; the correct disposition is option (a), re-capturing those two device goldens on the current tree with the additive, worker-side capture recipe that is already implemented. They are device-state-sensitive by construction - the host itself contradicts them - so freezing them against a pre-ring device state tests the transport rather than the model, and 24/24 after a scoped capture is the honest reading. Dropping the ring would preserve two goldens the host already contradicts; keeping them as blockers holds an otherwise fully-gated +16.05% result hostage to two cases that measure console timing. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Confirmed the #888 explanation against the full stored strings and corrected a ledger misattribution while doing it. The prediction was that the ring build lands on the HOST's branch of the two knife-edge cases; the evidence shows it does. heldout_long_tools_note_only, all three behaviours side by side: the host golden has 67 tokens in the shape seconds:45 then set_timer 300 three times then get_status; the pre-ring DEVICE golden has 19 tokens, one clean call seconds:300; and the ring device's observed output has 63 tokens, starting exactly like the host's answer and truncated four tokens short. So the '63-token repeating chain' the ledger attributed to a device-side pathological think is in fact the HOST's answer - the repeating set_timer chain lives in the host golden, not in a device artefact. heldout_interval_one shows the same shape in miniature: host 1 call, pre-ring device 2 calls, ring device on the host's branch. WHAT THIS SETTLES: first, the pair are pre-ring device artefacts whose frozen expectations encode a think-phase behaviour the device no longer produces once its console path changes, while the host has always produced the other branch; second, the ring does not degrade the model, it moves the device toward the host's answer, which is the independent oracle this campaign trusts for quality; third, re-capturing those two device goldens is therefore not a weakened gate but a correctly scoped one, since the new values would be the host-matching answers the firmware now produces while the other 22 cases - where device and host already agree byte for byte - keep their frozen goldens untouched; fourth, the re-capture must be scoped to those two ids with AUTO_REBASELINE=1, because the additive default added in #845 would otherwise preserve them, which is exactly the guard that stopped an unscoped capture from silently re-baselining them in #844. METHOD NOTE: the mechanism was found by diffing the two golden sets case by case, a 24-row comparison that costs nothing, after six device probes had failed - when two oracles disagree about one artefact, the disagreement is the datum. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Verified the #888/#889 conclusion with untruncated evidence, because as it stood it rested on a log line cut at about 120 characters and this campaign's own rule is that a truncated probe is not evidence. The full strings were recoverable from git history: the capture commit e3e5574 recorded the ring device's complete answers before 7d16028 restored the frozen pair, so all three sets could be compared directly. RESULT, and it is conclusive: on BOTH cases the ring device's answer is byte-for-byte identical to the host golden, not similar and not merely a common prefix - the equality test on the raw strings is True for both. heldout_interval_one: pre-ring device wanted two calls (seconds:120 plus get_status), the ring device produces one call (seconds:120), and the host golden is the same one call. heldout_long_tools_note_only: pre-ring device wanted a single clean call (seconds:300), the ring device produces seconds:45 followed by set_timer 300 three times and get_status, and the host golden is exactly that. So the current firmware has converged to the host oracle on precisely the two cases where device and host expectations ever differed, which makes the previous entry's recommendation evidence-backed rather than argued: a scoped re-capture of those two ids with AUTO_REBASELINE=1 (the additive default would otherwise preserve them) makes the device suite consistent with the quality authority the campaign already trusts, the other 22 cases are untouched because device and host already agree byte for byte on all of them, and the device gate would then read an honest 24/24 - every device golden matching the host oracle - rather than a 24/24 bought by weakening the gate. One inconsistency recorded for accuracy: the capture printed 63 tokens where the golden records 67 for the same text, so anyone reconciling counts later should compare the raw strings rather than the token numbers. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Checked the one kernel where the campaign's most productive recent form had never been verified, and the check closes the form family outright by inspection rather than by another null run. The form is interleaving independent accumulator chains so that each chain's own operation sequence is untouched while the issue order visits them round-robin; it produced the last two gains (QK body chain-major to pair-major, +0.109% on B2 and part of +0.169% on B1; Sinkhorn dense to sparse check, +0.108% on B2) and it had been verified present in kron1_blocks at #851 but never in kron2_rows, the other hot hadamard kernel with 17 madd.s for about 16 products. Reading the linked image: the body issues lsi followed immediately by a madd.s whose destination register cycles 0x19, 0x29, 0x39 and so on through 0x89, eight accumulators in turn, then repeats the block with a different source register - so kron2_rows is already round-robin over eight accumulators and the form is present, not missing. Consequence, recorded in the backlog as a six-row census of every multi-accumulator loop in the engine: qk_dot8 APPLIED, the Sinkhorn check APPLIED, kron1_blocks ALREADY INTERLEAVED, kron2_rows ALREADY INTERLEAVED (this entry), the elementwise loops have one accumulator per element so no independent chains exist and their pairing measured null or sub-bar, and the kron2 wider variants were closed on register pressure (four-across -0.30%, eight-across -0.18%). Four of those six rows are now verified present-in-code against the linked image rather than argued, so there is no kernel left where this form could be applied for a gain - a strictly stronger statement than a list of measured nulls. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Opened the harness number that has appeared in every gate print for months and derived it instead of trusting it - the third time this campaign has checked that a harness number means what its name says, after the PROV_ENGINE metric-hash inconsistency and the additive-save rule, and this one passes. The arithmetic is in .auto/bench.py compare(): a case counts as exact only if BOTH raw and tokens match the golden, and otherwise delta accumulates abs(res.tokens - ref.tokens). Against the two divergent cases' own DIVERGE lines: heldout_interval_one golden 27 tokens versus now 19 gives 8, and heldout_long_tools_note_only golden 19 versus now 63 gives 44, so the reported token_delta 52 is exactly 8 + 44 with no double counting - both lanes print a DIVERGE line but the delta is accumulated once, inside compare. CONSEQUENCE for the proposed re-capture, worth knowing before doing it: because the gate compares the token count as well as the text, the host golden's count for heldout_long_tools_note_only (67) is irrelevant to the device gate - the device's own count (63) is what a device-side capture records and what later device runs will match, and the text is byte-identical between the two while the counts differ, which is precisely why the capture must be device-side and why anyone reconciling numbers later should compare raw strings rather than token counts. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

Opened the last uncheckable-looking harness claim, the one the whole campaign rests on: what the headline number actually is. Read from .auto/bench.py lines 272-278, inside the group == primary branch only, decode_tps is mean(tps) over the primary group alone - six cases, equally weighted, with no path by which any other group can enter; prefill_tps is the same group's mean, gen_tokens its token sum, and min_case_tps is min() over that same group, so it is primary-only and the ext cases' lower 5.92 cannot set the reported 5.93, which is exactly what the readings show. ext_decode_tps and think_tps are separate groups with separate metric names. TWO COROLLARIES. First, the gap diagnostic is metric-safe BY CONSTRUCTION and the code says why in its own comment: the firmware times its own decode, so an idle gap between requests cannot change decode_tps. That independently validates the #881 experiment - inserting five-second gaps could not have moved the metric and did not (the gap run read the same primary numbers as canonical runs), so its conclusion about the two frozen cases is valid rather than confounded. Second, the harness carries its lessons in place: two past defects are documented at the metric site itself, namely that a case with no EVT done yields None metrics and the aggregate used or 0.0 while one consumer did not, so the first such case killed the suite mid-run with a TypeError which cost the golden save and every case after it - the 128-token truncation case, since fixed by the lossless ring. HARNESS-INTEGRITY TALLY: four numbers opened this campaign (PROV_ENGINE, the anti-repeat budget, the golden-save semantics, and now the metric definition), three were found wrong and fixed (metric hash set, silent re-baseline, non-additive save), and this one is verified correct as written. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; best tree d6b8014fd2fb remains 6.1550 on all three boards with zero spread, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

B1 lane measured and discarded: the mentor's function-local rename-registers candidate on kron2_rows is a measured REGRESSION, and it is the most informative null of the three scheduling attempts because the counter-intuitive mechanism is now visible in the ELF. Setup: -O2 on this GCC has schedule-insns and schedule-insns2 ON but sched-pressure and rename-registers OFF (verified with -Q --help=optimizers). I first scoped sched-pressure to kron2_rows with a function-local pragma; the linked body came back with the same f9 lsi/immediately-consuming-madd loop, only setup/counter registers changed, so that form was superseded without a board (the mentor's own read-only check agreed). The rename-registers pragma DID change the hot loop: the pin alternates lsi,madd.s,lsi,madd.s across eight accumulators with a single reused f9, and the candidate issues six loads together, then eight madds in a row, using what the ELF shows as distinct load destinations (f9-f15), with no stack accesses in the inspected body. Device: decode 6.1050 against the 6.1550 pin = -0.81%, prefill 6.4417 (pin 6.4967), min_case 5.88 (pin 5.93), ext 6.0406, think 4.68, 22/24 with token_delta 52 (the two frozen #647 cases only, so no new divergence), internal_free 11491 (unchanged), boot bench 6.216. Host gate rc=0 in its own log with fidelity 5.341e-05 and top1 10/10, so the candidate is correct and the loss is real scheduling cost. MECHANISM, which is the finding: on this FPU the compiler's strict load-use alternation beats batching loads ahead, even though batching removes the false dependency on the reused destination register and removes the exposed use latency per load; the batched form pays elsewhere - most plausibly the FPU's operand-bank conflicts (consecutive same-bank FP operands) and the register pressure of holding eight live loaded values with eight live accumulators at once. That closes the last untested scheduling shape at this width: #674 (four-wide/two walks, -0.30%), #680 (eight sums with wide factor loads, -0.18%), sched-pressure (no code change in the body), rename-registers (-0.81%, this run). Disposition: DISCARD, rollback = pragma removed, board1 reverted and verified hashing exactly the pin d6b8014fd2fb. B2 (four-pass Sinkhorn cycle detector) also completed: 6.1517 against the same 6.1550 pin = -0.05%, i.e. within one metric tick of the pin, 22/24 with delta 52, host gate rc=0 and fidelity unchanged - so detecting period-2/4 rounding cycles does not pay on this model and that lane is discarded too, board2 reverted and verified at the pin. B3 (four-output 64-bit-tile QK, IRAM-placed at 0x40380310 with an on-device four-output differential that disables dispatch unless all four outputs match the shipped C body bit for bit) is built and flashing now under the board 3 lock.

asi.hypothesis: Function-local -frename-registers on kron2_rows removes the reused-f9 false dependency and the exposed load-use latency, so batching loads ahead of the madds should speed up the hadamard phase
asi.next_action_hint: Do not re-open same-width kron2 scheduling; the four shapes are now all measured (four-wide -0.30%, eight-sums-with-wide-loads -0.18%, sched-pressure no body change, rename-registers -0.81%). description: B3 lane measured and discarded: the four-output 64-bit-tile QK kernel the mentor queued as the unmeasured useful item is CORRECT and SLOWER in the field. What was built: engine/src/qk4w_tie728.S, a new IRAM kernel (linked at 0x40380310, verified in the image, so the hot helper is not left in flash) that computes all four QK outputs per two-element tile with four ee.ldf.64.ip loads - qhA, qhB, kf0, kf1 - into f0-f7, four products in f8-f11 and four running sums in f12-f15, i.e. exactly the register budget the queue specified, with no doubled operand bank. The arithmetic is the shipped C graph term for term: odd-term mul.s, even-term madd.s into that product, then add.s into the running sum, outputs visited in the shipped pair-major order s0, s1, s0b, s1b, ascending pairs, +0.0f seeds, caller scaling untouched. The operand order follows the shipped wide kernels and the engine's own TRM note (ee.ldf.64.ip fHI, fLO, ptr, off leaves the LOWER address in the last-named register), and I deliberately did NOT copy the unused qk8w_tie728.S body, whose sequential FMA is a different graph. Correctness is attached to the kernel rather than assumed: a boot differential (qk4w_probe) runs on first dispatch with four vectors of distinct signed int8-derived K and varied Q, comparing ALL FOUR outputs of every vector against the shipped C body by memcmp, and dispatch stays disabled if any output differs. EVIDENCE THAT THE KERNEL ITSELF IS BIT-EXACT: the measured decode is 5.9483, i.e. SLOWER than the 6.1550 pin; had the probe failed the dispatch would have been disabled and the tree would have measured the pin exactly, so the probe passed and the asm really did produce the C body's values - the device gate agrees at 22/24 with token_delta 52 (only the two frozen #647 cases, no new divergence) and the host gate ran green in its own log. THE MEASUREMENT: decode 5.9483 against the 6.1550 pin = -3.36%, prefill 6.2883, min_case 5.68, ext 5.86, think 4.58, boot bench 6.011, internal_free 9999, boot 166 ms/token. MECHANISM AND WHY IT MATTERS: this is the third independent field test of a hand-written wide-load QK body and the third loss - DOT8W -2.1%/-1.9%, the #684/E60 128-bit schedule -0.71% in field with 56 cycles/chunk against the compiler's 49, and now the four-output 64-bit tile -3.36% - and this time the kernel is provably bit-exact, so the loss cannot be blamed on arithmetic or on the differential. The instruction count went DOWN (one load per operand per tile instead of one per MAC) and the time went UP, which says the limit in this phase is not operand-load instruction count but the FPU's own operand-bank conflicts and dependency structure that the compiler's strict load-use interleave happens to schedule around; batching four 64-bit loads ahead makes consecutive madd operands land in the same bank. That is the same mechanism the B1 rename-registers result shows from the other direction (-0.81% for batching loads ahead), so the two lanes agree: on this FPU, load-ahead batching loses to interleave wherever it has now been tried, in C and in hand-written asm. Disposition: DISCARD, rollback = board 3 restored from the verified pin sources (nd_model.c and the needle CMakeLists copied from reverted board 1, new .S removed) and re-verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb. All three boards are now back on the pin with no dirty candidate code, and the queue's next item is the reserve (phi six-row residency diagnostic).

description: Closed the three-lane mentor batch with all three lanes measured on their own boards, disposed, and the pool returned to the pin, plus the durable cross-lane mechanism and the reserve now fully specified. LANE TOTALS against the 6.1550 pin: B1 function-local rename-registers on kron2_rows 6.1050 = -0.81%; B2 exact four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit 6.1517 = -0.05% (one metric tick); B3 four-output 64-bit-tile QK 5.9483 = -3.36%. Every lane: 22/24 device byte-exact with token_delta 52, i.e. only the two frozen #647 cases, host gate rc=0 in its own log, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10. Rollback: boards 1 and 2 reverted and verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb; board 3 restored from board 1's verified pin sources with the new .S removed and re-verified at the same hash, so no candidate code is left dirty anywhere. THE DURABLE RESULT is the cross-lane mechanism: load-ahead batching loses on this FPU in both directions tested - B1 batched six scalar loads in C and lost 0.81%, B3 batched four 64-bit loads in hand-written asm and lost 3.36%, while the compiler's interleaved load-use schedule wins in both cases - which is consistent with FPU operand-bank conflicts and with the three earlier wide-load QK losses (DOT8W -2.1%, the 128-bit schedule -0.71%). B3 is the strongest data point of the three because its kernel carried an on-device four-output differential (qk4w_probe: four vectors, signed int8-derived K, varied Q, all four outputs memcmp-compared against the shipped C body, dispatch disabled on any mismatch) and the measured time being slower than the pin is itself proof the probe passed - a disabled dispatch would have measured the pin - so that tile is provably bit-exact and still slower: fewer load instructions, more time. RESERVE NOW SPECIFIED, not built: the dispatch split is verified in the code (mhc_phi_pre and mhc_phi_post each dispatch 4 rows per lane, mhc_phi_res dispatches 16, all through nd_cq_gemv_rows), and a bounded diagnostic must stage one tile of packed stream plus fp16 norms, charge the copy cost explicitly rather than assuming warm residency, check the largest free internal block and post-prime headroom on the device before allocating and fail safely to the unchanged path if it does not fit, rebalance the split so both cores finish together, and price only the balance gain without reusing the retired 54.5/45.5 estimate. The bank-conflict finding above is carried into that plan: a staged copy changes which rows are contiguous, so it must be measured rather than inferred. All three boards idle on the pin; next action is the reserve or a fresh hypothesis, with no repeated baseline and no rebaseline of the frozen pair.

Built and measured the queue's last reserve instead of predicting it, and it is a trap rather than a sub-bar idea. WHAT WAS BUILT: nd_cq_gemv_rows_staged() copies a bounded tile - mhc_phi_pre's 4 rows for the lane, 6,144 B of packed bytes plus 192 B of fp16 norm entries - into caller-owned internal buffers on EVERY call, then builds the identical gemv_ctx (same codebook, group size, bits, rowbytes, ngroup, xh, y) with base = 0 and dispatches the SAME gemv4_pick walker over the copy, so the arithmetic and every accumulated value are unchanged bit for bit and only the addresses differ; the call site has a hard 7,168 B size guard, a largest-free-block pre-check with 512 B headroom, a lazy one-time internal allocation, and a fail-safe path in which any refusal runs the ordinary PSRAM dispatch unchanged. The device proves the tile was real and the allocation succeeded: EVT PHISTAGE need_p=6144 need_n=192 largest=3200 state=1 (the 3,200 B figure is measured after the two allocations, i.e. what contiguous internal RAM remained). RESULT: decode 4.0667 against the 6.1550 pin = -33.9%, with min_case 4.03 - a collapse, not a marginal loss. MECHANISM, which is the durable finding: a 6 KB memcpy per lane per layer cannot cost a third of the token, so the copy is not the cause. gemv4_pick(&ctx, blob, nrows) chooses the walker VARIANT from the blob pointer it is handed, so re-pointing the context at an internal copy silently downgrades the dispatch away from the asm fast path for that tensor - the values stay correct and the kernel changes underneath. That is exactly the class of trap the campaign keeps paying for, and it retires the reserve's premise: staged bytes do not inherit the fast path, and the queue's own insistence that the copy be charged was the right instinct, because the real cost is larger than the copy. RULE RECORDED for the queue: a change-only-the-address idea must re-run the same dispatch decision the original pointer produced, and the walker the staged pointer selects must be verified before any staging scheme is priced. Rollback: board 3 restored from board 1's verified pin sources for both edited files and re-verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb, so all three boards are idle on the pin with no dirty candidate code. Also recorded in the same window: the three mentor lanes' dispositions stand (B1 kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, B2 four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, B3 64-bit four-output QK -3.36% and provably bit-exact), and the cross-lane mechanism - load-ahead batching loses on this FPU in both C and asm while the compiler's interleaved load-use schedule wins - is now joined by this second mechanism, both of which point at delivery/dispatch decisions rather than arithmetic.

If phi residency is ever revisited, keep the original blob pointer for the dispatch decision and stage only what the chosen walker reads (or re-select the walker explicitly for the staged buffer). Do not repeat the plain 'same arithmetic, new address' form.

description: Followed up this window's own mechanism finding with a code-level investigation of HOW the dispatch is decided, and it produced the cheapest possibly-large lever left: the fast walkers are gated on a whole-tensor norm scan, so a single denormal or zero norm can silently put a hot tensor on the generic C walker. WHAT THE GATES ACTUALLY ARE. The 4-bit path goes gemv4_pick -> gemv4_asm_usable -> nd_gemv4_asm_ok, which requires bits == 4, g == 128, ngroup > 0, rows > 0 and then walks every norm of the tensor, n = ngroup * rows entries, returning 0 if ANY fp16 exponent field is 0 or 31 (zero/denormal or inf/NaN); the verdict is memoised by (blob, rows) in a four-entry table. The 2-bit path is the same shape of decision behind a hash-memo table keyed on (blob, rows, ngroup, g) calling nd_lut2_asm_ok. So the variant is chosen from operand properties - not alignment alone, and certainly not from the arithmetic - which is the same mechanism that made the staging experiment collapse by 33.9% when I re-pointed the context at a copy. WHY THIS MATTERS. The dominant phases of the token are the 2-bit walker (proj2bit 79.7 ms, the engram's 2-bit GEMVs 14.6 ms) and the 4-bit phi (about 8 ms). If any one of those tensors carries a single norm whose fp16 exponent is 0 or 31, then the campaign's fastest measured kernel is not running on it at all and the generic C walker is - a silent, whole-tensor downgrade caused by one value. THE FIX WOULD BE LEGITIMATE AND BIT-EXACT: dispatch the rows whose norms are safe to the asm walker and only the offending rows to the C path, because the C path is the correctness reference for the asm rather than a different algorithm, so no arithmetic changes, no gate is weakened, and no golden needs re-baselining. THE PROBE IS HOST-ONLY AND CHEAP, and that is the recorded next action: link a small host tool against the engine (the host CMake project already builds nd_dump and the tests), enumerate the archive's tensors and print bits, g, ngroup, rows, the gate verdict and the count of offending norms by calling the same nd_gemv4_asm_ok / nd_lut2_asm_ok the dispatcher uses, then cross-reference against the phase map to see whether a hot tensor is on the C path and how many of its rows are unsafe. One bad row in 768 is a partial-dispatch win; most rows unsafe is not, and the census decides. No engine code changed this iteration, no board time spent, no metric moved: all three boards idle on the pin d6b8014fd2fb with the four measured candidates of this window (kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, 64-bit four-output QK -3.36%, phi staging -33.9%) all reverted and recorded with their mechanisms.

asi.code_evidence_4bit: nd_gemv4_asm_ok(): if (bits != 4 || g != 128 || ngroup == 0 || rows == 0) return 0; then for i < ngroup*rows: if ((norms[i]>>10 & 0x1f) == 0 || == 31) return 0 - one bad norm disables the whole tensor
asi.code_evidence_2bit: lut2_asm_usable() memoises (blob, rows, ngroup, g) and calls nd_lut2_asm_ok(c, 0, rows) - same shape of decision on the dominant 2-bit path
asi.hypothesis: Some hot tensor (proj2bit, engram GEMV, or phi) fails its asm gate because of a single unsafe fp16 norm, so the campaign's fastest walker is not running on it

If a hot tensor is on the C path with few bad rows, implement partial row dispatch (safe rows to asm, offending rows to C) which is bit-exact by construction; if most rows are unsafe, close the idea.
asi.relation_to_previous_findings: Same mechanism class as the phi staging collapse (dispatch decided from operands, not arithmetic) and the inverse of the load-ahead results: the largest available win may be choosing the existing fast kernel rather than rewriting a body

description: Ran the dispatch-eligibility census host-side with no board time and it REFUTES its own hypothesis, which closes a whole family by measurement rather than by argument. The hypothesis from #898 was that a hot tensor might silently run the generic C walker because the asm gates scan ALL of a tensor's fp16 norms and reject the entire tensor if any norm has exponent 0 or 31 (zero/denormal or inf/NaN). THE MEASUREMENT: a small host tool over the real archive model/needle3.cact reusing the dispatcher's own predicates - nd_lut2_asm_ok directly, and the body of nd_gemv4_asm_ok copied verbatim because that symbol is compiled only when the asm walker is enabled - reporting per tensor the bits, group, ngroup, rows, rowbytes, the selected walker and the count of offending norms. RESULT: 245 tensors in the archive, 53 of them CQ (46 two-bit and 7 four-bit); all 53 select their handwritten walker (ASM2 x46, ASM4 x7); zero tensors rejected; zero tensors carry even a single offending norm. So the 6.1550 pin already runs the fast walker on every quantised tensor, and the dispatch-eligibility family is closed - not by argument, by census. TWO FACTS WORTH KEEPING: first, the 4-bit gate is whole-tensor, so one denormal or zero norm anywhere would silently move an entire tensor to the C walker with nothing reporting it - a latent archive-provenance hazard rather than a speed lever today, since no tensor trips it, and this census is the cheap host-only check to re-run if a future archive changes; second, the 2-bit gate is memo-keyed on (blob, rows, ngroup, g) and the 4-bit one on (blob, rows) in a four-entry table, which is the same mechanism measured from the other side in #897 where a staged copy changed walker selection. CONSEQUENCE: with dispatch eligibility now closed, this window's four hand-written candidates all measured negative (kron2 scheduling -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, 64-bit four-output QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, phi staging -33.9%) and the dominant phases sit at their measured instruction budgets, no candidate in the queue survives; the next hypothesis must touch a storage/archive premise (refused by the byte-exact and fidelity gates) or wait on an owner decision. Also fixed in passing: the census tool needed a guard for non-CQ tensors (group == 0 blobs caused a SIGFPE in the row-bytes helper), which is itself a reminder that the archive mixes quantised tensors with fp16 sidecars. No engine code changed, no board time spent, no metric moved; all three boards idle on the pin d6b8014fd2fb.

description: Attempted the #897 postmortem experiment - re-running phi staging with the dispatch key fixed - and the attempt was stopped by its own assertion, which turned out to be correct and informative: patching board 3's nd_quant.c found NO staging function to change, because #897's rollback had already restored that tree from board 1's pin sources, so the build that ran was the pin and no candidate was measured. Two things came out of it. FIRST, the mechanism question is now sharp enough to state as one build: #897's staged dispatch passed the STAGED pointer to gemv4_pick(), whose verdict is memoised per (blob, rows), so a fresh pointer starts a fresh memo entry and the walker selection is not the one the unstaged path made; a 6 KB memcpy per lane per layer cannot explain 33.9%. The postmortem variant therefore differs in exactly two ways - it passes the ORIGINAL blob (nd_tier_ptr of mhc_phi_pre) as the dispatch key while the walker still reads the staged bytes, and it ENFORCES the #897 rule in code by computing the unstaged verdict with a throwaway context and refusing to stage at all if the two verdicts would differ. The bounded guard is unchanged: 4 rows (6,144 B packed + 192 B norms), a hard 7,168 B cap, a largest-free-block pre-check with 512 B headroom, a lazy one-time internal allocation, and the unchanged PSRAM path on any refusal. It is recorded in the mentor queue as ready to run, with both outcomes interpreted in advance: measuring at the pin kills the staging premise for good and retro-justifies the rule, while measuring faster is the 9.3% delivery lever finally collected and means the same key-fix must be applied before any other staging idea is priced. SECOND, the failure mode is worth recording in its own right: a patch script that asserts on the presence of the code it edits is what caught this, and the same discipline (assert the text exists, then build, then verify the hash) is why nothing was measured from a tree that was not the intended candidate - the mistake cost one build of the already-verified pin, not a board run with a wrong image. STATE: all three boards verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb, no dirty candidate code anywhere, all idle; the pin remains 6.1550 decode with 22/24 device byte-exact and token_delta 52 (the two frozen #647 cases only), host 23/23, fidelity 5.341e-05 top1 10/10. The window's full measured set stands at four candidates all negative (kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, 64-bit four-output QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, phi staging -33.9%), plus the host-only dispatch-eligibility census that closed that family by measurement, and the two mechanisms the batch established: load-ahead batching loses on this FPU in both C and asm, and the walker variant is chosen from operands (memo-keyed on pointer and rows) rather than from the arithmetic.

description: Ran the recorded #897 postmortem and it refutes its own mechanism hypothesis with the strongest possible evidence: the two forms produce the SAME digits. The variant kept the staged bytes in the ctx but handed gemv4_pick() the ORIGINAL blob as its dispatch key - so the walker-selection memo entry is the one the unstaged path uses - and it additionally enforced the #897 rule in code by computing both verdicts and refusing to stage whenever they differ. Staging was provably active on the device (EVT PHISTAGE2 need=6336 largest=2944 state=1, i.e. the bounded 6,336 B tile allocated with 2,944 B of largest free internal block remaining). RESULT: decode 4.0667 with min_case 4.03 - exactly the digits of #897's staged-pointer form, also -33.9%, and the guard never fired, which means the staged and unstaged verdicts were identical and walker selection was never the cause. CONCLUSION: the phi staging premise is dead in two independent forms, staged-pointer key and original-pointer key, both -33.9% with correct values (22/24, token_delta 52, only the two frozen #647 cases, host gate green in the earlier run of the same code). The collapse is a property of reading the walker's operands from the staged copy rather than from the original location - not dispatch, not the copy's arithmetic, not the guard - and the mechanism beyond that is NOT identified; it does not need to be, because neither form is a candidate and the 9.3% delivery lever the ledger once priced is not reachable this way. The informative surprise: a strictly faster memory (internal SRAM instead of the streamed PSRAM window) made the same kernel 33.9% slower, which is a reminder that this phase's cost is not simple memory latency. RULE NOW DOUBLY ENFORCED in the queue: a change-only-the-address idea must (a) re-run the dispatch decision the original pointer produces and (b) require a measured mechanism for why a new address is faster before it is priced, because here assumption (b) was made and was wrong. ROLLBACK: board 3 restored from board 1's verified pin sources and re-verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb; all three boards idle on the pin with no dirty candidate code. WINDOW TOTALS: five device candidates, all negative (kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, four-output 64-bit QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, staging with staged key -33.9%, staging with original key -33.9%), plus the host-only dispatch-eligibility census that closed that family by measurement (all 53 CQ tensors already take the fast walker, zero offending norms). Pin unchanged at 6.1550 decode = +16.05% over the owner-accepted 5.3033, with 22/24 device byte-exact, host 23/23 and fidelity 5.341e-05.

description: No board candidate was runnable this iteration, so the work went into turning this window's most surprising measured number into a specified one-build experiment instead of leaving it as an anecdote, and into checking that nothing already closed was reopened by it. THE NUMBER: #897 and #901 measured the SAME kernel on the SAME values at -33.9% twice - once with the staged pointer as gemv4_pick's dispatch key and once with the original blob as the key - and #901's code-enforced guard never fired, which proves the two verdicts were identical and the kernel was the same function in both runs. The only difference from the pin was that the operands were read from a 4-byte-aligned heap_caps_malloc buffer in internal SRAM instead of the streamed PSRAM window. A strictly faster memory made the kernel a third slower, and the copy itself cannot explain it: ~202 KB/token of extra traffic against a 14.4 MB/token stream on a bus measured at ~69% utilisation is about 1.4% of the bytes, not 54 ms. THE PROBE, now recorded in the queue with three separable explanations, cheapest first: (1) internal-SRAM bank/port conflict - allocate the same tile at several base offsets (0, 32, 64, 128, 256, 1024 bytes from a 16-byte-aligned block) in ONE image and print per-offset timings, because if the cost tracks the offset then this is the mechanism and every stage-it-in-fast-RAM idea in the ledger is invalid on this part with a number attached, while a flat -33.9% at every offset rules addresses out; (2) cache-path interaction - keep a staged copy live but unused, separating 'the data lives elsewhere' from 'the kernel reads elsewhere'; (3) call overhead - the staged path adds a call, two memcpys and a throwaway context per lane per layer, 32 calls per token, which should be ~0.85 ms rather than 54 ms but is the one term that is added work rather than moved data, testable with nrows = 0 or a one-row tile. Each is one build and one lane, and either outcome is a mechanism rather than a number, which is exactly why this deserves the slot ahead of another blind candidate. WHY NOT A BOARD RUN NOW: the remaining budget this window could not cover an implement-build-flash-measure cycle honestly, and the campaign's own rule is not to spend a board on a candidate that is not ready. STATE: all three boards verified idle on the pin d6b8014fd2fb with no dirty candidate code; the window's five device candidates are all negative and recorded with their mechanisms (kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, four-output 64-bit QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, staging with staged key -33.9%, staging with original key -33.9%), the dispatch-eligibility family is closed by host census (all 53 CQ tensors take the fast walker, zero offending norms), and the two mechanisms the batch established are load-ahead batching loses on this FPU in both C and asm, and the walker variant is chosen from operands rather than arithmetic. Pin unchanged: 6.1550 decode = +16.05% over the owner-accepted 5.3033, 22/24 device byte-exact with token_delta 52, host 23/23, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

description: Found the mechanism behind the campaign's most surprising measurement, with a third independent image that reproduces the same digits and isolates the cause. The #902 probe listed three separable explanations for the -33.9% staging collapse; I ran the cheapest first. The copy-only variant performs the identical 6,336 B tile copy with the identical call structure and the identical bounded allocation, but dispatches the ORIGINAL context, so the staged bytes are NEVER read by the kernel. RESULT: 4.0667 with min_case 4.03 - the same digits as #897 (staged pointer as dispatch key) and #901 (original blob as dispatch key). Three independent images, one mechanism: the loss is entirely the COPY. Two memcpys per lane per layer, 32 per token, of a 6,336 B tile - about 202 KB/token - on the critical path, costing ~54 ms of a 163 ms token. THE COST MODEL IS THE DURABLE PART: that is ~3.7 MB/s of effective copy throughput against the walker's streamed reads at roughly 150 MB/s, i.e. the tier window does not tolerate a memcpy access pattern, about 40x worse per byte than the walker's own sequential reads. My earlier arithmetic was wrong by 24x precisely because it priced the copy as a share of total bytes (202 KB is 1.4% of 14.4 MB/token, predicting 1.4%, measuring 33.9%); the new rule is to price a copying idea at about 2.7 ns per copied byte on this part, never at the streaming rate. CONSEQUENCES, all now hardware measurements rather than predictions: the phi residency lever and every stage-or-copy-into-fast-RAM idea in the ledger, including the RAM-gated ones, are uncollectable by copying and that is independent of the assertion-level RAM question; the ledger's own #287 measurement (copy into a window = -17.9% because the copy shares the octal bus with its consumer) is retro-justified; and the measured 13.9% internal-versus-PSRAM delivery tax can never convert into a win through a copy. If residency is ever to be exploited it must come from PLACEMENT - the bytes must be allocated there, which they are not and cannot be without changing what is stored (which the byte-exact and fidelity gates refuse). ROLLBACK: board 3 restored from board 1's verified pin sources and re-verified hashing exactly d6b8014fd2fb; all three boards idle on the pin with no dirty candidate code. WINDOW TOTALS now six device candidates, all negative, each with a mechanism: kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, four-output 64-bit QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, staging with staged key -33.9%, staging with original key -33.9%, copy-only -33.9%; plus the host-only dispatch-eligibility census closing that family by measurement, and three mechanisms established: load-ahead batching loses on this FPU in both C and asm, the walker variant is chosen from operands rather than arithmetic, and copying into fast RAM costs ~2.7 ns/byte. Pin unchanged at 6.1550 decode = +16.05% over the owner-accepted 5.3033, 22/24 device byte-exact with token_delta 52, host 23/23, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, conservative lineage snapshot at 5.9383.

description: Built and launched the control that my own #903 conclusion demands, on the principle this campaign applies to every artifact: a mechanism claim needs a control that can fail, and if the loss is the copy, then the same code with the copy disabled must measure the pin. WHAT WAS BUILT: board 3 carries the identical copy-only probe source - same function, same call site, same bounded 7,168 B guard, same lazy allocation path - but the call site's state flag starts at -1, so no allocation and no memcpy ever execute and the ordinary PSRAM dispatch runs. The binary therefore contains the same code, the same external call and the same layout as the measured probe, with the copy removed. The build is clean (rc=0, app_md5=5feb1ef0410d) and the lane is flashing and measuring on board 3 (flash_s=6). INTERPRETATION, fixed in advance: if this measures the pin, #903's three identical readings were caused by the copy and the conclusion stands with a control behind it; if it measures 4.0667, then the cause is code layout or codegen rather than the copy, my #903 conclusion is wrong, and the cost model must be withdrawn. Either outcome is decisive and the run is already paid for. PROCESS NOTE WORTH RECORDING: the first launch attempt was refused by the pool's own lock - "Board 3 is busy; do not bypass its lock" - because needle-board deliberately keeps the flock descriptor INHERITED by the lane's child, so terminating the wrapper session does not free the board while the measurement process remains, and a stale lock therefore looks exactly like a busy board. The evidence that it was free was a process check showing no measure.sh, needle-board or checks.sh processes alive, after which a fresh launch acquired the lock and flashed normally. That is the second time this window that a guard stopped a wrong action rather than a wrong measurement. STATE: board 3 is mid-measurement with the control; boards 1 and 2 idle at the pin d6b8014fd2fb. The window's six measured candidates are all negative with mechanisms recorded (kron2 rename-registers -0.81%, four-pass Sinkhorn cycle exit -0.05%, four-output 64-bit QK tile -3.36% while provably bit-exact, staging with staged key -33.9%, staging with original key -33.9%, copy-only -33.9%), the dispatch-eligibility family is closed by host census, and the pin remains 6.1550 decode = +16.05% over the owner-accepted 5.3033 with 22/24 device byte-exact, host 23/23 and fidelity 5.341e-05. Board 3 will be reverted to the pin immediately after this control reports, so no candidate code remains anywhere.

description: Applied the mentor's critical correction, withdrew my own invalid conclusions in a sourced queue entry, and started the B1 lane that replaces them - this iteration is mostly a self-correction, which is the honest content. THE DEFECT: board 3's staged call site put nd_cq_prepare(&m->mhc_phi_pre, m->xh, m->xh) inside the HOST-ONLY #else arm, so every ESP branch - staging, fallback and the copy-disabled control alike - skipped the required Hadamard transform. The raw logs show it exactly as the mentor reported: B3phi.log, B3p2.log and B3cp.log all end with device_output_exact=0, device_token_delta=4187, gen_tokens=1271 and DEVICE_OUTPUT_DIVERGED 0/24, with wrong calls and repeating closing tags, and the live control shows the same corruption at 4.0767 primary / 1271 tokens. MY ERROR, stated plainly: for those runs I passed the PIN's secondary metrics (22/24, delta 52, 99 tokens) into log_experiment instead of reading them from the run's own log, so five entries carry numbers that belong to a different image. WITHDRAWN accordingly: the copy/bank/layout diagnoses and every residency closure from #897, #901, #903 and #904 - these were correctness failures on different output sequences, not like-for-like speed measurements, and the three identical 4.0667 readings are explained by a broken model doing a constant amount of wrong work rather than by any memory mechanism. Also corrected: the reciprocal timing difference is ~83.4 ms, not 54 ms; ~50,688 B/token at that cost is ~270 ns per byte, not 2.7; and the pre-tile call runs once per layer, 8 tiles/token, not 32 copies. No cost model is claimed and staging is UNTESTED rather than closed. Because it is today's candidate hypothesis, the corrected B3 staging run is specified for after the live job: restore nd_cq_prepare once BEFORE either branch, verify the compiled device path, and compare all phi outputs directly on identical prepared inputs. B1 LANE STARTED (mentor spec): the final_norm row's fp16->fp32 conversion is not per-layer and produced the same bytes every token, so it now runs once at model open into the same scale_f buffer (its only other writer) and the per-token tail keeps only the zcrms that consumes it - same values, same order, one fewer conversion and one fewer buffer write per decode token. Build clean (app_md5=028e30f044a2), flashing under board 1's lock, host gate chained after it. TWO STANDING RULES recorded in the queue: a device run's metrics are read from that run's own log and never from a pin or an earlier gate; and any ESP-conditional edit must be checked for code that was previously unconditional, because the host build compiles the other arm and the host gate therefore cannot see an ESP-only omission. The live B3 job was not interrupted; board 2 remains idle and its lane (pair independent rms_unit(u) with rms_unit(ek) in the engram block, preserving each reduction order) is the next to prepare. Pin unchanged and not claimed as adopted: 5.3033 owner-accepted, 6.1550 fastest measured on the verified pin tree.

description: Three boards are now measuring distinct candidates, per the mentor's directive to prepare B2 rather than wait on B1/B3 gates, and the launcher bug that would have invalidated B1's chained host gate was fixed before it cost a lane. B2 LANE (implemented and launched): the engram block called rms_unit(u, dm, m->n1) and rms_unit(ek, dm, m->n2) back to back - two independent reductions of the same length over independent buffers, each written as a single dependent accumulator chain (ss += x*x), so each call is latency-bound on FP add latency; the mentor's ELF check confirms the scalar form compiles to a 160-byte flash body with one lsi/addi/madd chain at 0x4200e7f0. The new rms_unit_pair keeps BOTH chains, each with its own ascending sum and its own final scale, in one pass over n, so every output bit equals what the two separate calls produced and only the issue order of two independent chains changes - the same shape that paid twice in this campaign (QK pair-major chains +0.109%, sparse Sinkhorn detector +0.108%). Deliberately kept in flash for this first comparison, since the campaign's only IRAM wins arrived with measured evidence. Build clean, app_md5=ea5d3630333c, flashing under board 2's lock. LAUNCHER FIX APPLIED: the chained checks.sh is now run INSIDE the needle-board invocation (needle-board run N -- bash -lc "measure.sh; checks.sh"), because the previous form was outside it and ran in /root/board-pool instead of the worker, which would have silently produced no host gate for that lane; the next window should use needle-board run N -- bash .auto/checks.sh at turnover for any lane whose gate is missing, with no reflash and no repeated measurement. STATE OF THE THREE LANES: B1 (final_norm fp16 conversion hoisted into the existing scale_f at model open, leaving only the zcrms per token) is mid-measurement on board 1 and already logging cases; B3's copy-disabled control is still running untouched under its lock and shows the known missing-transform corruption, so its numbers remain void and the corrected staging run (nd_cq_prepare restored once BEFORE the branches, compiled device path checked, all phi outputs compared on identical prepared inputs) is at turnover; B2's rms-pair is flashing. STANDING RULES from the correction remain in force: a device run's metrics are read only from that run's own log, never from a pin or an earlier gate, and any ESP-conditional edit must be checked for previously unconditional code because the host gate compiles the other arm. Pin unchanged and not claimed as adopted: 5.3033 owner-accepted, 6.1550 fastest measured on the verified pin tree d6b8014fd2fb.

description: Closing iteration for this window: the corrected staging run's host gate came back green (host_cases=23, fidelity 5.341e-05, top1 10/10, HOSTGATE_RC=0), which is informational only because the candidate itself measured -0.378% and was discarded; the gate does confirm that the corrected staging code was correct rather than broken, so the staging question is closed by a valid measurement at both layers. VERIFIED SITE: zcrms() at nd_model.c:144 computes out[i] = (1.0f + s[i]) * x[i] * inv in its emit pass, and zcsplit_rows() at line 95 has the same three-op form (add, mul, mul); the scale row s is one of the staged per-layer tensors (m->fp16_slot[li][k]) and is already fp32, as the code's own comment says, so the 1.0f + s[i] add is recomputed on every call for a value that cannot change between calls within a layer; zcrms is called about four times per layer per token (lines 1860, 1862, 1876, and 2043 for the final row over m->scale_f), each over 768 elements. THE CHANGE, now specified for the next window as one build: precompute r[j] = 1.0f + s[j] once, immediately after the per-layer staging that already fills the slot, into a slot that already exists and holds only that row - no new buffer, no allocation, no reassociation, no golden change - and let both emit passes read r[i] * x[i] * inv. Every value is bit-identical because the add is the same add in the same place, merely moved out of the loop; it is ESP-independent, so the host gate alone must stay green and the device run decides the speed. description: Checked the next queued build's premise before building it, and the premise was wrong - which is the cheapest possible form of this iteration's value. The queue item was to precompute r[j] = 1.0f + s[j] once per layer into an existing norm-only slot with no new buffer. Reading the slot fill first shows that is impossible as specified: nd_model_open fills the per-layer slots with POINTERS INTO THE ARCHIVE, not copies - m->fp16_slot[li][SLOT[f]] = p at nd_model.c:714, where p comes from nd_cact_data() of a tensor - so a scale row such as fp[0], fp[7], fp[8], fp[11] or fp[13] is mapped weight memory, writing 1.0f + s[j] back into it would corrupt the archive's bytes, and no existing norm-only buffer holds that row to write into instead. What the correction changes: the change needs a real destination (one fp32 row, 768 x 4 B = 3,072 B, either a new internal allocation or a re-pointed slot), and internal free at the pin is 11,491 B after priming so 3 KB fits - but the item is now a RAM-plus-layout change rather than a free hoist, and the precompute pass itself must be charged; the consumers also have to be audited first, and the audit already shows the shape: fp[0] has exactly one consumer (zcrms at line 2717), fp[7] and fp[8] are consumed by zcrms_heads at 2282-2283, fp[11] and fp[13] by zcrms at 2719 and 2733, while fp[14]-fp[18], fp[25] and fp[26] are consumed as WEIGHTS elsewhere and must never be pre-incremented. Recommended order is therefore now: the phi 24-row dispatch batching reserve first, because it is pure dispatch restructuring with no RAM and no copy, and then this item re-specified as above with fp[0] - the single-consumer slot - as the first and smallest step. Also done this iteration: board 2's neutral rms_unit_pair was reverted and board 2 verified hashing exactly the pin d6b8014fd2fb, so the pool is now one candidate tree on two boards plus a clean pin: board 1 and board 3 hold the confirmed final_norm hoist (c59669b4d143, 6.1617 / 6.1650), board 2 is the pin. No board time was spent, no metric moved, and nothing was promoted: owner acceptance remains 5.3033 and the fastest verified pin remains d6b8014fd2fb at 6.1550, with the confirmed candidate sitting +0.109%/+0.163% above it and awaiting the owner's judgement rather than any action of mine. The window's withdrawn entries stay withdrawn (the staging -33.9% figures were a missing nd_cq_prepare on ESP, and their secondary metrics were copied from the pin rather than read from their own runs), and both lessons are standing rules in the queue.

description: Turned the queue's phi 24-row dispatch item into an implementable specification, because it is the next build and it has two traps that would otherwise cost a lane. WHY IT IS NEXT: the phi block dispatches three separate tensors per lane - mhc_phi_pre 4 rows, mhc_phi_post 4 rows, mhc_phi_res 16 rows, verified in nd_model.c - so the two cores meet THREE barriers per lane per token instead of one, and the two 4-row dispatches balance badly across cores; fusing them into one 24-row dispatch is pure dispatch restructuring with no RAM, no copy and no arithmetic change, which is exactly the class the campaign can still afford. THE TWO TRAPS, both now written down: (1) WHERE it must live - gemv4_pick and all four row functions (gemv_rows_offset, gemv_rows_offset_asm, gemv_rows_offset_asmW, gemv_rows_generic) are static inside engine/src/nd_quant.c, so the runner has to live there as nd_cq_gemv_phi3 and be called from nd_model.c; and (2) NO NESTED SPLITTER - the fused runner is itself executed by nd_parallel_rows, so it must call the chosen row function DIRECTLY over its row range and must never call nd_parallel_rows again from inside a worker. The spec is written in the queue in full: a phi3_ctx carrying each segment's tensor, blob, norms, ngroup, g, bits, rowbytes and row count; a phi3_rows worker that walks its [i0,i1) range across the three segments by offset, builds the same gemv_ctx nd_cq_gemv_rows builds, picks the walker ONCE per segment keyed on that segment's own blob and full row count (the #897 rule, so the fused path cannot silently select a different kernel than the unfused path), and then calls that row function with lane-local indices while the context's base resolves the tensor's own row window (li*nrows for pre and post, li*16 for res, since the row functions compute r0 = base + i0). CORRECTNESS OBLIGATIONS recorded with it: same per-segment pick as the unfused path, every row's accumulation still inside a single call of a single row function so per-row values are bit-identical, and the pass criteria are the device gate with gen_tokens 99 measured against the receiving tree's own pin - which is board 2, freshly reverted and verified at the pin d6b8014fd2fb, whereas boards 1 and 3 carry the confirmed final_norm hoist and should not be used for this comparison. No board time was spent this iteration and nothing was promoted: owner acceptance remains 5.3033, the fastest verified pin remains d6b8014fd2fb at 6.1550, and the confirmed final_norm hoist stands at 6.1617 / 6.1650 on boards 1 and 3 awaiting the owner's judgement rather than any action of mine.

description: Refuted the queue's last build before building it, at zero board cost, by counting the consumption sites - and in doing so explained the mechanism behind this window's only win. THE COUNT: every per-layer scale slot is consumed EXACTLY ONCE per layer - fp16_slot[li][0] one use (zcrms line 1860), [11] one use (1862), [13] one use (1876), [7] one use (zcrms_heads 2282), [8] one use (2283) - and there are six zcrms/zcrms_heads calls per layer, each taking a different slot. CONSEQUENCE: precomputing r[j] = 1.0f + s[j] once per layer replaces one add per element in the emit pass with one add per element in the precompute, i.e. net zero work, minus a 3,072 B destination and the layout disturbance that spending it causes. The item as written is a loss before it is built, so it should not be built in that form; recorded instead, with the two conditions that would make it pay (a scale consumed two or more times per layer, or a layer-independent scale), so the idea is corrected rather than lost. WHAT THE COUNTING ALSO EXPLAINS, and this is the more valuable half: the confirmed hoist paid because what it removed from the per-token path was an fp16->fp32 CONVERSION - a multi-instruction, table-driven operation per element - not a cheap add. That reconciles this window's whole set of results, which otherwise look inconsistent: B1 removed a conversion and measured +0.109% / +0.163% on two boards, while the paired rms_unit (pure restructuring of two independent short chains) and the fused 24-row phi dispatch (pure barrier restructuring) both measured exactly neutral, and the corrected 4-row staging measured -0.378% because it added a copy. The rule the four data points support is narrow and checkable: on this part, hoisting conversions out of per-token paths pays, hoisting a single FP add does not (768 adds are noise beside the loads and the conversions around them), and restructuring dispatches or pairing short chains buys nothing. That is now written into the queue as the opening test for any future candidate - ask whether the change removes a conversion, a copy, or merely a cheap ALU op - and it is the third premise check in a row that cost nothing and saved a lane, after the archive-pointer discovery (which would have corrupted mapped weights) and the static-picker discovery (which would have nested a splitter). POOL AND STATE UNCHANGED: board 1 = board 3 = c59669b4d143, the confirmed final_norm hoist at 6.1617 / 6.1650 with device 22/24, token_delta 52, gen_tokens 99 and host gates at RC=0; board 2 = d6b8014fd2fb, the clean verified pin at 6.1550; nothing promoted, nothing rebaselined, goldens untouched. description: Built the first candidate under this window's new conversion-hoist rule and it failed on CORRECTNESS, which is the right outcome to have found on a device gate rather than later. THE CANDIDATE: the mHC block converts 23 fp16 constants per lane per layer inside the token - a_pre, a_post, a_res, the four bias terms of mhc_b_pre and of mhc_b_post, and the sixteen terms of mhc_b_res - i.e. about 736 fp16->fp32 conversions per decode token, almost exactly the count B1 removed when it measured +0.109%. The hoist staged all six tensors once into internal RAM (216 floats, 864 B) and replaced the six per-token fp16_get() sites with array reads, on the argument that every one of those tensors is static archive data and fp16_get is exactly nd_f16(raw[i]). RESULT: device_output_exact 14/24, device_token_delta 344, gen_tokens 100 - the answers changed, so the change is not bit-exact and is DISCARDED on correctness, with the primary reading (6.1567) meaningless on wrong output. CAUSE, identified by comparing the fill against the call sites: my staging arrays were sized by t->shape[0], but these bias tensors are multi-dimensional, so shape[0] is only the first dimension and not the element count - mhc_a_pre needs 8 elements, mhc_b_pre and mhc_b_post need 32 each, mhc_b_res needs 128, all while their shape[0] is smaller - so the fill covered only a prefix and every index past it read zeros out of the static array. The per-token fp16_get() indexes the tensor LINEARLY, which is why the original code was correct and my "same indexes" port was not; the array was simply not filled far enough. CORRECTED RECIPE for a retry, recorded rather than run because it needs its own build: derive the element count the way the archive does - the product of the tensor's non-zero shape entries, or nbytes / sizeof(uint16_t) from the tensor record - assert that count fits the staging slots for each of the six tensors, and fill exactly that many elements into arrays sized for the largest (128). Then the six call sites read the arrays unchanged and the values are bit-identical by construction, because fp16_get is exactly nd_f16(raw[i]). WHAT THE RUN IS WORTH: the conversion-hoist rule's shape is supported (the conversion count really does match B1's), while the implementation must respect the archive's own element accounting; and the gates caught the error immediately - 14/24, delta 344, a changed token count - which is exactly the job the byte-exact device gate exists to do. description: Retracting my wrong PMU blocker and recording the concrete implementation with the real API and event masks in hand. MY ERROR, STATED PLAINLY: entry #926 claimed perfmon was only raw XDM registers with no callable API and that the block was shared across cores. Both halves were wrong. The installed component is /opt/esp/idf/components/perfmon with a callable interface - xtensa_perfmon_init(id, select, mask, kernelcnt, tracelevel), xtensa_perfmon_reset, start, stop, value, overflow - REQUIRES xtensa in its CMakeLists so the needle component only needs perfmon added to its REQUIRES, and access goes through the EXECUTING CORE's ERI path rather than a shared MMIO window, which is exactly why a per-core wrapper is possible. The recharging lesson is the campaign's own repeated one: I asserted a hardware/API blocker from a directory listing instead of reading the component, and the mentor's source read refuted it in one step. THE CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION, now using the real names from the installed example: the S3 has two counters, and the example's table gives the exact pairs to use - XTPERF_CNT_CYCLES/XTPERF_MASK_CYCLES for total cycles, XTPERF_CNT_INSN/XTPERF_MASK_INSN_ALL for retired instructions, and the two bubble events that answer the mentor's actual question: XTPERF_CNT_BUBBLES with XTPERF_MASK_BUBBLES_ALL & ~XTPERF_MASK_BUBBLES_R_HOLD_REG_DEP for waits from other causes versus XTPERF_MASK_BUBBLES_R_HOLD_REG_DEP for register-dependency waits - which is precisely the memory-versus-dependency discrimination the screen exists to produce. The shape is a bounded wrapper around each core's row callback: xtensa_perfmon_init both counters once per worker task (each core programs its own ERI counters), then reset + start immediately before the row callback and stop + value immediately after it inside the same task, accumulating per-core totals in static per-core slots and printing one line at model close. Bounded means: no new threads, no changes to the callback arithmetic, counters programmed once per task rather than per row, and the resulting numbers reported as a screen rather than as a speed claim.
