description: Two mentor corrections accepted and one of my own builds honestly relabelled. CORRECTION ONE: divisibility by 4 or 2 is not a dtype check. My B3 repair used nbytes % 4u == 0u for the permutation tables and nbytes % 2u == 0u for the mHC constants, but a length being a multiple of the element size says nothing about what TYPE the archive stored - the real check is to read the dtype enum in nd_cact.h and compare tp1->dtype, tp2->dtype and t[k]->dtype against the expected entries explicitly. The length checks I wrote remain useful as bounds (the tables must hold at least `need` entries and the mHC tensors at least the consumed counts) but they must not be described or relied on as dtype validation, and the dtype comparison has to be added. CORRECTION TWO, about my own label: what is running on board 3 is a GUARD-ONLY build - the same metadata path with stricter guards - and it is NOT the inverse-P2 performance test. I named its lane B3inv, which overstates it; the honest identification is that this run tests the guard repairs on the metadata path, and the inverse-P2 candidate has not been written at all. Its result may confirm that the guards cost nothing, which is worth knowing, but it must not be cited as an inverse-P2 measurement. ON B2: the residual clone exists but is unwired, and before wiring I need one thing I have not read - how kron1_blocks' output relates to kron2_rows' input in the shared wrapper, since kron2_rows reads c->b (a weight tensor) and c->m->hada_c (the activation) rather than the buffer kron1 wrote. Guessing that data flow is exactly the class of error that has cost this window several lanes, so the wiring waits for that one read rather than being invented; the prepared patch also still needs its wrapper, its caller switch and fail-closed checks before any build, as the earlier warning said. STATE RIGHT NOW: B1w3 is live on board 1 carrying the W3-prefix transfer onto the 6.1933 lineage, its six saved-file checks green before launch, and it is the one lane whose semantics are exactly what its name says; board 3 is running the guard-only metadata build just described; board 2 is free and its next edit is the residual wiring after the data-flow read. description: Read B3's saved diff before patching further, exactly as instructed, and it shows my partial edit is harmless but incomplete - which is worth stating precisely rather than discovering by a failed run. WHAT B3 CONTAINS NOW, versus its preserved metadata base: silu_ctx gained two fields (src, perm); silu_rows gained an if (c->perm) branch containing the fused P1 gather with the identical d2*sc*x+b2 expression and the same sigmoidf_pair and stores, with the original loop kept as the else arm; and the caller's initializer passes m->hada_b plus (const float *)0. Since nothing anywhere sets that perm field, the branch is UNREACHABLE and the else arm runs - so the program is behaviourally identical to the metadata base, which is why this is harmless-but-dead rather than wrong. TWO THINGS IT STILL NEEDS, both now identified from the diff rather than guessed: (1) a live perm source. The ctx field is declared const float * because the fused loop indexes c->perm[i] and multiplies by nothing - it is a float-indexed gather - but the numeric metadata is uint16_t, so a single float pointer cannot carry it; the ctx needs BOTH a const float *perm for the FP32 fallback path and a uint16_t *perm16 for the metadata path, with the loop selecting on perm16 and converting through (uint32_t) at the index, exactly as the original serial gather did. (2) The dtype guards never landed: my replace patterns for tp1->dtype == ND_DT_FP32 and t[k]->dtype != ND_DT_FP16 did not match the saved text, so the metadata path is still guarded only by divisibility and length, which the mentor has already ruled out as dtype validation. The enum values exist in nd_cact.h - ND_DT_FP16 = 1 and ND_DT_FP32 = 2 - so the correct edit is a direct comparison against those names. Also noted from the diff: the P2 consumer and its trailing * d3[i] term are untouched, which is what the lane requires. B2 IS FROZEN AS DIRECTED: B2resid2 is genuinely live (needle-board 477065, lane 477146, preflash checks 477466, host bench 477662), the duplicate argument is confirmed removed in the current source, and I did not edit, kill or relaunch it; my last assert had simply refused because the bad tail was already gone, which is the right outcome for a guard whose target no longer exists.
